title: [trd:trd-2026-8d825f54-tool-abstraction-layer:task:TRD-017-TEST] - [ ] **TRD-017-TEST** Test AC for confirmation behavior (4h)
description:
## Test Task: TRD-017-TEST
## References
TRD: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-8d825f54-tool-abstraction-layer.md
TRD Task: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-8d825f54-tool-abstraction-layer.md#trd-017-test
PRD: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-8d825f54-tool-abstraction-layer.md
PRD Requirement: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-8d825f54-tool-abstraction-layer.md#req-011
PRD ACs: AC-011-1, AC-011-2, AC-011-3, AC-011-4, AC-011-5
Verifies Task: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-8d825f54-tool-abstraction-layer.md#trd-017
Parent Epic: [trd:trd-2026-8d825f54-tool-abstraction-layer]
Read-first: read the TRD, TRD Task section, PRD and PRD Requirement above before any work on this bead.


--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-011**: Confirm resolved provider interactively; deterministic in non-interactive runs
Confirm resolved provider interactively; deterministic in non-interactive runs Priority: Must In an interactive session, the resolved adapter for a category is shown and confirmed once before the first externally visible action in that category, and re-confirmed if configuration changes mid-session. An externally visible action is any write outside the local working tree: pushing a branch, creating or updating a work item or change request, posting a comment, merging, deploying. Reads and local-only changes never prompt. In non-interactive runs (Foreman, `--foreman`, CI) the precedence chain decides with no prompt and the resolved adapter and its source are logged.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-011-1: Given an interactive session about to take its first write outside the local working tree in a category | When the adapter is resolved | Then it is shown and the action waits for confirmation
- AC-011-2: Given a confirmation already given | When a second action in the same category occurs | Then no new prompt appears
- AC-011-3: Given a non-interactive run | When resolution completes | Then no prompt appears and the log records adapter and source
- AC-011-4: Given configuration edited mid-session to select a different adapter | When the next action runs | Then confirmation is requested again
- AC-011-5: Given an interactive session making a read-only call or a local-only change | When the capability runs | Then no confirmation prompt appears

--- TRD Context ---
### Alternatives Considered

| Option | Approach | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|---|
| A: Prose-only adapters | Adapter is a skill; the agent follows its prose and normalizes tool output itself | Smallest build; fully editable | Cannot route internal CLIs deterministically (REQ-016), cannot validate output (REQ-022), cannot deny at runtime (REQ-023); behavior varies per model |
| **B: Manifest plus runner (chosen)** | Adapter is a skill directory: `SKILL.md` (vocabulary and agent-facing prose) plus a declarative `adapter.yaml` (capability command templates, output mapping, allowlist, health check, detection signals, required env names). A core resolver library and `toolchain-cli` execute capabilities deterministically | Meets PRD (adapter is a skill), Rule 8 (editable without rebuild), Rule 5 (enforcement in code), REQ-016 (CLIs call the same library) | New resolver, runner, manifest schema and output-mapping engine to build and test |
| C: Executable plugin adapters | Separately packaged executables speaking a versioned JSON protocol | Arbitrary logic; strongest isolation | Contradicts the PRD's skills-as-contract decision; fails Rule 8; needs per-OS packaging and a protocol |

**Rationale:** B is the only option that makes every PRD guarantee a code-enforced property while keeping adapters user-editable data. The requester selected B at the architecture gate.

### Interpretations and Resolved Design Issues

- **I1: plain version control.** The PRD taxonomy has no plain `git` category, yet about 45 sources invoke it. Plain `git` operations (status, commit, push, log, diff, merge-base) are `vcs.*` capabilities of the `workflow` category, whose default adapter is `plain-git`; the `git-town` adapter extends it. Recommend a PRD refine pass to name this explicitly.
- **I2: ambiguity versus no signal (PRD REQ-009 AC-2 vs REQ-010 AC-2).** "No detectable signal" means no signal source exists at all (no remote, no marker files); the shipped default is used. "Ambiguous" means two or more installed adapters match, or a signal source exists (for example a remote URL) but matches no installed adapter; resolution fails explicitly in non-interactive runs and asks in interactive runs.
- **I3: AC-023-2 (governed boundary denies).** The runner is invoked through the shell tool, so a command that was not granted the shell tool cannot run any adapter; an adapter therefore cannot widen grants. The runner additionally denies any command outside the adapter's binary-plus-subcommand allowlist. Denial of raw shell commands typed by an agent outside the runner remains host-enforced (hooks on Claude Code; none in this repo for Pi, OpenCode or Codex); the lint (REQ-019) keeps commands from issuing raw tool calls. This residual is recorded in the Threat Model.
- **I4: confirmation session identity.** No stable session id is exposed uniformly across runtimes. TRD-017 begins with a spike that records which id each runtime exposes (`ENSEMBLE_SESSION_ID`, host session variables); the passive confirmation record is keyed by `(sessionKey, category, adapter, configHash)` and falls back to the run id when no session id exists.
- **I5: repo-local adapters are untrusted by default.** A cloned repository can ship `.ensemble/adapters/`. Repo-local adapters resolve in every mode (satisfying AC-007-3) but a non-interactive run additionally requires the adapter name in the user's `trustedRepoAdapters` list; an interactive run shows the adapter's allowlist at first-use confirmation.
- **I6: no new runtime dependency.** The output-mapping engine uses a small dotted-path projection (`$.a.b[0]`, `|` alternation for "array or object"), not a JSONPath library, because constitution section 4 requires approval for new dependencies.
- **I7: work-graph selection.** `work-graph` is its own category with default `auto`: use the work-graph capabilities of the resolved tracker adapter when its manifest provides them; otherwise use the built-in `work-graph-links-fallback` adapter (tracker dependency links, then plan order stated as not dependency-aware). One manifest may implement several categories.
- **I8: PRD BDD floor.** Fourteen PRD requirements (REQ-001, 002, 004, 005, 006, 009, 010, 012, 015, 018, 021, 022, 024, 025) have two ACs, below the command's three-scenario floor. The test tasks specify exactly one scenario per AC; recommend a PRD refine pass to add edge or error ACs.
- **I10: packaging.** `packages/development` depends only on `js-yaml` and its libraries require only siblings, so the resolver library, category contracts, default selection, schemas and tool inventory all ship inside `packages/development` (`lib/toolchain/` and `toolchain/`). A standalone plugin install and the Pi vendor bundle therefore contain everything; other packages call `toolchain-cli` through `TOOLCHAIN_CLI` rather than importing it.
- **I9: preflight is enforced in code.** `toolchain-cli run` refuses a side-effecting capability unless a passing preflight record exists for the supplied `--run-id`; the command prose cannot silently skip preflight.
Verifies: TRD-017
Satisfies: REQ-011
PRD ACs Proven: AC-011-1, AC-011-2, AC-011-3, AC-011-4, AC-011-5
Proof of requirement: 
Target Files: 
Actions:

Test AC:
- [ ] Scenario: First external write waits for confirmation -- Given an interactive session about to take its first write outside the local working tree in a category, When the adapter is resolved, Then it is shown and the action waits for confirmation
- [ ] Scenario: Confirmation is not repeated -- Given a confirmation already given, When a second action in the same category occurs, Then no new prompt appears
- [ ] Scenario: Non-interactive run does not prompt -- Given a non-interactive run, When resolution completes, Then no prompt appears and the log records adapter and source
- [ ] Scenario: Config edit re-triggers confirmation -- Given configuration edited mid-session to select a different adapter, When the next action runs, Then confirmation is requested again
- [ ] Scenario: Read-only call needs no confirmation -- Given an interactive session making a read-only call or a local-only change, When the capability runs, Then no confirmation prompt appears

description:
## Test Task: TRD-024-TEST
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-15aa5acd-live-behavior-dispatch-autofix.md#trd-024-test
PRD Reference: #req-006

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen: Option C — single enforcement seam, additive.**

A new `MutationGuard` chokepoint in `agent-core` is the one place `policy.mode`, `capabilities.mutation_classes` (via the existing `hasMutationAuthority()`), and protected-path rules are resolved. It is wired once at the loader boundary rather than replicated per tool registration. The translator, matcher, and auto-fix loop are added to `pi-extension`. Discovery roots and `execution.test_command` are additive changes to existing schema/discovery code. `ToolRegistry`, `outbox`, and the compiler are reused unchanged.

### Alternatives considered

| Option | Summary | Why not chosen |
|---|---|---|
| **A — In-place extension** | Enforce mode/mutation/path rules as wrapper checks inside `behavior-loader`'s per-tool `execute()` closures. | Enforcement scattered across call sites; every future tool registration must remember to wrap. The PRD's central failure mode is *guarantees that exist in one place but are not reached from another* — Option A reproduces exactly that shape. |
| **B — Governance kernel** | Route every mutation through a `MutationBroker` + `GovernedWorkspace` in `agent-core`; `pi-extension` becomes a thin adapter. | Strongest long-term design and the right eventual target, but it re-opens already-shipped code across every tool path for a ~6-7 PR refactor before a single PRD requirement is demonstrable. Deferred deliberately, not rejected. |
| **C — Single enforcement seam** *(chosen)* | One `MutationGuard` chokepoint, wired once; everything else additive. | Gets a single auditable chokepoint (Option B's main benefit) without Option B's refactor surface. Fits the existing `agent-core` / `pi-extension` split. |

### Architectural note carried from grounding

Two defects found while grounding this design are folded into PR 1 rather than left implicit:

1. `pi-events.ts` emits `runtime.tool_result` / `runtime.tool.called` / `runtime.tool.failed` / `runtime.tool.completed`, none of which appear in `HARNESS_EVENT_TYPES` (which defines `runtime.tool_call.started` / `runtime.tool_call.completed`). `normalizeEvent` does not currently reject uncatalogued types, so PRD AC-002-1's "validated against the closed catalog" would be vacuous. Addressed by TRD-001 (`[satisfies INFRA]`).
2. `behavior-loader.ts:79` calls `registry.grant(...)` unconditionally immediately before `registry.invoke(...)`, making the grant boundary a rubber stamp for behavior-governed tools (unlike the echo path, where the grant is CLI-flag-gated). Addressed by TRD-003.

description:
## Task: TRD-021
## References
TRD: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-8d825f54-tool-abstraction-layer.md
TRD Task: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-8d825f54-tool-abstraction-layer.md#trd-021
PRD: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-8d825f54-tool-abstraction-layer.md
PRD Requirement: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-8d825f54-tool-abstraction-layer.md#req-021
PRD ACs: AC-021-1, AC-021-2
Parent Epic: [trd:trd-2026-8d825f54-tool-abstraction-layer]
Read-first: read the TRD, TRD Task section, PRD and PRD Requirement above before any work on this bead.


--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-021**: Identical resolution across generated runtimes
Identical resolution across generated runtimes Priority: Must Adapter resolution behaves identically in every runtime ensemble generates content for. The first-release supported runtimes are Claude Code, OpenCode, Pi/OMP and Codex.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-021-1: Given the same project config | When resolved in each supported runtime | Then the same adapter and source are reported per category
- AC-021-2: Given a runtime lacking support for a needed mechanism | When resolution runs there | Then it fails explicitly rather than falling back

--- TRD Context ---
### Alternatives Considered

| Option | Approach | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|---|
| A: Prose-only adapters | Adapter is a skill; the agent follows its prose and normalizes tool output itself | Smallest build; fully editable | Cannot route internal CLIs deterministically (REQ-016), cannot validate output (REQ-022), cannot deny at runtime (REQ-023); behavior varies per model |
| **B: Manifest plus runner (chosen)** | Adapter is a skill directory: `SKILL.md` (vocabulary and agent-facing prose) plus a declarative `adapter.yaml` (capability command templates, output mapping, allowlist, health check, detection signals, required env names). A core resolver library and `toolchain-cli` execute capabilities deterministically | Meets PRD (adapter is a skill), Rule 8 (editable without rebuild), Rule 5 (enforcement in code), REQ-016 (CLIs call the same library) | New resolver, runner, manifest schema and output-mapping engine to build and test |
| C: Executable plugin adapters | Separately packaged executables speaking a versioned JSON protocol | Arbitrary logic; strongest isolation | Contradicts the PRD's skills-as-contract decision; fails Rule 8; needs per-OS packaging and a protocol |

**Rationale:** B is the only option that makes every PRD guarantee a code-enforced property while keeping adapters user-editable data. The requester selected B at the architecture gate.

### Interpretations and Resolved Design Issues

- **I1: plain version control.** The PRD taxonomy has no plain `git` category, yet about 45 sources invoke it. Plain `git` operations (status, commit, push, log, diff, merge-base) are `vcs.*` capabilities of the `workflow` category, whose default adapter is `plain-git`; the `git-town` adapter extends it. Recommend a PRD refine pass to name this explicitly.
- **I2: ambiguity versus no signal (PRD REQ-009 AC-2 vs REQ-010 AC-2).** "No detectable signal" means no signal source exists at all (no remote, no marker files); the shipped default is used. "Ambiguous" means two or more installed adapters match, or a signal source exists (for example a remote URL) but matches no installed adapter; resolution fails explicitly in non-interactive runs and asks in interactive runs.
- **I3: AC-023-2 (governed boundary denies).** The runner is invoked through the shell tool, so a command that was not granted the shell tool cannot run any adapter; an adapter therefore cannot widen grants. The runner additionally denies any command outside the adapter's binary-plus-subcommand allowlist. Denial of raw shell commands typed by an agent outside the runner remains host-enforced (hooks on Claude Code; none in this repo for Pi, OpenCode or Codex); the lint (REQ-019) keeps commands from issuing raw tool calls. This residual is recorded in the Threat Model.
- **I4: confirmation session identity.** No stable session id is exposed uniformly across runtimes. TRD-017 begins with a spike that records which id each runtime exposes (`ENSEMBLE_SESSION_ID`, host session variables); the passive confirmation record is keyed by `(sessionKey, category, adapter, configHash)` and falls back to the run id when no session id exists.
- **I5: repo-local adapters are untrusted by default.** A cloned repository can ship `.ensemble/adapters/`. Repo-local adapters resolve in every mode (satisfying AC-007-3) but a non-interactive run additionally requires the adapter name in the user's `trustedRepoAdapters` list; an interactive run shows the adapter's allowlist at first-use confirmation.
- **I6: no new runtime dependency.** The output-mapping engine uses a small dotted-path projection (`$.a.b[0]`, `|` alternation for "array or object"), not a JSONPath library, because constitution section 4 requires approval for new dependencies.
- **I7: work-graph selection.** `work-graph` is its own category with default `auto`: use the work-graph capabilities of the resolved tracker adapter when its manifest provides them; otherwise use the built-in `work-graph-links-fallback` adapter (tracker dependency links, then plan order stated as not dependency-aware). One manifest may implement several categories.
- **I8: PRD BDD floor.** Fourteen PRD requirements (REQ-001, 002, 004, 005, 006, 009, 010, 012, 015, 018, 021, 022, 024, 025) have two ACs, below the command's three-scenario floor. The test tasks specify exactly one scenario per AC; recommend a PRD refine pass to add edge or error ACs.
- **I10: packaging.** `packages/development` depends only on `js-yaml` and its libraries require only siblings, so the resolver library, category contracts, default selection, schemas and tool inventory all ship inside `packages/development` (`lib/toolchain/` and `toolchain/`). A standalone plugin install and the Pi vendor bundle therefore contain everything; other packages call `toolchain-cli` through `TOOLCHAIN_CLI` rather than importing it.
- **I9: preflight is enforced in code.** `toolchain-cli run` refuses a side-effecting capability unless a passing preflight record exists for the supplied `--run-id`; the command prose cannot silently skip preflight.
Satisfies: REQ-021
Target File: 
Actions:

Implementation AC:
- [ ] Given one fixture `.ensemble/toolchain.yaml`, when the harness resolves via the four runtime entry points, then the 14-category `{adapter, source}` maps are deep-equal across all four
- [ ] Given a runtime bundle with `toolchain/` removed, when its CLI is invoked, then the harness observes a non-zero exit and an error naming the missing mechanism, never a default-adapter fallback
- [ ] Given the harness is wired into the root `npx jest scripts/tests` run (the step `.github/workflows/validate.yml` and `scripts/ci-local.js` execute), when one runtime returns a different source for one category, then the test fails naming runtime and category

Every result records what it was run against (Must)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-013-3: Given a finished suite | When results are stored | Then a small per-skill baseline summary is written for committing to the repository and the full run logs are kept as CI artifacts
- AC-013-4: Given a baseline summary in the repository | When a regression check runs locally or in CI | Then it compares against that committed summary

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen: Option C, extend `evals/` and put runtimes behind adapters.**

The repository already has a headless behavioral eval harness (`evals/run.js`, `evals/lib/sandbox.js`, `evals/lib/graders.js`, `.github/workflows/evals.yml`, five task-keyed scenarios, unit tests with a stub `claude`). It already provides a throwaway git sandbox, deterministic graders, a total spend cap (`--max-usd`), results files and an on-demand workflow. It lacks what the PRD is mostly about:

| PRD need | State today |
|---|---|
| Evals keyed by skill, editable as files | Scenarios are keyed by task, one `scenario.json` each |
| With-skill and no-skill arms | One arm only |
| Repeats and a reliability bar | One run per scenario |
| Scrubbed environment | `spawnSync` inherits the whole environment |
| Model, skill version, eval version, runtime in results | Only a model tag |
| Coverage per skill, result cache, replay, regression compare | None |
| Pi | None |

| Option | Summary | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| A. Extend in place | Add the above to `run.js`; Pi logic added inline | Simplest, but Claude Code and Pi logic would tangle in one file |
| B. Adopt an external eval tool | Replace the runner with a third-party tool and port graders | Needs a spike and a new-dependency approval (constitution, Approval Requirements); rework of five tested scenarios; unknown support for a no-skill arm and Pi |
| **C. Extend with runner adapters** | Keep the tested runner, sandbox and graders. Add skill-keyed eval files, arms, repeats, an env allowlist, a results schema, coverage, cache and compare, behind a small runner interface with Claude Code and Pi adapters | **Chosen.** No new dependency (Node built-ins only), builds on tested code, and the eval format stays tool-neutral so an external runner could consume it later |

The PRD's Entry criterion (tool spike, fallback to a minimal in-repo runner) resolves to the fallback: this TRD is that runner, built on the existing harness. No new dependency is introduced, so no dependency approval is needed. If the owner later wants an external tool, the eval files in `evals/skills/` are the stable input.

Decisions fixed by the PRD and carried here: deterministic checks decide verdicts; judged checks only supplement and use a different model; 5 runs per arm with 4 of 5 required; $50 per suite and 900 s per run by default; results committed as per-skill baseline summaries with full logs as CI artifacts; Claude Code and Pi; on-demand CI only; advisory regression check.

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-004**: Approval checkpoints auto-grant and are recorded (Must) [RISK: weakens a human checkpoint, so the record must be unambiguous]
Approval checkpoints auto-grant and are recorded (Must) [RISK: weakens a human checkpoint, so the record must be unambiguous]

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-004-1: Given `--foreman` and `ELIGIBLE_STAGE == implementation_approval` | When the checkpoint runs | Then no question is asked and one `RunIndexStore
- AC-004-2: Given the grant happened | When `--status` later reports the run | Then it shows that detail, so an auto-grant can never be mistaken for a human approval
- AC-004-3: Given `--foreman` is absent | When the checkpoint runs | Then it asks for explicit approval and, on absent or declined approval, makes no `mutate()` call, exactly as today
- AC-004-4: Given the material-plan-change staleness check finds the approved plan changed | When `--foreman` is set | Then approval is cleared and re-granted through the same recorded path, never silently kept

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen approach:** a prompt-only change to two YAML command sources. No TypeScript changes.

- `packages/development/commands/new-feature.yaml` gains a boolean `foreman` parameter and one derived variable, `FOREMAN`, defined once in Entry Point Resolution Step 1 and referenced by every later step. Each step that asks the user gets a `FOREMAN == true` branch that takes a deterministic, recorded, non-interactive decision. Each step that dispatches a stage skill appends `--foreman` when `FOREMAN == true`.
- `packages/development/commands/feature.yaml` (the `/ensemble:feature` front door) recognizes `--foreman` as the first token after the keyword and forwards it.
- Generated OMP, Pi and Codex artifacts are regenerated from the repo root, never hand-edited.

**Why prompt-only (Constitution Rule 8):** how a workflow behaves when no one can answer is something a maintainer would plausibly tune (for example, switching the PR gate to park instead of auto-grant). That belongs in the command prose, not in TypeScript. `RunIndexStore` already supports everything needed: `StageOutcome.detail` carries the "granted by `--foreman` policy" record.

**Additive-only edits (found in refinement):** the existing suites (`new-feature-command.test.js`, `feature-command.test.js`, `feature-input-validation-boundary.test.js`, `feature-concurrency-passthrough.test.js`) pin exact sentences in both YAML files, for example "any remaining text is an unsupported flag or argument rejected here". So no pre-existing sentence may be reworded or removed. Foreman behavior is added as new actions or appended sentences, and the existing suites must pass unchanged. For the front door that means: a new action, placed before the validation action, removes a leading `--foreman` token and sets `FOREMAN`, so the pinned validation sentences still read "remaining text" correctly; and a new action, placed after the invocation is constructed, inserts `--foreman` right after `/ensemble:new-feature` in whatever invocation was built.

**Alternatives rejected:**
- *Env-var-only detection (no flag).* Rejected: the maintainer asked for a `--foreman` flag, and the five stage skills already key on that flag.
- *A new RunRecord field `autoGranted`.* Rejected: TypeScript and schema change for information `StageOutcome.detail` already carries.
- *Parking at the approval gates.* Rejected by the maintainer: it stalls every no-user run.

description: Unresolved review-bot finding (github-actions[bot]) left on merged PR #241. Comment: https://github.com/Sunstone-Partners/ensemble/pull/241#discussion_r4476747459. Dedupe key: finding:pr241:comment4476747459. Recorded by ensemble-pr-merge pre-merge sweep while merging PR 244.

title: E2E fixtures embed copies of shipped behavior manifests and have already drifted
description:
FOUND 2026-09-29 while verifying br-zcxb.

reference-flow.e2e.test.ts is the repository's end-to-end proof that the behavior flow works. It does not run the manifests that ship. It embeds its own inline copies as template literals (FIX_BEHAVIOR, LEARN_BEHAVIOR).

THE COPIES HAVE ALREADY DRIFTED. The inline constitution-learning passes only:
  proposalRef, detail
The shipped .ensemble/behaviors/constitution-learning/behavior.yaml passes:
  proposalRef, detail, command, diagnosis, evidence
The diagnosis and evidence inputs are the br-zcxb fix. The e2e test asserts the flow works while exercising a manifest that predates that fix, so it would have stayed green if the shipped manifest lost those inputs entirely.

WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN AN ORDINARY STALE FIXTURE. The e2e is specifically the artifact cited when asking whether the system works end to end. Its value comes entirely from being the real thing. A copy that shares a name with the shipped manifest but not its contents reports on a behavior that nobody runs, and nothing signals the divergence -- the copy is valid YAML and compiles cleanly.

The same pattern applies to FIX_BEHAVIOR versus .ensemble/behaviors/fix-failing-test/behavior.yaml; I have not diffed that pair.

MITIGATED, NOT FIXED, in 5eb36b0: agent-core/tests/shipped-constitution-manifest.test.ts loads the SHIPPED manifest and proves the diagnosis reaches the assessment (mutation-checked: removing the input fails 2 tests). That covers the one input pair br-zcxb was about. It does not stop the e2e copies drifting again, anywhere else.

OPTIONS
(a) Have the e2e read the shipped manifests instead of embedding copies. Loses the ability to test variants inline, and couples the e2e to whatever the repo currently ships -- which is arguably the point of an e2e.
(b) Keep the copies but assert they are byte-identical to the shipped files, so drift fails loudly.
(c) Keep the copies and accept them as fixtures, renaming them so they do not read as the shipped behaviors.

NOTE: reference-flow.e2e.test.ts is a protected guardrail file, so whichever option is chosen needs operator approval to edit.

title: [trd:trd-2026-4dec59b8-local-ci-pr-approval:task:TRD-008] - [ ] **TRD-008** Finding and CI-failure sweep (`local-ci-sweep.js`) (5h)
description:
## Task: TRD-008
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-4dec59b8-local-ci-pr-approval.md#trd-008
PRD Reference: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-4dec59b8-local-ci-pr-approval.md#req-007

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-007**: Bot review findings become tracked work (Must)
Bot review findings become tracked work (Must) Findings that bot reviewers (such as CodeRabbit) raise on a PR, before or after it lands, are captured as follow-up beads so they are not lost when review no longer gates the merge.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-007-1: Given a PR merged while bot reviewers had unresolved actionable findings | When the merge completes | Then each is recorded as a bead linking back to the original comment
- AC-007-2: Given bot findings posted after a PR has merged | When the merge flow next runs | Then it sweeps recently merged PRs and records any finding not already tracked as a bead, without creating duplicates for findings already recorded
- AC-007-3: Given no unresolved bot findings | When the merge completes | Then no beads are created
- AC-008-1: Given a PR merged on local evidence | When hosted CI later fails for that commit or the resulting base-branch commit | Then the next merge-flow run records a regression bead linked to the failing run
- AC-008-2: Given a push to a PR | When hosted CI triggers | Then it runs as it does today
- AC-008-3: Given a hosted-CI failure already recorded as a bead | When the merge flow next runs | Then it does not create a duplicate
- AC-012-1: Given the feature is installed | When no maintainer invokes it | Then nothing runs in the background
- AC-012-2: Given the late-finding and post-merge-failure sweeps | When no merge-flow run occurs | Then no sweep occurs; detection happens only as part of a run a maintainer starts

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen approach (Option C):** A `local-ci-gate` skill owns the editable procedure; a small set of pure-JS helpers in `packages/development/lib/` owns only what must be unforgeable; `pr-merge.yaml` invokes the skill.

- `packages/development/skills/local-ci-gate/SKILL.md` is the single reusable procedure and owns everything a maintainer would plausibly tune (Constitution Rule 8): the order of the run, the messages, the bead wording, and how failures are explained.
- Pure-JS modules in `packages/development/lib/` own only what grades a claim or protects a boundary (Rules 7 and 8's enforcement exception): run-record verification, bot-vs-human classification, bead dedupe keys, approval-set config validation, and GitHub App credential handling. They make no network calls except the one module whose purpose is to post a status.
- `packages/git/commands/pr-merge.yaml` calls the skill at its existing Merge phase. It does not restate gate logic.
- The gate runs in-session in the maintainer's own process. There is no daemon, scheduler or background sweep (Rule 4; REQ-012).

**Alternatives considered (user chose C):**

- **Option A -- prose-only:** fewest files, but head-binding, run-record verification and human/bot classification would be prose a model can misread, and tests could only assert wording. Rejected: the PRD's core property is that evidence cannot be reused across commits.
- **Option B -- TypeScript runtime in agent-core:** strongest typing, but adds a build/dist surface and pulls editable criteria toward code against Rule 8. Rejected: the one place a real client is tempting (App JWT signing) needs only Node's built-in `crypto`.

**Dependency decision (user approved):** no new dependency. The App's RS256 JWT is signed with Node `crypto`; the REST calls use `fetch`. This avoids the constitution's new-dependency approval gate and keeps the signing path small and auditable.

**Rationale:** Option C matches repository precedent (TRD-2026-82b6a138), keeps editable behavior out of TypeScript, and is the minimum code that makes the trust properties testable.
Satisfies: REQ-007
PRD ACs: AC-007-1, AC-007-2, AC-007-3, AC-008-1, AC-008-2, AC-008-3, AC-012-1, AC-012-2
Target File: packages/development/lib/local-ci-sweep.js
Actions:

Implementation AC:
- [ ] Given fetched facts for recently merged PRs, when `findUntracked` runs, then it returns each unresolved Bot finding and each failed hosted-CI run not already represented by an existing bead
- [ ] Given a finding, when its dedupe key is built, then the key is derived from the PR number, comment id or check run id and never from text, so re-running yields the same key
- [ ] Given the same facts twice, when it runs twice, then the second run returns nothing new
- [ ] Given no unresolved findings and no failures, when it runs, then it returns an empty result and the skill creates no beads
- [ ] Given the module and skill, when inspected, then neither registers a timer, daemon, hook or schedule
Dependencies:

title: [trd:trd-2026-15aa5acd-live-behavior-dispatch-autofix:task:TRD-010-TEST] - [ ] **TRD-010-TEST** Auto-mode test-command validation tests (2h)
description:
## Test Task: TRD-010-TEST
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-15aa5acd-live-behavior-dispatch-autofix.md#trd-010-test
PRD Reference: #req-012

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen: Option C — single enforcement seam, additive.**

A new `MutationGuard` chokepoint in `agent-core` is the one place `policy.mode`, `capabilities.mutation_classes` (via the existing `hasMutationAuthority()`), and protected-path rules are resolved. It is wired once at the loader boundary rather than replicated per tool registration. The translator, matcher, and auto-fix loop are added to `pi-extension`. Discovery roots and `execution.test_command` are additive changes to existing schema/discovery code. `ToolRegistry`, `outbox`, and the compiler are reused unchanged.

### Alternatives considered

| Option | Summary | Why not chosen |
|---|---|---|
| **A — In-place extension** | Enforce mode/mutation/path rules as wrapper checks inside `behavior-loader`'s per-tool `execute()` closures. | Enforcement scattered across call sites; every future tool registration must remember to wrap. The PRD's central failure mode is *guarantees that exist in one place but are not reached from another* — Option A reproduces exactly that shape. |
| **B — Governance kernel** | Route every mutation through a `MutationBroker` + `GovernedWorkspace` in `agent-core`; `pi-extension` becomes a thin adapter. | Strongest long-term design and the right eventual target, but it re-opens already-shipped code across every tool path for a ~6-7 PR refactor before a single PRD requirement is demonstrable. Deferred deliberately, not rejected. |
| **C — Single enforcement seam** *(chosen)* | One `MutationGuard` chokepoint, wired once; everything else additive. | Gets a single auditable chokepoint (Option B's main benefit) without Option B's refactor surface. Fits the existing `agent-core` / `pi-extension` split. |

### Architectural note carried from grounding

Two defects found while grounding this design are folded into PR 1 rather than left implicit:

1. `pi-events.ts` emits `runtime.tool_result` / `runtime.tool.called` / `runtime.tool.failed` / `runtime.tool.completed`, none of which appear in `HARNESS_EVENT_TYPES` (which defines `runtime.tool_call.started` / `runtime.tool_call.completed`). `normalizeEvent` does not currently reject uncatalogued types, so PRD AC-002-1's "validated against the closed catalog" would be vacuous. Addressed by TRD-001 (`[satisfies INFRA]`).
2. `behavior-loader.ts:79` calls `registry.grant(...)` unconditionally immediately before `registry.invoke(...)`, making the grant boundary a rubber stamp for behavior-governed tools (unlike the echo path, where the grant is CLI-flag-gated). Addressed by TRD-003.

title: [trd:trd-2026-b6db9749-behavior-habits-runtime:task:TRD-025] - [ ] **TRD-025** Run the conformance suite on a Linux runner and record the results (3h)
description:
## Task: TRD-025
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-b6db9749-behavior-habits-runtime.md#trd-025
PRD Reference: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-b6db9749-behavior-habits-runtime.md#req-021

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-021**: The complete local path is independently verified on Windows, Linux, and macOS
The complete local path is independently verified on Windows, Linux, and macOS Priority: Must [RISK: verification evidence does not yet exist for any of the three platforms as of this PRD]

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-021-1: Given the trigger/dispatch/notification path | When run on each of Windows | Then each platform has its own passing conformance suite run
- AC-021-2: Given a behavior works on one platform | When parity is claimed for another | Then that claim is backed by that platform's own conformance evidence, never inferred

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen: Option B — dedicated adapter modules per new trigger-source type, plus a shared notification-state module.** Unchanged from 1.0.0.

New `file-source-adapter.ts` and `release-source-adapter.ts` under `packages/agent-core/src/behavior/` each produce a `BehaviorEvent` through `normalizeEvent`, mirroring the existing `pi-events.ts` → `event-translator.ts` → `normalizeEvent` → `LocalEventMatcher` chain. A new `notification-state.ts` in `pi-extension` centralises busy, duplicate and stale tracking for every behavior. Package quarantine gets its own `package-quarantine.ts` beside `package-discovery.ts`.

### Decisions added in 1.1.0

1. **How artifact changes are detected: content hashes checked at lifecycle points.** No `fs.watch`, no new dependency.
   - The adapter derives its watch set from the compiled `artifact.changed` triggers (the `path` predicate).
   - It hashes those files at `tool_result` and at `agent_end`, and emits an event when a digest differs from the last one seen in the session.
   - The hooks it relies on already exist, which is what AC-001-2 means by "supported host API".
   - It behaves the same on every OS (see REQ-023).
   - It needs no new dependency, which constitution §4 would require approval for.

   | Option | Why not chosen |
   |---|---|
   | `fs.watch` | Event semantics differ between macOS, Linux and Windows (rename-vs-change, recursive support). That is exactly the kind of per-platform behavior difference REQ-023 forbids absorbing silently. It also keeps a handle open for the whole session. |
   | `chokidar` | A new runtime dependency (constitution §4), for a problem that lifecycle-point hashing already solves. |

   The limitation, stated rather than hidden: a change is seen at the next tool call or at the end of the run, not instantly. NFR-001 measures from event validation, so this latency is outside its budget. TRD-003 reports it separately.

2. **Release signal (resolves the PRD's REQ-002 clarification): a new `v*` tag in local refs.** This matches this repo's `release.yml` (`on: push: tags: ['v*']`).
   - The tag pattern is a trigger predicate, so repositories with different conventions change configuration, not code (Rule 8).
   - It is detected two ways. First, from a successful tag-creating tool call (`git tag`, `gh release create`), in the same way `repository.changed` is derived today. Second, by diffing tag refs at session start and at `agent_end`, which covers tags that arrive by fetch.
   - It emits the **existing** catalog type `release.completed`, carrying `{ tag, sha, source }`.
   - One tag produces one event per session, whichever path sees it first.

3. **Coverage metric (resolves the PRD's REQ-016 clarification): Jest `json-summary` output, per file, `lines.pct` and `branches.pct` by default.**
   - Each package's `test:coverage` is `jest --coverage`. Jest's default reporters (`json`, `lcov`, `text`, `clover`) produce raw maps, not percentages.
   - So the behavior watches `coverage/coverage-summary.json`, and its README tells repositories to enable `json-summary`.
   - The metrics and the threshold (default 1.0 percentage point) are behavior configuration.
   - If the artifact never appears, the behavior shows up as an inert trigger in `/ensemble-status`; it is never silently idle.
   - The baseline is the previous snapshot seen **in the same session** (Rule 4). The first observation in a session only sets the baseline.

4. **The comparison is a generic command: `artifact.compare` (TRD-033).** It compares numeric JSON paths between the previous and current snapshot of an artifact and knows nothing about coverage.
   - The alternatives were rejected. Doing the comparison in an agent step would make the reported delta an unverified model claim (REQ-012). A coverage-specific command would make the third behavior need Ensemble code (REQ-018).
   - It lands in PR 1, which is why PR 5 can be configuration only.

5. **Notification transport** (REQ-009, REQ-010). `notification-state.ts` delivers to two sinks:
   - **The user**, through `SessionUiBridge.notify`, a new method that wraps `ctx.ui.notify`. Headless sessions fall back to the console.
   - **The model's context**, through `pi.sendMessage` with `display: true` and `triggerTurn: false`.

   `triggerTurn: false` is deliberate. #107 deleted the continuation path because a message that makes the agent act bypasses `MutationGuard` (`extension.ts:118-140`); a notification is data, never an instruction. Any test-derived text in a notification is fenced and labelled as data, a lesson from #94's live runs. `sendMessage` is added to `assertRequiredCapabilities`.

6. **Verified fix application** (REQ-033). This is configuration plus two small code changes.
   - A new behavior, `apply-verified-fix`, runs `mode: auto`. It triggers on `fix.verified` with the predicate `verdict: passed`, declares only `fix.apply` with no tools, and calls `fix.apply { proposalRef: ${event.payload.proposalRef} }`.
   - `CommandRegistry` then asks `ApprovalGate`. Today the prompt is only `descriptor.description` ("Apply a verified fix proposal…"), so the human would approve without seeing what changes. Code change 1 (TRD-019): the prompt names the proposal, its files and a diff summary.
   - `commit-policy.ts` has no importers today. Code change 2 (TRD-021): wire it in so an applied fix is committed with attribution.

### Alternatives considered (architecture)

| Option | Summary | Why not chosen |
|---|---|---|
| **A — Widen the existing translator, inline notification** | Add file and release branches inside `event-translator.ts`; keep notification-state logic at each `ctx.ui.notify` call site. | `event-translator.ts` would cover three unrelated source domains. Busy/duplicate/stale logic would be copied per behavior, which is the per-reaction duplication the PRD sets out to remove. |
| **B — Dedicated adapter modules + shared notification-state module** *(chosen)* | One adapter module per source type, all feeding the same ingress; one shared notification-state module. | Matches the existing boundary (`agent-core` = provider-neutral logic, `pi-extension` = host wiring), and centralises notification state once. |
| **C — Single generic "external signal" adapter** | One configurable "watch path X for condition Y" abstraction for both sources. | Risks becoming an arbitrary-condition escape hatch around the closed, versioned catalog (REQ-CQRS-005); still duplicates notification state. |
Satisfies: REQ-021
PRD ACs: AC-021-1, AC-021-2
Target File: .github/workflows/test.yml` (OS matrix job), docs/platform-conformance.md` (new)

- [ ] Given the job's steps, when a test fails, then the job fails on that command's own exit status: no pipes into `tail` (constitution Amendment 2026-09-29).

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-005**: A contributor can start a new eval from a template (Should)
A contributor can start a new eval from a template (Should) Execution

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-005-1: Given a contributor wants an eval for a new skill | When they use the provided template | Then they get a runnable skeleton that passes loading checks once its fields are filled in

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen: Option C, extend `evals/` and put runtimes behind adapters.**

The repository already has a headless behavioral eval harness (`evals/run.js`, `evals/lib/sandbox.js`, `evals/lib/graders.js`, `.github/workflows/evals.yml`, five task-keyed scenarios, unit tests with a stub `claude`). It already provides a throwaway git sandbox, deterministic graders, a total spend cap (`--max-usd`), results files and an on-demand workflow. It lacks what the PRD is mostly about:

| PRD need | State today |
|---|---|
| Evals keyed by skill, editable as files | Scenarios are keyed by task, one `scenario.json` each |
| With-skill and no-skill arms | One arm only |
| Repeats and a reliability bar | One run per scenario |
| Scrubbed environment | `spawnSync` inherits the whole environment |
| Model, skill version, eval version, runtime in results | Only a model tag |
| Coverage per skill, result cache, replay, regression compare | None |
| Pi | None |

| Option | Summary | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| A. Extend in place | Add the above to `run.js`; Pi logic added inline | Simplest, but Claude Code and Pi logic would tangle in one file |
| B. Adopt an external eval tool | Replace the runner with a third-party tool and port graders | Needs a spike and a new-dependency approval (constitution, Approval Requirements); rework of five tested scenarios; unknown support for a no-skill arm and Pi |
| **C. Extend with runner adapters** | Keep the tested runner, sandbox and graders. Add skill-keyed eval files, arms, repeats, an env allowlist, a results schema, coverage, cache and compare, behind a small runner interface with Claude Code and Pi adapters | **Chosen.** No new dependency (Node built-ins only), builds on tested code, and the eval format stays tool-neutral so an external runner could consume it later |

The PRD's Entry criterion (tool spike, fallback to a minimal in-repo runner) resolves to the fallback: this TRD is that runner, built on the existing harness. No new dependency is introduced, so no dependency approval is needed. If the owner later wants an external tool, the eval files in `evals/skills/` are the stable input.

Decisions fixed by the PRD and carried here: deterministic checks decide verdicts; judged checks only supplement and use a different model; 5 runs per arm with 4 of 5 required; $50 per suite and 900 s per run by default; results committed as per-skill baseline summaries with full logs as CI artifacts; Claude Code and Pi; on-demand CI only; advisory regression check.

## Test Task: TRD-020-TEST
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-70e784f2-code-review-process.md#trd-020-test
PRD Reference: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-70e784f2-code-review-process.md#req-004

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-004**: Multiple fresh-context reviewers (Must)
Multiple fresh-context reviewers (Must) A review is performed by more than one reviewer, each starting with fresh context rather than the context that produced the change.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-004-3: Given a reviewer or verifier runs | When it completes | Then it has made no change to the repository or to PR state other than recording or posting findings
- AC-004-2: Given reviewers disagree on whether something is a defect | When findings are collected | Then every candidate finding from every reviewer is recorded with its source

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen approach (Option C):** extend the pattern TRD-2026-82b6a138 established: **editable behavior in skills, agents and markdown; a small set of pure, deterministic libraries for what must not be self-certified by a model.**

- **User-owned (Constitution Rule 8), prose or data a maintainer edits without a toolchain:** per-area rules (`REVIEW.md` files), the policy block inside the root `REVIEW.md` (round cap, depth table, bot and maintainer logins, sensitive and High paths, Low-waiver state), severity definitions, reviewer, verifier, classifier and security-lane prompts, the PR template, the sweep and explainer procedures. All of it is read from the **target branch**, never from the PR head (REQ-024).
- **Enforcement (Rules 5 and 7), code that grades a model's claim:** vote tally, tier assignment with its sensitive-path floor and Low-waiver evidence, approval evaluation bound to a commit, the merge gate, round-cap derivation, repeat suppression, delta-range selection, depth bounds, slice coverage, metrics and eval scoring. Each is a pure CommonJS module in `packages/development/lib/`, exposed as a JSON-in/JSON-out subcommand of the existing `pr-review-cli.js`, following the 82b6a138 precedent. None performs network I/O or holds a timer.
- **Entry points (Rule 6):** every capability is reached through the one `pr-review-cycle` skill, which `fix-issue`, `implement-trd-beads` and `pr-merge` already invoke or will invoke (a new `MODE=gate` for `pr-merge`). YAML callers reference the skill only, never the CLI, as the existing parity tests require.
- **Recurrence (Rule 4):** nightly or weekly sweeps and daily eval runs are on-demand skills; a workflow template for the host repository is opt-in and scaffolded by init-project. Ensemble's own workflows gain no `schedule` trigger.

**Alternatives considered (user chose C):**

- **Option A -- prose-only skills and agents:** fewest files and fastest to ship. Rejected: the vote threshold, the tier floor, commit-bound approvals and the round cap would be prose a model can misread or skip, so none of these gates could be shown to fail (Rule 7), and "a bot approval never counts" would be a request, not a guarantee.
- **Option B -- a new TypeScript review engine in `agent-core`:** strongest typing and one runtime. Rejected: a new build and `dist` surface and cross-package coupling for a prompt-level feature, editable criteria pulled into code (against Rule 8), and drift toward an ensemble-owned dispatcher that competes with Foreman (Rule 4).

**Rationale:** Option C is the best fit for this brownfield repo. It adds only the code that grades claims, keeps everything a maintainer or adopting team would tune in files they can edit, adds no dependency (Constitution §4) and no CI secret, vendors into Pi automatically through the existing require-closure bundler, and each gate can be mutation-proven using the harness that already exists.

**Decisions taken where the PRD left a choice** (each is editable policy, not a hidden constant):

| Decision | Value | Where it lives |
|---|---|---|
| Policy format | Fenced `ensemble-review-policy` JSON block in the root `REVIEW.md` (no new parser dependency) | REVIEW.md, read from the base commit |
| "Cannot vouch for" a push (AC-010-3, AC-014-2) | Commit is unvouched when its tree differs from the reviewed tree and it is not a remediation commit recorded in the review-state report, or it is a merge commit | `pr-review-scope.js`, `pr-review-approvals.js` |
| Slice threshold for large PRs (AC-018-1) | 1500 changed lines, configurable | policy block |
| Area rules vs policy keys | Policy keys are read from the **root** file only; area files carry guidance, and the more restrictive instruction wins when areas conflict (AC-001-2) | skill prose |
| First PR that introduces REVIEW.md | No base copy exists, so strict defaults apply (Low treated as Medium, cap 3, default sensitive set) | `pr-review-policy.js` |
| Verifier majority | Strict majority of the expected verifier count (2 of 3, 3 of 5) | `pr-review-votes.js` |

title: [trd:trd-2026-f08a2a09-command-lifecycle-hooks:task:TRD-019-TEST] - [ ] **TRD-019-TEST** Trust store behavior (3h)
description:
## Test Task: TRD-019-TEST
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-f08a2a09-command-lifecycle-hooks.md#trd-019-test
PRD Reference: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-f08a2a09-command-lifecycle-hooks.md#req-022

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-022**: Hooks run only in a project the user has explicitly trusted (Must) [RISK: a cloned repository could run arbitrary executables at its first command]
Hooks run only in a project the user has explicitly trusted (Must) [RISK: a cloned repository could run arbitrary executables at its first command] Measured in Pi 1.2.0: the host reports a project as trusted by default in every mode, with no prompt, and as untrusted only when the user passes `--no-approve`. Host trust alone therefore protects almost no one, so the user's explicit trust of a project's hooks is a separate, required condition. Goals and Non-Goals Goals: Deterministic start and end boundaries for Ensemble commands, in a harness that can honor them. A configuration contract that is validated before it can do anything. Honest reporting where a harness cannot honor a hook. Non-goals: Replacing or wrapping every harness's command execution (deferred wrapper). Observing sessions, turns or tool calls (the harnesses' own events already do). Letting a handler change what a command did. Open Questions These become the interview agenda in `/ensemble:refine-prd`. 1. Can the Pi extension host observe an aborted run? Settled by measurement: an abort emits no `agent_before_settle`, but `agent_settled` reports `aborted: true` (10 of 10 runs), so cancellation is observable. (REQ-004, REQ-021) 2. What is the handler output bound? The TRD sets it; the PRD requires only that a documented bound exists. (AC-009-4) Probe evidence (2026-10-15, Pi 1.2.0, `pi -p`, a throwaway extension logging events; not part of the repository): Start is observable. `input` fired with the raw slash text (`/probe-cmd hello`), then `before_agent_start` fired with the expanded template prompt, then `agent_start` and `turn_start`. The command's name and arguments are readable at `input`. A loop's end is observable, in this order: `agent_end`, then `agent_before_settle`, then `agent_settled`. Outcome is carried by `agent_before_settle`. It reported `outcome: "completed"` for a model that answered and `outcome: "error"` for three runs where the model call failed. In those error runs `agent_settled` still reported `aborted: false`, so `agent_settled` alone cannot tell success from failure. Not observed: `ui_prompt_start` / `ui_prompt_end` and any event that names one command's completion. This confirms that a completion step (REQ-021) is needed, because a loop's settling says only that the loop stopped. Measured in the implementation probe (2026-10-15, Pi 1.2.0; print, RPC and the interactive TUI; `litellm/qwen`): Abort: in 10 of 10 aborted runs `agent_before_settle` never fired, so no `aborted` outcome exists; the event order was `agent_end` then `agent_settled` with `aborted: true`. The reliable cancel signal is `agent_settled.aborted === true`. Completed runs fire `agent_before_settle` with `outcome: "completed"`; an error run fires it with `outcome: "error"` (observed earlier). Shutdown: the host awaited an async `session_shutdown` handler on every normal exit measured (print, RPC stdin close and `SIGTERM`, TUI `/quit`, Ctrl+D, Ctrl+C twice), up to the longest wait tried, 100 000 ms. RPC `SIGINT` kills the process at once and runs no handler. Trust: `ctx.isProjectTrusted()` was `true` in all six combinations of mode and directory with no prompt, and `false` only with `--no-approve`. Input forms: a prompt template arrives as `/<name> <args>` and a skill as `/skill:<name> <args>`. Limits of this evidence: one `completed` run, three `error` runs with the outcome logged, three runs that produced no settle event (timeout or no response), and print mode only. The first error run predates logging of the outcome field and is not counted. Resolved in refinement (2026-10-15): A rejected invocation produces a start and an end with outcome `failed` (AC-002-2). This replaced the earlier decision that a rejected invocation produces no events: in Pi the command's own prompt validates its arguments, so the start must fire from the runtime before the workflow if it is to be deterministic and a start handler's block is to be enforced by the runtime. Found while designing the TRD (2026-10-15). For harnesses with no adapter, the guide, the capability table and a status check state that hooks are inactive; nothing is shown at command time (AC-017-2). A start handler's block produces an end event with outcome `failed` (AC-004-5). `on_error` is required on every handler (AC-010-4). The source recommendation both required explicit error behavior and defaulted end hooks to `continue`; the maintainer chose to require it. A command's end in Pi is an explicit completion step (REQ-021). Default timeouts are 5 seconds for shell handlers and 30 seconds for prompt handlers, overridable per handler (AC-009-5, AC-011-5). Selections list each command explicitly; wildcards and groups are rejected (AC-006-4). No handler runs until the host trusts the project and the user has explicitly trusted that project's hooks (REQ-022). The second condition was added after the Pi probe showed host trust is true by default; the user's trust is stored outside the repository and is voided when the hooks file or a handler file it names changes. A settled loop never ends a command (AC-021-4); a command that never signals completion ends as `cancelled` when the session ends or the next command begins (AC-021-5). This replaced an earlier rule that ended it as `failed` on every settle, which would have ended any command that paused to ask the user a plain-text question. Found while designing the TRD (2026-10-15). The completion instruction is carried by the adapter at run time rather than generated into every command (AC-021-1). Dependency Map REQ-001 -> none. REQ-002 depends on REQ-001. REQ-003 depends on REQ-001. REQ-004 depends on REQ-001, REQ-002. REQ-005 depends on REQ-001. REQ-006 -> none. REQ-007 depends on REQ-006. REQ-008 depends on REQ-006. REQ-009 depends on REQ-005, REQ-006, REQ-010. REQ-010 depends on REQ-006, REQ-007. REQ-011 depends on REQ-005, REQ-006, REQ-010. REQ-012 depends on REQ-009, REQ-011. REQ-013 depends on REQ-012. REQ-014 depends on REQ-001. REQ-015 depends on REQ-001 through REQ-007, REQ-009, REQ-010, REQ-012, REQ-014, REQ-021, REQ-022. REQ-016 depends on REQ-014. REQ-017 depends on REQ-014. REQ-018 depends on REQ-005, REQ-006, REQ-009, REQ-011, REQ-014. REQ-019 depends on REQ-001 through REQ-017, REQ-021, REQ-022. REQ-020 depends on REQ-009, REQ-011. REQ-021 depends on REQ-001, REQ-004, REQ-014. REQ-022 depends on REQ-006, REQ-009, REQ-017. Clusters to deliver together: Lifecycle contract: REQ-001 to REQ-005. Configuration: REQ-006 to REQ-008. Handlers: REQ-009 to REQ-013, REQ-020 and REQ-022. Adapter proof: REQ-014, REQ-015, REQ-017 and REQ-021. No circular dependencies. Implementation Readiness Gate | Dimension | Score | Note | | --- | --- | --- | | Completeness | 4 | All feature areas covered; the handler output bound is deliberately left to the TRD. | | Testability | 4 | Every Must requirement has verifiable ACs. | | Clarity | 4 | Edge cases around rejected, blocked and unfinished invocations are decided or marked, not guessed. | | Feasibility | 3 | Start, the completed/error outcomes, the abort signal, tool registration, the trust check and per-turn injection are confirmed in Pi. The completion signal is still performed by the model. | Overall: 3.75 (CONCERNS), not re-scored. The amendments since 1.0.2 removed rules that could not be implemented and added the trust requirement, but the score was not re-evaluated, so it is left as it was. No open question remains except the handler output bound, which the TRD sets. Changelog 1.0.0 (2026-10-15): Initial draft. 1.0.1 (2026-10-15): Refinement. Resolved 5 of 6 clarification items and added REQ-021 (uniform completion step) and REQ-022 (project trust). AC-005-3 made testable, AC-006-4 added, default timeouts stated. 1.0.2 (2026-10-15): Second refinement pass. Recorded Pi 1.2.0 probe evidence (start, loop end, `completed`/`error` outcome from `agent_before_settle`); narrowed Open Question 1 to the pending-question and abort cases. 1.0.3 (2026-10-15): Amended during TRD design. AC-021-1, AC-021-4 and AC-021-5 rewritten (a settle never ends a command; completion instruction carried at run time); Open Question 2 closed; clarification markers now 0. Readiness score not re-evaluated. 1.0.4 (2026-10-15): Amended during TRD design. AC-002-1, AC-002-2, AC-017-2 and AC-021-2 rewritten, AC-021-7 added: `command.start` fires at input, a rejected invocation ends as `failed`, and adapter-less harnesses are covered by documentation and a status check. Readiness score not re-evaluated. 1.0.5 (2026-10-15): Amended during implementation after the Pi probe. REQ-022 now requires the user's explicit trust of a project's hooks in addition to host trust, because host trust is true by default; AC-022-5 to AC-022-8 added. Open Question 1 closed by measurement (cancellation is observable through `agent_settled.aborted`). Probe measurements recorded. Readiness score not re-evaluated.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-022-5: Given the host trusts the project but the user has not explicitly trusted its hooks | When a command runs | Then no handler runs, and the user sees a warning that names the hooks file and says how to trust it
- AC-022-6: Given the user trusted a project's hooks | When the hooks file or any handler file it names (an executable or a prompt file inside the project) later changes | Then the next command runs no handler until the user trusts it again
- AC-022-7: Given a repository ships its own trust data or its own hooks file | When it is opened | Then that data cannot grant trust, because the user's trust is stored outside the repository
- AC-022-8: Given the user is asked to trust a project's hooks | When the question is shown | Then it lists every handler with its exact executable and arguments or prompt file, and trust is recorded only after an explicit confirmation made by the user, never by a model's tool call

--- TRD Context ---
**Decision:** Build the lifecycle as a harness-neutral core in `packages/agent-core` (event payloads, configuration validation, redaction, a shell runner, a prompt runner, a serial dispatcher, and a per-session command-run tracker) and one adapter in `packages/pi-extension` that connects it to Pi. The adapter is the only code that knows Pi's event names.

**Decisions made by the maintainer during design (all recorded in PRD v1.0.2 to v1.0.4):**

- The first release is adapter-specific, with Pi as the proving harness. A runtime-owned wrapper is deferred.
- `command.start` fires from the runtime when the command's slash input is seen, so it never depends on the model and a start handler's block is enforced by the runtime. A command whose own prompt then rejects its arguments has already produced a start and ends as `failed`.
- A command's completion is signalled by a silent `ensemble_command_complete` tool that the model is told to call last. The instruction is injected per turn by the adapter, not generated into every Pi prompt, so projects without hooks see no change.
- A settled loop never ends a command. A command that never signals completion ends as `cancelled` when the session ends or the next command begins.
- A prompt handler is evaluated by an isolated headless child (`pi -p --no-session -ne -nt -np`), parsed against a typed response contract.
- No handler runs until the host reports the project as trusted (`ctx.isProjectTrusted()`) **and** the user has explicitly trusted this project's hooks. The Pi probe measured host trust as true by default in every mode, so it alone blocks nothing. The user's trust is recorded outside the repository against a digest of the hooks file and every handler file it names, and a change to any of them voids it.
- Cancellation is detected from `agent_settled.aborted === true`, not from an `aborted` outcome: the probe found that an abort fires no `agent_before_settle`. An error is detected from `agent_before_settle.outcome === "error"`.
- `on_error` is required on every handler. Default timeouts are 5 seconds for shell handlers and 30 seconds for prompt handlers.
- Selections list commands by name. Wildcards and groups are rejected.
- For harnesses with no adapter, the guide, a capability table and a status check say hooks are inactive. Nothing is shown at command time there.

**Why code and not a prompt (Constitution rule 8):** what runs at a command boundary, the trust check, the environment allowlist, redaction, timeouts and process cleanup are enforcement boundaries and must not be editable by a model or a user prompt. What a team wants to run (the hooks file, the executables, the prompt files) is user-owned and stays in files they edit without a toolchain.

**Chosen approach: Option C — `agent-core` + `pi-extension` (balanced, matches source architecture doc)**

Two new npm workspace packages:

- `packages/agent-core` — shared, provider-neutral event/tool/protocol/behavior-compiler code. No Pi/OMP-specific types.
- `packages/pi-extension` — thin Pi-specific adapter over `agent-core`, loaded into a live Pi session via Pi's native extension mechanism.

### Where the behavior-package compiler lives

The source architecture doc's package shape (§4) does not name a distinct package for the behavior schema/compiler (§7-§8: `compile`, `validate`, `match`, `simulate`, `conformance_run`). Because those APIs are explicitly provider-neutral, this TRD places them inside `packages/agent-core/src/behavior/` (`schema.ts`, `discovery.ts`, `compiler.ts`, `conformance.ts`), consistent with the doc's statement that "shared event/tool/protocol code belongs in `agent-core`." --- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-008**: Return a normalized `InvocationResult` {#req-008}
Return a normalized `InvocationResult` {#req-008} Priority: Must | Complexity: Medium After a bounded invocation, the extension must return a provider-neutral `InvocationResult` (status, output, usage, toolCalls, failure) matching the documented contract shape.

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen approach: Option C — `agent-core` + `pi-extension` (balanced, matches source architecture doc)**

Two new npm workspace packages:

- `packages/agent-core` — shared, provider-neutral event/tool/protocol/behavior-compiler code. No Pi/OMP-specific types.
- `packages/pi-extension` — thin Pi-specific adapter over `agent-core`, loaded into a live Pi session via Pi's native extension mechanism.

`packages/omp-adapter` and `packages/session-launcher` are explicitly deferred (per the source PRD's Non-Goals): they are built only after the OMP extension API is confirmed compatible and only when Foreman needs to own a session, respectively. Building them now would contradict the PRD's approved Won't items (Phase E3 hooks, Phase E4 Foreman protocol, Phase E5 pilot package are out of scope this release).

### Alternatives Considered

- **Option A (single `pi-extension` package, inline types):** rejected — collapses the provider-neutral/Pi-specific boundary the source architecture doc requires (§4, §6), making a future OMP adapter a rewrite rather than an addition.
- **Option B (build all four packages now, including `omp-adapter`/`session-launcher`):** rejected — directly contradicts the PRD's Non-Goals and the architecture doc's explicit sequencing ("Do not build the Elixir activation runner first... before testing the extension API"; "packages/omp-adapter # only if OMP compatibility is proven").

### Where the behavior-package compiler lives

The source architecture doc's package shape (§4) does not name a distinct package for the behavior schema/compiler (§7-§8: `compile`, `validate`, `match`, `simulate`, `conformance_run`). Because those APIs are explicitly provider-neutral, this TRD places them inside `packages/agent-core/src/behavior/` (`schema.ts`, `discovery.ts`, `compiler.ts`, `conformance.ts`), consistent with the doc's statement that "shared event/tool/protocol code belongs in `agent-core`." This is a TRD-level architecture decision, not a change to the source PRD's package names.

Register and invoke one governed custom tool {#req-005} Priority: Must | Complexity: Medium The extension must register at least one governed custom tool via Pi's native tool registration API and make it callable from an agent turn.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-005-1: Given the extension is active | When the agent calls the registered tool | Then the tool executes and returns a typed result
- AC-005-2: Given a tool call with an unauthorized tool grant | When invoked | Then the runtime boundary denies it with an "unauthorized" result — prompt text cannot bypass this

--- TRD Context ---

- `packages/pi-extension` — thin Pi-specific adapter over `agent-core`, loaded into a live Pi session via Pi's native extension mechanism.

`packages/omp-adapter` and `packages/session-launcher` are explicitly deferred (per the source PRD's Non-Goals): they are built only after the OMP extension API is confirmed compatible and only when Foreman needs to own a session, respectively. title: [trd:trd-2026-1d3e0dd6-new-feature-foreman-flag:task:TRD-009] - [ ] **TRD-009** Hard-stop invariants stated in the constraints (`packages/development/commands/new-feature.yaml`) (1h)
description:
## Task: TRD-009
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-1d3e0dd6-new-feature-foreman-flag.md#trd-009
PRD Reference: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-1d3e0dd6-new-feature-foreman-flag.md#req-009

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-009**: Hard stops and exclusivity are unchanged (Must)
Hard stops and exclusivity are unchanged (Must)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-009-1: Given `--foreman` | When a run is already active | Then `RUN_ALREADY_ACTIVE` is still reported and no run is created
- AC-009-2: Given `--foreman` | When `--status` runs | Then it is still read-only and makes no `mutate()` call
- AC-009-3: Given `--foreman` | When a stage fails | Then it is parked at that stage and never auto-retried in the same invocation

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen approach:** a prompt-only change to two YAML command sources. No TypeScript changes.

- `packages/development/commands/new-feature.yaml` gains a boolean `foreman` parameter and one derived variable, `FOREMAN`, defined once in Entry Point Resolution Step 1 and referenced by every later step. Each step that asks the user gets a `FOREMAN == true` branch that takes a deterministic, recorded, non-interactive decision. Each step that dispatches a stage skill appends `--foreman` when `FOREMAN == true`.
- `packages/development/commands/feature.yaml` (the `/ensemble:feature` front door) recognizes `--foreman` as the first token after the keyword and forwards it.
- Generated OMP, Pi and Codex artifacts are regenerated from the repo root, never hand-edited.

**Why prompt-only (Constitution Rule 8):** how a workflow behaves when no one can answer is something a maintainer would plausibly tune (for example, switching the PR gate to park instead of auto-grant). That belongs in the command prose, not in TypeScript. `RunIndexStore` already supports everything needed: `StageOutcome.detail` carries the "granted by `--foreman` policy" record.

**Additive-only edits (found in refinement):** the existing suites (`new-feature-command.test.js`, `feature-command.test.js`, `feature-input-validation-boundary.test.js`, `feature-concurrency-passthrough.test.js`) pin exact sentences in both YAML files, for example "any remaining text is an unsupported flag or argument rejected here". So no pre-existing sentence may be reworded or removed. Foreman behavior is added as new actions or appended sentences, and the existing suites must pass unchanged. For the front door that means: a new action, placed before the validation action, removes a leading `--foreman` token and sets `FOREMAN`, so the pinned validation sentences still read "remaining text" correctly; and a new action, placed after the invocation is constructed, inserts `--foreman` right after `/ensemble:new-feature` in whatever invocation was built.

**Alternatives rejected:**
- *Env-var-only detection (no flag).* Rejected: the maintainer asked for a `--foreman` flag, and the five stage skills already key on that flag.
- *A new RunRecord field `autoGranted`.* Rejected: TypeScript and schema change for information `StageOutcome.detail` already carries.
- *Parking at the approval gates.* Rejected by the maintainer: it stalls every no-user run.
Satisfies: REQ-009
PRD ACs: AC-009-1, AC-009-2, AC-009-3
Target File: 
Actions:

Implementation AC:
- [ ] Given the constraints block, when read, then it states that `--foreman` never bypasses `RUN_ALREADY_ACTIVE`, the read-only `--status`, or the no-retry-in-invocation rule
- [ ] Given `--foreman` with `--status`, when it runs, then it is read-only and makes no `mutate()` call
Dependencies: TRD-007

title: [trd:trd-2026-15aa5acd-live-behavior-dispatch-autofix:task:TRD-019-TEST] - [ ] **TRD-019-TEST** Path-classification tests including near-miss ordinary paths (4h)
description:
## Test Task: TRD-019-TEST
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-15aa5acd-live-behavior-dispatch-autofix.md#trd-019-test
PRD Reference: #req-015

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen: Option C — single enforcement seam, additive.**

A new `MutationGuard` chokepoint in `agent-core` is the one place `policy.mode`, `capabilities.mutation_classes` (via the existing `hasMutationAuthority()`), and protected-path rules are resolved. It is wired once at the loader boundary rather than replicated per tool registration. The translator, matcher, and auto-fix loop are added to `pi-extension`. Discovery roots and `execution.test_command` are additive changes to existing schema/discovery code. `ToolRegistry`, `outbox`, and the compiler are reused unchanged.

### Alternatives considered

| Option | Summary | Why not chosen |
|---|---|---|
| **A — In-place extension** | Enforce mode/mutation/path rules as wrapper checks inside `behavior-loader`'s per-tool `execute()` closures. | Enforcement scattered across call sites; every future tool registration must remember to wrap. The PRD's central failure mode is *guarantees that exist in one place but are not reached from another* — Option A reproduces exactly that shape. |
| **B — Governance kernel** | Route every mutation through a `MutationBroker` + `GovernedWorkspace` in `agent-core`; `pi-extension` becomes a thin adapter. | Strongest long-term design and the right eventual target, but it re-opens already-shipped code across every tool path for a ~6-7 PR refactor before a single PRD requirement is demonstrable. Deferred deliberately, not rejected. |
| **C — Single enforcement seam** *(chosen)* | One `MutationGuard` chokepoint, wired once; everything else additive. | Gets a single auditable chokepoint (Option B's main benefit) without Option B's refactor surface. Fits the existing `agent-core` / `pi-extension` split. |

### Architectural note carried from grounding

Two defects found while grounding this design are folded into PR 1 rather than left implicit:

1. `pi-events.ts` emits `runtime.tool_result` / `runtime.tool.called` / `runtime.tool.failed` / `runtime.tool.completed`, none of which appear in `HARNESS_EVENT_TYPES` (which defines `runtime.tool_call.started` / `runtime.tool_call.completed`). `normalizeEvent` does not currently reject uncatalogued types, so PRD AC-002-1's "validated against the closed catalog" would be vacuous. Addressed by TRD-001 (`[satisfies INFRA]`).
2. `behavior-loader.ts:79` calls `registry.grant(...)` unconditionally immediately before `registry.invoke(...)`, making the grant boundary a rubber stamp for behavior-governed tools (unlike the echo path, where the grant is CLI-flag-gated). Addressed by TRD-003.
