## Test Task: TRD-030-TEST
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-70e784f2-code-review-process.md#trd-030-test
PRD Reference: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-70e784f2-code-review-process.md#req-019

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-019**: Review metrics with a revert and incident guardrail (Must)
Review metrics with a revert and incident guardrail (Must) The process reports the measures behind the success criteria, so improvement is shown rather than assumed.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-019-1: Given a cohort of merged PRs | When metrics are produced | Then they include human approvals per PR (median and p95), human comments, wait-on-human time, rounds-to-pass, and the share of PRs needing five or more rounds
- AC-019-2: Given findings were presented | When metrics are produced | Then each is classified by how the author responded (fixed, said wrong, said intentional, judged unimportant) and a noise rate is reported

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen approach (Option C):** extend the pattern TRD-2026-82b6a138 established: **editable behavior in skills, agents and markdown; a small set of pure, deterministic libraries for what must not be self-certified by a model.**

- **User-owned (Constitution Rule 8), prose or data a maintainer edits without a toolchain:** per-area rules (`REVIEW.md` files), the policy block inside the root `REVIEW.md` (round cap, depth table, bot and maintainer logins, sensitive and High paths, Low-waiver state), severity definitions, reviewer, verifier, classifier and security-lane prompts, the PR template, the sweep and explainer procedures. All of it is read from the **target branch**, never from the PR head (REQ-024).
- **Enforcement (Rules 5 and 7), code that grades a model's claim:** vote tally, tier assignment with its sensitive-path floor and Low-waiver evidence, approval evaluation bound to a commit, the merge gate, round-cap derivation, repeat suppression, delta-range selection, depth bounds, slice coverage, metrics and eval scoring. Each is a pure CommonJS module in `packages/development/lib/`, exposed as a JSON-in/JSON-out subcommand of the existing `pr-review-cli.js`, following the 82b6a138 precedent. None performs network I/O or holds a timer.
- **Entry points (Rule 6):** every capability is reached through the one `pr-review-cycle` skill, which `fix-issue`, `implement-trd-beads` and `pr-merge` already invoke or will invoke (a new `MODE=gate` for `pr-merge`). YAML callers reference the skill only, never the CLI, as the existing parity tests require.
- **Recurrence (Rule 4):** nightly or weekly sweeps and daily eval runs are on-demand skills; a workflow template for the host repository is opt-in and scaffolded by init-project. Ensemble's own workflows gain no `schedule` trigger.

**Alternatives considered (user chose C):**

- **Option A -- prose-only skills and agents:** fewest files and fastest to ship. Rejected: the vote threshold, the tier floor, commit-bound approvals and the round cap would be prose a model can misread or skip, so none of these gates could be shown to fail (Rule 7), and "a bot approval never counts" would be a request, not a guarantee.
- **Option B -- a new TypeScript review engine in `agent-core`:** strongest typing and one runtime. Rejected: a new build and `dist` surface and cross-package coupling for a prompt-level feature, editable criteria pulled into code (against Rule 8), and drift toward an ensemble-owned dispatcher that competes with Foreman (Rule 4).

**Rationale:** Option C is the best fit for this brownfield repo. It adds only the code that grades claims, keeps everything a maintainer or adopting team would tune in files they can edit, adds no dependency (Constitution §4) and no CI secret, vendors into Pi automatically through the existing require-closure bundler, and each gate can be mutation-proven using the harness that already exists.

**Decisions taken where the PRD left a choice** (each is editable policy, not a hidden constant):

| Decision | Value | Where it lives |
|---|---|---|
| Policy format | Fenced `ensemble-review-policy` JSON block in the root `REVIEW.md` (no new parser dependency) | REVIEW.md, read from the base commit |
| "Cannot vouch for" a push (AC-010-3, AC-014-2) | Commit is unvouched when its tree differs from the reviewed tree and it is not a remediation commit recorded in the review-state report, or it is a merge commit | `pr-review-scope.js`, `pr-review-approvals.js` |
| Slice threshold for large PRs (AC-018-1) | 1500 changed lines, configurable | policy block |
| Area rules vs policy keys | Policy keys are read from the **root** file only; area files carry guidance, and the more restrictive instruction wins when areas conflict (AC-001-2) | skill prose |
| First PR that introduces REVIEW.md | No base copy exists, so strict defaults apply (Low treated as Medium, cap 3, default sensitive set) | `pr-review-policy.js` |
| Verifier majority | Strict majority of the expected verifier count (2 of 3, 3 of 5) | `pr-review-votes.js` |

Full title: - [ ] **TRD-001** Define the 14-category taxonomy (host, workflow, worktree, tracker, work-graph, ci-local, review, lint, test-runner, e2e-quality, container-deploy, iac, platform-cloud, package-runner) and the category-contract schema; create `packages/development/toolchain/schemas/category-contract-schema.json`, skeleton `packages/development/toolchain/categories/<category>.yaml` files (capabilities with inputs, outputs, required/optional, `sideEffect`, fallback id) and `packages/development/lib/toolchain/contracts.js` (`loadContracts()`, `validateContract()`) (6h)

## Task: TRD-001
## References
TRD: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-8d825f54-tool-abstraction-layer.md
TRD Task: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-8d825f54-tool-abstraction-layer.md#trd-001
PRD: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-8d825f54-tool-abstraction-layer.md
PRD Requirement: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-8d825f54-tool-abstraction-layer.md#req-001
PRD Requirement: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-8d825f54-tool-abstraction-layer.md#req-002
PRD ACs: AC-002-1
Parent Epic: [trd:trd-2026-8d825f54-tool-abstraction-layer]
Read-first: read the TRD, TRD Task section, PRD and PRD Requirement above before any work on this bead.


--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-001**: Capability taxonomy covering all tool categories
Capability taxonomy covering all tool categories Priority: Must Ensemble defines a taxonomy of tool categories covering every external tool its sources invoke: source-control host and change requests, branching workflow, worktree manager, work tracking, work graph and ready-work queue, local CI, review automation, lint automation, test runner, end-to-end and quality checks, container and deployment, infrastructure as code, platform and cloud, and package/build runner. The CI category covers only tools an agent invokes to run CI locally; hosted CI definitions are repository infrastructure and out of scope.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-002-1: Given a category | When its contract is read | Then every capability states inputs, outputs and required/optional status

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-002**: Capability contract per category
Capability contract per category Priority: Must Each category has a contract listing its named capabilities (for example "create change request", "list ready work"). For each capability the contract states required inputs, normalized outputs, and whether it is required or optional.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-002-1: Given a category | When its contract is read | Then every capability states inputs, outputs and required/optional status

--- TRD Context ---
### Alternatives Considered

| Option | Approach | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|---|
| A: Prose-only adapters | Adapter is a skill; the agent follows its prose and normalizes tool output itself | Smallest build; fully editable | Cannot route internal CLIs deterministically (REQ-016), cannot validate output (REQ-022), cannot deny at runtime (REQ-023); behavior varies per model |
| **B: Manifest plus runner (chosen)** | Adapter is a skill directory: `SKILL.md` (vocabulary and agent-facing prose) plus a declarative `adapter.yaml` (capability command templates, output mapping, allowlist, health check, detection signals, required env names). A core resolver library and `toolchain-cli` execute capabilities deterministically | Meets PRD (adapter is a skill), Rule 8 (editable without rebuild), Rule 5 (enforcement in code), REQ-016 (CLIs call the same library) | New resolver, runner, manifest schema and output-mapping engine to build and test |
| C: Executable plugin adapters | Separately packaged executables speaking a versioned JSON protocol | Arbitrary logic; strongest isolation | Contradicts the PRD's skills-as-contract decision; fails Rule 8; needs per-OS packaging and a protocol |

**Rationale:** B is the only option that makes every PRD guarantee a code-enforced property while keeping adapters user-editable data. The requester selected B at the architecture gate.

### Interpretations and Resolved Design Issues

- **I1: plain version control.** The PRD taxonomy has no plain `git` category, yet about 45 sources invoke it. Plain `git` operations (status, commit, push, log, diff, merge-base) are `vcs.*` capabilities of the `workflow` category, whose default adapter is `plain-git`; the `git-town` adapter extends it. Recommend a PRD refine pass to name this explicitly.
- **I2: ambiguity versus no signal (PRD REQ-009 AC-2 vs REQ-010 AC-2).** "No detectable signal" means no signal source exists at all (no remote, no marker files); the shipped default is used. "Ambiguous" means two or more installed adapters match, or a signal source exists (for example a remote URL) but matches no installed adapter; resolution fails explicitly in non-interactive runs and asks in interactive runs.
- **I3: AC-023-2 (governed boundary denies).** The runner is invoked through the shell tool, so a command that was not granted the shell tool cannot run any adapter; an adapter therefore cannot widen grants. The runner additionally denies any command outside the adapter's binary-plus-subcommand allowlist. Denial of raw shell commands typed by an agent outside the runner remains host-enforced (hooks on Claude Code; none in this repo for Pi, OpenCode or Codex); the lint (REQ-019) keeps commands from issuing raw tool calls. This residual is recorded in the Threat Model.
- **I4: confirmation session identity.** No stable session id is exposed uniformly across runtimes. TRD-017 begins with a spike that records which id each runtime exposes (`ENSEMBLE_SESSION_ID`, host session variables); the passive confirmation record is keyed by `(sessionKey, category, adapter, configHash)` and falls back to the run id when no session id exists.
- **I5: repo-local adapters are untrusted by default.** A cloned repository can ship `.ensemble/adapters/`. Repo-local adapters resolve in every mode (satisfying AC-007-3) but a non-interactive run additionally requires the adapter name in the user's `trustedRepoAdapters` list; an interactive run shows the adapter's allowlist at first-use confirmation.
- **I6: no new runtime dependency.** The output-mapping engine uses a small dotted-path projection (`$.a.b[0]`, `|` alternation for "array or object"), not a JSONPath library, because constitution section 4 requires approval for new dependencies.
- **I7: work-graph selection.** `work-graph` is its own category with default `auto`: use the work-graph capabilities of the resolved tracker adapter when its manifest provides them; otherwise use the built-in `work-graph-links-fallback` adapter (tracker dependency links, then plan order stated as not dependency-aware). One manifest may implement several categories.
- **I8: PRD BDD floor.** Fourteen PRD requirements (REQ-001, 002, 004, 005, 006, 009, 010, 012, 015, 018, 021, 022, 024, 025) have two ACs, below the command's three-scenario floor. The test tasks specify exactly one scenario per AC; recommend a PRD refine pass to add edge or error ACs.
- **I10: packaging.** `packages/development` depends only on `js-yaml` and its libraries require only siblings, so the resolver library, category contracts, default selection, schemas and tool inventory all ship inside `packages/development` (`lib/toolchain/` and `toolchain/`). A standalone plugin install and the Pi vendor bundle therefore contain everything; other packages call `toolchain-cli` through `TOOLCHAIN_CLI` rather than importing it.
- **I9: preflight is enforced in code.** `toolchain-cli run` refuses a side-effecting capability unless a passing preflight record exists for the supplied `--run-id`; the command prose cannot silently skip preflight.
Satisfies: REQ-001, REQ-002
Target File: 
Actions:

Implementation AC:
- [ ] Given the repo after this task, when `ls packages/development/toolchain/categories/*.yaml` runs, then exactly 14 files exist named for the 14 categories listed above.
- [ ] Given any `packages/development/toolchain/categories/<category>.yaml`, when `validateContract()` in `packages/development/lib/toolchain/contracts.js` runs, then every capability has non-empty `inputs`, `outputs` and a boolean `required` field, or the validator returns an error naming the file and capability.
- [ ] Given a contract fixture with a capability missing `outputs`, when `validateContract()` runs, then it returns an error naming that capability (unit test in `scripts/tests/toolchain-contracts.test.js`).

title: Verification command can report success over a suite that never ran (router/pytest)
description:
Residual from br-srbd.

execution.test_command is now 'env -u CI npm test'. Unsetting CI is what
makes the command pass, but it also changes what packages/router does when
pytest is missing:

  pytest present  -> run the suite
  pytest absent + CI set    -> ERROR, exit 1
       ("CI must not report success on a suite it never ran")
  pytest absent + CI unset  -> print "Skipping Python tests", exit 0

So on a machine without pytest, the loop's verification runs 161 suites,
skips the router suite entirely, and reports exit 0. Measured: 3292 tests
pass, 107 router tests never execute.

Defensible: the loop should not fail because an optional toolchain is
missing on a developer's machine, and the router package's own guard is
explicitly designed to distinguish CI from local. Unsetting CI is the correct
way to get local semantics.

The problem is that the loop cannot tell the two apart. A verification that
returns "passed" while a suite was skipped is the exact shape of gap the rule
provider proposed an amendment about, unprompted, when shown a similar
failure:

  "Any test suite that fails to load, compile, or be discovered must make the
   test command exit non-zero, and a passing run must execute every test file
   in the repo; a green result where any suite did not load or was left out
   counts as a failure."

Worth noting that the system diagnosed this class of bug correctly before we
hit an instance of it.

OPTIONS
(a) Treat a skip notice in output as INCONCLUSIVE rather than passed, the
    same way an unloadable suite is already handled (verify-suite.ts:138).
    Consistent with the existing design, and cheap.
(b) Install pytest in the dev environment so the suite runs. Fixes this
    instance, not the class.
(c) Accept it and document that the loop's verification covers the JS/TS
    workspaces only.

(a) is the one that matches how unloadable suites are already graded.
close_reason: Fixed: verifyOutput now returns inconclusive when a run ANNOUNCES it skipped part of the suite, checked before the framework adapters and independently of the exit code. findAnnouncedSkips matches whole-line 'Skipping X tests' / 'Skipped X tests' / 'No X tests to run', which is exactly what packages/router prints when pytest is absent and CI is unset. Requires an explicit announcement rather than inferring from counts: a per-test '3 skipped' is routine and must not trip it, and a test NAMED 'handles skipping empty input' must not either -- both covered. 10 tests in agent-core/tests/announced-skip.test.ts.

comments.author: ldangelo
comments.text: Related to br-cwrh (behavior: flag a test run that passed without running tests). The verifyOutput defect this bead describes was fixed for the Elixir/jest unloadable-suite case during br-behavior-runtime-cqrs-xl24 (br-gwww), but the router/pytest path here is NOT covered, and more importantly verifyOutput has only one caller -- fix.verify -- so it never sees an ordinary test run. Re-check scope against verification.ts before implementing.

title: [trd:trd-2026-f08a2a09-command-lifecycle-hooks:task:TRD-004-TEST] - [ ] **TRD-004-TEST** Shell runner behavior (4h)
description:
## Test Task: TRD-004-TEST
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-f08a2a09-command-lifecycle-hooks.md#trd-004-test
PRD Reference: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-f08a2a09-command-lifecycle-hooks.md#req-009

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-009**: Shell handlers run an executable with the event as input (Must) [RISK: arbitrary code execution at a command boundary]
Shell handlers run an executable with the event as input (Must) [RISK: arbitrary code execution at a command boundary]

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-009-1: Given a shell handler is configured | When its event fires | Then the configured executable runs with the event delivered as structured input
- AC-009-2: Given the command's arguments contain shell metacharacters | When the handler runs | Then they are never interpreted by a shell
- AC-009-3: Given a shell handler runs | When it starts | Then it sees only a documented allowlist of environment variables and not the full environment
- AC-009-4: Given a handler produces more output than the stated bound | When it runs | Then the output is truncated at the bound and the user is told it was truncated
- AC-009-5: Given a handler exceeds its timeout (5 seconds when a shell handler states none) | When a shell handler states none) | Then the handler and every process it started are terminated and its error behavior applies
- AC-009-6: Given a handler exits with status zero | When it finishes | Then it is a success

--- TRD Context ---
**Decision:** Build the lifecycle as a harness-neutral core in `packages/agent-core` (event payloads, configuration validation, redaction, a shell runner, a prompt runner, a serial dispatcher, and a per-session command-run tracker) and one adapter in `packages/pi-extension` that connects it to Pi. The adapter is the only code that knows Pi's event names.

**Decisions made by the maintainer during design (all recorded in PRD v1.0.2 to v1.0.4):**

- The first release is adapter-specific, with Pi as the proving harness. A runtime-owned wrapper is deferred.
- `command.start` fires from the runtime when the command's slash input is seen, so it never depends on the model and a start handler's block is enforced by the runtime. A command whose own prompt then rejects its arguments has already produced a start and ends as `failed`.
- A command's completion is signalled by a silent `ensemble_command_complete` tool that the model is told to call last. The instruction is injected per turn by the adapter, not generated into every Pi prompt, so projects without hooks see no change.
- A settled loop never ends a command. A command that never signals completion ends as `cancelled` when the session ends or the next command begins.
- A prompt handler is evaluated by an isolated headless child (`pi -p --no-session -ne -nt -np`), parsed against a typed response contract.
- No handler runs until the host reports the project as trusted (`ctx.isProjectTrusted()`).
- `on_error` is required on every handler. Default timeouts are 5 seconds for shell handlers and 30 seconds for prompt handlers.
- Selections list commands by name. Wildcards and groups are rejected.
- For harnesses with no adapter, the guide, a capability table and a status check say hooks are inactive. Nothing is shown at command time there.

**Why code and not a prompt (Constitution rule 8):** what runs at a command boundary, the trust check, the environment allowlist, redaction, timeouts and process cleanup are enforcement boundaries and must not be editable by a model or a user prompt. What a team wants to run (the hooks file, the executables, the prompt files) is user-owned and stays in files they edit without a toolchain.

title: [trd:trd-2026-1d3e0dd6-new-feature-foreman-flag:task:TRD-004] - [ ] **TRD-004** Auto-grant implementation approval and record it (`packages/development/commands/new-feature.yaml`) (2h)
description:
## Task: TRD-004
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-1d3e0dd6-new-feature-foreman-flag.md#trd-004
PRD Reference: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-1d3e0dd6-new-feature-foreman-flag.md#req-004

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-004**: Approval checkpoints auto-grant and are recorded (Must) [RISK: weakens a human checkpoint, so the record must be unambiguous]
Approval checkpoints auto-grant and are recorded (Must) [RISK: weakens a human checkpoint, so the record must be unambiguous]

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-004-1: Given `--foreman` and `ELIGIBLE_STAGE == implementation_approval` | When the checkpoint runs | Then no question is asked and one `RunIndexStore
- AC-004-2: Given the grant happened | When `--status` later reports the run | Then it shows that detail, so an auto-grant can never be mistaken for a human approval
- AC-004-3: Given `--foreman` is absent | When the checkpoint runs | Then it asks for explicit approval and, on absent or declined approval, makes no `mutate()` call, exactly as today
- AC-004-4: Given the material-plan-change staleness check finds the approved plan changed | When `--foreman` is set | Then approval is cleared and re-granted through the same recorded path, never silently kept

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen approach:** a prompt-only change to two YAML command sources. No TypeScript changes.

- `packages/development/commands/new-feature.yaml` gains a boolean `foreman` parameter and one derived variable, `FOREMAN`, defined once in Entry Point Resolution Step 1 and referenced by every later step. Each step that asks the user gets a `FOREMAN == true` branch that takes a deterministic, recorded, non-interactive decision. Each step that dispatches a stage skill appends `--foreman` when `FOREMAN == true`.
- `packages/development/commands/feature.yaml` (the `/ensemble:feature` front door) recognizes `--foreman` as the first token after the keyword and forwards it.
- Generated OMP, Pi and Codex artifacts are regenerated from the repo root, never hand-edited.

**Why prompt-only (Constitution Rule 8):** how a workflow behaves when no one can answer is something a maintainer would plausibly tune (for example, switching the PR gate to park instead of auto-grant). That belongs in the command prose, not in TypeScript. `RunIndexStore` already supports everything needed: `StageOutcome.detail` carries the "granted by `--foreman` policy" record.

**Additive-only edits (found in refinement):** the existing suites (`new-feature-command.test.js`, `feature-command.test.js`, `feature-input-validation-boundary.test.js`, `feature-concurrency-passthrough.test.js`) pin exact sentences in both YAML files, for example "any remaining text is an unsupported flag or argument rejected here". So no pre-existing sentence may be reworded or removed. Foreman behavior is added as new actions or appended sentences, and the existing suites must pass unchanged. For the front door that means: a new action, placed before the validation action, removes a leading `--foreman` token and sets `FOREMAN`, so the pinned validation sentences still read "remaining text" correctly; and a new action, placed after the invocation is constructed, inserts `--foreman` right after `/ensemble:new-feature` in whatever invocation was built.

**Alternatives rejected:**
- *Env-var-only detection (no flag).* Rejected: the maintainer asked for a `--foreman` flag, and the five stage skills already key on that flag.
- *A new RunRecord field `autoGranted`.* Rejected: TypeScript and schema change for information `StageOutcome.detail` already carries.
- *Parking at the approval gates.* Rejected by the maintainer: it stalls every no-user run.
Satisfies: REQ-004
PRD ACs: AC-004-1, AC-004-2, AC-004-3, AC-004-4
Target File: 
Actions:

Implementation AC:
- [ ] Given `FOREMAN == true` at `implementation_approval`, when the checkpoint runs, then no question is asked and one `mutate()` sets `implementationApprovedAt` and `stage = "implementation"` with `stageOutcome` `{ kind: "approval_wait", detail: "implementation approval granted by --foreman policy (no human present)" }`
- [ ] Given the staleness check clears approval under `FOREMAN == true`, when the checkpoint re-runs, then approval is re-granted through the same recorded path
- [ ] Given `FOREMAN` is not true, when the checkpoint runs, then it asks for explicit approval and makes no `mutate()` call on absent or declined approval
- [ ] Given `--status` reports a run, when the detail is present, then it is printed so an auto-grant is never mistaken for a human approval

Read-first: read the TRD, TRD Task section, PRD and PRD Requirement above before any work on this bead.


--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-015**: Commands and skills depend on capabilities, not tools
Commands and skills depend on capabilities, not tools Priority: Must | `[RISK: about 10 heavily coupled commands plus skills must be refactored without changing default behavior]` Shared commands, agents and skills reference capabilities and resolved adapters. They no longer name a specific tool outside an adapter. Acceptance is asserted through the commands' real entry points, not around them.

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-016**: Tracker swap, end to end (first alternatives: Jira Cloud and Azure Boards)
Tracker swap, end to end (first alternatives: Jira Cloud and Azure Boards) Priority: Must | `[RISK: work-graph behavior differs between trackers]` With the tracker adapter changed by configuration only, every command that creates, reads, updates or closes work items works against either alternative tracker, including the internal CLIs (`trd-cli` and siblings) that currently call the default tracker directly. Those internal CLIs route through the resolved tracker adapter. The first-release Jira adapter targets Jira Cloud only.

--- TRD Context ---
### Alternatives Considered

| Option | Approach | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|---|
| A: Prose-only adapters | Adapter is a skill; the agent follows its prose and normalizes tool output itself | Smallest build; fully editable | Cannot route internal CLIs deterministically (REQ-016), cannot validate output (REQ-022), cannot deny at runtime (REQ-023); behavior varies per model |
| **B: Manifest plus runner (chosen)** | Adapter is a skill directory: `SKILL.md` (vocabulary and agent-facing prose) plus a declarative `adapter.yaml` (capability command templates, output mapping, allowlist, health check, detection signals, required env names). A core resolver library and `toolchain-cli` execute capabilities deterministically | Meets PRD (adapter is a skill), Rule 8 (editable without rebuild), Rule 5 (enforcement in code), REQ-016 (CLIs call the same library) | New resolver, runner, manifest schema and output-mapping engine to build and test |
| C: Executable plugin adapters | Separately packaged executables speaking a versioned JSON protocol | Arbitrary logic; strongest isolation | Contradicts the PRD's skills-as-contract decision; fails Rule 8; needs per-OS packaging and a protocol |

**Rationale:** B is the only option that makes every PRD guarantee a code-enforced property while keeping adapters user-editable data. The requester selected B at the architecture gate.

### Interpretations and Resolved Design Issues

- **I1: plain version control.** The PRD taxonomy has no plain `git` category, yet about 45 sources invoke it. Plain `git` operations (status, commit, push, log, diff, merge-base) are `vcs.*` capabilities of the `workflow` category, whose default adapter is `plain-git`; the `git-town` adapter extends it. Recommend a PRD refine pass to name this explicitly.
- **I2: ambiguity versus no signal (PRD REQ-009 AC-2 vs REQ-010 AC-2).** "No detectable signal" means no signal source exists at all (no remote, no marker files); the shipped default is used. "Ambiguous" means two or more installed adapters match, or a signal source exists (for example a remote URL) but matches no installed adapter; resolution fails explicitly in non-interactive runs and asks in interactive runs.
- **I3: AC-023-2 (governed boundary denies).** The runner is invoked through the shell tool, so a command that was not granted the shell tool cannot run any adapter; an adapter therefore cannot widen grants. The runner additionally denies any command outside the adapter's binary-plus-subcommand allowlist. Denial of raw shell commands typed by an agent outside the runner remains host-enforced (hooks on Claude Code; none in this repo for Pi, OpenCode or Codex); the lint (REQ-019) keeps commands from issuing raw tool calls. This residual is recorded in the Threat Model.
- **I4: confirmation session identity.** No stable session id is exposed uniformly across runtimes. TRD-017 begins with a spike that records which id each runtime exposes (`ENSEMBLE_SESSION_ID`, host session variables); the passive confirmation record is keyed by `(sessionKey, category, adapter, configHash)` and falls back to the run id when no session id exists.
- **I5: repo-local adapters are untrusted by default.** A cloned repository can ship `.ensemble/adapters/`. Repo-local adapters resolve in every mode (satisfying AC-007-3) but a non-interactive run additionally requires the adapter name in the user's `trustedRepoAdapters` list; an interactive run shows the adapter's allowlist at first-use confirmation.
- **I6: no new runtime dependency.** The output-mapping engine uses a small dotted-path projection (`$.a.b[0]`, `|` alternation for "array or object"), not a JSONPath library, because constitution section 4 requires approval for new dependencies.
- **I7: work-graph selection.** `work-graph` is its own category with default `auto`: use the work-graph capabilities of the resolved tracker adapter when its manifest provides them; otherwise use the built-in `work-graph-links-fallback` adapter (tracker dependency links, then plan order stated as not dependency-aware). One manifest may implement several categories.
- **I8: PRD BDD floor.** Fourteen PRD requirements (REQ-001, 002, 004, 005, 006, 009, 010, 012, 015, 018, 021, 022, 024, 025) have two ACs, below the command's three-scenario floor. The test tasks specify exactly one scenario per AC; recommend a PRD refine pass to add edge or error ACs.
- **I10: packaging.** `packages/development` depends only on `js-yaml` and its libraries require only siblings, so the resolver library, category contracts, default selection, schemas and tool inventory all ship inside `packages/development` (`lib/toolchain/` and `toolchain/`). A standalone plugin install and the Pi vendor bundle therefore contain everything; other packages call `toolchain-cli` through `TOOLCHAIN_CLI` rather than importing it.
- **I9: preflight is enforced in code.** `toolchain-cli run` refuses a side-effecting capability unless a passing preflight record exists for the supplied `--run-id`; the command prose cannot silently skip preflight.
Satisfies: REQ-015, REQ-016

title: [trd:trd-2026-d6bbf322-new-feature-workflow:task:TRD-013] - [ ] **TRD-013**: Implement event-triggered human review, PRD elicitation gate, and invalid-payload handling (5h)
description:
## Task: TRD-013
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-d6bbf322-new-feature-workflow.md#trd-013
PRD Reference: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-d6bbf322-new-feature-workflow.md#req-009

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-009**: Support manual and explicitly configured event-triggered starts
Support manual and explicitly configured event-triggered starts Priority: Must | Complexity: High | [RISK: event payloads can be incomplete, untrusted, or mistaken for user intent]

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-009-2: Given a project explicitly configures an event mapping and an allowed event occurs | When the event is delivered | Then the workflow presents the event source and payload for human review and completes required PRD elicitation before creating or advancing the PRD stage
- AC-009-3: Given the event payload is invalid | When the workflow handles it | Then it creates no PRD and does not advance the run; it reports which validation or review step is pending

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen: Option C — hardened in-session stage composition with a dedicated atomic run-index store.**

`new-feature` is authored the same way every other product command in this repo is authored: a single orchestrating skill (`packages/development/commands/new-feature.yaml`, generated to runtime-specific prompts exactly like `fix-issue.yaml`) that executes each stage's existing skill body in-session — the same mechanism that loaded `ensemble-refine-prd`'s content into this session and had the agent execute its Phases directly. This is forced, not merely preferred: Pi's `ExtensionAPI` has no completion/invoke primitive that would let an extension programmatically run another skill and get its result back (confirmed — no `pi.invokeCommand` or equivalent exists); the only code-level "run a skill" mechanism, `createAgentPort()`, spawns a bounded, disposable `omp -p --no-session --no-extensions` subprocess in an isolated worktree, and does not fit a long-lived, project-resident workflow whose PRD/TRD stages use the interactive `--collab` review server.

What is new, and is the one piece of real infrastructure this TRD adds: a `RunIndexStore` (`packages/agent-core/src/new-feature/run-index.ts`) built on the one proven concurrency-safe pattern in this repo — `session.js`'s temp-file-then-`renameSync` atomic write plus `expectedRevision`/409-style optimistic concurrency — rather than `ProposalStore`'s plain `writeFileSync` (no atomicity, no lock, not adequate for PRD AC-005-3's fail-closed-on-malformed-index requirement). Runs are stored at `.ensemble/new-feature/<run-id>.json`, mirroring `ProposalStore`'s `.ensemble/proposals/<ref>.json` convention (also excluded from `tree-baseline.ts` drift detection, so this is consistent runtime-owned state, not a project-source mutation).

### Alternatives considered

| Option | Summary | Why not chosen |
|---|---|---|
| A — Plain JSON checkpoint | Same in-session composition, but checkpoints are a single `writeFileSync`, no atomicity/locking. | Fastest to build, but a crash mid-write can corrupt the run index, which directly violates AC-005-3's "fail closed with a recoverable diagnostic" requirement — the repo's own `ProposalStore` already demonstrates this gap is real, not hypothetical. |
| B — Subprocess-dispatched stages | New orchestrator module dispatches every stage as a bounded `createAgentPort()` subprocess; advances the run index only after subprocess exit 0 + artifact-on-disk confirmation. | Most rigorous completion signal (a real process boundary instead of self-reported bookkeeping), but substantially more build effort, and does not fit the interactive `--collab` review-server stages `create-prd`/`refine-prd` already use — those are long-lived, human-attended HTTP sessions, not bounded one-shot subprocess work, and would need bespoke carve-out handling under this option. |
| **C — Hardened in-session composition** *(chosen)* | In-session stage execution (like every existing product command), backed by a dedicated atomic `RunIndexStore`. | Reuses 100% of the existing skill-composition and `ask_user`-approval infrastructure (including the `--collab` review server, which needs no special-casing), while fixing Option A's one real correctness gap with the repo's one proven atomic-write pattern. Matches user-confirmed direction. |

### Honest trust-boundary note

Because stage execution stays in-session (per Option C), the approval gates implemented by TRD-014/TRD-017/TRD-019 are enforced by the orchestrating skill's own conditional logic checking `RunIndexStore`-persisted approval fields before it issues an implementation or `gh pr create` tool call — not by a separate runtime authorization chokepoint like `agent-core`'s `MutationGuard` (which exists elsewhere in this repo, gating CQRS-registered commands, but `new-feature`'s mutating actions are ordinary skill-level tool calls, same as `fix-issue`'s own gated PR-creation step, not CQRS commands). This is the same trust boundary every existing Ensemble product command already operates under. Building a `MutationGuard`-equivalent chokepoint for skill-level tool calls is a materially larger investment this PRD does not request and no other product command has; REQ-014's "runtime authority" is satisfied here by making the check a required precondition over persisted, validated store state rather than over prompt claims — which is what AC-014-2 actually asks for — not by inventing a new enforcement subsystem.
Satisfies: REQ-009
PRD ACs: AC-009-2, AC-009-3
Target File: packages/development/commands/new-feature.yaml
Actions:
1. When a project has an explicit `event-mapping.json` and an allowed event type occurs, present the event source and full payload to the user via `ask_user` for review before any PRD-stage work begins.
2. Require the same PRD elicitation (idea clarification) that manual `create-prd` invocation already requires — an event payload is never treated as a complete PRD input by itself.
3. On an invalid, incomplete, or user-declined payload: create no PRD, advance no run, and report which validation or review step is pending.
Implementation AC:
- [ ] Given an allowed configured event, when delivered, then the event source and payload are shown for human review and PRD elicitation completes before any PRD file is written.
- [ ] Given an invalid/incomplete/declined payload, when handled, then no PRD exists afterward and the reported message names the specific pending step.
Dependencies: TRD-012

Package quarantine gets its own `package-quarantine.ts` beside `package-discovery.ts`.

1. **How artifact changes are detected: content hashes checked at lifecycle points.** No `fs.watch`, no new dependency.

   - If the artifact never appears, the behavior shows up as an inert trigger in `/ensemble-status`; it is never silently idle.
   - The baseline is the previous snapshot seen **in the same session** (Rule 4). The first observation in a session only sets the baseline.

   - A new behavior, `apply-verified-fix`, runs `mode: auto`. It triggers on `fix.verified` with the predicate `verdict: passed`, declares only `fix.apply` with no tools, and calls `fix.apply { proposalRef: ${event.payload.proposalRef} }`.

| Option | Summary | Why not chosen |
|---|---|---|

description:
## Task: TRD-018
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-70e784f2-code-review-process.md#trd-018
PRD Reference: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-70e784f2-code-review-process.md#req-005

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-005**: Verification before posting (Must) [RISK: a verifier that votes wrongly can suppress a real bug or admit noise]
Verification before posting (Must) [RISK: a verifier that votes wrongly can suppress a real bug or admit noise] Each candidate finding is checked by independent verifiers, and only findings enough of them judge real are presented to the author.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-005-1: Given candidate findings exist | When verification runs | Then each finding receives independent votes from verifiers who did not produce it, and a finding is presented to the author only if a majority of its verifiers judge it real; the number of verifiers is 0 at Quick, 3 at Standard and 5 at Deep
- AC-016-1: Given a mode is selected | When review runs | Then the number of reviewers and verifiers does not exceed that mode's bound (Quick: a single reviewer and no verifiers; Standard: at least two reviewers and 3 verifiers; Deep: at least two reviewers and 5 verifiers)
- AC-018-1: Given a PR is too large for one reviewer to cover in a pass | When review runs | Then it is split by area (using the sensitive-area and rules boundaries) and every slice is reviewed

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen approach (Option C):** extend the pattern TRD-2026-82b6a138 established: **editable behavior in skills, agents and markdown; a small set of pure, deterministic libraries for what must not be self-certified by a model.**

- **User-owned (Constitution Rule 8), prose or data a maintainer edits without a toolchain:** per-area rules (`REVIEW.md` files), the policy block inside the root `REVIEW.md` (round cap, depth table, bot and maintainer logins, sensitive and High paths, Low-waiver state), severity definitions, reviewer, verifier, classifier and security-lane prompts, the PR template, the sweep and explainer procedures. All of it is read from the **target branch**, never from the PR head (REQ-024).
- **Enforcement (Rules 5 and 7), code that grades a model's claim:** vote tally, tier assignment with its sensitive-path floor and Low-waiver evidence, approval evaluation bound to a commit, the merge gate, round-cap derivation, repeat suppression, delta-range selection, depth bounds, slice coverage, metrics and eval scoring. Each is a pure CommonJS module in `packages/development/lib/`, exposed as a JSON-in/JSON-out subcommand of the existing `pr-review-cli.js`, following the 82b6a138 precedent. None performs network I/O or holds a timer.
- **Entry points (Rule 6):** every capability is reached through the one `pr-review-cycle` skill, which `fix-issue`, `implement-trd-beads` and `pr-merge` already invoke or will invoke (a new `MODE=gate` for `pr-merge`). YAML callers reference the skill only, never the CLI, as the existing parity tests require.
- **Recurrence (Rule 4):** nightly or weekly sweeps and daily eval runs are on-demand skills; a workflow template for the host repository is opt-in and scaffolded by init-project. Ensemble's own workflows gain no `schedule` trigger.

**Alternatives considered (user chose C):**

- **Option A -- prose-only skills and agents:** fewest files and fastest to ship. Rejected: the vote threshold, the tier floor, commit-bound approvals and the round cap would be prose a model can misread or skip, so none of these gates could be shown to fail (Rule 7), and "a bot approval never counts" would be a request, not a guarantee.
- **Option B -- a new TypeScript review engine in `agent-core`:** strongest typing and one runtime. Rejected: a new build and `dist` surface and cross-package coupling for a prompt-level feature, editable criteria pulled into code (against Rule 8), and drift toward an ensemble-owned dispatcher that competes with Foreman (Rule 4).

**Rationale:** Option C is the best fit for this brownfield repo. It adds only the code that grades claims, keeps everything a maintainer or adopting team would tune in files they can edit, adds no dependency (Constitution §4) and no CI secret, vendors into Pi automatically through the existing require-closure bundler, and each gate can be mutation-proven using the harness that already exists.

**Decisions taken where the PRD left a choice** (each is editable policy, not a hidden constant):

| Decision | Value | Where it lives |
|---|---|---|
| Policy format | Fenced `ensemble-review-policy` JSON block in the root `REVIEW.md` (no new parser dependency) | REVIEW.md, read from the base commit |
| "Cannot vouch for" a push (AC-010-3, AC-014-2) | Commit is unvouched when its tree differs from the reviewed tree and it is not a remediation commit recorded in the review-state report, or it is a merge commit | `pr-review-scope.js`, `pr-review-approvals.js` |
| Slice threshold for large PRs (AC-018-1) | 1500 changed lines, configurable | policy block |
| Area rules vs policy keys | Policy keys are read from the **root** file only; area files carry guidance, and the more restrictive instruction wins when areas conflict (AC-001-2) | skill prose |
| First PR that introduces REVIEW.md | No base copy exists, so strict defaults apply (Low treated as Medium, cap 3, default sensitive set) | `pr-review-policy.js` |
| Verifier majority | Strict majority of the expected verifier count (2 of 3, 3 of 5) | `pr-review-votes.js` |

title: Autofix: dispatch via pi.sendUserMessage() continuation turn, not handler-awaited work
description:
## Problem

Autofix cannot complete inside a Pi/omp session, because dispatch is driven
from extension event handlers and the host bounds them:

- tool_call / tool_result handlers: killed at 30_000ms
  ("Extension error: handler timed out after 30000ms")
- session_shutdown handlers: killed at 2_000ms
  ("handler timed out after 2000ms")

A real fix provider spawns an agent subprocess and takes tens of seconds at
best. Awaiting it inside the handler aborted the chain mid-flight every time:
`test.failure.observed` was logged, no dispatch/invocation record followed,
and the source was unchanged.

Dispatch is now out-of-band (tracked promise set + drainDispatches join
point), which stops the handler from being killed. But in a one-shot
`omp -p`, the process exits as soon as the turn ends and the background work
dies with it. Joining at shutdown cannot rescue it -- 2s is far short of a
model call.

## Evidence

Verified outside the handler lifecycle, the loop works end to end against a
real failing suite (packages/agent-core/src/live-math.ts, `a - b`):

    CANDIDATE writes: [ 'packages/agent-core/src/live-math.ts' ]
    OUTCOME: {"status":"accepted","attempt":1,...}
    AFTER: return a + b;

and correctly rejects a fix that does not work:

    OUTCOME: {"status":"rejected","reason":"target test still fails",
              "restored":["packages/agent-core/src/live-math.ts"]}

So the provider, mutation guard, snapshot, apply, suite re-run and rollback
are all sound. The ONLY missing piece is a execution context whose lifetime is
independent of the session.

## Why a command is not the answer

An `/ensemble-fix-now` command was considered. A command handler is still a
handler; even if its budget is larger, the design would rest on "hope the cap
is generous enough" -- the same bet that already failed at two different
limits (30s, then 2s).

## Proposed direction

Dispatch spawns a DETACHED worker process that outlives the session:

- parent returns immediately; no handler ever awaits it
- worker writes progress/outcome to .ensemble/ (runtime-log.jsonl plus a
  per-invocation record)
- the session reports results via /ensemble-status and on next session start
- needs: concurrency control (one worker per issue key), crash/orphan
  handling, and a way to surface a completed fix for review

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A failing test in a real `omp -p` run produces an applied, verified fix
      with no handler timeout anywhere in the log.
- [ ] The parent session exiting does not kill an in-flight fix.
- [ ] A fix that does not make the suite pass is still rolled back.
- [ ] Two failures of the same issue key do not spawn duplicate workers.
- [ ] Verified live, not only in unit tests.
close_reason: Detected, dispatched and fixed a real failing test in this repo; verified live

comments.text:
REPRODUCED 2026-09-25, isolated from all ensemble code
(/tmp/hang/slow.ts via: omp -p --no-session --no-extensions -e ./slow.ts).
tool_call handler sleeps 45s; session_shutdown handler sleeps 10s:

  [slow] tool_call START read
  Extension error (/tmp/hang/slow.ts): handler timed out after 30000ms
  [slow] tool_call START bash
  [slow] tool_call FINISHED after 45002ms
  Extension error (/tmp/hang/slow.ts): handler timed out after 30000ms
  [slow] shutdown START
  Extension error (/tmp/hang/slow.ts): handler timed out after 2000ms

Caps CONFIRMED: 30000ms tool_call, 2000ms session_shutdown. Enforced by the
OMP host, NOT by @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent: 'handler timed out',
'handlerTimeout' and 'HANDLER_TIMEOUT' appear ZERO times in that package's
source, dist and minified chunks. Prior searches looked in the wrong place;
absence there was not absence.

TWO FACTS NOT VISIBLE FROM THE ERROR STRING:

1. The handler is NOT cancelled. 'FINISHED after 45002ms' printed AFTER the
   timeout was reported: the host stops awaiting and moves on while the work
   continues orphaned. Awaited fix work could still mutate files after the
   host has given up on it.

2. The timeout BLOCKS THE TOOL (documented tool_call fail-safe). In the repro
   the agent's read AND bash both failed, and it told the user to open another
   terminal. A slow handler does not merely delay a session, it breaks the
   agent's ability to work. This is a stronger justification for out-of-band
   dispatch (41ebbd3) than the reasoning it was committed with.

REVISED DESIGN -- the detached worker is the wrong shape and is WITHDRAWN.

Per pi.dev/docs/latest/extensions: 'turn_end and agent_before_settle are
actionable boundaries. Their handlers can chain proposed entries and return
continue: true for one next model request.' Confirmed in the installed host:
AgentBeforeSettleEvent (types.d.ts:620), registered types.d.ts:1000, result
BoundaryResult { entries?: SessionBoundaryDraft[]; continue?: boolean }.

The handler appends an entry and returns continue:true in milliseconds; the
SESSION'S OWN AGENT LOOP then performs the fix on its next turn:
  - no handler awaits model work, so no cap of any size applies
  - the session cannot exit early -- agent_settled has not fired
  - no second process: no lockfile, no orphan recovery, no unattended
    background process editing the repo
  - the fix lands in the user's transcript, under their tools and approvals

Risk moves to continuation control. The docs warn 'an unconditional
continuation can loop', so continuation must be guarded by issue key and
attempt count.

REVISED ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- [ ] A failing test in a real omp -p run produces an applied, verified fix
      with NO handler timeout anywhere in stderr.
- [ ] No handler exceeds ~100ms; assert this in the repro harness.
- [ ] A fix that does not make the suite pass is still rolled back.
- [ ] The same issue key cannot request a second continuation (no loop).
- [ ] Verified live, not only in unit tests.

  START 08:35:37
  [bg] scheduling background work at 2026-09-25T13:35:44.580Z
  EXIT  08:35:47            <- process exited ~3s later
  done.txt: ABSENT

The background work did NOT survive. Note node would normally stay alive for
a pending timer, so the host calls process.exit() explicitly on one-shot
completion.

TWO DISTINCT MECHANISMS, previously conflated:
  1. Handler deadline (30s/2s): host stops waiting; work CONTINUES; tool is
     blocked as a fail-safe. Survivable.
  2. Process exit (one-shot omp -p): HARD KILL of unawaited work. No amount
     of promise tracking, unref, or out-of-band scheduling survives it.

CONSEQUENCE FOR 41ebbd3: out-of-band dispatch correctly avoids mechanism 1
(and avoids blocking the user's tools, which is a stronger justification than
the commit message gave). It does NOT address mechanism 2.

WHY agent_before_settle IS THE ANSWER, not merely the lighter option:
it does not try to OUTLIVE the session, it PREVENTS the session from settling
until the fix turn completes. The work stays inside the agent loop's lifetime,
where the process is guaranteed alive. A detached worker would also survive
mechanism 2, but only by leaving the process -- reintroducing lockfiles,
orphan recovery and unattended repo edits for no additional benefit.

ADDITIONAL ACCEPTANCE CRITERION
- [ ] A repro proving the fix turn completes before process exit in one-shot
      `omp -p` (i.e. mechanism 2 is actually defeated, not just mechanism 1).

NOT FIRED: agent_before_settle, agent_settled. Registration silently succeeds

{continue:true} from turn_end #1, no second turn occurred. Its payload is
{type,turnIndex,message,toolResults} -- NOT the documented BoundaryState

continuation contract is not available here.

Real ExtensionAPI surface in OMP includes sendMessage and sendUserMessage.

The cap keyed on the literal command string. Observed live: one failure
retried as `... | tail -5` then `... | sed -n 1,60p` counted as two issues,

title: [trd:trd-2026-f08a2a09-command-lifecycle-hooks:task:TRD-014-TEST] - [ ] **TRD-014-TEST** Capability and status behavior (2h)
description:
## Test Task: TRD-014-TEST
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-f08a2a09-command-lifecycle-hooks.md#trd-014-test
PRD Reference: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-f08a2a09-command-lifecycle-hooks.md#req-014

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-014**: Each adapter declares its lifecycle capabilities (Must) [RISK: approximating command end with a session or turn event]
Each adapter declares its lifecycle capabilities (Must) [RISK: approximating command end with a session or turn event]

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-014-1: Given an adapter | When it is described | Then it states whether it supports `command_start`, `command_end` and `command_end_on_cancel`
- AC-014-2: Given an adapter cannot reliably observe a boundary | When its capabilities are declared | Then that capability is marked unsupported and is never approximated with a session or turn event
- AC-014-3: Given a hook is configured for a capability the active harness does not support | When a command runs | Then the user sees a warning naming the hook and the unsupported capability, and the command runs
- AC-014-4: Given the capability declarations | When they are read | Then they are discoverable without running a command
- AC-015-5: Given the Pi adapter defines a command's end by the completion step of REQ-021 | When it declares its capabilities | Then it states exactly that definition, and the declaration is checked against the real host
- AC-017-1: Given a hook is selected for `command_end_on_cancel` on an adapter that does not support it | When the configuration is loaded in that harness | Then the unsupported capability is reported
- AC-017-2: Given a harness with no adapter at all | When the guide's capability table or the hooks status check is read | Then it states that lifecycle hooks are not active in that harness

--- TRD Context ---
**Decision:** Build the lifecycle as a harness-neutral core in `packages/agent-core` (event payloads, configuration validation, redaction, a shell runner, a prompt runner, a serial dispatcher, and a per-session command-run tracker) and one adapter in `packages/pi-extension` that connects it to Pi. The adapter is the only code that knows Pi's event names.

**Decisions made by the maintainer during design (all recorded in PRD v1.0.2 to v1.0.4):**

- The first release is adapter-specific, with Pi as the proving harness. A runtime-owned wrapper is deferred.
- `command.start` fires from the runtime when the command's slash input is seen, so it never depends on the model and a start handler's block is enforced by the runtime. A command whose own prompt then rejects its arguments has already produced a start and ends as `failed`.
- A command's completion is signalled by a silent `ensemble_command_complete` tool that the model is told to call last. The instruction is injected per turn by the adapter, not generated into every Pi prompt, so projects without hooks see no change.
- A settled loop never ends a command. A command that never signals completion ends as `cancelled` when the session ends or the next command begins.
- A prompt handler is evaluated by an isolated headless child (`pi -p --no-session -ne -nt -np`), parsed against a typed response contract.
- No handler runs until the host reports the project as trusted (`ctx.isProjectTrusted()`).
- `on_error` is required on every handler. Default timeouts are 5 seconds for shell handlers and 30 seconds for prompt handlers.
- Selections list commands by name. Wildcards and groups are rejected.
- For harnesses with no adapter, the guide, a capability table and a status check say hooks are inactive. Nothing is shown at command time there.

**Why code and not a prompt (Constitution rule 8):** what runs at a command boundary, the trust check, the environment allowlist, redaction, timeouts and process cleanup are enforcement boundaries and must not be editable by a model or a user prompt. What a team wants to run (the hooks file, the executables, the prompt files) is user-owned and stays in files they edit without a toolchain.

title: [trd:trd-2026-b6db9749-behavior-habits-runtime:task:TRD-026] - [ ] **TRD-026** Run the conformance suite on a Windows runner, and document gaps instead of patching around them per platform (5h) [RISK: 8h+ candidate if path handling or POSIX-only shell patterns in `event-translator.ts` fail]
description:
## Task: TRD-026
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-b6db9749-behavior-habits-runtime.md#trd-026
PRD Reference: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-b6db9749-behavior-habits-runtime.md#req-021

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-021**: The complete local path is independently verified on Windows, Linux, and macOS
The complete local path is independently verified on Windows, Linux, and macOS Priority: Must [RISK: verification evidence does not yet exist for any of the three platforms as of this PRD]

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-021-1: Given the trigger/dispatch/notification path | When run on each of Windows | Then each platform has its own passing conformance suite run
- AC-021-2: Given a behavior works on one platform | When parity is claimed for another | Then that claim is backed by that platform's own conformance evidence, never inferred
- AC-023-1: Given a capability is unavailable on one platform (e.g. a specific filesystem-watch primitive) | When discovered | Then it is recorded as a named, documented gap rather than worked around silently in a way that changes behavior semantics per-platform

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen: Option B — dedicated adapter modules per new trigger-source type, plus a shared notification-state module.** Unchanged from 1.0.0.

New `file-source-adapter.ts` and `release-source-adapter.ts` under `packages/agent-core/src/behavior/` each produce a `BehaviorEvent` through `normalizeEvent`, mirroring the existing `pi-events.ts` → `event-translator.ts` → `normalizeEvent` → `LocalEventMatcher` chain. A new `notification-state.ts` in `pi-extension` centralises busy, duplicate and stale tracking for every behavior. Package quarantine gets its own `package-quarantine.ts` beside `package-discovery.ts`.

### Decisions added in 1.1.0

1. **How artifact changes are detected: content hashes checked at lifecycle points.** No `fs.watch`, no new dependency.
   - The adapter derives its watch set from the compiled `artifact.changed` triggers (the `path` predicate).
   - It hashes those files at `tool_result` and at `agent_end`, and emits an event when a digest differs from the last one seen in the session.
   - The hooks it relies on already exist, which is what AC-001-2 means by "supported host API".
   - It behaves the same on every OS (see REQ-023).
   - It needs no new dependency, which constitution §4 would require approval for.

   | Option | Why not chosen |
   |---|---|
   | `fs.watch` | Event semantics differ between macOS, Linux and Windows (rename-vs-change, recursive support). That is exactly the kind of per-platform behavior difference REQ-023 forbids absorbing silently. It also keeps a handle open for the whole session. |
   | `chokidar` | A new runtime dependency (constitution §4), for a problem that lifecycle-point hashing already solves. |

   The limitation, stated rather than hidden: a change is seen at the next tool call or at the end of the run, not instantly. NFR-001 measures from event validation, so this latency is outside its budget. TRD-003 reports it separately.

2. **Release signal (resolves the PRD's REQ-002 clarification): a new `v*` tag in local refs.** This matches this repo's `release.yml` (`on: push: tags: ['v*']`).
   - The tag pattern is a trigger predicate, so repositories with different conventions change configuration, not code (Rule 8).
   - It is detected two ways. First, from a successful tag-creating tool call (`git tag`, `gh release create`), in the same way `repository.changed` is derived today. Second, by diffing tag refs at session start and at `agent_end`, which covers tags that arrive by fetch.
   - It emits the **existing** catalog type `release.completed`, carrying `{ tag, sha, source }`.
   - One tag produces one event per session, whichever path sees it first.

3. **Coverage metric (resolves the PRD's REQ-016 clarification): Jest `json-summary` output, per file, `lines.pct` and `branches.pct` by default.**
   - Each package's `test:coverage` is `jest --coverage`. Jest's default reporters (`json`, `lcov`, `text`, `clover`) produce raw maps, not percentages.
   - So the behavior watches `coverage/coverage-summary.json`, and its README tells repositories to enable `json-summary`.
   - The metrics and the threshold (default 1.0 percentage point) are behavior configuration.
   - If the artifact never appears, the behavior shows up as an inert trigger in `/ensemble-status`; it is never silently idle.
   - The baseline is the previous snapshot seen **in the same session** (Rule 4). The first observation in a session only sets the baseline.

4. **The comparison is a generic command: `artifact.compare` (TRD-033).** It compares numeric JSON paths between the previous and current snapshot of an artifact and knows nothing about coverage.
   - The alternatives were rejected. Doing the comparison in an agent step would make the reported delta an unverified model claim (REQ-012). A coverage-specific command would make the third behavior need Ensemble code (REQ-018).
   - It lands in PR 1, which is why PR 5 can be configuration only.

5. **Notification transport** (REQ-009, REQ-010). `notification-state.ts` delivers to two sinks:
   - **The user**, through `SessionUiBridge.notify`, a new method that wraps `ctx.ui.notify`. Headless sessions fall back to the console.
   - **The model's context**, through `pi.sendMessage` with `display: true` and `triggerTurn: false`.

   `triggerTurn: false` is deliberate. #107 deleted the continuation path because a message that makes the agent act bypasses `MutationGuard` (`extension.ts:118-140`); a notification is data, never an instruction. Any test-derived text in a notification is fenced and labelled as data, a lesson from #94's live runs. `sendMessage` is added to `assertRequiredCapabilities`.

6. **Verified fix application** (REQ-033). This is configuration plus two small code changes.
   - A new behavior, `apply-verified-fix`, runs `mode: auto`. It triggers on `fix.verified` with the predicate `verdict: passed`, declares only `fix.apply` with no tools, and calls `fix.apply { proposalRef: ${event.payload.proposalRef} }`.
   - `CommandRegistry` then asks `ApprovalGate`. Today the prompt is only `descriptor.description` ("Apply a verified fix proposal…"), so the human would approve without seeing what changes. Code change 1 (TRD-019): the prompt names the proposal, its files and a diff summary.
   - `commit-policy.ts` has no importers today. Code change 2 (TRD-021): wire it in so an applied fix is committed with attribution.

### Alternatives considered (architecture)

| Option | Summary | Why not chosen |
|---|---|---|
| **A — Widen the existing translator, inline notification** | Add file and release branches inside `event-translator.ts`; keep notification-state logic at each `ctx.ui.notify` call site. | `event-translator.ts` would cover three unrelated source domains. Busy/duplicate/stale logic would be copied per behavior, which is the per-reaction duplication the PRD sets out to remove. |
| **B — Dedicated adapter modules + shared notification-state module** *(chosen)* | One adapter module per source type, all feeding the same ingress; one shared notification-state module. | Matches the existing boundary (`agent-core` = provider-neutral logic, `pi-extension` = host wiring), and centralises notification state once. |
| **C — Single generic "external signal" adapter** | One configurable "watch path X for condition Y" abstraction for both sources. | Risks becoming an arbitrary-condition escape hatch around the closed, versioned catalog (REQ-CQRS-005); still duplicates notification state. |
Satisfies: REQ-021
PRD ACs: AC-021-1, AC-021-2, AC-023-1
Target File: .github/workflows/test.yml, docs/platform-conformance.md
Actions:

Implementation AC:
- [ ] Given the matrix job on `windows-latest`, when it runs, then results are recorded. Each failure is either fixed with the same semantics on every OS, or recorded as a named gap.
- [ ] Given Seatbelt write confinement is macOS-only, when Windows is documented, then the gap is named ("no OS write confinement; isolated worktree and grant enforcement only").

description:
## Task: TRD-010
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-1d3e0dd6-new-feature-foreman-flag.md#trd-010
PRD Reference: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-1d3e0dd6-new-feature-foreman-flag.md#req-010

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-010**: Generated artifacts match their sources (Must)
Generated artifacts match their sources (Must)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-010-1: Given the edited sources | When `npm run generate` | Then the generated command docs, Pi prompts and Codex skills carry the new behavior in the rendered step text, and `npm run generate:validate` and `npm run validate` pass
- AC-010-2: Given the rendered text carries only a step's `description` and `actions[]` | When rules live in a step's `instructions` | Then they are mirrored into the description or actions so no runtime loses them

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen approach:** a prompt-only change to two YAML command sources. No TypeScript changes.

- `packages/development/commands/new-feature.yaml` gains a boolean `foreman` parameter and one derived variable, `FOREMAN`, defined once in Entry Point Resolution Step 1 and referenced by every later step. Each step that asks the user gets a `FOREMAN == true` branch that takes a deterministic, recorded, non-interactive decision. Each step that dispatches a stage skill appends `--foreman` when `FOREMAN == true`.
- `packages/development/commands/feature.yaml` (the `/ensemble:feature` front door) recognizes `--foreman` as the first token after the keyword and forwards it.
- Generated OMP, Pi and Codex artifacts are regenerated from the repo root, never hand-edited.

**Why prompt-only (Constitution Rule 8):** how a workflow behaves when no one can answer is something a maintainer would plausibly tune (for example, switching the PR gate to park instead of auto-grant). That belongs in the command prose, not in TypeScript. `RunIndexStore` already supports everything needed: `StageOutcome.detail` carries the "granted by `--foreman` policy" record.

**Additive-only edits (found in refinement):** the existing suites (`new-feature-command.test.js`, `feature-command.test.js`, `feature-input-validation-boundary.test.js`, `feature-concurrency-passthrough.test.js`) pin exact sentences in both YAML files, for example "any remaining text is an unsupported flag or argument rejected here". So no pre-existing sentence may be reworded or removed. Foreman behavior is added as new actions or appended sentences, and the existing suites must pass unchanged. For the front door that means: a new action, placed before the validation action, removes a leading `--foreman` token and sets `FOREMAN`, so the pinned validation sentences still read "remaining text" correctly; and a new action, placed after the invocation is constructed, inserts `--foreman` right after `/ensemble:new-feature` in whatever invocation was built.

**Alternatives rejected:**
- *Env-var-only detection (no flag).* Rejected: the maintainer asked for a `--foreman` flag, and the five stage skills already key on that flag.
- *A new RunRecord field `autoGranted`.* Rejected: TypeScript and schema change for information `StageOutcome.detail` already carries.
- *Parking at the approval gates.* Rejected by the maintainer: it stalls every no-user run.
Satisfies: REQ-010
PRD ACs: AC-010-1, AC-010-2
Target File: 
Actions:

Implementation AC:
- [ ] Given the edited sources, when `npm run generate`, `npm run generate:pi` and `npm run generate:codex` run from the repo root, then the OMP command docs, Pi prompts and Codex skills for `new-feature` and `feature` carry the new behavior in their rendered step text
- [ ] Given a rule lives only in a step's `instructions`, when rendering is checked, then it is mirrored into the description or actions
- [ ] Given the regeneration, when `git status` is read, then only the expected generated files changed and the Pi version bumped at most once

## Test Task: TRD-041-TEST
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-70e784f2-code-review-process.md#trd-041-test
PRD Reference: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-70e784f2-code-review-process.md#req-013

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-013**: Strict by default, raise-only, protected floor (Must)
Strict by default, raise-only, protected floor (Must) The tier policy starts strict and can only be loosened with evidence.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-013-1: Given fewer than 20 Low-tier PRs over 30 days have merged with zero reverts and zero incidents | When a Low PR is evaluated | Then it is treated as Medium and requires one human approval; once that evidence exists and a code owner explicitly enables it, Low means "no human required"
- AC-013-4: Given tier relaxation is attempted without the recorded evidence | When approval is evaluated | Then it is refused
- AC-015-1: Given a tier is assigned | When the PR's review state is read | Then it contains the tier, the characteristics that drove it, and who or what assigned it
- AC-015-2: Given a tier was raised by a sensitive path or a second assessment | When the record is read | Then it shows the original and final tier and the reason

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen approach (Option C):** extend the pattern TRD-2026-82b6a138 established: **editable behavior in skills, agents and markdown; a small set of pure, deterministic libraries for what must not be self-certified by a model.**

- **User-owned (Constitution Rule 8), prose or data a maintainer edits without a toolchain:** per-area rules (`REVIEW.md` files), the policy block inside the root `REVIEW.md` (round cap, depth table, bot and maintainer logins, sensitive and High paths, Low-waiver state), severity definitions, reviewer, verifier, classifier and security-lane prompts, the PR template, the sweep and explainer procedures. All of it is read from the **target branch**, never from the PR head (REQ-024).
- **Enforcement (Rules 5 and 7), code that grades a model's claim:** vote tally, tier assignment with its sensitive-path floor and Low-waiver evidence, approval evaluation bound to a commit, the merge gate, round-cap derivation, repeat suppression, delta-range selection, depth bounds, slice coverage, metrics and eval scoring. Each is a pure CommonJS module in `packages/development/lib/`, exposed as a JSON-in/JSON-out subcommand of the existing `pr-review-cli.js`, following the 82b6a138 precedent. None performs network I/O or holds a timer.
- **Entry points (Rule 6):** every capability is reached through the one `pr-review-cycle` skill, which `fix-issue`, `implement-trd-beads` and `pr-merge` already invoke or will invoke (a new `MODE=gate` for `pr-merge`). YAML callers reference the skill only, never the CLI, as the existing parity tests require.
- **Recurrence (Rule 4):** nightly or weekly sweeps and daily eval runs are on-demand skills; a workflow template for the host repository is opt-in and scaffolded by init-project. Ensemble's own workflows gain no `schedule` trigger.

**Alternatives considered (user chose C):**

- **Option A -- prose-only skills and agents:** fewest files and fastest to ship. Rejected: the vote threshold, the tier floor, commit-bound approvals and the round cap would be prose a model can misread or skip, so none of these gates could be shown to fail (Rule 7), and "a bot approval never counts" would be a request, not a guarantee.
- **Option B -- a new TypeScript review engine in `agent-core`:** strongest typing and one runtime. Rejected: a new build and `dist` surface and cross-package coupling for a prompt-level feature, editable criteria pulled into code (against Rule 8), and drift toward an ensemble-owned dispatcher that competes with Foreman (Rule 4).

**Rationale:** Option C is the best fit for this brownfield repo. It adds only the code that grades claims, keeps everything a maintainer or adopting team would tune in files they can edit, adds no dependency (Constitution §4) and no CI secret, vendors into Pi automatically through the existing require-closure bundler, and each gate can be mutation-proven using the harness that already exists.

**Decisions taken where the PRD left a choice** (each is editable policy, not a hidden constant):

| Decision | Value | Where it lives |
|---|---|---|
| Policy format | Fenced `ensemble-review-policy` JSON block in the root `REVIEW.md` (no new parser dependency) | REVIEW.md, read from the base commit |
| "Cannot vouch for" a push (AC-010-3, AC-014-2) | Commit is unvouched when its tree differs from the reviewed tree and it is not a remediation commit recorded in the review-state report, or it is a merge commit | `pr-review-scope.js`, `pr-review-approvals.js` |
| Slice threshold for large PRs (AC-018-1) | 1500 changed lines, configurable | policy block |
| Area rules vs policy keys | Policy keys are read from the **root** file only; area files carry guidance, and the more restrictive instruction wins when areas conflict (AC-001-2) | skill prose |
| First PR that introduces REVIEW.md | No base copy exists, so strict defaults apply (Low treated as Medium, cap 3, default sensitive set) | `pr-review-policy.js` |
| Verifier majority | Strict majority of the expected verifier count (2 of 3, 3 of 5) | `pr-review-votes.js` |

description:
## Test Task: TRD-005-TEST
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-1d3e0dd6-new-feature-foreman-flag.md#trd-005-test
PRD Reference: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-1d3e0dd6-new-feature-foreman-flag.md#req-005

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-005**: PR approval and PR creation need no human (Must)
PR approval and PR creation need no human (Must)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-005-1: Given `--foreman` and `ELIGIBLE_STAGE == pr_approval` | When the checkpoint runs | Then the opt-in and the repo/branch/title/body question are not asked; one `mutate()` call sets `prApprovedAt` and advances to `pr_create`, never in the same call as `implementationApprovedAt`
- AC-005-2: Given `isAvailable()` is false under `--foreman` | When the checkpoint runs | Then no PR is created, the outcome records "no PR provider available", and the run advances to `done`, exactly as without the flag
- AC-005-3: Given `pr_create` runs | When `prApprovedAt` is null in the loaded run | Then the call is still denied regardless of any claim of approval (the store-persisted-approval precondition is unchanged)
- AC-005-4: Given `--foreman` is absent | When the checkpoint runs | Then the opt-in and the separate explicit approval are both required as today

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen approach:** a prompt-only change to two YAML command sources. No TypeScript changes.

- `packages/development/commands/new-feature.yaml` gains a boolean `foreman` parameter and one derived variable, `FOREMAN`, defined once in Entry Point Resolution Step 1 and referenced by every later step. Each step that asks the user gets a `FOREMAN == true` branch that takes a deterministic, recorded, non-interactive decision. Each step that dispatches a stage skill appends `--foreman` when `FOREMAN == true`.
- `packages/development/commands/feature.yaml` (the `/ensemble:feature` front door) recognizes `--foreman` as the first token after the keyword and forwards it.
- Generated OMP, Pi and Codex artifacts are regenerated from the repo root, never hand-edited.

**Why prompt-only (Constitution Rule 8):** how a workflow behaves when no one can answer is something a maintainer would plausibly tune (for example, switching the PR gate to park instead of auto-grant). That belongs in the command prose, not in TypeScript. `RunIndexStore` already supports everything needed: `StageOutcome.detail` carries the "granted by `--foreman` policy" record.

**Additive-only edits (found in refinement):** the existing suites (`new-feature-command.test.js`, `feature-command.test.js`, `feature-input-validation-boundary.test.js`, `feature-concurrency-passthrough.test.js`) pin exact sentences in both YAML files, for example "any remaining text is an unsupported flag or argument rejected here". So no pre-existing sentence may be reworded or removed. Foreman behavior is added as new actions or appended sentences, and the existing suites must pass unchanged. For the front door that means: a new action, placed before the validation action, removes a leading `--foreman` token and sets `FOREMAN`, so the pinned validation sentences still read "remaining text" correctly; and a new action, placed after the invocation is constructed, inserts `--foreman` right after `/ensemble:new-feature` in whatever invocation was built.

**Alternatives rejected:**
- *Env-var-only detection (no flag).* Rejected: the maintainer asked for a `--foreman` flag, and the five stage skills already key on that flag.
- *A new RunRecord field `autoGranted`.* Rejected: TypeScript and schema change for information `StageOutcome.detail` already carries.
- *Parking at the approval gates.* Rejected by the maintainer: it stalls every no-user run.

title: Constitution changes apply in-place after approval; PR becomes delivery, not gate
description:
DESIGN DECISION by the user, 2026-09-25. Supersedes an acceptance criterion
of a consumed TRD, so it is recorded here rather than by editing TRD-029.

SUPERSEDED (TRD-029 / REQ-007, encoded in constitution-proposal.ts):
  "constitution.md is never modified in place by this path, on either answer.
   'Yes' opens a PR and the file changes only if a human merges it."

REPLACEMENT:
  Approval edits docs/standards/constitution.md DIRECTLY in the working tree.
  The change then reaches main the same way every other change does -- commit,
  push, PR into dev, release PR dev -> main. The PR is not the approval
  mechanism; it is the delivery mechanism.

WHY THIS IS NOW SAFE, WHEN IT WAS NOT BEFORE
REQ-007 was written when main had no protection and every marketplace source
was an unpinned relative path, so a merge to main shipped instantly to every
consumer. "Never touch the file in-session" was the only available guard.
Since then the repository has a dev integration branch, main is protected
(enforce_admins, required checks release-gate + source-branch, no force-push)
and main advances only through a dev -> main release PR. Human review is now
structural, so it no longer has to be smuggled in as "the approval IS a PR".

CONSEQUENCES TO IMPLEMENT
- ConstitutionProposal stops calling openPullRequest on approval and applies
  the change instead.
- WriteBoundaryMonitor must permit exactly that one authorized write.
  Everything else under docs/standards stays reverted. The exception must be
  scoped to the approved change and revoked immediately after -- an
  open-ended "constitution edits allowed" flag would delete the protection
  this session proved works.
- Denial, and a headless session with no UI, must still change nothing. The
  fail-closed property of ApprovalGate is unchanged.

WHAT IS NOT CHANGING
- Protected-path enforcement for every other writer and every other path.
- The fail-closed rule: absence of a UI is a denial, never an implicit yes.
