description:
## Test Task: TRD-003-TEST
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-82b6a138-pr-review-cycle-time.md#trd-003-test
PRD Reference: #req-007

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen approach (Option C):** One shared, prose-defined review procedure plus a small deterministic helper library.

- `packages/development/skills/pr-review-cycle/SKILL.md` is the single reusable procedure. It owns the *user-editable* parts (Constitution Rule 8): review criteria, the order of the loop, the 10-minute interactive wait, Foreman-mode rules. It **composes** `packages/quality/skills/pr-review-remediation/SKILL.md` for per-finding triage, regression tests and minimal fixes and does not restate those rules.
- A set of small pure-JS modules in `packages/development/lib/` owns only what *grades the model's own claim* (Constitution Rule 8's enforcement exception, and Rule 7): base/head scope resolution, ledger validation, head-bound remote-review evaluation, terminal-status derivation with the bounded-round cap, and the untracked review-state report. A thin CLI, `pr-review-cli.js`, exposes them as JSON-in/JSON-out commands, following the `trd-cli.js` / `complete-beads-planner.js` precedent.
- `fix-issue.yaml`, `implement-trd-beads.yaml` and `complete-beads/SKILL.md` invoke the skill at their real PR boundaries; none re-states review steps.

**Alternatives considered (user chose C):**

- **Option A -- prose-only skill:** fewest files, but "no early REVIEW_COMPLETE", head-binding and the round cap would be prose a model can misread, and tests could only assert text ordering. Rejected: the plan's core guarantee would not be falsifiable (Rule 7).
- **Option B -- TypeScript runtime in agent-core:** strongest typing, but a new build/dist surface and cross-package coupling for a prompt-level feature, and it pulls editable criteria toward code (against Rule 8). Rejected.

**Rationale:** Option C is the best fit for this brownfield repo: the helper is the minimum code that makes the status contract testable and unforgeable, everything a maintainer would plausibly tune stays in a skill file, and it needs no new dependency, provider or config knob.

title: behavior runtime: CQRS commands, closed event catalog, declarative workflows
description:
Evolve the behavior runtime from a test-failure-specific automation path into a
behavior-driven local harness built on CQRS: typed commands, a closed event
catalog, and declarative behavior packages interpreted by one engine.

Source: `docs/architecture/ensemble-behavior-cqrs-implementation-requirements.md`

## The shape of it

    skill / UI command / runtime event
      -> typed command request
      -> handler validates policy and evidence
      -> authorized state transition
      -> resulting fact/event
      -> declarative behavior workflow reacts

An event records a fact that occurred. It is not an instruction to mutate.
A command expresses intent; its handler validates authority and invariants,
performs the effect, and emits the result event only once the outcome is known.

## Why this is not theoretical

The current runtime has already failed in exactly the ways this contract is
written to prevent, observed live during the loop-trial work:

- Two dispatch paths for one event. The governed path correctly refused a write
  under `policy.mode: propose` and the continuation path repaired the file
  anyway. The second path masked the first being dead for three days, because
  every run still looked successful (br-dowt, br-cxn8, br-boam).
- `propose` mutating the user's tree. A verified fix was left applied with no
  human asked, because a missing baseline was treated as permission (br-dowt).
- Tool grants that do not grant. `--tools=read,grep,glob` does not restrict
  tools; a fix child reached `_write`, `_learn` and `_manage_skill` and wrote a
  skill into the operator's HOME that loads in every future session (br-33co).
- Verification accepting a runner it had just judged defective: a suite that
  never loaded counted as passed (br-gwww).

REQ-CQRS-002, REQ-SAFE-001, REQ-SAFE-003 and REQ-SAFE-006 each exist because of
one of those. Treat them as regression requirements, not aspirations.

## Ownership boundary

Ensemble owns portable behavior packages, validation, simulation and local
Pi/OMP execution. Foreman owns durable activation, scheduling, recovery,
approvals and audit history. Do not add durable scheduling, leases, retries or
recovery here (REQ-RUN-002), and do not modify Foreman as part of this work.

## Phase order

Phases are sequential and each has an exit gate. Do not start with a broad
rewrite of generated commands or existing packages.

  Phase 0  resolve the runtime split, prove the boundaries
  Phase 1  versioned command/event contracts
  Phase 2  constrained workflow interpreter
  Phase 3  port the test-failure slice and constitution proposal
  Phase 4  authoring, compatibility, handoff
acceptance_criteria:
All 12 system-wide acceptance criteria in section 6 hold, in particular:
new behaviors need no behavior-specific TypeScript; every mutation uses one
authorization boundary regardless of how it was initiated; propose mode
demonstrably cannot mutate the working tree including via native tools and
shell; concurrent edits are never lost; no ambiguous/zero-test/timeout result
is accepted as success; constitution changes are evidence-backed proposals
applied only through a separate authorized transition.
close_reason: All 20 stories and exit gates delivered; constitution.apply reachability carved out to br-dlol

title: report where the tree differs from the CQRS spec
description:
Section 8 requires this BEFORE implementation: inspect the checked-out branch
and report every difference between the specification and the actual tree.

Source: `docs/architecture/ensemble-behavior-cqrs-implementation-requirements.md`

Produce a written gap report covering at least:

- the continuation queue, `BehaviorRunner`, `AutofixLoop`, the matcher and the
  event translator: what each does today and which of them can mutate state
- every path that can write files or run shell/network operations
- which existing behavior.yaml fields map to the contract in section 3.1, and
  which have no equivalent (migration note)
- which of the 12 acceptance criteria in section 6 currently fail, with the
  evidence that shows it

Known starting points from live runs, all reproducible: two dispatch paths for
one event (br-dowt); propose mode leaving a fix applied (br-dowt); tool grants
not restricting tools (br-33co); verification trusting a defective runner
(br-gwww); per-invocation cwd confusion across call sites (br-nft8).

The report is the input to Story 0.1 and should be attached to this issue.
acceptance_criteria: A written gap report exists naming every mutation path and every failing acceptance criterion with evidence; no implementation has begun.
close_reason: Completed

title: interpret bounded workflow steps
description:
Story 2.2 / REQ-BEH-002, REQ-SAFE-007. Source: `docs/architecture/ensemble-behavior-cqrs-implementation-requirements.md`

Implement the five step kinds: `agent`, `command`, `condition`, `approval`,
`outcome`. Sequential steps plus simple conditionals are enough initially --
reject anything unsupported rather than skipping it silently.

Every step has a bounded timeout, attempt budget, cancellation path, output-size
bound and explicit failure outcome. No unbounded recursion, event-trigger loop
or automatic child-behavior cycle (REQ-SAFE-007).

`condition` branches only on structured validated results, never on model prose.
Keep the interpreter provider-neutral; Pi/OMP invocation goes through adapters.

The `approval` step is not a formality: an approval gate that asks and a reply
that is read correctly are two different things. A live run recorded "declined
by user" for an approval the operator had granted, because the reply shape did
not match what the host read. Test the accept path, not just the deny path.
acceptance_criteria: Fixture-driven workflows run deterministically; unsupported steps are rejected; timeout, cancel and no-orphan tests pass; recursion and duplicate-event limits hold; a workflow-step command denial matches the direct tool-call denial.
close_reason: Completed

title: load prompts and workflow data without a rebuild
description:
Story 2.3 / REQ-BEH-003. Source: `docs/architecture/ensemble-behavior-cqrs-implementation-requirements.md`

Load prompt and skill files and workflow data at activation/invocation.
Demonstrate that a prompt or workflow edit takes effect with no TypeScript
rebuild, while an invalid edit still fails validation.

Include the prompt files in the behavior digest, so "what ran" stays
identifiable even though the text is editable.

Practical note from live work: the installed extension bundle was once built
from a stale checkout three commits behind, and several runs tested code that
did not include the fixes under test. Whatever mechanism loads package assets,
the status output must make the ACTIVE path and digest visible (see Story 4.1).
acceptance_criteria: Editing a prompt file changes behavior with no rebuild; an invalid workflow edit fails validation with a clear diagnostic; the digest reflects prompt content.
close_reason: Completed

title: exit gate 2: a behavior runs from package data alone
description:
Phase 2 exit gate. Source: `docs/architecture/ensemble-behavior-cqrs-implementation-requirements.md`

A minimal behavior with two agent/command steps runs solely from a package and
the shared interpreter, and no behavior-name-specific branch exists in runtime
code.

The second half is the part that is easy to fake: grep the runtime for
behavior names and assert none appear in dispatch logic.
acceptance_criteria: A new fixture behavior runs end to end without code changes; no behavior name appears in runtime dispatch code.
close_reason: Completed

title: port the test-failure investigation to package data
description:
Story 3.1. Source: `docs/architecture/ensemble-behavior-cqrs-implementation-requirements.md`

Express detection, investigation, fix proposal, structured evidence and outcome
in behavior data plus shared typed commands. Remove test-specific workflow logic
from the Pi adapter once parity tests pass.

The reference flow (section 4):

    test.failure.observed
      -> investigate (read-only agent step, capture diagnosis/evidence)
      -> fix.propose (typed command; create candidate, do not edit the project)
      -> optional isolated verification of the candidate
      -> outcome: fix.proposed | investigation.inconclusive | behavior.blocked

Detection errors must not grant mutation authority. Where runner identification
or failure evidence is ambiguous, record a diagnostic or skip -- do not trigger
an apply path (section 4, REQ-SAFE-006).
acceptance_criteria: The test-failure behavior runs from package data with no test-specific branch in the adapter; parity tests against the current behavior pass.
close_reason: Completed

title: separate proposal, verification, approval and application
description:
Story 3.2 / REQ-SAFE-001, REQ-SAFE-002, REQ-SAFE-005, REQ-SAFE-006. Source: `docs/architecture/ensemble-behavior-cqrs-implementation-requirements.md`

Explicit proposal artifacts, structured verifier results, apply only through an
authorized handler in an isolated workspace after any required approval.
Approval and application are separate facts.

Four live failures this must close, all reproduced:

- a verified fix was LEFT APPLIED with no approval because a missing baseline
  was treated as permission -- fail-open in a system that fails closed
  everywhere else (br-dowt, partially fixed in PR #105)
- verification accepted `2 passed, 2 total` from a runner that had counted a
  suite which never loaded as passed; the same run's constitution amendment
  described that exact defect (br-gwww)
- whole-tree restore is used as rollback in the interactive workspace, which
  REQ-SAFE-005 forbids as routine; concurrent edits must survive
- the applier writes to the failing command's worktree, which may not be where
  the canonical project lives (br-nft8)

REQ-SAFE-006 is explicit that unknown output, zero tests, a missing runner, a
timeout or an unattributable result is `inconclusive`, never passed, and that a
single generic regex must not be the authority across frameworks.
acceptance_criteria: Propose mode creates a proposal and changes nothing; apply requires an explicit authorized command; a zero-test or unattributable verifier result is never accepted as success; concurrent edits survive.
close_reason: Completed

title: add the constitution-learning behavior
description:
Story 3.3 / REQ-SAFE-008. Source: `docs/architecture/ensemble-behavior-cqrs-implementation-requirements.md`

A separately packageable behavior that triggers only on verified/accepted fix
evidence -- not on the initial failure -- and outputs an evidence-backed
constitution proposal with rationale, source evidence, affected rule and diff.
Never a direct write, never auto-accepted because a test passed.

Approval/PR opening and canonical application are separate auditable operations.

This flow has been observed working end to end and is worth preserving as the
reference: a run proposed "a test suite that fails to load, import or compile
must count as a failure and make the run exit non-zero", reasoned about the
existing rule it was amending, asked for approval, and wrote the amendment only
after consent. Two independent runs produced equivalent rules in different
words. The scenario that warranted it matters: a one-line arithmetic bug
legitimately implies no constitution change.
acceptance_criteria: The behavior triggers only from verified evidence; a proposal is never applied without a separate approved apply step; a trivial fix produces no proposal.
close_reason: Completed

title: exit gate 3: the reference flow is package-defined and reproducible
description:
Phase 3 exit gate. Source: `docs/architecture/ensemble-behavior-cqrs-implementation-requirements.md`

The reference flow is package-defined, reviewable, reproducible from fixtures,
and does not mutate canonical project or constitution state without the explicit
apply workflow.

Required tests: end-to-end failure -> investigation -> proposal; no project
change in propose mode; an inaccurate model success claim rejected by
independent verification; zero/unrecognized tests cannot pass; unrelated
concurrent edits survive; a constitution proposal is never auto-applied;
duplicate or recursive triggers bounded.

Reproducible from fixtures means: without a hand-driven RPC harness. The
current end-to-end proof depends on a bespoke driver script on one machine,
which is not reproducibility.
acceptance_criteria: The full flow runs from fixtures in CI; every listed test passes; no canonical state changes without an explicit apply.
close_reason: Completed

title: add package validation, simulation and a truthful status report
description:
Story 4.1 / REQ-RUN-003. Source: `docs/architecture/ensemble-behavior-cqrs-implementation-requirements.md`

Package validation/preview and fixture-based simulation for event matching,
workflow branches and command authorization. A status report showing behavior
digest, ACTIVE package path, workflow state, and concrete skip/error reasons.

Status output must distinguish discovered, validated, matched, invoked, pending,
completed, failed and skipped. Do not log secrets or unrestricted prompt/tool
contents.

Make diagnostics describe the condition that actually fired. A live example of
the opposite cost real time: baseline capture reported "not a git work tree"
when the repository was a clean clone -- the real cause was one untracked
symlink that `git hash-object` could not hash. A diagnostic that guesses is
worse than one that says nothing.
acceptance_criteria: Simulation runs with no side effects; status distinguishes all listed states; every skip reason names the actual condition, verified by a test that forces each one.
close_reason: Completed

title: preserve existing commands, skills, agents and hooks
description:
Story 4.2 / REQ-BEH-005. Source: `docs/architecture/ensemble-behavior-cqrs-implementation-requirements.md`

Generated artifact snapshots and compatibility suites for commands, skills and
agents. Host hooks stay optional and normalize through shared event schemas.

Section 7 guardrail: do not broaden this into rewriting all legacy skills,
commands or provider adapters.
acceptance_criteria: Generated-output regression passes; the same event fixtures produce equivalent normalized matches across local adapters; existing artifacts are unchanged unless a migration was explicitly approved.

title: spike: publish the cross-repository contract proposal
description:
Spike 4.3 / REQ-CQRS-006, REQ-RUN-002. Source: `docs/architecture/ensemble-behavior-cqrs-implementation-requirements.md`

Document the provider-neutral package, event, command-result and invocation
contracts for future Foreman consumption. Coordinate the CONTRACT only.

Do not implement durable Foreman behavior in Ensemble, and do not modify Foreman
as part of this work (section 7).
acceptance_criteria: A versioned contract document exists; conformance tests run without a durable Foreman dependency; no durable scheduling or recovery API was added to Ensemble.

title: establish one behavior execution path
description:
Story 0.1. Source: `docs/architecture/ensemble-behavior-cqrs-implementation-requirements.md`

Remove or disable duplicate test-failure repair dispatch so one event cannot
start two competing fix agents (REQ-CQRS-002).

This is the highest-value item in Phase 0 and it is not speculative. Observed
live: the governed path rejected a direct write under `mode: propose` while the
continuation path repaired the same file in the same run. The duplicate path
also hid two P0 defects for three days by repairing code whenever the governed
path failed, so every session looked successful.

Scope:

- inventory the continuation queue, `BehaviorRunner`, `AutofixLoop`, matcher and
  event translator (input: the gap report)
- choose ONE governed route; remove or strictly isolate the other. Section 7 is
  explicit that silently merging them is not acceptable.
- produce the migration note mapping existing behavior fields to this contract

Do not keep both paths behind a flag that defaults to the ungoverned one.
acceptance_criteria: One failure event demonstrably starts at most one workflow; a regression test proves it; the migration note exists.
close_reason: Completed

title: exit gate 4: behaviors are authorable from package files alone
description:
Phase 4 exit gate. Source: `docs/architecture/ensemble-behavior-cqrs-implementation-requirements.md`

Maintainers can add or alter a behavior using package files and fixtures alone
when existing primitives suffice. Code changes are required only for genuinely
new trusted runtime capabilities.

This is also acceptance criterion 1 and the clearest single measure of whether
the epic succeeded.
acceptance_criteria: A maintainer adds a working behavior with no TypeScript change and no rebuild, demonstrated end to end from fixtures.
close_reason: Completed

title: spike: prove what Pi/OMP can actually enforce
description:
Spike 0.2. Source: `docs/architecture/ensemble-behavior-cqrs-implementation-requirements.md`

Determine whether Pi/OMP can provide per-invocation tool grants and a reliable
approval/cancellation boundary, and whether OS-level isolation or worktree
execution is viable locally. Document residual risks.

Start from the measured answer, not the documented one: `--tools=read,grep,glob`
does NOT restrict tools. A child reported `_read _grep _glob _manage_skill
_learn _write`, and `--no-tools --no-skills` changed nothing. A probe child
created `~/.omp/agent/managed-skills/containment-probe-delete-me/SKILL.md` in
the operator's HOME, which would load in every future session in every repo.
Measured three times; see br-33co.

That makes REQ-SAFE-003 currently unmet and gives the spike a concrete
question: if the grant boundary cannot be enforced at the tool-call layer, what
is the fallback -- OS sandbox, worktree, or keeping mutation disabled?

Section 7: do not label a post-tool monitor a sandbox. Document exactly what is
and is not prevented (REQ-SAFE-004).
acceptance_criteria: A written finding states which boundaries Pi/OMP can enforce, which it cannot, and what the fallback is; no mechanism is described as a sandbox unless it isolates at the OS or process level.
close_reason: Completed

title: exit gate 0: propose mode proven non-mutating under hostile tools
description:
Phase 0 exit gate. Source: `docs/architecture/ensemble-behavior-cqrs-implementation-requirements.md`

One dispatch path is demonstrated AND propose mode is proven non-mutating in an
end-to-end hostile-tool test. If Pi cannot enforce the boundary, mutation stays
disabled pending a sandbox or a safer adapter design.

Required tests (section 5, Phase 0):

- one failure event starts at most one workflow
- a propose-mode event cannot alter project files through native tools, shell
  redirects, subprocesses, or a continuation
- a concurrent user edit is preserved
- process cancellation terminates child work, leaving no orphan

"Hostile" means the test actively tries to escape: shell redirection, a child
tool call, a skill write outside the repo. A test that only checks the happy
path proves nothing here -- br-33co was found by trying to escape on purpose.

This gate cannot pass while br-33co is open.
acceptance_criteria: The hostile-tool suite passes on CI and is not skippable; propose mode alters nothing in the user's tree by any route; cancellation leaves no orphan process.
close_reason: Completed

title: add typed command descriptors and handler registry
description:
Story 1.1 / REQ-CQRS-001. Source: `docs/architecture/ensemble-behavior-cqrs-implementation-requirements.md`

A provider-neutral registry of code-owned command descriptors. Each descriptor
defines a stable command ID and version, input schema, result schema, required
capability, mutation class, handler, and emitted event types.

The Pi adapter exposes these descriptors as governed tools; workflow steps call
the same registry. There must be no second privileged implementation -- that
duplication is exactly what Phase 0 removes, and re-introducing it at the
command layer would undo it.

Centralize capability checks, mutation authorization, approval requirements,
idempotency/deduplication and error mapping here rather than in each handler.

Keep it provider-neutral: no Pi/OMP types in the registry (REQ-RUN-004).
acceptance_criteria: A command invoked from a workflow step and the same command invoked as a Pi tool traverse identical authorization code; an unauthorized command is denied identically on both routes.
close_reason: Completed

title: complete event authority semantics
description:
Story 1.2 / REQ-CQRS-003, REQ-CQRS-004, REQ-CQRS-005. Source: `docs/architecture/ensemble-behavior-cqrs-implementation-requirements.md`

Define observed, requested, proposed, verified, applied, rejected and failed as
separate facts. Stamp runtime-owned metadata (event ID, session/execution IDs,
timestamp, source, causation/correlation, behavior identity and digest) in the
runtime, never from an agent payload.

A handler emits a success event only after confirming the transition occurred.
An agent saying "done" is not evidence. This has a live precedent worth keeping
in mind: a fix agent reported a correct diagnosis and a correct fix in prose
while having written nothing, because it had no tool that could edit files. The
reply parsed as failure only by luck of shape, not by contract.

A result must never describe a proposed or queued operation as completed
(REQ-CQRS-003). Unknown or context-incompatible events fail closed.
acceptance_criteria: Schema contract tests pass; no success event can be emitted before a successful handler result; unknown event types are rejected; causation metadata is stable across command and result events.
close_reason: Completed

title: spike: decide what the local event sink guarantees
description:
Spike 1.3 / REQ-CQRS-006. Source: `docs/architecture/ensemble-behavior-cqrs-implementation-requirements.md`

Decide and document what the local sink guarantees across process exit, and how
acceptance and forwarding behave. Production durability and recovery stay
outside Ensemble.

The specific failure to avoid: local acceptance being represented as Foreman
acceptance. A local outbox is not a durable event store and cannot claim
scheduling, retries, replay, recovery or production approval guarantees.

Relevant local evidence: a shutdown drain exists and has been observed
completing, but nothing currently distinguishes "written to the local log" from
"accepted by anything durable".
acceptance_criteria: A written decision states the local sink's guarantees across process exit; a test proves local acceptance is never reported as Foreman acceptance.
close_reason: Completed

title: exit gate 1: a command proposes through one handler and reports truthfully
description:
Phase 1 exit gate. Source: `docs/architecture/ensemble-behavior-cqrs-implementation-requirements.md`

A test command can be proposed through one registered handler and yields a
truthful typed result and event, with no direct agent writes.

Required tests: schema contracts; unauthorized command denied regardless of
invocation path; no success event before a successful handler result; unknown
command/event rejected; local acceptance never represented as Foreman
acceptance; stable causation metadata.
acceptance_criteria: The exit-gate suite passes; the same command denied via tool call and via workflow step produces the same denial.
close_reason: Completed

title: validate and compile package workflow data
description:
Story 2.1 / REQ-BEH-001, REQ-BEH-004. Source: `docs/architecture/ensemble-behavior-cqrs-implementation-requirements.md`

Static validation of step IDs, references, command bindings, event types, tool
grants, mutation classes, timeout bounds and failure branches, before
invocation. Preserve package digests and deterministic output.

Fail closed for unknown commands, event types, workflow primitives or
capabilities. Diagnostics name the behavior and the step, and one invalid
package must not suppress unrelated valid ones.

Note the failure mode this prevents, observed live: a behavior's own
`fix-prompt.md` silently replaced the entire prompt including the response
contract, because loading used `template ?? default` with no validation that
the result still satisfied the runtime's requirements. Validation has to cover
what the package REPLACES, not only what it adds.
acceptance_criteria: Unsupported constructs are rejected with a diagnostic naming behavior and step; an invalid package does not prevent valid packages loading; digests stay deterministic.
close_reason: Completed

title: [trd:trd-2026-15aa5acd-live-behavior-dispatch-autofix:task:TRD-021] - [ ] **TRD-021** Implement `WorkspaceSnapshot` capture and exact restore (6h)
description:
## Task: TRD-021
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-15aa5acd-live-behavior-dispatch-autofix.md#trd-021
PRD Reference: #req-015

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen: Option C — single enforcement seam, additive.**

A new `MutationGuard` chokepoint in `agent-core` is the one place `policy.mode`, `capabilities.mutation_classes` (via the existing `hasMutationAuthority()`), and protected-path rules are resolved. It is wired once at the loader boundary rather than replicated per tool registration. The translator, matcher, and auto-fix loop are added to `pi-extension`. Discovery roots and `execution.test_command` are additive changes to existing schema/discovery code. `ToolRegistry`, `outbox`, and the compiler are reused unchanged.

### Alternatives considered

| Option | Summary | Why not chosen |
|---|---|---|
| **A — In-place extension** | Enforce mode/mutation/path rules as wrapper checks inside `behavior-loader`'s per-tool `execute()` closures. | Enforcement scattered across call sites; every future tool registration must remember to wrap. The PRD's central failure mode is *guarantees that exist in one place but are not reached from another* — Option A reproduces exactly that shape. |
| **B — Governance kernel** | Route every mutation through a `MutationBroker` + `GovernedWorkspace` in `agent-core`; `pi-extension` becomes a thin adapter. | Strongest long-term design and the right eventual target, but it re-opens already-shipped code across every tool path for a ~6-7 PR refactor before a single PRD requirement is demonstrable. Deferred deliberately, not rejected. |
| **C — Single enforcement seam** *(chosen)* | One `MutationGuard` chokepoint, wired once; everything else additive. | Gets a single auditable chokepoint (Option B's main benefit) without Option B's refactor surface. Fits the existing `agent-core` / `pi-extension` split. |

### Architectural note carried from grounding

Two defects found while grounding this design are folded into PR 1 rather than left implicit:

1. `pi-events.ts` emits `runtime.tool_result` / `runtime.tool.called` / `runtime.tool.failed` / `runtime.tool.completed`, none of which appear in `HARNESS_EVENT_TYPES` (which defines `runtime.tool_call.started` / `runtime.tool_call.completed`). `normalizeEvent` does not currently reject uncatalogued types, so PRD AC-002-1's "validated against the closed catalog" would be vacuous. Addressed by TRD-001 (`[satisfies INFRA]`).
2. `behavior-loader.ts:79` calls `registry.grant(...)` unconditionally immediately before `registry.invoke(...)`, making the grant boundary a rubber stamp for behavior-governed tools (unlike the echo path, where the grant is CLI-flag-gated). Addressed by TRD-003.
Satisfies: REQ-015
PRD ACs: AC-015-3, AC-005-4
Target File: packages/agent-core/src/behavior/workspace-snapshot.ts
Actions:

Implementation AC:
- [ ] Given a set of files modified during an attempt, when `restore()` runs, then every file's content and mode is byte-identical to capture time, and files created during the attempt are removed.

title: [trd:trd-2026-1d3e0dd6-new-feature-foreman-flag:task:TRD-009-TEST] - [ ] **TRD-009-TEST** Invariants and the question guard (2h)
description:
## Test Task: TRD-009-TEST
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-1d3e0dd6-new-feature-foreman-flag.md#trd-009-test
PRD Reference: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-1d3e0dd6-new-feature-foreman-flag.md#req-009

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-009**: Hard stops and exclusivity are unchanged (Must)
Hard stops and exclusivity are unchanged (Must)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-009-1: Given `--foreman` | When a run is already active | Then `RUN_ALREADY_ACTIVE` is still reported and no run is created
- AC-009-2: Given `--foreman` | When `--status` runs | Then it is still read-only and makes no `mutate()` call
- AC-009-3: Given `--foreman` | When a stage fails | Then it is parked at that stage and never auto-retried in the same invocation

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen approach:** a prompt-only change to two YAML command sources. No TypeScript changes.

- `packages/development/commands/new-feature.yaml` gains a boolean `foreman` parameter and one derived variable, `FOREMAN`, defined once in Entry Point Resolution Step 1 and referenced by every later step. Each step that asks the user gets a `FOREMAN == true` branch that takes a deterministic, recorded, non-interactive decision. Each step that dispatches a stage skill appends `--foreman` when `FOREMAN == true`.
- `packages/development/commands/feature.yaml` (the `/ensemble:feature` front door) recognizes `--foreman` as the first token after the keyword and forwards it.
- Generated OMP, Pi and Codex artifacts are regenerated from the repo root, never hand-edited.

**Why prompt-only (Constitution Rule 8):** how a workflow behaves when no one can answer is something a maintainer would plausibly tune (for example, switching the PR gate to park instead of auto-grant). That belongs in the command prose, not in TypeScript. `RunIndexStore` already supports everything needed: `StageOutcome.detail` carries the "granted by `--foreman` policy" record.

**Additive-only edits (found in refinement):** the existing suites (`new-feature-command.test.js`, `feature-command.test.js`, `feature-input-validation-boundary.test.js`, `feature-concurrency-passthrough.test.js`) pin exact sentences in both YAML files, for example "any remaining text is an unsupported flag or argument rejected here". So no pre-existing sentence may be reworded or removed. Foreman behavior is added as new actions or appended sentences, and the existing suites must pass unchanged. For the front door that means: a new action, placed before the validation action, removes a leading `--foreman` token and sets `FOREMAN`, so the pinned validation sentences still read "remaining text" correctly; and a new action, placed after the invocation is constructed, inserts `--foreman` right after `/ensemble:new-feature` in whatever invocation was built.

**Alternatives rejected:**
- *Env-var-only detection (no flag).* Rejected: the maintainer asked for a `--foreman` flag, and the five stage skills already key on that flag.
- *A new RunRecord field `autoGranted`.* Rejected: TypeScript and schema change for information `StageOutcome.detail` already carries.
- *Parking at the approval gates.* Rejected by the maintainer: it stalls every no-user run.

title: [trd:trd-2026-82b6a138-pr-review-cycle-time:task:TRD-001] - [ ] **TRD-001** Review scope resolver (`pr-review-scope.js`) (3h)
description:
## Task: TRD-001
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-82b6a138-pr-review-cycle-time.md#trd-001
PRD Reference: #req-002

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen approach (Option C):** One shared, prose-defined review procedure plus a small deterministic helper library.

- `packages/development/skills/pr-review-cycle/SKILL.md` is the single reusable procedure. It owns the *user-editable* parts (Constitution Rule 8): review criteria, the order of the loop, the 10-minute interactive wait, Foreman-mode rules. It **composes** `packages/quality/skills/pr-review-remediation/SKILL.md` for per-finding triage, regression tests and minimal fixes and does not restate those rules.
- A set of small pure-JS modules in `packages/development/lib/` owns only what *grades the model's own claim* (Constitution Rule 8's enforcement exception, and Rule 7): base/head scope resolution, ledger validation, head-bound remote-review evaluation, terminal-status derivation with the bounded-round cap, and the untracked review-state report. A thin CLI, `pr-review-cli.js`, exposes them as JSON-in/JSON-out commands, following the `trd-cli.js` / `complete-beads-planner.js` precedent.
- `fix-issue.yaml`, `implement-trd-beads.yaml` and `complete-beads/SKILL.md` invoke the skill at their real PR boundaries; none re-states review steps.

**Alternatives considered (user chose C):**

- **Option A -- prose-only skill:** fewest files, but "no early REVIEW_COMPLETE", head-binding and the round cap would be prose a model can misread, and tests could only assert text ordering. Rejected: the plan's core guarantee would not be falsifiable (Rule 7).
- **Option B -- TypeScript runtime in agent-core:** strongest typing, but a new build/dist surface and cross-package coupling for a prompt-level feature, and it pulls editable criteria toward code (against Rule 8). Rejected.

**Rationale:** Option C is the best fit for this brownfield repo: the helper is the minimum code that makes the status contract testable and unforgeable, everything a maintainer would plausibly tune stays in a skill file, and it needs no new dependency, provider or config knob.
Satisfies: REQ-002
PRD ACs: AC-002-1, AC-002-2, AC-002-3
Target File: 
Actions:

Implementation AC:
- [ ] Given a resolvable base and head, when `resolveReviewScope` runs, then it returns `baseSha`, `headSha` and `range = baseSha..headSha` and nothing else is reviewable
- [ ] Given the base SHA or merge-base cannot be established, when it runs, then it returns `ok:false`, `status:'REVIEW_BLOCKED'` and `missing[]` naming each absent input, and never substitutes a guessed base
- [ ] Given a stacked phase whose base is the parent phase branch tip, when it runs, then `range` starts at that parent tip so later phases and the base's own commits are excluded

title: [trd:trd-2026-70e784f2-code-review-process:task:TRD-025] - [ ] **TRD-025** Merge gate with answered findings and security lane (`pr-review-gate.js`) (7h)
description:
## Task: TRD-025
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-70e784f2-code-review-process.md#trd-025
PRD Reference: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-70e784f2-code-review-process.md#req-008

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-008**: Every finding is answered before merge (Must)
Every finding is answered before merge (Must) An Important finding must be fixed or resolved with a stated reason before the PR can merge. Convergence

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-008-1: Given an Important finding is open | When merge is attempted | Then it is refused and names the open finding
- AC-008-4: Given a finding is Nit or Pre-existing | When merge is attempted | Then it does not block
- AC-017-1: Given a PR is reviewed | When the security review finds an issue | Then merge is blocked until it is fixed or closed with a stated reason
- AC-017-2: Given a later commit fixes the issue | When re-review runs | Then the security finding clears on its own
- AC-017-3: Given a security finding is a false positive | When the author closes it with a reason | Then the reason is recorded in the ledger
- AC-002-3: Given a PR description is missing any of the three sections | When its review status is computed | Then the PR is reported as not ready for approval and names the missing section

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen approach (Option C):** extend the pattern TRD-2026-82b6a138 established: **editable behavior in skills, agents and markdown; a small set of pure, deterministic libraries for what must not be self-certified by a model.**

description:
## Test Task: TRD-030-TEST
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-b6db9749-behavior-habits-runtime.md#trd-030-test
PRD Reference: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-b6db9749-behavior-habits-runtime.md#req-026

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-026**: Ensemble never asserts Foreman commitment from a local result alone
Ensemble never asserts Foreman commitment from a local result alone Priority: Must Feature Area 10: Extensibility Proof

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-026-1: Given a local tool or transport call returns success | When reported | Then this is never represented as "committed by Foreman" absent a Foreman-sourced confirmation

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen: Option B — dedicated adapter modules per new trigger-source type, plus a shared notification-state module.** Unchanged from 1.0.0.

New `file-source-adapter.ts` and `release-source-adapter.ts` under `packages/agent-core/src/behavior/` each produce a `BehaviorEvent` through `normalizeEvent`, mirroring the existing `pi-events.ts` → `event-translator.ts` → `normalizeEvent` → `LocalEventMatcher` chain. A new `notification-state.ts` in `pi-extension` centralises busy, duplicate and stale tracking for every behavior. Package quarantine gets its own `package-quarantine.ts` beside `package-discovery.ts`.

### Decisions added in 1.1.0

1. **How artifact changes are detected: content hashes checked at lifecycle points.** No `fs.watch`, no new dependency.
   - The adapter derives its watch set from the compiled `artifact.changed` triggers (the `path` predicate).
   - It hashes those files at `tool_result` and at `agent_end`, and emits an event when a digest differs from the last one seen in the session.
   - The hooks it relies on already exist, which is what AC-001-2 means by "supported host API".
   - It behaves the same on every OS (see REQ-023).
   - It needs no new dependency, which constitution §4 would require approval for.

   | Option | Why not chosen |
   |---|---|
   | `fs.watch` | Event semantics differ between macOS, Linux and Windows (rename-vs-change, recursive support). That is exactly the kind of per-platform behavior difference REQ-023 forbids absorbing silently. It also keeps a handle open for the whole session. |
   | `chokidar` | A new runtime dependency (constitution §4), for a problem that lifecycle-point hashing already solves. |

   The limitation, stated rather than hidden: a change is seen at the next tool call or at the end of the run, not instantly. NFR-001 measures from event validation, so this latency is outside its budget. TRD-003 reports it separately.

2. **Release signal (resolves the PRD's REQ-002 clarification): a new `v*` tag in local refs.** This matches this repo's `release.yml` (`on: push: tags: ['v*']`).
   - The tag pattern is a trigger predicate, so repositories with different conventions change configuration, not code (Rule 8).
   - It is detected two ways. First, from a successful tag-creating tool call (`git tag`, `gh release create`), in the same way `repository.changed` is derived today. Second, by diffing tag refs at session start and at `agent_end`, which covers tags that arrive by fetch.
   - It emits the **existing** catalog type `release.completed`, carrying `{ tag, sha, source }`.
   - One tag produces one event per session, whichever path sees it first.

3. **Coverage metric (resolves the PRD's REQ-016 clarification): Jest `json-summary` output, per file, `lines.pct` and `branches.pct` by default.**
   - Each package's `test:coverage` is `jest --coverage`. Jest's default reporters (`json`, `lcov`, `text`, `clover`) produce raw maps, not percentages.
   - So the behavior watches `coverage/coverage-summary.json`, and its README tells repositories to enable `json-summary`.
   - The metrics and the threshold (default 1.0 percentage point) are behavior configuration.
   - If the artifact never appears, the behavior shows up as an inert trigger in `/ensemble-status`; it is never silently idle.
   - The baseline is the previous snapshot seen **in the same session** (Rule 4). The first observation in a session only sets the baseline.

4. **The comparison is a generic command: `artifact.compare` (TRD-033).** It compares numeric JSON paths between the previous and current snapshot of an artifact and knows nothing about coverage.
   - The alternatives were rejected. Doing the comparison in an agent step would make the reported delta an unverified model claim (REQ-012). A coverage-specific command would make the third behavior need Ensemble code (REQ-018).
   - It lands in PR 1, which is why PR 5 can be configuration only.

5. **Notification transport** (REQ-009, REQ-010). `notification-state.ts` delivers to two sinks:
   - **The user**, through `SessionUiBridge.notify`, a new method that wraps `ctx.ui.notify`. Headless sessions fall back to the console.
   - **The model's context**, through `pi.sendMessage` with `display: true` and `triggerTurn: false`.

   `triggerTurn: false` is deliberate. #107 deleted the continuation path because a message that makes the agent act bypasses `MutationGuard` (`extension.ts:118-140`); a notification is data, never an instruction. Any test-derived text in a notification is fenced and labelled as data, a lesson from #94's live runs. `sendMessage` is added to `assertRequiredCapabilities`.

6. **Verified fix application** (REQ-033). This is configuration plus two small code changes.
   - A new behavior, `apply-verified-fix`, runs `mode: auto`. It triggers on `fix.verified` with the predicate `verdict: passed`, declares only `fix.apply` with no tools, and calls `fix.apply { proposalRef: ${event.payload.proposalRef} }`.
   - `CommandRegistry` then asks `ApprovalGate`. Today the prompt is only `descriptor.description` ("Apply a verified fix proposal…"), so the human would approve without seeing what changes. Code change 1 (TRD-019): the prompt names the proposal, its files and a diff summary.
   - `commit-policy.ts` has no importers today. Code change 2 (TRD-021): wire it in so an applied fix is committed with attribution.

### Alternatives considered (architecture)

| Option | Summary | Why not chosen |
|---|---|---|
| **A — Widen the existing translator, inline notification** | Add file and release branches inside `event-translator.ts`; keep notification-state logic at each `ctx.ui.notify` call site. | `event-translator.ts` would cover three unrelated source domains. Busy/duplicate/stale logic would be copied per behavior, which is the per-reaction duplication the PRD sets out to remove. |
| **B — Dedicated adapter modules + shared notification-state module** *(chosen)* | One adapter module per source type, all feeding the same ingress; one shared notification-state module. | Matches the existing boundary (`agent-core` = provider-neutral logic, `pi-extension` = host wiring), and centralises notification state once. |
| **C — Single generic "external signal" adapter** | One configurable "watch path X for condition Y" abstraction for both sources. | Risks becoming an arbitrary-condition escape hatch around the closed, versioned catalog (REQ-CQRS-005); still duplicates notification state. |

title: fix sandbox dies on any untracked symlink, silently disabling the whole governed path
description:
OBSERVED LIVE, twice, in an rpc-ui session against a trial repo.

createFixSandbox() mirrors untracked-but-not-ignored files into the throwaway worktree with copyFileSync. git ls-files --others reports a SYMLINKED DIRECTORY as a single entry, and copyFileSync on it throws:

  ENOTSUP: operation not supported on socket,
  copyfile '/tmp/loop-trial-run/node_modules' -> '<sandbox>/work/node_modules'

The throw is caught by the blanket try/catch at fix-sandbox.ts:116, which returns undefined. agent-fix-provider then fails CLOSED (correctly, by design) and returns no candidate. behavior-runner records:

  note: 'no fix candidate offered'
  constitution: { status: 'none', detail: 'rule provider ran and implied no constitution change' }

CONSEQUENCE. This is the whole product failing, not a corner. With no fix candidate the governed path has nothing to verify, so the constitution provider is handed nothing to reason about and reports 'none'. The amendment step -- the feature the runtime exists for -- can never fire. The fix still LANDS, because the continuation path repairs the code independently, so the session looks successful. Two live runs both showed a repaired src/math.js, a passing verification, and no constitution change.

TIMING TELL. The invocation returns in 65-67ms. The fix agent child takes ~15s when it actually runs (measured). Anything in the tens of milliseconds means the model was never called.

node_modules as a symlink is not exotic -- it is what workspace/monorepo setups produce, and what this project's own worktree instructions create.

TWO DEFECTS, FIX BOTH:

1. The copy loop must handle symlinks (recreate with symlinkSync(readlinkSync(from))) rather than copyFileSync, and one uncopyable entry must not abandon the entire sandbox. node_modules specifically is already handled by linkNodeModules(), so copying it is redundant as well as fatal.

2. The failure is INVISIBLE. fix-sandbox returns undefined with no reason and the provider's catch returns undefined with no reason, so the log says 'no fix candidate offered' -- which reads as 'the model had no idea', not 'the harness broke before the model was asked'. Record the cause. This is the same class as br-zcxb: a step that cannot run reports the same thing as a step that ran and found nothing.

title: Fix sandbox symlinks node_modules, so writes through it reach the live tree
description:
Residual gap in the br-r3om containment fix (b59d2bf).

createFixSandbox() symlinks node_modules into the disposable worktree rather
than copying it. A child that writes THROUGH that path -- npm install, or
writing into a package directory -- reaches the live tree's dependencies.

Why it was built that way: copying node_modules per fix run is slow enough to
make autofix unusable, and node_modules is not a protected path, so the threat
the bead was about (source and guardrail writes) is contained regardless.

What this bead is really for: the CLAIM. "The child cannot modify the live
working tree" is wider than what is true. The accurate claim is "cannot modify

description:
## Test Task: TRD-029-TEST
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-b6db9749-behavior-habits-runtime.md#trd-029-test
PRD Reference: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-b6db9749-behavior-habits-runtime.md#req-027

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-027**: At least three reference behaviors run end-to-end with zero unapproved mutations
At least three reference behaviors run end-to-end with zero unapproved mutations Priority: Must

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-027-1: Given test-failure monitoring | When all three are exercised in a real session | Then each completes its documented flow with no mutation outside an explicitly approved path

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen: Option B — dedicated adapter modules per new trigger-source type, plus a shared notification-state module.** Unchanged from 1.0.0.

New `file-source-adapter.ts` and `release-source-adapter.ts` under `packages/agent-core/src/behavior/` each produce a `BehaviorEvent` through `normalizeEvent`, mirroring the existing `pi-events.ts` → `event-translator.ts` → `normalizeEvent` → `LocalEventMatcher` chain. A new `notification-state.ts` in `pi-extension` centralises busy, duplicate and stale tracking for every behavior. Package quarantine gets its own `package-quarantine.ts` beside `package-discovery.ts`.

### Decisions added in 1.1.0

1. **How artifact changes are detected: content hashes checked at lifecycle points.** No `fs.watch`, no new dependency.
   - The adapter derives its watch set from the compiled `artifact.changed` triggers (the `path` predicate).
   - It hashes those files at `tool_result` and at `agent_end`, and emits an event when a digest differs from the last one seen in the session.
   - The hooks it relies on already exist, which is what AC-001-2 means by "supported host API".
   - It behaves the same on every OS (see REQ-023).
   - It needs no new dependency, which constitution §4 would require approval for.

   | Option | Why not chosen |
   |---|---|
   | `fs.watch` | Event semantics differ between macOS, Linux and Windows (rename-vs-change, recursive support). That is exactly the kind of per-platform behavior difference REQ-023 forbids absorbing silently. It also keeps a handle open for the whole session. |
   | `chokidar` | A new runtime dependency (constitution §4), for a problem that lifecycle-point hashing already solves. |

   The limitation, stated rather than hidden: a change is seen at the next tool call or at the end of the run, not instantly. NFR-001 measures from event validation, so this latency is outside its budget. TRD-003 reports it separately.

2. **Release signal (resolves the PRD's REQ-002 clarification): a new `v*` tag in local refs.** This matches this repo's `release.yml` (`on: push: tags: ['v*']`).
   - The tag pattern is a trigger predicate, so repositories with different conventions change configuration, not code (Rule 8).
   - It is detected two ways. First, from a successful tag-creating tool call (`git tag`, `gh release create`), in the same way `repository.changed` is derived today. Second, by diffing tag refs at session start and at `agent_end`, which covers tags that arrive by fetch.
   - It emits the **existing** catalog type `release.completed`, carrying `{ tag, sha, source }`.
   - One tag produces one event per session, whichever path sees it first.

3. **Coverage metric (resolves the PRD's REQ-016 clarification): Jest `json-summary` output, per file, `lines.pct` and `branches.pct` by default.**
   - Each package's `test:coverage` is `jest --coverage`. Jest's default reporters (`json`, `lcov`, `text`, `clover`) produce raw maps, not percentages.
   - So the behavior watches `coverage/coverage-summary.json`, and its README tells repositories to enable `json-summary`.
   - The metrics and the threshold (default 1.0 percentage point) are behavior configuration.
   - If the artifact never appears, the behavior shows up as an inert trigger in `/ensemble-status`; it is never silently idle.
   - The baseline is the previous snapshot seen **in the same session** (Rule 4). The first observation in a session only sets the baseline.

4. **The comparison is a generic command: `artifact.compare` (TRD-033).** It compares numeric JSON paths between the previous and current snapshot of an artifact and knows nothing about coverage.
   - The alternatives were rejected. Doing the comparison in an agent step would make the reported delta an unverified model claim (REQ-012). A coverage-specific command would make the third behavior need Ensemble code (REQ-018).
   - It lands in PR 1, which is why PR 5 can be configuration only.

5. **Notification transport** (REQ-009, REQ-010). `notification-state.ts` delivers to two sinks:
   - **The user**, through `SessionUiBridge.notify`, a new method that wraps `ctx.ui.notify`. Headless sessions fall back to the console.
   - **The model's context**, through `pi.sendMessage` with `display: true` and `triggerTurn: false`.

   `triggerTurn: false` is deliberate. #107 deleted the continuation path because a message that makes the agent act bypasses `MutationGuard` (`extension.ts:118-140`); a notification is data, never an instruction. Any test-derived text in a notification is fenced and labelled as data, a lesson from #94's live runs. `sendMessage` is added to `assertRequiredCapabilities`.

6. **Verified fix application** (REQ-033). This is configuration plus two small code changes.
   - A new behavior, `apply-verified-fix`, runs `mode: auto`. It triggers on `fix.verified` with the predicate `verdict: passed`, declares only `fix.apply` with no tools, and calls `fix.apply { proposalRef: ${event.payload.proposalRef} }`.
   - `CommandRegistry` then asks `ApprovalGate`. Today the prompt is only `descriptor.description` ("Apply a verified fix proposal…"), so the human would approve without seeing what changes. Code change 1 (TRD-019): the prompt names the proposal, its files and a diff summary.
   - `commit-policy.ts` has no importers today. Code change 2 (TRD-021): wire it in so an applied fix is committed with attribution.

### Alternatives considered (architecture)

| Option | Summary | Why not chosen |
|---|---|---|
| **A — Widen the existing translator, inline notification** | Add file and release branches inside `event-translator.ts`; keep notification-state logic at each `ctx.ui.notify` call site. | `event-translator.ts` would cover three unrelated source domains. Busy/duplicate/stale logic would be copied per behavior, which is the per-reaction duplication the PRD sets out to remove. |
| **B — Dedicated adapter modules + shared notification-state module** *(chosen)* | One adapter module per source type, all feeding the same ingress; one shared notification-state module. | Matches the existing boundary (`agent-core` = provider-neutral logic, `pi-extension` = host wiring), and centralises notification state once. |
| **C — Single generic "external signal" adapter** | One configurable "watch path X for condition Y" abstraction for both sources. | Risks becoming an arbitrary-condition escape hatch around the closed, versioned catalog (REQ-CQRS-005); still duplicates notification state. |

**Acceptance Criteria:**

| Evals keyed by skill, editable as files | Scenarios are keyed by task, one `scenario.json` each |

Add skill-keyed eval files, arms, repeats, an env allowlist, a results schema, coverage, cache and compare, behind a small runner interface with Claude Code and Pi adapters | **Chosen.** No new dependency (Node built-ins only), builds on tested code, and the eval format stays tool-neutral so an external runner could consume it later |

The PRD's Entry criterion (tool spike, fallback to a minimal in-repo runner) resolves to the fallback: this TRD is that runner, built on the existing harness. title: [trd:trd-2026-70e784f2-code-review-process:task:TRD-003] - [ ] **TRD-003** Applicable review-rules resolver (`pr-review-rules.js`) (3h)
description:
## Task: TRD-003
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-70e784f2-code-review-process.md#trd-003
PRD Reference: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-70e784f2-code-review-process.md#req-001

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-001**: Area-specific review rules (Must)
Area-specific review rules (Must) A repository can state, per area of the code, what matters to a reviewer, in a plain editable file that every review reads.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-001-1: Given a repository contains a review rules file for an area | When a PR touching that area is reviewed | Then the reviewer applies those rules and the review report names which rules file(s) were applied
- AC-001-2: Given a PR touches two areas that each have rules | When it is reviewed | Then both sets of rules apply and the more restrictive instruction wins on conflict
- AC-001-4: Given no rules file exists for an area | When a PR is reviewed | Then review proceeds using repository-wide guidance and the report states that no area-specific rules were found

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen approach (Option C):** extend the pattern TRD-2026-82b6a138 established: **editable behavior in skills, agents and markdown; a small set of pure, deterministic libraries for what must not be self-certified by a model.**

- **User-owned (Constitution Rule 8), prose or data a maintainer edits without a toolchain:** per-area rules (`REVIEW.md` files), the policy block inside the root `REVIEW.md` (round cap, depth table, bot and maintainer logins, sensitive and High paths, Low-waiver state), severity definitions, reviewer, verifier, classifier and security-lane prompts, the PR template, the sweep and explainer procedures. All of it is read from the **target branch**, never from the PR head (REQ-024).
- **Enforcement (Rules 5 and 7), code that grades a model's claim:** vote tally, tier assignment with its sensitive-path floor and Low-waiver evidence, approval evaluation bound to a commit, the merge gate, round-cap derivation, repeat suppression, delta-range selection, depth bounds, slice coverage, metrics and eval scoring. Each is a pure CommonJS module in `packages/development/lib/`, exposed as a JSON-in/JSON-out subcommand of the existing `pr-review-cli.js`, following the 82b6a138 precedent. None performs network I/O or holds a timer.
- **Entry points (Rule 6):** every capability is reached through the one `pr-review-cycle` skill, which `fix-issue`, `implement-trd-beads` and `pr-merge` already invoke or will invoke (a new `MODE=gate` for `pr-merge`). YAML callers reference the skill only, never the CLI, as the existing parity tests require.
- **Recurrence (Rule 4):** nightly or weekly sweeps and daily eval runs are on-demand skills; a workflow template for the host repository is opt-in and scaffolded by init-project. Ensemble's own workflows gain no `schedule` trigger.

**Alternatives considered (user chose C):**

- **Option A -- prose-only skills and agents:** fewest files and fastest to ship. Rejected: the vote threshold, the tier floor, commit-bound approvals and the round cap would be prose a model can misread or skip, so none of these gates could be shown to fail (Rule 7), and "a bot approval never counts" would be a request, not a guarantee.
- **Option B -- a new TypeScript review engine in `agent-core`:** strongest typing and one runtime. Rejected: a new build and `dist` surface and cross-package coupling for a prompt-level feature, editable criteria pulled into code (against Rule 8), and drift toward an ensemble-owned dispatcher that competes with Foreman (Rule 4).

**Rationale:** Option C is the best fit for this brownfield repo. It adds only the code that grades claims, keeps everything a maintainer or adopting team would tune in files they can edit, adds no dependency (Constitution §4) and no CI secret, vendors into Pi automatically through the existing require-closure bundler, and each gate can be mutation-proven using the harness that already exists.

**Decisions taken where the PRD left a choice** (each is editable policy, not a hidden constant):

| Decision | Value | Where it lives |
|---|---|---|
| Policy format | Fenced `ensemble-review-policy` JSON block in the root `REVIEW.md` (no new parser dependency) | REVIEW.md, read from the base commit |
| "Cannot vouch for" a push (AC-010-3, AC-014-2) | Commit is unvouched when its tree differs from the reviewed tree and it is not a remediation commit recorded in the review-state report, or it is a merge commit | `pr-review-scope.js`, `pr-review-approvals.js` |
| Slice threshold for large PRs (AC-018-1) | 1500 changed lines, configurable | policy block |
| Area rules vs policy keys | Policy keys are read from the **root** file only; area files carry guidance, and the more restrictive instruction wins when areas conflict (AC-001-2) | skill prose |
| First PR that introduces REVIEW.md | No base copy exists, so strict defaults apply (Low treated as Medium, cap 3, default sensitive set) | `pr-review-policy.js` |
| Verifier majority | Strict majority of the expected verifier count (2 of 3, 3 of 5) | `pr-review-votes.js` |
Satisfies: REQ-001
PRD ACs: AC-001-1, AC-001-2, AC-001-4
Target File: 
Actions:

Implementation AC:
- [ ] Given changed paths and the list of REVIEW.md files present at the base commit, when `resolveRuleFiles` runs, then each path maps to its nearest ancestor rules file plus the root file, and the union (deduplicated, root first) is returned as `applied[]`
- [ ] Given a PR touching two areas that each have rules, when `resolveRuleFiles` runs, then both files are returned in a stable order so the skill can apply both and let the more restrictive instruction win
- [ ] Given no rules file for an area and no root file, when `resolveRuleFiles` runs, then `applied` is empty and `notes` states that no area-specific rules were found
Dependencies: TRD-001

**Requirement REQ-010**: Generated artifacts match their sources (Must)
Generated artifacts match their sources (Must)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-010-1: Given the edited sources | When `npm run generate` | Then the generated command docs, Pi prompts and Codex skills carry the new behavior in the rendered step text, and `npm run generate:validate` and `npm run validate` pass
- AC-010-2: Given the rendered text carries only a step's `description` and `actions[]` | When rules live in a step's `instructions` | Then they are mirrored into the description or actions so no runtime loses them

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen approach:** a prompt-only change to two YAML command sources. No TypeScript changes.

- `packages/development/commands/new-feature.yaml` gains a boolean `foreman` parameter and one derived variable, `FOREMAN`, defined once in Entry Point Resolution Step 1 and referenced by every later step. Each step that asks the user gets a `FOREMAN == true` branch that takes a deterministic, recorded, non-interactive decision. Each step that dispatches a stage skill appends `--foreman` when `FOREMAN == true`.
- `packages/development/commands/feature.yaml` (the `/ensemble:feature` front door) recognizes `--foreman` as the first token after the keyword and forwards it.
- Generated OMP, Pi and Codex artifacts are regenerated from the repo root, never hand-edited.

**Why prompt-only (Constitution Rule 8):** how a workflow behaves when no one can answer is something a maintainer would plausibly tune (for example, switching the PR gate to park instead of auto-grant). That belongs in the command prose, not in TypeScript. `RunIndexStore` already supports everything needed: `StageOutcome.detail` carries the "granted by `--foreman` policy" record.

**Additive-only edits (found in refinement):** the existing suites (`new-feature-command.test.js`, `feature-command.test.js`, `feature-input-validation-boundary.test.js`, `feature-concurrency-passthrough.test.js`) pin exact sentences in both YAML files, for example "any remaining text is an unsupported flag or argument rejected here". So no pre-existing sentence may be reworded or removed. Foreman behavior is added as new actions or appended sentences, and the existing suites must pass unchanged. For the front door that means: a new action, placed before the validation action, removes a leading `--foreman` token and sets `FOREMAN`, so the pinned validation sentences still read "remaining text" correctly; and a new action, placed after the invocation is constructed, inserts `--foreman` right after `/ensemble:new-feature` in whatever invocation was built.

**Alternatives rejected:**
- *Env-var-only detection (no flag).* Rejected: the maintainer asked for a `--foreman` flag, and the five stage skills already key on that flag.
- *A new RunRecord field `autoGranted`.* Rejected: TypeScript and schema change for information `StageOutcome.detail` already carries.
- *Parking at the approval gates.* Rejected by the maintainer: it stalls every no-user run.

title: Verification re-runs the whole && chain, re-applying the bug it was meant to fix
description:
OBSERVED LIVE 2026-09-25 in this repo, during a user-requested demonstration.

A test was broken by a compound shell command:

  cd packages/agent-core && python3 -c "<edit that introduces the bug>" \
    && sed -n '18,21p' src/behavior/outbox.ts \
    && npx jest 2>&1 | grep -E "Tests:|..."

Detection worked: test.failure.observed fired and a continuation turn was
injected with both behaviors matched.

THE DEFECT: the captured issue command is the ENTIRE compound command,
including the python3 invocation that CAUSED the failure. The runtime log
records it verbatim:

  "issue": "cd /Users/.../agent-core && python3 -c \"\np='src/behavior/outbox.ts'
            ...s.replace(...)...\"\nsed -n '18,21p' ...\nnpx jest ..."

Verification re-runs that exact command. So the sequence is self-defeating:

  1. model repairs the source correctly
  2. verification re-runs the captured command
  3. the python3 step MATCHES AGAIN (the repair restored the original text
     that its .replace() searches for) and re-introduces the bug
  4. jest fails
  5. the correct fix is rolled back as rejected

A correct fix is indistinguishable from no fix, and the rollback destroys it.

WHY IT SLIPPED THROUGH: every prior proof, in the fixture and in this repo,
used a command whose only effect was running tests. The breakage was always
applied in a SEPARATE earlier command. This is the first observation of a
test run chained onto a mutating command in the same invocation -- the normal
shape of a one-liner.

NOT the same as f11da8d, which pinned that the verified command stays RAW and
is never normalized. That decision is about not rewriting the command. This
is about WHICH command gets captured in the first place: the failing test
invocation, not the whole && chain that contained it.

DESIGN QUESTION (do not patch blindly)
Extracting the trailing test invocation from a && chain is the obvious move,
but it is a shell parser, with all the quoting hazards this session already
hit. Alternatives worth weighing first:
  - capture only the segment isTestCommand() actually matched, which is
    already computed during detection
  - refuse to verify (report inconclusive) when the observed command contains
    a mutating segment, rather than re-running something unsafe
  - re-run the declared execution.test_command instead of the observed one
    when they disagree

ACCEPTANCE
- [ ] A test broken and run in ONE compound command is detected, fixed, and
      verified without the verification step re-applying the breakage.
- [ ] Mutation: reverting the fix makes this repro fail again.
- [ ] A verified command is never one with side effects beyond running tests,
      or verification declares itself inconclusive instead of rolling back a
      correct fix.

title: Behavior: check workspace integrity at session start
description:
RECOMMENDATION 5 of 5. Cheap, deterministic, catches latent breakage before it wastes a session.

TRIGGER: runtime.session.started.
ACTION: verify workspace symlinks resolve and the lockfile is coherent with package.json.

EVIDENCE, from this session: the ROOT node_modules/@sunstone-partners/ensemble-agent-core symlink pointed at /tmp/wt-guard/packages/agent-core -- a deleted throwaway worktree. Tests passed anyway because a nested symlink in packages/pi-extension shadowed it, so the breakage was invisible. npm install then rewrote 56 lines of package-lock.json that had drifted. Either would have broken the next contributor or CI, silently, with a confusing error far from the cause.

WORK: one command workspace.check (read-only). No model involvement.
close_reason: workspace.check command + workspace-integrity behavior delivered. Detects dangling workspace symlinks (including the shadowed case that made the original incident invisible) and lockfile drift. Read-only, no model, 20 tests.

comments.author: ldangelo
comments.text:
DELIVERED.

src/workspace/integrity.ts -- two deterministic checks, no model, no network:
1. DANGLING SYMLINKS, with the shadowed case called out separately. That distinction is the whole value: the original incident was a ROOT link to a deleted /tmp worktree that a NESTED link shadowed, so tests passed and every local signal read healthy while the workspace was already broken for anyone else. A shadowed break is strictly more dangerous than an obvious one, and the finding says so in words.
2. LOCKFILE DRIFT -- root dependencies/devDependencies ranges that package-lock.json does not match. Deliberately narrow: it does not re-resolve the tree, because a partial reimplementation of npm would produce false findings and teach people to ignore the check.

REPORTS, NEVER REPAIRS. The remedy is npm install, which is the developer's call; a runtime that silently rewrote a dependency tree would be a worse problem than the one it fixed. A test asserts the link is still there afterwards, and policy mode is propose with a note that auto is a category error here rather than a future upgrade.

COUNTS ARE PART OF THE RESULT (checked.linkCount, checked.lockfile). 'No findings' from a check that examined nothing is the most reassuring possible lie -- and silence is exactly what hid the original breakage.

VERIFIED AGAINST REALITY, not just fixtures: run against this repo it reports 30 links examined, lockfile compared, 0 findings -- consistent with the earlier npm install fix. The detection itself is proven by reconstructing the incident synthetically (root dangling + nested shadowing), not by trusting the clean result.

SIDE EFFECT THAT CLOSES AN OPEN QUESTION IN br-d7lm: this command emits behavior.observation.recorded, which had no producer and no identified consumer. Its disposition moves EMIT -> KEEP, and event-authority.ts gained an entry with authority 'diagnostic' (a report ABOUT the repo, not a fact the runtime caused). Running split is now KEEP 15 / EMIT 8 / LAUNCH-INPUT 25 / REMOVE 6.

title: [trd:trd-2026-d6bbf322-new-feature-workflow:task:TRD-004-TEST] - [ ] **TRD-004-TEST**: Verify exact artifact-reference recording and consumption (3h)
description:
## Test Task: TRD-004-TEST
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-d6bbf322-new-feature-workflow.md#trd-004-test
PRD Reference: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-d6bbf322-new-feature-workflow.md#req-004

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-004**: Bind every stage to explicit, traceable artifacts
Bind every stage to explicit, traceable artifacts Priority: Must | Complexity: High | [RISK: an incorrect artifact association can cause implementation of an unreviewed or unrelated plan]

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-004-1: Given a stage produces or refines an artifact | When its outcome is recorded | Then the run record identifies the exact artifact reference, artifact type, producing stage, and the run to which it belongs
- AC-004-2: Given a later stage requires a PRD | When that stage begins | Then it consumes the exact reference recorded by its prerequisite stage and not a path selected by recency, filename similarity, or conversation context
- AC-004-3: Given a PRD or TRD is revised during its refinement stage | When the revised artifact is accepted | Then the run's current reference is updated while the prior artifact/version remains available for review and recovery

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen: Option C — hardened in-session stage composition with a dedicated atomic run-index store.**

`new-feature` is authored the same way every other product command in this repo is authored: a single orchestrating skill (`packages/development/commands/new-feature.yaml`, generated to runtime-specific prompts exactly like `fix-issue.yaml`) that executes each stage's existing skill body in-session — the same mechanism that loaded `ensemble-refine-prd`'s content into this session and had the agent execute its Phases directly. This is forced, not merely preferred: Pi's `ExtensionAPI` has no completion/invoke primitive that would let an extension programmatically run another skill and get its result back (confirmed — no `pi.invokeCommand` or equivalent exists); the only code-level "run a skill" mechanism, `createAgentPort()`, spawns a bounded, disposable `omp -p --no-session --no-extensions` subprocess in an isolated worktree, and does not fit a long-lived, project-resident workflow whose PRD/TRD stages use the interactive `--collab` review server.

What is new, and is the one piece of real infrastructure this TRD adds: a `RunIndexStore` (`packages/agent-core/src/new-feature/run-index.ts`) built on the one proven concurrency-safe pattern in this repo — `session.js`'s temp-file-then-`renameSync` atomic write plus `expectedRevision`/409-style optimistic concurrency — rather than `ProposalStore`'s plain `writeFileSync` (no atomicity, no lock, not adequate for PRD AC-005-3's fail-closed-on-malformed-index requirement). Runs are stored at `.ensemble/new-feature/<run-id>.json`, mirroring `ProposalStore`'s `.ensemble/proposals/<ref>.json` convention (also excluded from `tree-baseline.ts` drift detection, so this is consistent runtime-owned state, not a project-source mutation).

### Alternatives considered

| Option | Summary | Why not chosen |
|---|---|---|
| A — Plain JSON checkpoint | Same in-session composition, but checkpoints are a single `writeFileSync`, no atomicity/locking. | Fastest to build, but a crash mid-write can corrupt the run index, which directly violates AC-005-3's "fail closed with a recoverable diagnostic" requirement — the repo's own `ProposalStore` already demonstrates this gap is real, not hypothetical. |
| B — Subprocess-dispatched stages | New orchestrator module dispatches every stage as a bounded `createAgentPort()` subprocess; advances the run index only after subprocess exit 0 + artifact-on-disk confirmation. | Most rigorous completion signal (a real process boundary instead of self-reported bookkeeping), but substantially more build effort, and does not fit the interactive `--collab` review-server stages `create-prd`/`refine-prd` already use — those are long-lived, human-attended HTTP sessions, not bounded one-shot subprocess work, and would need bespoke carve-out handling under this option. |
| **C — Hardened in-session composition** *(chosen)* | In-session stage execution (like every existing product command), backed by a dedicated atomic `RunIndexStore`. | Reuses 100% of the existing skill-composition and `ask_user`-approval infrastructure (including the `--collab` review server, which needs no special-casing), while fixing Option A's one real correctness gap with the repo's one proven atomic-write pattern. Matches user-confirmed direction. |

### Honest trust-boundary note

Because stage execution stays in-session (per Option C), the approval gates implemented by TRD-014/TRD-017/TRD-019 are enforced by the orchestrating skill's own conditional logic checking `RunIndexStore`-persisted approval fields before it issues an implementation or `gh pr create` tool call — not by a separate runtime authorization chokepoint like `agent-core`'s `MutationGuard` (which exists elsewhere in this repo, gating CQRS-registered commands, but `new-feature`'s mutating actions are ordinary skill-level tool calls, same as `fix-issue`'s own gated PR-creation step, not CQRS commands). This is the same trust boundary every existing Ensemble product command already operates under. Building a `MutationGuard`-equivalent chokepoint for skill-level tool calls is a materially larger investment this PRD does not request and no other product command has; REQ-014's "runtime authority" is satisfied here by making the check a required precondition over persisted, validated store state rather than over prompt claims — which is what AC-014-2 actually asks for — not by inventing a new enforcement subsystem.
