Read-first: read the TRD, TRD Task section, PRD and PRD Requirement above before any work on this bead.


--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-004**: Required capabilities and documented fallbacks
Required capabilities and documented fallbacks Priority: Must Each command and skill declares the capabilities it requires and which optional ones it can use. When an optional capability is absent from the resolved adapter, the command follows that capability's documented fallback instead of failing or silently skipping. Adapters

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-004-1: Given a command that requires capability X and the resolved adapter lacks X | When the command starts | Then it halts before any side effect and names X and the adapter
- AC-004-2: Given an optional capability absent from the resolved adapter | When the command reaches it | Then the documented fallback runs and the output states that the fallback was used

--- TRD Context ---
### Alternatives Considered

| Option | Approach | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|---|
| A: Prose-only adapters | Adapter is a skill; the agent follows its prose and normalizes tool output itself | Smallest build; fully editable | Cannot route internal CLIs deterministically (REQ-016), cannot validate output (REQ-022), cannot deny at runtime (REQ-023); behavior varies per model |
| **B: Manifest plus runner (chosen)** | Adapter is a skill directory: `SKILL.md` (vocabulary and agent-facing prose) plus a declarative `adapter.yaml` (capability command templates, output mapping, allowlist, health check, detection signals, required env names). A core resolver library and `toolchain-cli` execute capabilities deterministically | Meets PRD (adapter is a skill), Rule 8 (editable without rebuild), Rule 5 (enforcement in code), REQ-016 (CLIs call the same library) | New resolver, runner, manifest schema and output-mapping engine to build and test |
| C: Executable plugin adapters | Separately packaged executables speaking a versioned JSON protocol | Arbitrary logic; strongest isolation | Contradicts the PRD's skills-as-contract decision; fails Rule 8; needs per-OS packaging and a protocol |

**Rationale:** B is the only option that makes every PRD guarantee a code-enforced property while keeping adapters user-editable data. The requester selected B at the architecture gate.

### Interpretations and Resolved Design Issues

- **I1: plain version control.** The PRD taxonomy has no plain `git` category, yet about 45 sources invoke it. Plain `git` operations (status, commit, push, log, diff, merge-base) are `vcs.*` capabilities of the `workflow` category, whose default adapter is `plain-git`; the `git-town` adapter extends it. Recommend a PRD refine pass to name this explicitly.
- **I2: ambiguity versus no signal (PRD REQ-009 AC-2 vs REQ-010 AC-2).** "No detectable signal" means no signal source exists at all (no remote, no marker files); the shipped default is used. "Ambiguous" means two or more installed adapters match, or a signal source exists (for example a remote URL) but matches no installed adapter; resolution fails explicitly in non-interactive runs and asks in interactive runs.
- **I3: AC-023-2 (governed boundary denies).** The runner is invoked through the shell tool, so a command that was not granted the shell tool cannot run any adapter; an adapter therefore cannot widen grants. The runner additionally denies any command outside the adapter's binary-plus-subcommand allowlist. Denial of raw shell commands typed by an agent outside the runner remains host-enforced (hooks on Claude Code; none in this repo for Pi, OpenCode or Codex); the lint (REQ-019) keeps commands from issuing raw tool calls. This residual is recorded in the Threat Model.
- **I4: confirmation session identity.** No stable session id is exposed uniformly across runtimes. TRD-017 begins with a spike that records which id each runtime exposes (`ENSEMBLE_SESSION_ID`, host session variables); the passive confirmation record is keyed by `(sessionKey, category, adapter, configHash)` and falls back to the run id when no session id exists.
- **I5: repo-local adapters are untrusted by default.** A cloned repository can ship `.ensemble/adapters/`. Repo-local adapters resolve in every mode (satisfying AC-007-3) but a non-interactive run additionally requires the adapter name in the user's `trustedRepoAdapters` list; an interactive run shows the adapter's allowlist at first-use confirmation.
- **I6: no new runtime dependency.** The output-mapping engine uses a small dotted-path projection (`$.a.b[0]`, `|` alternation for "array or object"), not a JSONPath library, because constitution section 4 requires approval for new dependencies.
- **I7: work-graph selection.** `work-graph` is its own category with default `auto`: use the work-graph capabilities of the resolved tracker adapter when its manifest provides them; otherwise use the built-in `work-graph-links-fallback` adapter (tracker dependency links, then plan order stated as not dependency-aware). One manifest may implement several categories.
- **I8: PRD BDD floor.** Fourteen PRD requirements (REQ-001, 002, 004, 005, 006, 009, 010, 012, 015, 018, 021, 022, 024, 025) have two ACs, below the command's three-scenario floor. The test tasks specify exactly one scenario per AC; recommend a PRD refine pass to add edge or error ACs.
- **I10: packaging.** `packages/development` depends only on `js-yaml` and its libraries require only siblings, so the resolver library, category contracts, default selection, schemas and tool inventory all ship inside `packages/development` (`lib/toolchain/` and `toolchain/`). A standalone plugin install and the Pi vendor bundle therefore contain everything; other packages call `toolchain-cli` through `TOOLCHAIN_CLI` rather than importing it.
- **I9: preflight is enforced in code.** `toolchain-cli run` refuses a side-effecting capability unless a passing preflight record exists for the supplied `--run-id`; the command prose cannot silently skip preflight.

Read-first: read the TRD, TRD Task section, PRD and PRD Requirement above before any work on this bead.


--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-018**: Other categories registered with default adapters only
Other categories registered with default adapters only Priority: Must In the first release, categories other than tracker and source-control host ship the taxonomy entry, contract and default adapter only. Alternatives for them are added later as additive releases.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-018-1: Given the first release | When the categories other than tracker and host are inspected | Then each has a contract and a default adapter and no alternative adapter
- AC-018-2: Given a user selecting an unshipped alternative for such a category | When resolved | Then resolution fails naming the category and the available adapters

--- TRD Context ---
### Alternatives Considered

| Option | Approach | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|---|
| A: Prose-only adapters | Adapter is a skill; the agent follows its prose and normalizes tool output itself | Smallest build; fully editable | Cannot route internal CLIs deterministically (REQ-016), cannot validate output (REQ-022), cannot deny at runtime (REQ-023); behavior varies per model |
| **B: Manifest plus runner (chosen)** | Adapter is a skill directory: `SKILL.md` (vocabulary and agent-facing prose) plus a declarative `adapter.yaml` (capability command templates, output mapping, allowlist, health check, detection signals, required env names). A core resolver library and `toolchain-cli` execute capabilities deterministically | Meets PRD (adapter is a skill), Rule 8 (editable without rebuild), Rule 5 (enforcement in code), REQ-016 (CLIs call the same library) | New resolver, runner, manifest schema and output-mapping engine to build and test |
| C: Executable plugin adapters | Separately packaged executables speaking a versioned JSON protocol | Arbitrary logic; strongest isolation | Contradicts the PRD's skills-as-contract decision; fails Rule 8; needs per-OS packaging and a protocol |

**Rationale:** B is the only option that makes every PRD guarantee a code-enforced property while keeping adapters user-editable data. The requester selected B at the architecture gate.

### Interpretations and Resolved Design Issues

- **I1: plain version control.** The PRD taxonomy has no plain `git` category, yet about 45 sources invoke it. Plain `git` operations (status, commit, push, log, diff, merge-base) are `vcs.*` capabilities of the `workflow` category, whose default adapter is `plain-git`; the `git-town` adapter extends it. Recommend a PRD refine pass to name this explicitly.
- **I2: ambiguity versus no signal (PRD REQ-009 AC-2 vs REQ-010 AC-2).** "No detectable signal" means no signal source exists at all (no remote, no marker files); the shipped default is used. "Ambiguous" means two or more installed adapters match, or a signal source exists (for example a remote URL) but matches no installed adapter; resolution fails explicitly in non-interactive runs and asks in interactive runs.
- **I3: AC-023-2 (governed boundary denies).** The runner is invoked through the shell tool, so a command that was not granted the shell tool cannot run any adapter; an adapter therefore cannot widen grants. The runner additionally denies any command outside the adapter's binary-plus-subcommand allowlist. Denial of raw shell commands typed by an agent outside the runner remains host-enforced (hooks on Claude Code; none in this repo for Pi, OpenCode or Codex); the lint (REQ-019) keeps commands from issuing raw tool calls. This residual is recorded in the Threat Model.
- **I4: confirmation session identity.** No stable session id is exposed uniformly across runtimes. TRD-017 begins with a spike that records which id each runtime exposes (`ENSEMBLE_SESSION_ID`, host session variables); the passive confirmation record is keyed by `(sessionKey, category, adapter, configHash)` and falls back to the run id when no session id exists.
- **I5: repo-local adapters are untrusted by default.** A cloned repository can ship `.ensemble/adapters/`. Repo-local adapters resolve in every mode (satisfying AC-007-3) but a non-interactive run additionally requires the adapter name in the user's `trustedRepoAdapters` list; an interactive run shows the adapter's allowlist at first-use confirmation.
- **I6: no new runtime dependency.** The output-mapping engine uses a small dotted-path projection (`$.a.b[0]`, `|` alternation for "array or object"), not a JSONPath library, because constitution section 4 requires approval for new dependencies.
- **I7: work-graph selection.** `work-graph` is its own category with default `auto`: use the work-graph capabilities of the resolved tracker adapter when its manifest provides them; otherwise use the built-in `work-graph-links-fallback` adapter (tracker dependency links, then plan order stated as not dependency-aware). One manifest may implement several categories.
- **I8: PRD BDD floor.** Fourteen PRD requirements (REQ-001, 002, 004, 005, 006, 009, 010, 012, 015, 018, 021, 022, 024, 025) have two ACs, below the command's three-scenario floor. The test tasks specify exactly one scenario per AC; recommend a PRD refine pass to add edge or error ACs.
- **I10: packaging.** `packages/development` depends only on `js-yaml` and its libraries require only siblings, so the resolver library, category contracts, default selection, schemas and tool inventory all ship inside `packages/development` (`lib/toolchain/` and `toolchain/`). A standalone plugin install and the Pi vendor bundle therefore contain everything; other packages call `toolchain-cli` through `TOOLCHAIN_CLI` rather than importing it.
- **I9: preflight is enforced in code.** `toolchain-cli run` refuses a side-effecting capability unless a passing preflight record exists for the supplied `--run-id`; the command prose cannot silently skip preflight.

title: [trd:trd-2026-d6bbf322-new-feature-workflow:task:TRD-015-TEST] - [ ] **TRD-015-TEST**: Verify material-change detection clears stale approval (2h)
description:
## Test Task: TRD-015-TEST
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-d6bbf322-new-feature-workflow.md#trd-015-test
PRD Reference: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-d6bbf322-new-feature-workflow.md#req-010

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-010**: Require explicit user approval before implementation
Require explicit user approval before implementation Priority: Must | Complexity: Medium

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-010-3: Given implementation is approved | When the workflow begins implementation | Then the approval applies only to the presented plan and any material change to that plan returns to the approval checkpoint

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen: Option C — hardened in-session stage composition with a dedicated atomic run-index store.**

`new-feature` is authored the same way every other product command in this repo is authored: a single orchestrating skill (`packages/development/commands/new-feature.yaml`, generated to runtime-specific prompts exactly like `fix-issue.yaml`) that executes each stage's existing skill body in-session — the same mechanism that loaded `ensemble-refine-prd`'s content into this session and had the agent execute its Phases directly. This is forced, not merely preferred: Pi's `ExtensionAPI` has no completion/invoke primitive that would let an extension programmatically run another skill and get its result back (confirmed — no `pi.invokeCommand` or equivalent exists); the only code-level "run a skill" mechanism, `createAgentPort()`, spawns a bounded, disposable `omp -p --no-session --no-extensions` subprocess in an isolated worktree, and does not fit a long-lived, project-resident workflow whose PRD/TRD stages use the interactive `--collab` review server.

What is new, and is the one piece of real infrastructure this TRD adds: a `RunIndexStore` (`packages/agent-core/src/new-feature/run-index.ts`) built on the one proven concurrency-safe pattern in this repo — `session.js`'s temp-file-then-`renameSync` atomic write plus `expectedRevision`/409-style optimistic concurrency — rather than `ProposalStore`'s plain `writeFileSync` (no atomicity, no lock, not adequate for PRD AC-005-3's fail-closed-on-malformed-index requirement). Runs are stored at `.ensemble/new-feature/<run-id>.json`, mirroring `ProposalStore`'s `.ensemble/proposals/<ref>.json` convention (also excluded from `tree-baseline.ts` drift detection, so this is consistent runtime-owned state, not a project-source mutation).

### Alternatives considered

| Option | Summary | Why not chosen |
|---|---|---|
| A — Plain JSON checkpoint | Same in-session composition, but checkpoints are a single `writeFileSync`, no atomicity/locking. | Fastest to build, but a crash mid-write can corrupt the run index, which directly violates AC-005-3's "fail closed with a recoverable diagnostic" requirement — the repo's own `ProposalStore` already demonstrates this gap is real, not hypothetical. |
| B — Subprocess-dispatched stages | New orchestrator module dispatches every stage as a bounded `createAgentPort()` subprocess; advances the run index only after subprocess exit 0 + artifact-on-disk confirmation. | Most rigorous completion signal (a real process boundary instead of self-reported bookkeeping), but substantially more build effort, and does not fit the interactive `--collab` review-server stages `create-prd`/`refine-prd` already use — those are long-lived, human-attended HTTP sessions, not bounded one-shot subprocess work, and would need bespoke carve-out handling under this option. |
| **C — Hardened in-session composition** *(chosen)* | In-session stage execution (like every existing product command), backed by a dedicated atomic `RunIndexStore`. | Reuses 100% of the existing skill-composition and `ask_user`-approval infrastructure (including the `--collab` review server, which needs no special-casing), while fixing Option A's one real correctness gap with the repo's one proven atomic-write pattern. Matches user-confirmed direction. |

### Honest trust-boundary note

Because stage execution stays in-session (per Option C), the approval gates implemented by TRD-014/TRD-017/TRD-019 are enforced by the orchestrating skill's own conditional logic checking `RunIndexStore`-persisted approval fields before it issues an implementation or `gh pr create` tool call — not by a separate runtime authorization chokepoint like `agent-core`'s `MutationGuard` (which exists elsewhere in this repo, gating CQRS-registered commands, but `new-feature`'s mutating actions are ordinary skill-level tool calls, same as `fix-issue`'s own gated PR-creation step, not CQRS commands). This is the same trust boundary every existing Ensemble product command already operates under. Building a `MutationGuard`-equivalent chokepoint for skill-level tool calls is a materially larger investment this PRD does not request and no other product command has; REQ-014's "runtime authority" is satisfied here by making the check a required precondition over persisted, validated store state rather than over prompt claims — which is what AC-014-2 actually asks for — not by inventing a new enforcement subsystem.

**Chosen approach (Option C):** One shared, prose-defined review procedure plus a small deterministic helper library.

title: [trd:trd-2026-15aa5acd-live-behavior-dispatch-autofix:task:TRD-018] - [ ] **TRD-018** Implement the proposal-artifact path used by `mode: propose` (4h)
description:
## Task: TRD-018
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-15aa5acd-live-behavior-dispatch-autofix.md#trd-018
PRD Reference: #req-004

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen: Option C — single enforcement seam, additive.**

A new `MutationGuard` chokepoint in `agent-core` is the one place `policy.mode`, `capabilities.mutation_classes` (via the existing `hasMutationAuthority()`), and protected-path rules are resolved. It is wired once at the loader boundary rather than replicated per tool registration. The translator, matcher, and auto-fix loop are added to `pi-extension`. Discovery roots and `execution.test_command` are additive changes to existing schema/discovery code. `ToolRegistry`, `outbox`, and the compiler are reused unchanged.

### Alternatives considered

| Option | Summary | Why not chosen |
|---|---|---|
| **A — In-place extension** | Enforce mode/mutation/path rules as wrapper checks inside `behavior-loader`'s per-tool `execute()` closures. | Enforcement scattered across call sites; every future tool registration must remember to wrap. The PRD's central failure mode is *guarantees that exist in one place but are not reached from another* — Option A reproduces exactly that shape. |
| **B — Governance kernel** | Route every mutation through a `MutationBroker` + `GovernedWorkspace` in `agent-core`; `pi-extension` becomes a thin adapter. | Strongest long-term design and the right eventual target, but it re-opens already-shipped code across every tool path for a ~6-7 PR refactor before a single PRD requirement is demonstrable. Deferred deliberately, not rejected. |
| **C — Single enforcement seam** *(chosen)* | One `MutationGuard` chokepoint, wired once; everything else additive. | Gets a single auditable chokepoint (Option B's main benefit) without Option B's refactor surface. Fits the existing `agent-core` / `pi-extension` split. |

### Architectural note carried from grounding

Two defects found while grounding this design are folded into PR 1 rather than left implicit:

1. `pi-events.ts` emits `runtime.tool_result` / `runtime.tool.called` / `runtime.tool.failed` / `runtime.tool.completed`, none of which appear in `HARNESS_EVENT_TYPES` (which defines `runtime.tool_call.started` / `runtime.tool_call.completed`). `normalizeEvent` does not currently reject uncatalogued types, so PRD AC-002-1's "validated against the closed catalog" would be vacuous. Addressed by TRD-001 (`[satisfies INFRA]`).
2. `behavior-loader.ts:79` calls `registry.grant(...)` unconditionally immediately before `registry.invoke(...)`, making the grant boundary a rubber stamp for behavior-governed tools (unlike the echo path, where the grant is CLI-flag-gated). Addressed by TRD-003.
Satisfies: REQ-004
PRD ACs: AC-004-1

Implementation AC:
- [ ] Given `mode: propose` and an attempted write, when the behavior completes, then a proposal artifact exists and the target file is unmodified.

description:
## Task: TRD-027
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-70e784f2-code-review-process.md#trd-027
PRD Reference: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-70e784f2-code-review-process.md#req-012

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-012**: Change-driven risk tier (Must) [RISK: a mislabelled tier merges risky code with too little human review]
Change-driven risk tier (Must) [RISK: a mislabelled tier merges risky code with too little human review] Each PR is assigned a Low, Medium or High risk tier from the change itself, not from who wrote it.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-012-3: Given a second assessment indicates a Low or Medium PR nonetheless needs another person | When it is evaluated | Then the tier is raised
- AC-013-2: Given an agent or the author proposes a tier | When it is lower than the assigned tier | Then it is ignored; only a code owner can lower a tier
- AC-014-3: Given an agent authored a PR on a person's instruction | When approvals are counted | Then that person counts as one of the required reviewers, as if they had written the code themselves
- AC-017-1: Given a PR is reviewed | When the security review finds an issue | Then merge is blocked until it is fixed or closed with a stated reason
- AC-008-1: Given an Important finding is open | When merge is attempted | Then it is refused and names the open finding

--- TRD Context ---

title: [trd:trd-2026-d6bbf322-new-feature-workflow:task:TRD-017-TEST] - [ ] **TRD-017-TEST**: Verify PR opt-in, separate approval, and unavailable-provider handling (4h)
description:
## Test Task: TRD-017-TEST
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-d6bbf322-new-feature-workflow.md#trd-017-test
PRD Reference: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-d6bbf322-new-feature-workflow.md#req-011

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-011**: Make PR creation optional and separately approved
Make PR creation optional and separately approved Priority: Must | Complexity: High | [RISK: opening a PR is an externally visible write and may notify collaborators] Product Entry, Safety, and Compatibility

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-011-1: Given all required implementation work is reported complete | When the user chooses not to create a PR | Then the workflow records completion without making a PR-hosting service write
- AC-011-2: Given the user requests PR creation and a supported PR-creation capability is configured | When the workflow is ready to create the PR | Then it presents the target repository/branch and proposed title/body and obtains a separate, immediate explicit approval before the external create operation
- AC-011-3: Given PR approval is absent | When the workflow reaches this optional stage | Then it creates no PR, reports the outcome, and preserves the completed implementation record

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen: Option C — hardened in-session stage composition with a dedicated atomic run-index store.**

`new-feature` is authored the same way every other product command in this repo is authored: a single orchestrating skill (`packages/development/commands/new-feature.yaml`, generated to runtime-specific prompts exactly like `fix-issue.yaml`) that executes each stage's existing skill body in-session — the same mechanism that loaded `ensemble-refine-prd`'s content into this session and had the agent execute its Phases directly. This is forced, not merely preferred: Pi's `ExtensionAPI` has no completion/invoke primitive that would let an extension programmatically run another skill and get its result back (confirmed — no `pi.invokeCommand` or equivalent exists); the only code-level "run a skill" mechanism, `createAgentPort()`, spawns a bounded, disposable `omp -p --no-session --no-extensions` subprocess in an isolated worktree, and does not fit a long-lived, project-resident workflow whose PRD/TRD stages use the interactive `--collab` review server.

What is new, and is the one piece of real infrastructure this TRD adds: a `RunIndexStore` (`packages/agent-core/src/new-feature/run-index.ts`) built on the one proven concurrency-safe pattern in this repo — `session.js`'s temp-file-then-`renameSync` atomic write plus `expectedRevision`/409-style optimistic concurrency — rather than `ProposalStore`'s plain `writeFileSync` (no atomicity, no lock, not adequate for PRD AC-005-3's fail-closed-on-malformed-index requirement). Runs are stored at `.ensemble/new-feature/<run-id>.json`, mirroring `ProposalStore`'s `.ensemble/proposals/<ref>.json` convention (also excluded from `tree-baseline.ts` drift detection, so this is consistent runtime-owned state, not a project-source mutation).

### Alternatives considered

| Option | Summary | Why not chosen |
|---|---|---|
| A — Plain JSON checkpoint | Same in-session composition, but checkpoints are a single `writeFileSync`, no atomicity/locking. | Fastest to build, but a crash mid-write can corrupt the run index, which directly violates AC-005-3's "fail closed with a recoverable diagnostic" requirement — the repo's own `ProposalStore` already demonstrates this gap is real, not hypothetical. |
| B — Subprocess-dispatched stages | New orchestrator module dispatches every stage as a bounded `createAgentPort()` subprocess; advances the run index only after subprocess exit 0 + artifact-on-disk confirmation. | Most rigorous completion signal (a real process boundary instead of self-reported bookkeeping), but substantially more build effort, and does not fit the interactive `--collab` review-server stages `create-prd`/`refine-prd` already use — those are long-lived, human-attended HTTP sessions, not bounded one-shot subprocess work, and would need bespoke carve-out handling under this option. |
| **C — Hardened in-session composition** *(chosen)* | In-session stage execution (like every existing product command), backed by a dedicated atomic `RunIndexStore`. | Reuses 100% of the existing skill-composition and `ask_user`-approval infrastructure (including the `--collab` review server, which needs no special-casing), while fixing Option A's one real correctness gap with the repo's one proven atomic-write pattern. Matches user-confirmed direction. |

### Honest trust-boundary note

Because stage execution stays in-session (per Option C), the approval gates implemented by TRD-014/TRD-017/TRD-019 are enforced by the orchestrating skill's own conditional logic checking `RunIndexStore`-persisted approval fields before it issues an implementation or `gh pr create` tool call — not by a separate runtime authorization chokepoint like `agent-core`'s `MutationGuard` (which exists elsewhere in this repo, gating CQRS-registered commands, but `new-feature`'s mutating actions are ordinary skill-level tool calls, same as `fix-issue`'s own gated PR-creation step, not CQRS commands). This is the same trust boundary every existing Ensemble product command already operates under. Building a `MutationGuard`-equivalent chokepoint for skill-level tool calls is a materially larger investment this PRD does not request and no other product command has; REQ-014's "runtime authority" is satisfied here by making the check a required precondition over persisted, validated store state rather than over prompt claims — which is what AC-014-2 actually asks for — not by inventing a new enforcement subsystem.

title: Behavior: flag a test run that passed without running tests
description:
RECOMMENDATION 1 of 5. Highest-evidence best-practice behavior.

EVIDENCE (this repo's own .ensemble/runtime-log.jsonl, 118 test.failure.observed events over two days): 29 had 'zero tests ran' in output and 9 'suite failed to load' -- 38 of 51 classifiable failures were 'the suite did not actually run'. This is also what br-gwww was, and what the current constitution amendment about pipefail / 'Test Suites: 0 failed' is about.

THE GAP. verifyOutput() already detects vacuous success and has 32 tests, but it has exactly ONE caller: cqrs/commands.ts:329, inside fix.verify. So the detector only runs when verifying a PROPOSED FIX. When a human or agent runs the suite normally, nothing checks it.

COST IS HIGHER THAN 'just wire it up' -- corrected during review. event-translator.ts only emits test.failure.observed, and every FAILURE_OUTPUT_PATTERNS entry requires [1-9]\\d* failed or a FAIL marker. A run with 'Tests: 0 total' and exit code 0 matches none of them and is not isError, so TODAY IT PRODUCES NO EVENT AT ALL. There is no trigger for this behavior to fire on.

WORK:
1. event-translator.ts: emit test.passed (already in the ingress catalog at event-catalog.ts:60 and currently emitted by nothing) for a recognised test command that did not report failure, with a payload carrying tests-run/suites-loaded counts.
2. New command descriptor verification.observe -- non-mutating, no approval -- that runs verifyOutput over that payload.
3. Behavior triggering on test.passed, condition on the vacuous verdict, outcome reports loudly.

Start in policy.mode: propose. Do NOT block initially.
close_reason: Delivered: event-translator emits test.passed for a run that reported it executed nothing; .ensemble/behaviors/vacuous-test-run/ reports it with no agent step and no commands; 11 tests. Emission narrowed to the vacuous case so the healthy-run contract is preserved.

comments.author: ldangelo
comments.text:
DELIVERED (partially) 2026-09-29, commits on feature/trd-2026-0fc1c1d0-behavior-runtime-pi-harness.

1. event-translator.ts now emits test.passed for a recognised test command that reported it executed NOTHING. readTestVolume() reads jest/vitest totals, pytest counts, 'no tests ran', '[no test files]' and explicit '0 total'.

2. .ensemble/behaviors/vacuous-test-run/ reports it. No agent step and no commands: the judgement is mechanical, so asking a model to re-decide it would add latency, cost and a way to be wrong. Outcome status is 'inconclusive', never 'failed' -- the suite did not fail, which is precisely the problem.

3. 11 new tests in agent-core/tests/vacuous-test-run.test.ts.

DESIGN CHANGE FROM THE ORIGINAL PLAN, worth knowing. The plan said emit test.passed for every non-failing run. That broke 5 existing tests asserting the translator returns undefined for a healthy suite -- a deliberate contract so behaviors cannot chase healthy code. Rather than rewrite protected test files, emission was narrowed to the vacuous case only. Strictly better: the original guarantee is preserved untouched, and test.passed does not become the highest-volume event in the system.

'silent' (no count AND no explicit disclaimer) is deliberately NOT emitted. Reporting an unfamiliar runner's healthy output as vacuous is the same error in the opposite direction, and would train people to ignore the signal.

NOT DONE: no verification.observe command was needed after all. Remaining scope is optional -- richer reporting, and the router/pytest gap tracked separately in br-91nr.

title: a behavior's fix-prompt.md can drop the response contract, making every reply unparseable
description:
OBSERVED LIVE. Once br-boam stopped masking it, this is the next thing that kills the governed path.

buildFixPrompt does 'const body = template ?? [default]'. A behavior that ships fix-prompt.md therefore replaces the ENTIRE prompt -- including the part that tells the agent how to answer.

The trial repo's fix-prompt.md is well written as strategy and catastrophic as protocol. It says 'Repair the SOURCE so it passes' and 'Your change is verified by re-running the exact command that failed' -- describing an agent that EDITS FILES. But the child is spawned --tools=read,grep,glob precisely so it cannot write, and its reply is parsed as a JSON patch.

So the agent did exactly as instructed, discovered it had no way to do it, and said so in prose. Verbatim from the runtime log:

  'I found the bug, but I couldn't apply the fix: this session has no tool
   that can edit files in the working tree. write only accepts xd:// device
   paths here... I have no edit or shell tool.'

It then gave a correct diagnosis and a correct one-line fix, in markdown. parseFixReply found no json block and returned undefined. Recorded as 'no fix candidate offered'.

Diagnosis right, fix right, protocol wrong, loop dead.

WHY IT HID SO LONG. Running the same prompt by hand parsed perfectly -- because a hand-run passes no behaviorDirFor, so it gets the DEFAULT template, which does carry the contract. The failure only appears when a behavior ships its own prompt, which is the configuration the product ships.

FIX. Split strategy from protocol. The behavior owns judgment: which file, what counts as a real fix, what never to touch. The runtime owns the interface: you have no write tools, reply with only this json shape. Append RESPONSE_CONTRACT to every prompt, template or not, and say in it that it overrides anything above that contradicts it.

A behavior author cannot be expected to know the wire format of a process they never see, and should not be able to break it by writing a better prompt.
close_reason: done

## Task: TRD-005
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-82b6a138-pr-review-cycle-time.md#trd-005
PRD Reference: #req-024

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen approach (Option C):** One shared, prose-defined review procedure plus a small deterministic helper library.

- `packages/development/skills/pr-review-cycle/SKILL.md` is the single reusable procedure. It owns the *user-editable* parts (Constitution Rule 8): review criteria, the order of the loop, the 10-minute interactive wait, Foreman-mode rules. It **composes** `packages/quality/skills/pr-review-remediation/SKILL.md` for per-finding triage, regression tests and minimal fixes and does not restate those rules.
- A set of small pure-JS modules in `packages/development/lib/` owns only what *grades the model's own claim* (Constitution Rule 8's enforcement exception, and Rule 7): base/head scope resolution, ledger validation, head-bound remote-review evaluation, terminal-status derivation with the bounded-round cap, and the untracked review-state report. A thin CLI, `pr-review-cli.js`, exposes them as JSON-in/JSON-out commands, following the `trd-cli.js` / `complete-beads-planner.js` precedent.
- `fix-issue.yaml`, `implement-trd-beads.yaml` and `complete-beads/SKILL.md` invoke the skill at their real PR boundaries; none re-states review steps.

**Alternatives considered (user chose C):**

- **Option A -- prose-only skill:** fewest files, but "no early REVIEW_COMPLETE", head-binding and the round cap would be prose a model can misread, and tests could only assert text ordering. Rejected: the plan's core guarantee would not be falsifiable (Rule 7).
- **Option B -- TypeScript runtime in agent-core:** strongest typing, but a new build/dist surface and cross-package coupling for a prompt-level feature, and it pulls editable criteria toward code (against Rule 8). Rejected.

**Rationale:** Option C is the best fit for this brownfield repo: the helper is the minimum code that makes the status contract testable and unforgeable, everything a maintainer would plausibly tune stays in a skill file, and it needs no new dependency, provider or config knob.

title: [trd:trd-2026-15aa5acd-live-behavior-dispatch-autofix:task:TRD-015] - [ ] **TRD-015** Implement `LocalEventMatcher`: per-session cached compile, match on outbox append, invoke matches in-session (7h)
description:
## Task: TRD-015
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-15aa5acd-live-behavior-dispatch-autofix.md#trd-015
PRD Reference: #req-003

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen: Option C — single enforcement seam, additive.**

A new `MutationGuard` chokepoint in `agent-core` is the one place `policy.mode`, `capabilities.mutation_classes` (via the existing `hasMutationAuthority()`), and protected-path rules are resolved. It is wired once at the loader boundary rather than replicated per tool registration. The translator, matcher, and auto-fix loop are added to `pi-extension`. Discovery roots and `execution.test_command` are additive changes to existing schema/discovery code. `ToolRegistry`, `outbox`, and the compiler are reused unchanged.

### Alternatives considered

| Option | Summary | Why not chosen |
|---|---|---|
| **A — In-place extension** | Enforce mode/mutation/path rules as wrapper checks inside `behavior-loader`'s per-tool `execute()` closures. | Enforcement scattered across call sites; every future tool registration must remember to wrap. The PRD's central failure mode is *guarantees that exist in one place but are not reached from another* — Option A reproduces exactly that shape. |
| **B — Governance kernel** | Route every mutation through a `MutationBroker` + `GovernedWorkspace` in `agent-core`; `pi-extension` becomes a thin adapter. | Strongest long-term design and the right eventual target, but it re-opens already-shipped code across every tool path for a ~6-7 PR refactor before a single PRD requirement is demonstrable. Deferred deliberately, not rejected. |
| **C — Single enforcement seam** *(chosen)* | One `MutationGuard` chokepoint, wired once; everything else additive. | Gets a single auditable chokepoint (Option B's main benefit) without Option B's refactor surface. Fits the existing `agent-core` / `pi-extension` split. |

### Architectural note carried from grounding

Two defects found while grounding this design are folded into PR 1 rather than left implicit:

1. `pi-events.ts` emits `runtime.tool_result` / `runtime.tool.called` / `runtime.tool.failed` / `runtime.tool.completed`, none of which appear in `HARNESS_EVENT_TYPES` (which defines `runtime.tool_call.started` / `runtime.tool_call.completed`). `normalizeEvent` does not currently reject uncatalogued types, so PRD AC-002-1's "validated against the closed catalog" would be vacuous. Addressed by TRD-001 (`[satisfies INFRA]`).
2. `behavior-loader.ts:79` calls `registry.grant(...)` unconditionally immediately before `registry.invoke(...)`, making the grant boundary a rubber stamp for behavior-governed tools (unlike the echo path, where the grant is CLI-flag-gated). Addressed by TRD-003.
Satisfies: REQ-003
PRD ACs: AC-003-1, AC-003-2
Target File: packages/pi-extension/src/local-event-matcher.ts

Implementation AC:
- [ ] Given a behavior whose trigger matches an appended event, when the append occurs, then its compiled artifact executes in the current session

description:
Full title: - [ ] **TRD-041** Add scripted host swap scenario `scripts/tests/host-swap-scenario.test.js`: push (`vcs.push`), open, check status, merge against the Azure DevOps adapter with stub `az` and no `gh` on PATH; assert the output uses Azure DevOps vocabulary ("pull request", "policy"), not GitHub terms (via the adapter's vocabulary block); and a second scenario with host `azure-devops` and tracker `azure-boards` linking a work item to a change request using config only (`host.change-request.link-work-item`) (6h)

## Task: TRD-041
## References
TRD: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-8d825f54-tool-abstraction-layer.md
TRD Task: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-8d825f54-tool-abstraction-layer.md#trd-041
PRD: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-8d825f54-tool-abstraction-layer.md
PRD Requirement: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-8d825f54-tool-abstraction-layer.md#req-017
PRD ACs: AC-017-1, AC-017-2, AC-017-3
Parent Epic: [trd:trd-2026-8d825f54-tool-abstraction-layer]
Read-first: read the TRD, TRD Task section, PRD and PRD Requirement above before any work on this bead.


--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-017**: Source-control host swap, end to end (first alternative: Azure DevOps)
Source-control host swap, end to end (first alternative: Azure DevOps) Priority: Must | `[RISK: review-thread and merge semantics differ between hosts]` With the source-control host adapter changed by configuration only, commands that open, review, gate and merge change requests work against the alternative host with that host's vocabulary. A team on the alternative vendor can change host and tracker together, because that vendor's work-item tracker ships as a tracker adapter (REQ-016).

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-017-1: Given host config set to the alternative adapter | When the scripted change-request scenario (push | Then it completes with the default host's tool not installed
- AC-017-2: Given the same scenario | When output is read | Then it uses the alternative host's vocabulary for change-request and review terms
- AC-017-3: Given host config set to the Azure DevOps adapter and tracker config set to the Azure Boards adapter | When the scripted scenario linking a work item to a change request runs | Then it completes using configuration changes only

--- TRD Context ---
### Alternatives Considered

| Option | Approach | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|---|
| A: Prose-only adapters | Adapter is a skill; the agent follows its prose and normalizes tool output itself | Smallest build; fully editable | Cannot route internal CLIs deterministically (REQ-016), cannot validate output (REQ-022), cannot deny at runtime (REQ-023); behavior varies per model |
| **B: Manifest plus runner (chosen)** | Adapter is a skill directory: `SKILL.md` (vocabulary and agent-facing prose) plus a declarative `adapter.yaml` (capability command templates, output mapping, allowlist, health check, detection signals, required env names). A core resolver library and `toolchain-cli` execute capabilities deterministically | Meets PRD (adapter is a skill), Rule 8 (editable without rebuild), Rule 5 (enforcement in code), REQ-016 (CLIs call the same library) | New resolver, runner, manifest schema and output-mapping engine to build and test |
| C: Executable plugin adapters | Separately packaged executables speaking a versioned JSON protocol | Arbitrary logic; strongest isolation | Contradicts the PRD's skills-as-contract decision; fails Rule 8; needs per-OS packaging and a protocol |

**Rationale:** B is the only option that makes every PRD guarantee a code-enforced property while keeping adapters user-editable data. The requester selected B at the architecture gate.

### Interpretations and Resolved Design Issues

- **I1: plain version control.** The PRD taxonomy has no plain `git` category, yet about 45 sources invoke it. Plain `git` operations (status, commit, push, log, diff, merge-base) are `vcs.*` capabilities of the `workflow` category, whose default adapter is `plain-git`; the `git-town` adapter extends it. Recommend a PRD refine pass to name this explicitly.
- **I2: ambiguity versus no signal (PRD REQ-009 AC-2 vs REQ-010 AC-2).** "No detectable signal" means no signal source exists at all (no remote, no marker files); the shipped default is used. "Ambiguous" means two or more installed adapters match, or a signal source exists (for example a remote URL) but matches no installed adapter; resolution fails explicitly in non-interactive runs and asks in interactive runs.
- **I3: AC-023-2 (governed boundary denies).** The runner is invoked through the shell tool, so a command that was not granted the shell tool cannot run any adapter; an adapter therefore cannot widen grants. The runner additionally denies any command outside the adapter's binary-plus-subcommand allowlist. Denial of raw shell commands typed by an agent outside the runner remains host-enforced (hooks on Claude Code; none in this repo for Pi, OpenCode or Codex); the lint (REQ-019) keeps commands from issuing raw tool calls. This residual is recorded in the Threat Model.
- **I4: confirmation session identity.** No stable session id is exposed uniformly across runtimes. TRD-017 begins with a spike that records which id each runtime exposes (`ENSEMBLE_SESSION_ID`, host session variables); the passive confirmation record is keyed by `(sessionKey, category, adapter, configHash)` and falls back to the run id when no session id exists.
- **I5: repo-local adapters are untrusted by default.** A cloned repository can ship `.ensemble/adapters/`. Repo-local adapters resolve in every mode (satisfying AC-007-3) but a non-interactive run additionally requires the adapter name in the user's `trustedRepoAdapters` list; an interactive run shows the adapter's allowlist at first-use confirmation.
- **I6: no new runtime dependency.** The output-mapping engine uses a small dotted-path projection (`$.a.b[0]`, `|` alternation for "array or object"), not a JSONPath library, because constitution section 4 requires approval for new dependencies.
- **I7: work-graph selection.** `work-graph` is its own category with default `auto`: use the work-graph capabilities of the resolved tracker adapter when its manifest provides them; otherwise use the built-in `work-graph-links-fallback` adapter (tracker dependency links, then plan order stated as not dependency-aware). One manifest may implement several categories.
- **I8: PRD BDD floor.** Fourteen PRD requirements (REQ-001, 002, 004, 005, 006, 009, 010, 012, 015, 018, 021, 022, 024, 025) have two ACs, below the command's three-scenario floor. The test tasks specify exactly one scenario per AC; recommend a PRD refine pass to add edge or error ACs.
- **I10: packaging.** `packages/development` depends only on `js-yaml` and its libraries require only siblings, so the resolver library, category contracts, default selection, schemas and tool inventory all ship inside `packages/development` (`lib/toolchain/` and `toolchain/`). A standalone plugin install and the Pi vendor bundle therefore contain everything; other packages call `toolchain-cli` through `TOOLCHAIN_CLI` rather than importing it.
- **I9: preflight is enforced in code.** `toolchain-cli run` refuses a side-effecting capability unless a passing preflight record exists for the supplied `--run-id`; the command prose cannot silently skip preflight.
Satisfies: REQ-017
Target File: 
Actions:

Implementation AC:
- [ ] Given a PATH with stub `az` and without `gh`, when the scenario runs with host config `azure-devops`, then push, create, view and merge each exit 0
- [ ] Given the scenario output, when scanned for the GitHub-only terms listed in the host vocabulary block (for example "pull request review decision"), then none appear and the Azure DevOps terms do appear
- [ ] Given config only (`.ensemble/toolchain.yaml` setting host `azure-devops` and tracker `azure-boards`), when the link scenario runs, then `az repos pr work-item add` is invoked and no source file changes are needed
Dependencies: TRD-033, TRD-036, TRD-040

title: Split the ingress catalog into what Ensemble produces and what it cannot receive
description:
MEASUREMENT (packages/agent-core, 2026-09-29): the catalog lists 54 trigger types. 10 are emitted. 44 (81%) are not.

Emitted: 6 harness runtime.* the Pi adapter publishes, 2 translated (test.failure.observed, test.passed), and command-emitted lifecycle events.

A catalog is a promise. 81% unfulfilled makes the other 19% untrustworthy too, because nothing distinguishes them -- which is why br-jgxo's load-time warning was needed at all. The warning makes the gap visible; it does not resolve it.

CRITICAL FINDING, verified not assumed: ENSEMBLE HAS NO INBOUND EVENT PATH. Exactly two things reach dispatchingSink (and therefore matcher.matchNames): session.ts publishing Pi host events plus their translations, and extension.ts:304 re-publishing command handler output. There is no webhook listener, no file tailer, no IPC, no subscribe. event-sinks.ts:14 states it: 'Foreman owns durable event ingestion.' The flow is outbound only.

So the prd/trd/implementation/review/pull_request/release families are not 'produced elsewhere and consumed here'. They CANNOT ARRIVE. Listing them as triggers advertises a capability with neither a producer nor a delivery mechanism.

PROPOSED DISPOSITION of the 44:

EMIT (13) -- Ensemble genuinely knows these in-session:
  behavior.completed / .blocked / .abandoned / .outcome.recorded / .observation.recorded (5) -- see br-j46q, do first
  approval.requested (1) -- the registry already calls the approval channel; 'a human was asked' is an auditable fact
  runtime.message.emitted / .session.failed / .cancelled / .timed_out (4) -- siblings already emitted, cheap completeness
  repository.changed / .branch.created (2) -- detectable from git tool calls; feeds the stale-base work (br-jg0l)
  test.regression_detected (1) -- needs cross-run memory; session-scoped only; most work of this group

NOT OURS (25) -- prd.* (4), trd.* (7), implementation.* (5), release.* (3), review.* (3), pull_request.* (3).
Two distinct reasons. PRD/TRD/implementation span sessions and need durability REQ-RUN-002 forbids adding here. review/pull_request/release have an AUTHORITATIVE source in GitHub; Ensemble emitting them would be a second, weaker, sometimes-disagreeing source. Move them to the cross-repository contract (docs/architecture/behavior-runtime-contract-v1.md) as Foreman's vocabulary. Do NOT describe them as 'consumed by Ensemble' until an inbound path exists -- that is a separate decision, and pull-based tailing with at-most-once semantics is the shape the local-sink spike (docs/architecture/cqrs-local-event-sink.md) points to.

REMOVE (6):
  validation.requested / .completed -- redundant with fix.verified
  change.proposed -- redundant with fix.proposed
  child_behavior.requested -- no child-behavior step kind exists; adding one is a much larger decision
  learning.observation.recorded -- overlaps br-u5o / br-pyg; decide there
  behavior.unblocked -- a session-scoped interpreter has no block-and-resume to unblock from

NOTE: behavior/event-catalog.ts is a protected guardrail file, so the operator must approve the edit.

AFTER: update trigger-producers.ts so the load-time warning stops firing on events that are correctly someone else's to emit, and distinguishes 'inert' from 'not ours'.

DONE. The 6 dead types are out of the catalog: validation.requested/.completed, change.proposed, child_behavior.requested, learning.observation.recorded, behavior.unblocked. Committed 9985a8e.

FINAL SPLIT: KEEP 17 / EMIT 6 / LAUNCH-INPUT 25 = 48 types, down from 54.

THE COMMIT TOUCHES FOUR FILES, NOT ONE, and the non-obvious ones are the point:
- DOMAIN_TOOL_EVENT_MAPPING in event-catalog.ts had entries for validation.completed (under ensemble.record_observation) and change.proposed (under ensemble.propose_change). That Record is typed Record<DomainToolName, readonly string[]> -- loose strings, NOT the catalog union -- so tsc would not have flagged the leftovers. execute() enforces emission against this mapping, so a stale entry would have let a domain tool emit a type the catalog no longer declares. Both lists retain other members, so no tool lost its vocabulary.
- domain-tool-vocabulary.ts needed a wording change rather than a rename: 'Reports or clears a blocked state' stopped being true once behavior.unblocked was gone.
- event-disposition.ts lost its 6 'remove' entries; its coverage test is what catches a half-done removal, and it duly failed while the removal was partial.
- behavior-command-event-reference.md regenerated from source.

A CLAIM I MADE EARLIER WAS WRONG: I reported validation.completed as sitting under ensemble.record_outcome. It was ensemble.record_observation.

PROVENANCE CAVEAT, recorded because it affects trust in the guardrail rather than this change. The protected-path mechanism reported 'reverted' for this edit and the file did not revert; a subsequent git checkout to restore it was also reported reverted and also did not happen. Approval ids incremented 29/30/31 with no observable effect in either direction. The committed content is exactly the 8-line removal reviewed on this bead and the operator approved and instructed the commit, but the guardrail's messages did not correspond to disk state, which is worth a look before relying on it elsewhere.

685 tests pass (agent-core 539, pi-extension 146), eslint clean.

NOT DONE HERE: the undocumented launch handoff. If 25 catalog types arrive as launch input, something must specify that contract. Left open as separate work.

comments.author: ldangelo
comments.text:
CORRECTION 2026-09-29, from the user: I had the Foreman/Ensemble relationship wrong when filing this.

WRONG MODEL (what this bead's 'NOT OURS' section assumes): two peer systems exchanging events, with Ensemble consuming prd/trd/review/pull_request/release from Foreman over some ingress path.

ACTUAL MODEL: Foreman OWNS THE SESSION. It launches a headless Ensemble session to do work, the session runs, it ends, Foreman collects the artifacts. Parent and child process. Neither attaches to the other's sessions. Corroborated by br-mr22, which records live headless runs in loop-trial dying when the session ends.

CONSEQUENCES FOR THIS BEAD:
- The 25 prd/trd/implementation/release/review/pull_request types should be REMOVED from the ingress catalog, not 'moved to the contract as consumed by Ensemble'. Foreman already holds these facts; it has no reason to send them to a child it started, and Ensemble has no path to receive them. Anything Ensemble needs (governing TRD, branch, acceptance criteria, mode) arrives as LAUNCH INPUT, not as an event.
- Disposition becomes EMIT 13 / REMOVE 31, with no third category.
- No ingress transport work is needed. Disregard any design for pull, cursors, git refs or HTTP; I had proposed those to solve a delivery problem that does not exist.

SEPARATE WORK THIS SURFACED (file if wanted): docs/architecture/behavior-runtime-contract-v1.md section 6 documents the AgentPort/ApprovalPort interfaces but never states how Foreman INVOKES Ensemble -- what is passed at launch and what may be relied on in the outbox at the end. That handoff is the actual contract between the two systems and it is undocumented.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERION, added at the user's request 2026-09-29.

THE IMPLEMENTATION MUST ASSERT TOTAL COVERAGE. A test fails if any entry in HARNESS_EVENT_TYPES + SEMANTIC_EVENT_TYPES is not assigned exactly one disposition, and fails if any disposition names a type that is not in the catalog. Both directions -- an unclassified event and a classification of a non-existent event are each a way for this list to rot.

WHY THIS IS AN ACCEPTANCE CRITERION AND NOT A NICETY. This bead was filed with dispositions expressed as FAMILY WILDCARDS (trd.*, prd.*, implementation.*). That read as complete coverage and was not: a later audit found only 23 of 54 types named anywhere in any bead, 31 covered by wildcard alone. Two of the unnamed ones -- constitution.proposed and test.failure.investigated -- are ACTIVELY EMITTED, so an implementer following 'remove what is not listed' would have deleted live events and broken the constitution-learning and investigation flows.

The failure mode is specific and repeatable: a wildcard reads like coverage. trd.* looks complete until you notice trd.implementation.* is a separate three-type family a reader may or may not fold in. Prose cannot hold this; only an assertion can.

SHAPE: put the disposition map in code next to the catalog (not in a doc, not in this bead), so the test can compare the two lists mechanically. The bead comment holding the 54-row enumeration is the INPUT to that map, not the record of it -- once the code exists, the code is authoritative.

Related precedent in this repo: agent-core/tests/catalog-reference.test.ts regenerates the command/event reference and compares, so documentation drift fails the build. Same principle, applied to disposition rather than documentation.

comments.text:
DECISION FROM THE USER 2026-09-29: 'we have a plan to have foreman emit these events in the future.'

THIS REVERSES THE 16:04 CORRECTION ON THIS BEAD, which said to REMOVE the 25 Foreman-domain types outright. Recording the tension rather than quietly switching, because the two statements are reconcilable and the reconciliation is the actual design.

THE RECONCILIATION. Both are true, because 'Foreman emits it' and 'Ensemble can trigger on it' are different claims separated by a delivery question:
- Foreman emitting prd.approved does NOT mean a running Ensemble session receives it. Foreman launches a session, the session runs, it ends. When Foreman emits prd.approved there is typically NO session alive to deliver it to, and building one that waits for such events is exactly the ingress layer REQ-RUN-002 forbids.
- What actually happens is the reverse: Foreman emits prd.approved, DECIDES to launch an Ensemble session in response, and the event is the LAUNCH INPUT for that session. The behavior then matches it at startup.

So these types are real, they are Foreman's to emit, and they ARE reachable by Ensemble behaviors -- via launch input, not via ingress. That is a delivery mechanism that exists today, needs no transport work, and contradicts neither statement.

REVISED DISPOSITION, 4 categories, 54 total:
  KEEP 14           -- emitted in-session today
  EMIT 9            -- Ensemble knows the fact in-session and should publish it
  LAUNCH INPUT 25   -- prd.* trd.* implementation.* trd.implementation.* review.* release.* pull_request.*
                       Foreman's vocabulary. Retained in the catalog. Matchable when the session is
                       launched with one as its triggering event. NOT awaited mid-session.
  REMOVE 6          -- validation.requested, validation.completed, change.proposed,
                       child_behavior.requested, learning.observation.recorded, behavior.unblocked
                       (redundant or no concept behind them; unchanged from the prior analysis)

CONSEQUENCES:
- Only 6 types get removed from event-catalog.ts, not 31. Much smaller protected-file edit.
- trigger-producers.ts must distinguish THREE states, not two: emitted in-session / expected as launch input / inert. A behavior triggering on trd.approved is correct and must stop warning; one triggering on a REMOVE type is still a mistake.
- The undocumented launch handoff (flagged in the 16:04 comment as 'separate work this surfaced') is now on the critical path: if launch input is the delivery mechanism for 25 catalog types, what Foreman passes at launch IS the contract. Worth filing.
- The total-coverage acceptance criterion is unchanged and now covers 4 categories.

title: [trd:trd-2026-70e784f2-code-review-process:task:TRD-017-TEST] - [ ] **TRD-017-TEST** Depth modes and area slices (4h)
description:
## Test Task: TRD-017-TEST
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-70e784f2-code-review-process.md#trd-017-test
PRD Reference: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-70e784f2-code-review-process.md#req-016

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-016**: Review depth modes (Should)
Review depth modes (Should) Review effort scales with risk through Quick, Standard and Deep modes that bound how many reviewers and verifiers run.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-016-1: Given a mode is selected | When review runs | Then the number of reviewers and verifiers does not exceed that mode's bound (Quick: a single reviewer and no verifiers; Standard: at least two reviewers and 3 verifiers; Deep: at least two reviewers and 5 verifiers)
- AC-016-3: Given no mode is chosen | When review starts | Then the mode defaults from the PR's tier: Low=Quick, Medium=Standard, High=Deep; while Low is treated as Medium (REQ-013), a Low PR gets Standard
- AC-018-1: Given a PR is too large for one reviewer to cover in a pass | When review runs | Then it is split by area (using the sensitive-area and rules boundaries) and every slice is reviewed
- AC-018-2: Given a PR is sliced | When findings are presented | Then they are combined in one sorted list and the report states which slices were reviewed

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen approach (Option C):** extend the pattern TRD-2026-82b6a138 established: **editable behavior in skills, agents and markdown; a small set of pure, deterministic libraries for what must not be self-certified by a model.**

- **User-owned (Constitution Rule 8), prose or data a maintainer edits without a toolchain:** per-area rules (`REVIEW.md` files), the policy block inside the root `REVIEW.md` (round cap, depth table, bot and maintainer logins, sensitive and High paths, Low-waiver state), severity definitions, reviewer, verifier, classifier and security-lane prompts, the PR template, the sweep and explainer procedures. All of it is read from the **target branch**, never from the PR head (REQ-024).
- **Enforcement (Rules 5 and 7), code that grades a model's claim:** vote tally, tier assignment with its sensitive-path floor and Low-waiver evidence, approval evaluation bound to a commit, the merge gate, round-cap derivation, repeat suppression, delta-range selection, depth bounds, slice coverage, metrics and eval scoring. Each is a pure CommonJS module in `packages/development/lib/`, exposed as a JSON-in/JSON-out subcommand of the existing `pr-review-cli.js`, following the 82b6a138 precedent. None performs network I/O or holds a timer.
- **Entry points (Rule 6):** every capability is reached through the one `pr-review-cycle` skill, which `fix-issue`, `implement-trd-beads` and `pr-merge` already invoke or will invoke (a new `MODE=gate` for `pr-merge`). YAML callers reference the skill only, never the CLI, as the existing parity tests require.
- **Recurrence (Rule 4):** nightly or weekly sweeps and daily eval runs are on-demand skills; a workflow template for the host repository is opt-in and scaffolded by init-project. Ensemble's own workflows gain no `schedule` trigger.

**Alternatives considered (user chose C):**

- **Option A -- prose-only skills and agents:** fewest files and fastest to ship. Rejected: the vote threshold, the tier floor, commit-bound approvals and the round cap would be prose a model can misread or skip, so none of these gates could be shown to fail (Rule 7), and "a bot approval never counts" would be a request, not a guarantee.
- **Option B -- a new TypeScript review engine in `agent-core`:** strongest typing and one runtime. Rejected: a new build and `dist` surface and cross-package coupling for a prompt-level feature, editable criteria pulled into code (against Rule 8), and drift toward an ensemble-owned dispatcher that competes with Foreman (Rule 4).

**Rationale:** Option C is the best fit for this brownfield repo. It adds only the code that grades claims, keeps everything a maintainer or adopting team would tune in files they can edit, adds no dependency (Constitution §4) and no CI secret, vendors into Pi automatically through the existing require-closure bundler, and each gate can be mutation-proven using the harness that already exists.

**Decisions taken where the PRD left a choice** (each is editable policy, not a hidden constant):

| Decision | Value | Where it lives |
|---|---|---|
| Policy format | Fenced `ensemble-review-policy` JSON block in the root `REVIEW.md` (no new parser dependency) | REVIEW.md, read from the base commit |
| "Cannot vouch for" a push (AC-010-3, AC-014-2) | Commit is unvouched when its tree differs from the reviewed tree and it is not a remediation commit recorded in the review-state report, or it is a merge commit | `pr-review-scope.js`, `pr-review-approvals.js` |
| Slice threshold for large PRs (AC-018-1) | 1500 changed lines, configurable | policy block |
| Area rules vs policy keys | Policy keys are read from the **root** file only; area files carry guidance, and the more restrictive instruction wins when areas conflict (AC-001-2) | skill prose |
| First PR that introduces REVIEW.md | No base copy exists, so strict defaults apply (Low treated as Medium, cap 3, default sensitive set) | `pr-review-policy.js` |
| Verifier majority | Strict majority of the expected verifier count (2 of 3, 3 of 5) | `pr-review-votes.js` |

description:
## Test Task: TRD-002-TEST
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-f08a2a09-command-lifecycle-hooks.md#trd-002-test
PRD Reference: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-f08a2a09-command-lifecycle-hooks.md#req-007

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-007**: Invalid hook configuration is rejected before any command runs (Must)
Invalid hook configuration is rejected before any command runs (Must)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-006-1: Given a project has `.ensemble/hooks.yaml` defining named handlers and per-command start and end selections | When a selected command runs | Then the named handlers run for the selected events
- AC-006-2: Given a handler is named in several commands' selections | When each command runs | Then the single handler definition is used for all of them
- AC-006-3: Given hook configuration exists | When the command's own definition is read | Then it contains no hook wiring and no shell implementation detail
- AC-006-4: Given a selection names a wildcard or a group instead of an explicit command | When the configuration is validated | Then it is rejected as an unknown command, so every command that carries hooks is listed by name
- AC-007-1: Given a handler lacks an explicit `type` | When the configuration is validated | Then it is rejected with a message naming the handler and the missing field
- AC-007-2: Given a command selection references a handler that is not defined | When validated | Then it is rejected naming the command and the unknown handler
- AC-007-3: Given the configuration names a command that does not exist | When validated | Then each is rejected with a message naming the offending entry
- AC-007-5: Given the configuration is valid | When validated | Then no output other than a success indication is produced
- AC-009-5: Given a handler exceeds its timeout (5 seconds when a shell handler states none) | When a shell handler states none) | Then the handler and every process it started are terminated and its error behavior applies
- AC-010-3: Given an end handler is configured with error behavior `block` | When the configuration is validated | Then it is rejected, because only start handlers may block
- AC-010-4: Given any handler | When the configuration is validated | Then it is rejected under REQ-007 and no default is silently applied
- AC-011-5: Given a prompt handler states no timeout | When it runs | Then a 30 second timeout applies, and exceeding it applies the handler's error behavior

--- TRD Context ---
**Decision:** Build the lifecycle as a harness-neutral core in `packages/agent-core` (event payloads, configuration validation, redaction, a shell runner, a prompt runner, a serial dispatcher, and a per-session command-run tracker) and one adapter in `packages/pi-extension` that connects it to Pi. The adapter is the only code that knows Pi's event names.

**Decisions made by the maintainer during design (all recorded in PRD v1.0.2 to v1.0.4):**

- The first release is adapter-specific, with Pi as the proving harness. A runtime-owned wrapper is deferred.
- `command.start` fires from the runtime when the command's slash input is seen, so it never depends on the model and a start handler's block is enforced by the runtime. A command whose own prompt then rejects its arguments has already produced a start and ends as `failed`.
- A command's completion is signalled by a silent `ensemble_command_complete` tool that the model is told to call last. The instruction is injected per turn by the adapter, not generated into every Pi prompt, so projects without hooks see no change.
- A settled loop never ends a command. A command that never signals completion ends as `cancelled` when the session ends or the next command begins.
- A prompt handler is evaluated by an isolated headless child (`pi -p --no-session -ne -nt -np`), parsed against a typed response contract.
- No handler runs until the host reports the project as trusted (`ctx.isProjectTrusted()`).
- `on_error` is required on every handler. Default timeouts are 5 seconds for shell handlers and 30 seconds for prompt handlers.
- Selections list commands by name. Wildcards and groups are rejected.
- For harnesses with no adapter, the guide, a capability table and a status check say hooks are inactive. Nothing is shown at command time there.

**Why code and not a prompt (Constitution rule 8):** what runs at a command boundary, the trust check, the environment allowlist, redaction, timeouts and process cleanup are enforcement boundaries and must not be editable by a model or a user prompt. What a team wants to run (the hooks file, the executables, the prompt files) is user-owned and stays in files they edit without a toolchain.

title: [trd:trd-2026-15aa5acd-live-behavior-dispatch-autofix:task:TRD-007] - [ ] **TRD-007** Add the fixture-constructibility conformance rule (5h)
description:
## Task: TRD-007
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-15aa5acd-live-behavior-dispatch-autofix.md#trd-007
PRD Reference: #req-010

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen: Option C — single enforcement seam, additive.**

A new `MutationGuard` chokepoint in `agent-core` is the one place `policy.mode`, `capabilities.mutation_classes` (via the existing `hasMutationAuthority()`), and protected-path rules are resolved. It is wired once at the loader boundary rather than replicated per tool registration. The translator, matcher, and auto-fix loop are added to `pi-extension`. Discovery roots and `execution.test_command` are additive changes to existing schema/discovery code. `ToolRegistry`, `outbox`, and the compiler are reused unchanged.

### Alternatives considered

| Option | Summary | Why not chosen |
|---|---|---|
| **A — In-place extension** | Enforce mode/mutation/path rules as wrapper checks inside `behavior-loader`'s per-tool `execute()` closures. | Enforcement scattered across call sites; every future tool registration must remember to wrap. The PRD's central failure mode is *guarantees that exist in one place but are not reached from another* — Option A reproduces exactly that shape. |
| **B — Governance kernel** | Route every mutation through a `MutationBroker` + `GovernedWorkspace` in `agent-core`; `pi-extension` becomes a thin adapter. | Strongest long-term design and the right eventual target, but it re-opens already-shipped code across every tool path for a ~6-7 PR refactor before a single PRD requirement is demonstrable. Deferred deliberately, not rejected. |
| **C — Single enforcement seam** *(chosen)* | One `MutationGuard` chokepoint, wired once; everything else additive. | Gets a single auditable chokepoint (Option B's main benefit) without Option B's refactor surface. Fits the existing `agent-core` / `pi-extension` split. |

title: constitution.apply is unreachable: MutationGuard denies its own sanctioned route
description:
`classifyPath` marks docs/standards/constitution.md protected and MutationGuard refuses every protected path unconditionally, so constitution.apply can never reach its write. REQ-SAFE-008's approval-gated application is currently satisfied by application being impossible.

AUTHORITY: br-9uqd (user design decision, 2026-09-25; commit 4914226 on dev, authored and committed by ldangelo) explicitly SUPERSEDES the older PR-as-gate design and states the consequence directly: 'WriteBoundaryMonitor must permit exactly that one authorized write.' Its rationale is that main is now protected and advances only through a dev -> main release PR, so human review is structural rather than smuggled in as 'the approval IS a PR'. Do NOT resolve this by reverting constitution.apply to PR-only; that re-implements the requirement the user retired.

REMAINING CHANGE (one file): in packages/agent-core/src/behavior/mutation-guard.ts, permit a protected path when verdict.reason === 'constitution' AND request.mutationClass === 'constitution.write'.

WHY THIS IS NARROW, AND NOW ENFORCED: mutation classes come from command descriptors, never from behavior data, so the class is not forgeable by a manifest. CommandRegistry.register() now throws if any descriptor claims SANCTIONED_PROTECTED_CLASS without requiresApproval, so the exemption cannot be widened later by adding an unapproved command in a file far from the guard that grants it. Covered by agent-core/tests/command-registry.test.ts ('the protected-path exemption cannot be widened by a new descriptor', 5 tests, incl. one asserting the exemption is not dead code).

BLOCKED ON: editing mutation-guard.ts is gated as guardrail-source; the OPERATOR must run /ensemble-approve for the pending violation id. Each retry mints a new id, so ask for the current one.

DELIVERED AND TESTED ALREADY: constitution.propose creates an evidence-backed artifact and writes nothing; constitution.apply checks approval, proposal kind, already-applied, and base-SHA drift before its write; the constitution-learning behavior triggers only on fix.verified with verdict passed.
close_reason: Carve-out landed via /ensemble-approve 27. constitution.apply reaches its write; 7 lifecycle tests cover apply, decline, no-approval-channel fail-closed, base-SHA drift, double-apply, undeclared capability, and that the exemption buys nothing for a non-constitution protected path.

description:
## Test Task: TRD-006-TEST
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-1d3e0dd6-new-feature-foreman-flag.md#trd-006-test
PRD Reference: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-1d3e0dd6-new-feature-foreman-flag.md#req-006

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-006**: Abandon needs no confirmation under `--foreman` (Should)
Abandon needs no confirmation under `--foreman` (Should)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-006-1: Given `--abandon` and `--foreman` together | When entry resolution runs | Then the confirmation question is not asked and `RunIndexStore
- AC-006-2: Given `--abandon` without `--foreman` | When it runs | Then the explicit confirmation is required as today

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen approach:** a prompt-only change to two YAML command sources. No TypeScript changes.

- `packages/development/commands/new-feature.yaml` gains a boolean `foreman` parameter and one derived variable, `FOREMAN`, defined once in Entry Point Resolution Step 1 and referenced by every later step. Each step that asks the user gets a `FOREMAN == true` branch that takes a deterministic, recorded, non-interactive decision. Each step that dispatches a stage skill appends `--foreman` when `FOREMAN == true`.
- `packages/development/commands/feature.yaml` (the `/ensemble:feature` front door) recognizes `--foreman` as the first token after the keyword and forwards it.
- Generated OMP, Pi and Codex artifacts are regenerated from the repo root, never hand-edited.

**Why prompt-only (Constitution Rule 8):** how a workflow behaves when no one can answer is something a maintainer would plausibly tune (for example, switching the PR gate to park instead of auto-grant). That belongs in the command prose, not in TypeScript. `RunIndexStore` already supports everything needed: `StageOutcome.detail` carries the "granted by `--foreman` policy" record.

**Additive-only edits (found in refinement):** the existing suites (`new-feature-command.test.js`, `feature-command.test.js`, `feature-input-validation-boundary.test.js`, `feature-concurrency-passthrough.test.js`) pin exact sentences in both YAML files, for example "any remaining text is an unsupported flag or argument rejected here". So no pre-existing sentence may be reworded or removed. Foreman behavior is added as new actions or appended sentences, and the existing suites must pass unchanged. For the front door that means: a new action, placed before the validation action, removes a leading `--foreman` token and sets `FOREMAN`, so the pinned validation sentences still read "remaining text" correctly; and a new action, placed after the invocation is constructed, inserts `--foreman` right after `/ensemble:new-feature` in whatever invocation was built.

**Alternatives rejected:**
- *Env-var-only detection (no flag).* Rejected: the maintainer asked for a `--foreman` flag, and the five stage skills already key on that flag.
- *A new RunRecord field `autoGranted`.* Rejected: TypeScript and schema change for information `StageOutcome.detail` already carries.
- *Parking at the approval gates.* Rejected by the maintainer: it stalls every no-user run.

title: hold fails OPEN when no tree baseline: fix is left applied
description: Observed live; see comment.
close_reason: Continuation path removed; propose cannot mutate; unverifiable state never resolves to allow

comments.author: ldangelo
comments.text:
Live, 2026-09-29T02:04:18Z, /tmp/loop-trial-run (a FRESH git clone, so 'not a git work tree' is NOT the explanation):

  verification { issue: 'npm test', cwd: '/tmp/loop-trial-run', status: 'passed',
                 detail: '2 passed, 2 total', heldForApproval: [],
                 holdSkipped: 'no tree baseline; fix left applied' }

  invocation   { outcome: { status: 'rejected',
                 reason: 'behavior "fix-failing-test" runs in mode: propose;
                          direct write to src/math.js is denied' } }

Read those together. The GOVERNED path correctly refused to write under mode: propose. The CONTINUATION path then repaired src/math.js anyway, and the hold that should have caught it was skipped -- because a baseline was missing, the fix was LEFT APPLIED.

That is fail-open, in a codebase that fails closed everywhere else (createFixSandbox rejects rather than falling back to the live repo; SessionUiBridge.confirm returns false rather than assuming yes; a missing approval host denies). Here a missing baseline is treated as permission.

It also explains why #98's propose-gating looks like it never engages: it does engage, and then the continuation writes anyway.

Fix direction: no baseline => HOLD, and say so. An unverifiable change is exactly the change that should not be silently kept. Whatever the reason a baseline cannot be captured, 'I could not check' must never resolve to 'therefore allow'.

Open question to answer first: why is there no baseline in a clean clone? The cwd recorded is correct. Suspect baseline capture runs at a different point (activation, or pre-continuation) against a different root than the one in the verification record.
