Parent Epic: [trd:trd-2026-8d825f54-tool-abstraction-layer]
Read-first: read the TRD, TRD Task section, PRD and PRD Requirement above before any work on this bead.


--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-024**: Default equivalence with no configuration
Default equivalence with no configuration Priority: Must | `[RISK: large refactor must be behavior-preserving]` A project that configures nothing behaves exactly as before: the same default adapters are selected and the same instruction sequences are produced.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-024-1: Given an unconfigured project | When refactored commands are generated | Then the default-toolchain equivalence snapshots match pre-refactor output
- AC-024-2: Given an unconfigured project | When a refactored command opens a change request | Then it produces the same default-host instruction sequence as before

--- TRD Context ---
### Alternatives Considered

| Option | Approach | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|---|
| A: Prose-only adapters | Adapter is a skill; the agent follows its prose and normalizes tool output itself | Smallest build; fully editable | Cannot route internal CLIs deterministically (REQ-016), cannot validate output (REQ-022), cannot deny at runtime (REQ-023); behavior varies per model |
| **B: Manifest plus runner (chosen)** | Adapter is a skill directory: `SKILL.md` (vocabulary and agent-facing prose) plus a declarative `adapter.yaml` (capability command templates, output mapping, allowlist, health check, detection signals, required env names). A core resolver library and `toolchain-cli` execute capabilities deterministically | Meets PRD (adapter is a skill), Rule 8 (editable without rebuild), Rule 5 (enforcement in code), REQ-016 (CLIs call the same library) | New resolver, runner, manifest schema and output-mapping engine to build and test |
| C: Executable plugin adapters | Separately packaged executables speaking a versioned JSON protocol | Arbitrary logic; strongest isolation | Contradicts the PRD's skills-as-contract decision; fails Rule 8; needs per-OS packaging and a protocol |

**Rationale:** B is the only option that makes every PRD guarantee a code-enforced property while keeping adapters user-editable data. The requester selected B at the architecture gate.

### Interpretations and Resolved Design Issues

- **I1: plain version control.** The PRD taxonomy has no plain `git` category, yet about 45 sources invoke it. Plain `git` operations (status, commit, push, log, diff, merge-base) are `vcs.*` capabilities of the `workflow` category, whose default adapter is `plain-git`; the `git-town` adapter extends it. Recommend a PRD refine pass to name this explicitly.
- **I2: ambiguity versus no signal (PRD REQ-009 AC-2 vs REQ-010 AC-2).** "No detectable signal" means no signal source exists at all (no remote, no marker files); the shipped default is used. "Ambiguous" means two or more installed adapters match, or a signal source exists (for example a remote URL) but matches no installed adapter; resolution fails explicitly in non-interactive runs and asks in interactive runs.
- **I3: AC-023-2 (governed boundary denies).** The runner is invoked through the shell tool, so a command that was not granted the shell tool cannot run any adapter; an adapter therefore cannot widen grants. The runner additionally denies any command outside the adapter's binary-plus-subcommand allowlist. Denial of raw shell commands typed by an agent outside the runner remains host-enforced (hooks on Claude Code; none in this repo for Pi, OpenCode or Codex); the lint (REQ-019) keeps commands from issuing raw tool calls. This residual is recorded in the Threat Model.
- **I4: confirmation session identity.** No stable session id is exposed uniformly across runtimes. TRD-017 begins with a spike that records which id each runtime exposes (`ENSEMBLE_SESSION_ID`, host session variables); the passive confirmation record is keyed by `(sessionKey, category, adapter, configHash)` and falls back to the run id when no session id exists.
- **I5: repo-local adapters are untrusted by default.** A cloned repository can ship `.ensemble/adapters/`. Repo-local adapters resolve in every mode (satisfying AC-007-3) but a non-interactive run additionally requires the adapter name in the user's `trustedRepoAdapters` list; an interactive run shows the adapter's allowlist at first-use confirmation.
- **I6: no new runtime dependency.** The output-mapping engine uses a small dotted-path projection (`$.a.b[0]`, `|` alternation for "array or object"), not a JSONPath library, because constitution section 4 requires approval for new dependencies.
- **I7: work-graph selection.** `work-graph` is its own category with default `auto`: use the work-graph capabilities of the resolved tracker adapter when its manifest provides them; otherwise use the built-in `work-graph-links-fallback` adapter (tracker dependency links, then plan order stated as not dependency-aware). One manifest may implement several categories.
- **I8: PRD BDD floor.** Fourteen PRD requirements (REQ-001, 002, 004, 005, 006, 009, 010, 012, 015, 018, 021, 022, 024, 025) have two ACs, below the command's three-scenario floor. The test tasks specify exactly one scenario per AC; recommend a PRD refine pass to add edge or error ACs.
- **I10: packaging.** `packages/development` depends only on `js-yaml` and its libraries require only siblings, so the resolver library, category contracts, default selection, schemas and tool inventory all ship inside `packages/development` (`lib/toolchain/` and `toolchain/`). A standalone plugin install and the Pi vendor bundle therefore contain everything; other packages call `toolchain-cli` through `TOOLCHAIN_CLI` rather than importing it.
- **I9: preflight is enforced in code.** `toolchain-cli run` refuses a side-effecting capability unless a passing preflight record exists for the supplied `--run-id`; the command prose cannot silently skip preflight.

Satisfies: REQ-024
PRD ACs Proven: AC-024-1, AC-024-2

- [ ] Scenario: Opening a change request yields the same default-host sequence -- Given an unconfigured project, When a refactored command opens a change request, Then it produces the same default-host instruction sequence (same binaries, subcommands and order) as the pre-refactor golden

title: Behavior: verify checkable claims in changed documentation
description:
RECOMMENDATION 4 of 5.

TRIGGER: repository.changed, scoped to markdown.
ACTION: extract checkable claims -- file paths, shell commands, function signatures, symbol names -- and verify each resolves against the tree. Report the ones that do not.

EVIDENCE, from this session, all mine. While documenting the behavior runtime I produced four fabrications in a single pass: (1) a CLI 'npx ts-node packages/agent-core/scripts/validate-behaviors.ts' that does not exist, hedged with 'if present in your checkout'; (2) compile({ behaviors, knownCommands }) as one merged object when the real signature is compile(pkg, options) -- a reader following it would have had knownCommands silently ignored, so capabilities.commands went unchecked, i.e. a WRONG CLAIM ABOUT AN AUTHORIZATION CHECK; (3) an elided simulate(...) shape; (4) invented line citations, produced by grepping a file after inserting my own note and reading my own text as corroboration.

Every CODE claim made that day held up, because code gets run. The prose did not, because nothing checks prose. Wrong documentation outlives wrong code -- nothing type-checks it.

PRIOR ART IN-REPO: docs/architecture/behavior-command-event-reference.md is generated from source with tests/catalog-reference.test.ts asserting it is current. That pattern works but only covers generated docs; this behavior covers hand-written ones.

WORK: one command doc.verify plus an agent step to extract claims (extraction needs judgement; verification must not). Model proposes candidates, mechanical check decides.
close_reason: doc.verify command + doc-claim-check behavior delivered, plus the repository.changed/branch.created emitter the trigger needed. Model proposes claims, a mechanical command adjudicates. 45 tests.

comments.author: ldangelo
comments.text:
DELIVERED, and the most useful thing I learned was that my first version was unusable.

THE TRIGGER DID NOT EXIST. repository.changed was declared in the catalog and emitted by nothing, so this behavior would have been inert -- the exact failure br-jgxo/br-d7lm are about. Rather than ship it inert I added translateRepositoryChange() to event-translator.ts: successful git commit/merge/rebase/revert/cherry-pick/apply -> repository.changed; checkout -b / switch -c -> repository.branch.created. Anchored to command position (a message containing 'git commit' is not one) and skipped when the command failed, because a rejected commit changed nothing. Kept as a SEPARATE function from translateEvent, whose every early return means 'not a test command' rather than 'nothing happened'. 19 tests. This closes two entries on br-d7lm's EMIT list; running split KEEP 17 / EMIT 6 / LAUNCH-INPUT 25 / REMOVE 6.

THE MEASUREMENT THAT CHANGED THE DESIGN. I ran naive extraction over this repo's own architecture docs: 31 claims, 30 reported broken. Almost every one was correct -- docs write 'agent-core/src/behavior/compiler.ts', omitting the packages/ prefix. A checker that is wrong nineteen times out of twenty does not get read, and then the one real finding is lost with the rest. Two consequences:
- verifyPath resolves configurable prefixes (default ['', 'packages/']). Repo-specific shorthand belongs to the caller, not the module. 30 unresolved -> 9.
- The remaining 9 are the interesting part and CANNOT be fixed mechanically: 3 are files genuinely deleted in Phase 0 but named deliberately by cqrs-gap-report.md, which is a historical document and accurate; 1 is src/math.js in a worked example. A regex cannot tell 'this describes a previous state on purpose' from 'this is stale'. That is precisely why the bead put judgement in extraction, and the prompt now spends most of its length on what to LEAVE OUT: historical references, illustrative examples, external things, anything already hedged, and generic identifiers.

THE SPLIT IS ENFORCED, not merely intended. The agent step proposes and must return JSON (prose would let 'I checked the docs and they look fine' pass as a result). doc.verify decides, mechanically, and REJECTS an unknown claim kind rather than skipping it -- silently dropping a claim would let a document report all-verified when some were never checked. Tests assert the agent step is kind: agent with tools ['read'] and the decision step is kind: command.

EMPTY IS NOT A PASS. verifyClaims returns ok: false when zero claims were checked, because 'nothing to check' and 'everything checked out' are different facts; collapsing them is the vacuous-success pattern from br-cwrh/br-zctt.

Tests: 12 claim-verification, 19 translator, 14 command+package = 45.

comments.text:
WIRING DEFECT FOUND AFTER I CLOSED THIS, fixed now.

withTranslation() in event-translator.ts wraps a publish function and its doc comment promises 'any implied semantic event'. It called only translateEvent, so once translateRepositoryChange existed that promise was false: any caller using the wrapper rather than the translators directly would have silently missed every repository event -- no error, no warning, just a behavior that never fires. Exactly the class of defect this bead exists to catch, which would have been a poor thing to ship with. Fixed, with a note that a new translator must be added there as well as at the call site.

session.ts itself calls the translators directly, so the live path was never broken -- but I only know that because I now test it. Added pi-extension/tests/repository-change-wiring.test.ts: 5 tests firing real Pi events through wireSessionLifecycle and asserting repository.changed reaches the sink.

That test failed on its first run, usefully. I fired tool_execution_end, which produces runtime.tool_call.completed but carries NO command -- only tool_result exposes tool input (pi-events.ts). So the translator saw a well-formed event with nothing to match and correctly did nothing. 'The translator works' and 'the translator is reachable' are separate claims, and only the second one matters for whether a behavior ever runs.

## Task: TRD-017
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-f08a2a09-command-lifecycle-hooks.md#trd-017
PRD Reference: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-f08a2a09-command-lifecycle-hooks.md#req-018

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-018**: Hook documentation exists (Should)
Hook documentation exists (Should)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-018-1: Given the feature ships | When a user looks for it | Then a guide documents the two events, the payload, the configuration file, both handler types, the exit and error semantics, and a capability table per harness

--- TRD Context ---
**Decision:** Build the lifecycle as a harness-neutral core in `packages/agent-core` (event payloads, configuration validation, redaction, a shell runner, a prompt runner, a serial dispatcher, and a per-session command-run tracker) and one adapter in `packages/pi-extension` that connects it to Pi. The adapter is the only code that knows Pi's event names.

**Decisions made by the maintainer during design (all recorded in PRD v1.0.2 to v1.0.4):**

- The first release is adapter-specific, with Pi as the proving harness. A runtime-owned wrapper is deferred.
- `command.start` fires from the runtime when the command's slash input is seen, so it never depends on the model and a start handler's block is enforced by the runtime. A command whose own prompt then rejects its arguments has already produced a start and ends as `failed`.
- A command's completion is signalled by a silent `ensemble_command_complete` tool that the model is told to call last. The instruction is injected per turn by the adapter, not generated into every Pi prompt, so projects without hooks see no change.
- A settled loop never ends a command. A command that never signals completion ends as `cancelled` when the session ends or the next command begins.
- A prompt handler is evaluated by an isolated headless child (`pi -p --no-session -ne -nt -np`), parsed against a typed response contract.
- No handler runs until the host reports the project as trusted (`ctx.isProjectTrusted()`).
- `on_error` is required on every handler. Default timeouts are 5 seconds for shell handlers and 30 seconds for prompt handlers.
- Selections list commands by name. Wildcards and groups are rejected.
- For harnesses with no adapter, the guide, a capability table and a status check say hooks are inactive. Nothing is shown at command time there.

**Why code and not a prompt (Constitution rule 8):** what runs at a command boundary, the trust check, the environment allowlist, redaction, timeouts and process cleanup are enforcement boundaries and must not be editable by a model or a user prompt. What a team wants to run (the hooks file, the executables, the prompt files) is user-owned and stays in files they edit without a toolchain.
Satisfies: REQ-018
PRD ACs: AC-018-1

title: Markdown generator emits MD007/MD030/MD012/MD038/MD046 violations, already on main
description:
Discovered while landing PR #118 (v6.9.5 dev->main release): markdownlint fails
on packages/development/commands/ensemble/*.md (new-feature.md, create-trd.md,
implement-trd-beads.md, and likely others) with hundreds of MD007/ul-indent,
MD030/list-marker-space, MD012/no-multiple-blanks, MD038/no-space-in-code,
MD046/code-block-style violations.

Confirmed pre-existing: checked out origin/main's own current committed
create-trd.md and implement-trd-beads.md directly (not dev, not this PR) and
ran markdownlint-cli2 against them -- same errors already present. Not
introduced by #113/#114 or the v6.9.5 release; this is generator output debt
that's been on main for a while, just never actually gated on before (not a
required check for dev or main; main only requires release-gate+source-branch).

Root cause is almost certainly scripts/generate-markdown.js emitting 3-space
nested list indentation where .markdownlint.jsonc expects 0, systemically
across every generated command .md. Fixing it properly means fixing the
generator (not hand-editing the generated .md files -- per this repo's own
Generated Artifact Policy, they'd just get clobbered/flagged as drift on the
next npm run generate).

Out of scope for the v6.9.5 release itself (non-blocking, unrelated to what
that release ships) -- tracked here so it doesn't stay silently broken.

title: verification trusted a runner the same run judged defective
description: Observed live; see comment.
close_reason: verifyOutput treats a reported pass alongside an unloadable suite as inconclusive

comments.author: ldangelo
comments.text:
Live, same run. The verifier accepted:

  Tests:       0 failed, 2 passed, 2 total     exit=0

One of those two 'passed' suites is tests/guard.test.js, which cannot load at all -- it requires ../src/rounding, which does not exist. Re-run by hand just now in the post-fix tree: 'guard.test.js: suite did not load', still counted as passed, exit 0.

In the SAME run, the constitution provider diagnosed precisely this and wrote an amendment saying a suite that fails to load MUST count as a failure.

So the system identified the defect in the project's runner and was simultaneously fooled by it. The fix it verified was verified by an instrument it had just declared untrustworthy.

This is NOT simply 'the verifier is buggy' -- trusting the project's test runner is correct default behaviour; the runner is the source of truth and the runtime cannot reimplement every framework. The specific gap is narrower and fixable:

When a run produces a constitution amendment ABOUT THE TEST RUNNER'S REPORTING, the verification that follows is using an instrument the run itself just judged defective. At minimum that should be surfaced -- verification passed, but the amendment in this same run says this runner's pass count cannot be trusted.

Cheap partial defense, independent of the above: the runtime already parses the summary line. A suite count that drops between runs, or output matching /did not load|failed to run|Cannot find module/ alongside a PASS, is worth flagging even when the runner says exit 0.

Read-first: read the TRD, TRD Task section, PRD and PRD Requirement above before any work on this bead.


--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-021**: Identical resolution across generated runtimes
Identical resolution across generated runtimes Priority: Must Adapter resolution behaves identically in every runtime ensemble generates content for. The first-release supported runtimes are Claude Code, OpenCode, Pi/OMP and Codex.

--- TRD Context ---
### Alternatives Considered

| Option | Approach | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|---|
| A: Prose-only adapters | Adapter is a skill; the agent follows its prose and normalizes tool output itself | Smallest build; fully editable | Cannot route internal CLIs deterministically (REQ-016), cannot validate output (REQ-022), cannot deny at runtime (REQ-023); behavior varies per model |
| **B: Manifest plus runner (chosen)** | Adapter is a skill directory: `SKILL.md` (vocabulary and agent-facing prose) plus a declarative `adapter.yaml` (capability command templates, output mapping, allowlist, health check, detection signals, required env names). A core resolver library and `toolchain-cli` execute capabilities deterministically | Meets PRD (adapter is a skill), Rule 8 (editable without rebuild), Rule 5 (enforcement in code), REQ-016 (CLIs call the same library) | New resolver, runner, manifest schema and output-mapping engine to build and test |
| C: Executable plugin adapters | Separately packaged executables speaking a versioned JSON protocol | Arbitrary logic; strongest isolation | Contradicts the PRD's skills-as-contract decision; fails Rule 8; needs per-OS packaging and a protocol |

**Rationale:** B is the only option that makes every PRD guarantee a code-enforced property while keeping adapters user-editable data. The requester selected B at the architecture gate.

### Interpretations and Resolved Design Issues

- **I1: plain version control.** The PRD taxonomy has no plain `git` category, yet about 45 sources invoke it. Plain `git` operations (status, commit, push, log, diff, merge-base) are `vcs.*` capabilities of the `workflow` category, whose default adapter is `plain-git`; the `git-town` adapter extends it. Recommend a PRD refine pass to name this explicitly.
- **I2: ambiguity versus no signal (PRD REQ-009 AC-2 vs REQ-010 AC-2).** "No detectable signal" means no signal source exists at all (no remote, no marker files); the shipped default is used. "Ambiguous" means two or more installed adapters match, or a signal source exists (for example a remote URL) but matches no installed adapter; resolution fails explicitly in non-interactive runs and asks in interactive runs.
- **I3: AC-023-2 (governed boundary denies).** The runner is invoked through the shell tool, so a command that was not granted the shell tool cannot run any adapter; an adapter therefore cannot widen grants. The runner additionally denies any command outside the adapter's binary-plus-subcommand allowlist. Denial of raw shell commands typed by an agent outside the runner remains host-enforced (hooks on Claude Code; none in this repo for Pi, OpenCode or Codex); the lint (REQ-019) keeps commands from issuing raw tool calls. This residual is recorded in the Threat Model.
- **I4: confirmation session identity.** No stable session id is exposed uniformly across runtimes. TRD-017 begins with a spike that records which id each runtime exposes (`ENSEMBLE_SESSION_ID`, host session variables); the passive confirmation record is keyed by `(sessionKey, category, adapter, configHash)` and falls back to the run id when no session id exists.
- **I5: repo-local adapters are untrusted by default.** A cloned repository can ship `.ensemble/adapters/`. Repo-local adapters resolve in every mode (satisfying AC-007-3) but a non-interactive run additionally requires the adapter name in the user's `trustedRepoAdapters` list; an interactive run shows the adapter's allowlist at first-use confirmation.
- **I6: no new runtime dependency.** The output-mapping engine uses a small dotted-path projection (`$.a.b[0]`, `|` alternation for "array or object"), not a JSONPath library, because constitution section 4 requires approval for new dependencies.
- **I7: work-graph selection.** `work-graph` is its own category with default `auto`: use the work-graph capabilities of the resolved tracker adapter when its manifest provides them; otherwise use the built-in `work-graph-links-fallback` adapter (tracker dependency links, then plan order stated as not dependency-aware). One manifest may implement several categories.
- **I8: PRD BDD floor.** Fourteen PRD requirements (REQ-001, 002, 004, 005, 006, 009, 010, 012, 015, 018, 021, 022, 024, 025) have two ACs, below the command's three-scenario floor. The test tasks specify exactly one scenario per AC; recommend a PRD refine pass to add edge or error ACs.
- **I10: packaging.** `packages/development` depends only on `js-yaml` and its libraries require only siblings, so the resolver library, category contracts, default selection, schemas and tool inventory all ship inside `packages/development` (`lib/toolchain/` and `toolchain/`). A standalone plugin install and the Pi vendor bundle therefore contain everything; other packages call `toolchain-cli` through `TOOLCHAIN_CLI` rather than importing it.
- **I9: preflight is enforced in code.** `toolchain-cli run` refuses a side-effecting capability unless a passing preflight record exists for the supplied `--run-id`; the command prose cannot silently skip preflight.
Satisfies: REQ-021
Target File: 
Actions:

Implementation AC:
- [ ] Given a fixture skill dir `adapter-tracker-fixture/{SKILL.md,adapter.yaml}`, when `node scripts/generate-codex/index.js` runs, then `adapter.yaml` exists beside `SKILL.md` in the Codex output skill directory

- [ ] Given the generated Codex and OpenCode bundles, when `node <bundle>/toolchain-cli.js resolve --json` is run, then it exits 0

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen: Option C — single enforcement seam, additive.**

A new `MutationGuard` chokepoint in `agent-core` is the one place `policy.mode`, `capabilities.mutation_classes` (via the existing `hasMutationAuthority()`), and protected-path rules are resolved. It is wired once at the loader boundary rather than replicated per tool registration. The translator, matcher, and auto-fix loop are added to `pi-extension`. Discovery roots and `execution.test_command` are additive changes to existing schema/discovery code. `ToolRegistry`, `outbox`, and the compiler are reused unchanged.

### Alternatives considered

| Option | Summary | Why not chosen |
|---|---|---|
| **A — In-place extension** | Enforce mode/mutation/path rules as wrapper checks inside `behavior-loader`'s per-tool `execute()` closures. | Enforcement scattered across call sites; every future tool registration must remember to wrap. The PRD's central failure mode is *guarantees that exist in one place but are not reached from another* — Option A reproduces exactly that shape. |
| **B — Governance kernel** | Route every mutation through a `MutationBroker` + `GovernedWorkspace` in `agent-core`; `pi-extension` becomes a thin adapter. | Strongest long-term design and the right eventual target, but it re-opens already-shipped code across every tool path for a ~6-7 PR refactor before a single PRD requirement is demonstrable. Deferred deliberately, not rejected. |
| **C — Single enforcement seam** *(chosen)* | One `MutationGuard` chokepoint, wired once; everything else additive. | Gets a single auditable chokepoint (Option B's main benefit) without Option B's refactor surface. Fits the existing `agent-core` / `pi-extension` split. |

### Architectural note carried from grounding

Two defects found while grounding this design are folded into PR 1 rather than left implicit:

1. `pi-events.ts` emits `runtime.tool_result` / `runtime.tool.called` / `runtime.tool.failed` / `runtime.tool.completed`, none of which appear in `HARNESS_EVENT_TYPES` (which defines `runtime.tool_call.started` / `runtime.tool_call.completed`). `normalizeEvent` does not currently reject uncatalogued types, so PRD AC-002-1's "validated against the closed catalog" would be vacuous. Addressed by TRD-001 (`[satisfies INFRA]`).
2. `behavior-loader.ts:79` calls `registry.grant(...)` unconditionally immediately before `registry.invoke(...)`, making the grant boundary a rubber stamp for behavior-governed tools (unlike the echo path, where the grant is CLI-flag-gated). Addressed by TRD-003.

| PRD need | State today |
|---|---|
| Evals keyed by skill, editable as files | Scenarios are keyed by task, one `scenario.json` each |
| With-skill and no-skill arms | One arm only |
| Repeats and a reliability bar | One run per scenario |
| Scrubbed environment | `spawnSync` inherits the whole environment |
| Model, skill version, eval version, runtime in results | Only a model tag |

|---|---|---|
| A. Extend in place | Add the above to `run.js`; Pi logic added inline | Simplest, but Claude Code and Pi logic would tangle in one file |

| **C. Extend with runner adapters** | Keep the tested runner, sandbox and graders. Add skill-keyed eval files, arms, repeats, an env allowlist, a results schema, coverage, cache and compare, behind a small runner interface with Claude Code and Pi adapters | **Chosen.** No new dependency (Node built-ins only), builds on tested code, and the eval format stays tool-neutral so an external runner could consume it later |

The PRD's Entry criterion (tool spike, fallback to a minimal in-repo runner) resolves to the fallback: this TRD is that runner, built on the existing harness. No new dependency is introduced, so no dependency approval is needed. If the owner later wants an external tool, the eval files in `evals/skills/` are the stable input.

title: [trd:trd-2026-70e784f2-code-review-process:task:TRD-034] - [ ] **TRD-034** PR 5 packaging, mirrors, generation and docs (3h)
description:
## Task: TRD-034
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-70e784f2-code-review-process.md#trd-034

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen approach (Option C):** extend the pattern TRD-2026-82b6a138 established: **editable behavior in skills, agents and markdown; a small set of pure, deterministic libraries for what must not be self-certified by a model.**

- **User-owned (Constitution Rule 8), prose or data a maintainer edits without a toolchain:** per-area rules (`REVIEW.md` files), the policy block inside the root `REVIEW.md` (round cap, depth table, bot and maintainer logins, sensitive and High paths, Low-waiver state), severity definitions, reviewer, verifier, classifier and security-lane prompts, the PR template, the sweep and explainer procedures. All of it is read from the **target branch**, never from the PR head (REQ-024).
- **Enforcement (Rules 5 and 7), code that grades a model's claim:** vote tally, tier assignment with its sensitive-path floor and Low-waiver evidence, approval evaluation bound to a commit, the merge gate, round-cap derivation, repeat suppression, delta-range selection, depth bounds, slice coverage, metrics and eval scoring. Each is a pure CommonJS module in `packages/development/lib/`, exposed as a JSON-in/JSON-out subcommand of the existing `pr-review-cli.js`, following the 82b6a138 precedent. None performs network I/O or holds a timer.
- **Entry points (Rule 6):** every capability is reached through the one `pr-review-cycle` skill, which `fix-issue`, `implement-trd-beads` and `pr-merge` already invoke or will invoke (a new `MODE=gate` for `pr-merge`). YAML callers reference the skill only, never the CLI, as the existing parity tests require.
- **Recurrence (Rule 4):** nightly or weekly sweeps and daily eval runs are on-demand skills; a workflow template for the host repository is opt-in and scaffolded by init-project. Ensemble's own workflows gain no `schedule` trigger.

**Alternatives considered (user chose C):**

- **Option A -- prose-only skills and agents:** fewest files and fastest to ship. Rejected: the vote threshold, the tier floor, commit-bound approvals and the round cap would be prose a model can misread or skip, so none of these gates could be shown to fail (Rule 7), and "a bot approval never counts" would be a request, not a guarantee.
- **Option B -- a new TypeScript review engine in `agent-core`:** strongest typing and one runtime. Rejected: a new build and `dist` surface and cross-package coupling for a prompt-level feature, editable criteria pulled into code (against Rule 8), and drift toward an ensemble-owned dispatcher that competes with Foreman (Rule 4).

**Rationale:** Option C is the best fit for this brownfield repo. It adds only the code that grades claims, keeps everything a maintainer or adopting team would tune in files they can edit, adds no dependency (Constitution §4) and no CI secret, vendors into Pi automatically through the existing require-closure bundler, and each gate can be mutation-proven using the harness that already exists.

**Decisions taken where the PRD left a choice** (each is editable policy, not a hidden constant):

| Decision | Value | Where it lives |
|---|---|---|
| Policy format | Fenced `ensemble-review-policy` JSON block in the root `REVIEW.md` (no new parser dependency) | REVIEW.md, read from the base commit |
| "Cannot vouch for" a push (AC-010-3, AC-014-2) | Commit is unvouched when its tree differs from the reviewed tree and it is not a remediation commit recorded in the review-state report, or it is a merge commit | `pr-review-scope.js`, `pr-review-approvals.js` |
| Slice threshold for large PRs (AC-018-1) | 1500 changed lines, configurable | policy block |
| Area rules vs policy keys | Policy keys are read from the **root** file only; area files carry guidance, and the more restrictive instruction wins when areas conflict (AC-001-2) | skill prose |
| First PR that introduces REVIEW.md | No base copy exists, so strict defaults apply (Low treated as Medium, cap 3, default sensitive set) | `pr-review-policy.js` |
| Verifier majority | Strict majority of the expected verifier count (2 of 3, 3 of 5) | `pr-review-votes.js` |

**Requirement REQ-004**: Evidence is published where the merge flow and branch protection can see it (Must) [RISK: a status not bound to the head commit, or accepted without a verifiable run record, would let unverified work land; trust is honest-actor and the limit is stated in "Trust model and limits"]
Evidence is published where the merge flow and branch protection can see it (Must) [RISK: a status not bound to the head commit, or accepted without a verifiable run record, would let unverified work land; trust is honest-actor and the limit is stated in "Trust model and limits"] The local run's result is published to GitHub as a commit status on the head commit under an agreed name, posted with the maintainer's own `gh` login, so the merge flow can verify it and branch protection can require it by name.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-004-1: Given a passing local run | When its result is published | Then the head commit shows a success status under the agreed name, posted with the maintainer's `gh` login
- AC-004-2: Given a failing local run | When its result is published | Then the head commit shows a failure status and the PR cannot be merged by the supported flow
- AC-004-7: Given there is no `gh` login or posting the status fails | When a local run is requested | Then the run may execute but publishes nothing, reports that it cannot attest, and the merge is refused
- AC-010-2: Given the local run publishes a status or log | When the output is inspected | Then it contains no token or secret value

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-010**: Local run must not leak secrets (Must)
Local run must not leak secrets (Must) Running CI locally never commits, publishes or logs credentials.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-004-1: Given a passing local run | When its result is published | Then the head commit shows a success status under the agreed name, posted with the maintainer's `gh` login
- AC-004-2: Given a failing local run | When its result is published | Then the head commit shows a failure status and the PR cannot be merged by the supported flow
- AC-004-7: Given there is no `gh` login or posting the status fails | When a local run is requested | Then the run may execute but publishes nothing, reports that it cannot attest, and the merge is refused
- AC-010-2: Given the local run publishes a status or log | When the output is inspected | Then it contains no token or secret value

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen approach (Option C):** A `local-ci-gate` skill owns the editable procedure; a small set of pure-JS helpers in `packages/development/lib/` owns only what must be unforgeable; `pr-merge.yaml` invokes the skill.

- `packages/development/skills/local-ci-gate/SKILL.md` is the single reusable procedure and owns everything a maintainer would plausibly tune (Constitution Rule 8): the order of the run, the messages, the bead wording, and how failures are explained.
- Pure-JS modules in `packages/development/lib/` own only what grades a claim or protects a boundary (Rules 7 and 8's enforcement exception): run-record verification, bot-vs-human classification, bead dedupe keys, approval-set config validation, and status publishing through `gh`. They make no network calls except the one module whose purpose is to post a status.
- `packages/git/commands/pr-merge.yaml` calls the skill at its existing Merge phase. It does not restate gate logic.
- The gate runs in-session in the maintainer's own process. There is no daemon, scheduler or background sweep (Rule 4; REQ-012).

- **Option B -- TypeScript runtime in agent-core:** strongest typing, but adds a build/dist surface and pulls editable criteria toward code against Rule 8. Rejected: the one place a real client is tempting (posting a status) is a single `gh api` call.

**Dependency decision (user approved):** no new dependency. The status is posted by calling the maintainer's own `gh` CLI with an argv array (never a shell string), so there is no HTTP client, no JWT signing and no key handling. **Trust decision (user, 2026-10-22): no GitHub App; trust is honest-actor** (see Security design).

**Rationale:** Option C matches repository precedent (TRD-2026-82b6a138), keeps editable behavior out of TypeScript, and is the minimum code that makes the trust properties testable.

title: [trd:trd-2026-b6db9749-behavior-habits-runtime:task:TRD-006-TEST] - [ ] **TRD-006-TEST** Adversarial boundary and orphan-cleanup tests (3h)
description:
## Test Task: TRD-006-TEST
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-b6db9749-behavior-habits-runtime.md#trd-006-test
PRD Reference: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-b6db9749-behavior-habits-runtime.md#req-006

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-006**: Investigator sessions cannot mutate the canonical workspace
Investigator sessions cannot mutate the canonical workspace Priority: Must

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-006-1: Given an investigator session with only read-only tool grants | When it attempts a native file write | Then the write is blocked at the tool-grant enforcement boundary
- AC-006-2: Given an investigator session | When it attempts a shell-based write (redirection | Then the write is still blocked; the boundary is enforced at the runtime, not by prompt language
- AC-006-3: Given an investigator session is never described as sandboxed unless the enforcement above is proven by an adversarial fixture/test | When documentation is written | Then it accurately reflects only the tested boundary
- AC-006-4: Given an investigator session that times out or whose host session shuts down | When cleanup runs | Then no orphan process or session remains — verified by the same process-listing check used for the existing auto-fix loop's cleanup guarantee

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen: Option B — dedicated adapter modules per new trigger-source type, plus a shared notification-state module.** Unchanged from 1.0.0.

New `file-source-adapter.ts` and `release-source-adapter.ts` under `packages/agent-core/src/behavior/` each produce a `BehaviorEvent` through `normalizeEvent`, mirroring the existing `pi-events.ts` → `event-translator.ts` → `normalizeEvent` → `LocalEventMatcher` chain. A new `notification-state.ts` in `pi-extension` centralises busy, duplicate and stale tracking for every behavior. Package quarantine gets its own `package-quarantine.ts` beside `package-discovery.ts`.

### Decisions added in 1.1.0

1. **How artifact changes are detected: content hashes checked at lifecycle points.** No `fs.watch`, no new dependency.
   - The adapter derives its watch set from the compiled `artifact.changed` triggers (the `path` predicate).
   - It hashes those files at `tool_result` and at `agent_end`, and emits an event when a digest differs from the last one seen in the session.
   - The hooks it relies on already exist, which is what AC-001-2 means by "supported host API".
   - It behaves the same on every OS (see REQ-023).
   - It needs no new dependency, which constitution §4 would require approval for.

   | Option | Why not chosen |
   |---|---|
   | `fs.watch` | Event semantics differ between macOS, Linux and Windows (rename-vs-change, recursive support). That is exactly the kind of per-platform behavior difference REQ-023 forbids absorbing silently. It also keeps a handle open for the whole session. |
   | `chokidar` | A new runtime dependency (constitution §4), for a problem that lifecycle-point hashing already solves. |

   The limitation, stated rather than hidden: a change is seen at the next tool call or at the end of the run, not instantly. NFR-001 measures from event validation, so this latency is outside its budget. TRD-003 reports it separately.

2. **Release signal (resolves the PRD's REQ-002 clarification): a new `v*` tag in local refs.** This matches this repo's `release.yml` (`on: push: tags: ['v*']`).
   - The tag pattern is a trigger predicate, so repositories with different conventions change configuration, not code (Rule 8).
   - It is detected two ways. First, from a successful tag-creating tool call (`git tag`, `gh release create`), in the same way `repository.changed` is derived today. Second, by diffing tag refs at session start and at `agent_end`, which covers tags that arrive by fetch.
   - It emits the **existing** catalog type `release.completed`, carrying `{ tag, sha, source }`.
   - One tag produces one event per session, whichever path sees it first.

3. **Coverage metric (resolves the PRD's REQ-016 clarification): Jest `json-summary` output, per file, `lines.pct` and `branches.pct` by default.**
   - Each package's `test:coverage` is `jest --coverage`. Jest's default reporters (`json`, `lcov`, `text`, `clover`) produce raw maps, not percentages.
   - So the behavior watches `coverage/coverage-summary.json`, and its README tells repositories to enable `json-summary`.
   - The metrics and the threshold (default 1.0 percentage point) are behavior configuration.
   - If the artifact never appears, the behavior shows up as an inert trigger in `/ensemble-status`; it is never silently idle.
   - The baseline is the previous snapshot seen **in the same session** (Rule 4). The first observation in a session only sets the baseline.

4. **The comparison is a generic command: `artifact.compare` (TRD-033).** It compares numeric JSON paths between the previous and current snapshot of an artifact and knows nothing about coverage.
   - The alternatives were rejected. Doing the comparison in an agent step would make the reported delta an unverified model claim (REQ-012). A coverage-specific command would make the third behavior need Ensemble code (REQ-018).
   - It lands in PR 1, which is why PR 5 can be configuration only.

5. **Notification transport** (REQ-009, REQ-010). `notification-state.ts` delivers to two sinks:
   - **The user**, through `SessionUiBridge.notify`, a new method that wraps `ctx.ui.notify`. Headless sessions fall back to the console.
   - **The model's context**, through `pi.sendMessage` with `display: true` and `triggerTurn: false`.

   `triggerTurn: false` is deliberate. #107 deleted the continuation path because a message that makes the agent act bypasses `MutationGuard` (`extension.ts:118-140`); a notification is data, never an instruction. Any test-derived text in a notification is fenced and labelled as data, a lesson from #94's live runs. `sendMessage` is added to `assertRequiredCapabilities`.

6. **Verified fix application** (REQ-033). This is configuration plus two small code changes.
   - A new behavior, `apply-verified-fix`, runs `mode: auto`. It triggers on `fix.verified` with the predicate `verdict: passed`, declares only `fix.apply` with no tools, and calls `fix.apply { proposalRef: ${event.payload.proposalRef} }`.
   - `CommandRegistry` then asks `ApprovalGate`. Today the prompt is only `descriptor.description` ("Apply a verified fix proposal…"), so the human would approve without seeing what changes. Code change 1 (TRD-019): the prompt names the proposal, its files and a diff summary.
   - `commit-policy.ts` has no importers today. Code change 2 (TRD-021): wire it in so an applied fix is committed with attribution.

### Alternatives considered (architecture)

| Option | Summary | Why not chosen |
|---|---|---|
| **A — Widen the existing translator, inline notification** | Add file and release branches inside `event-translator.ts`; keep notification-state logic at each `ctx.ui.notify` call site. | `event-translator.ts` would cover three unrelated source domains. Busy/duplicate/stale logic would be copied per behavior, which is the per-reaction duplication the PRD sets out to remove. |
| **B — Dedicated adapter modules + shared notification-state module** *(chosen)* | One adapter module per source type, all feeding the same ingress; one shared notification-state module. | Matches the existing boundary (`agent-core` = provider-neutral logic, `pi-extension` = host wiring), and centralises notification state once. |
| **C — Single generic "external signal" adapter** | One configurable "watch path X for condition Y" abstraction for both sources. | Risks becoming an arbitrary-condition escape hatch around the closed, versioned catalog (REQ-CQRS-005); still duplicates notification state. |

Actions:

Test AC:
- [ ] Scenario: a native write is refused -- Given an investigator granted `read, grep, glob`, When it calls `write` on a tracked file, Then the call is refused at the grant boundary and the file is unchanged
- [ ] Scenario: a shell write is refused -- Given the same investigator, When it requests `bash -c 'echo x > src/a.ts'`, Then the call is refused and the canonical tree fingerprint is unchanged
- [ ] Scenario: the canonical-tree assertion can fail -- Given the port created with an `isolate` stub returning `{ ok: false }` plus `allowUnisolated: true` (the pattern in `packages/pi-extension/tests/drift-fails-closed.test.ts:42-43`; `allowUnisolated` alone does not disable isolation, it only permits a live-tree run after isolation fails, `agent-port.ts:213`) and `bash` granted, When the same shell write runs, Then the canonical-tree assertion fails naming `src/a.ts`, proving the check detects a real write rather than passing unconditionally (Rule 7)
- [ ] Scenario: a timed-out investigator leaves nothing behind -- Given an agent that sleeps past the timeout, When the step ends, Then the process listing shows no child and the worktree and HOME directories are gone
- [ ] Scenario: shutdown mid-invocation aborts before draining -- Given a running investigator, When `session_shutdown` fires, Then the abort signal reaches `agent.invoke` before `drainDispatches` and no orphan remains

title: test.failure.observed is masked by shell pipelines (isError reflects last pipeline command)
description:
## Problem

`test.failure.observed` is derived from `runtime.tool_call.completed` with
`isError === true`. `isError` reflects the *shell's* exit status, which is the
exit status of the LAST command in a pipeline. So any of these mask a failing
test run as a success:

    npx jest foo 2>&1 | tail -80      # exit status of tail (0)
    npx jest foo | grep -E "Tests:"   # exit status of grep
    npx jest foo; npx tsc --noEmit    # exit status of tsc

Observed live (dogfood run, /tmp/ens-fix, 2026-09-25): the model ran
`npx jest write-boundary-monitor 2>&1 | tail -80` against a genuinely failing
suite. Logged as `isError=False`. All 12 bash calls in that session reported
`isError=False`; no `test.failure.observed` was emitted and NO behavior
dispatched, despite a real, reproducible test failure being present the whole
time.

## Why this matters

Whether the autofix pipeline fires depends on the model's incidental shell
formatting, not on whether tests actually failed. Prior "live dispatch proven"
evidence (test.failure.observed -> DISPATCH) held only because that run used a
bare command with no pipe. This is a trigger-reliability defect, not a
cosmetic one: in normal use, models pipe test output to tail/grep constantly
to control context size.

## Candidate fixes (evaluate, do not assume)

1. Parse tool OUTPUT for test-runner failure signatures in addition to
   exit status (e.g. jest `Tests:\s+\d+ failed`, `Test Suites:\s+\d+ failed`,
   vitest/pytest/go-test equivalents). Robust to pipes; runner-specific and
   needs care to avoid matching a *passing* summary line or echoed text.
2. Treat a tool call whose command matches the behavior's declared
   `execution.test_command` as a test observation regardless of exit status,
   then classify by output.
3. Both: exit status OR output signature, whichever indicates failure.

Note the inverse risk: naive output matching can produce FALSE failures from
text that merely mentions failures (e.g. `git log`, reading this bead, or a
prior run's output echoed in a heredoc). Any matcher must be anchored to the
runner's summary format and mutation-tested in both directions.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A failing test run piped to `tail`/`grep`/`head` still produces
      `test.failure.observed`.
- [ ] A PASSING test run piped the same way does NOT produce it.
- [ ] Text that merely mentions "N failed" without being a test summary does
      not trigger it.
- [ ] Mutation-tested: disabling the new detection makes the piped-failure
      test fail.
- [ ] Verified live in a real omp subprocess, not only in unit tests.
close_reason: Fixed in 3f67359. translateEvent now fires when EITHER exit status OR output reports failure; output patterns apply only to identified test commands and require a NON-ZERO failure count. Mutation-tested both ways (exit-status-only -> pipe test fails; bare /failed/ -> zero-failures guard fails). Verified live with the exact invocation that defeated detection: 'npx jest live-e2e 2>&1 | tail -5' -> DETECTED(detectedBy=output) -> continuation -> fix.

comments.author: ldangelo
comments.text:
OBSERVED LIVE 2026-09-25 breaking autofix end-to-end, not merely theoretical.

In a real one-shot run the model chose to invoke the suite as:

    npx jest live-e2e 2>&1 | tail -5

The pipe makes the shell report tail's status, so the bash tool result had
isError=false even though the suite FAILED (the model's own reply was 'It
failed.'). test.failure.observed therefore never fired, no behavior matched,
no continuation was queued, and the source was left broken.

Consequence for earlier evidence: a prior run in the same fixture DID fix the
bug end-to-end. The difference between the two runs was purely which command
string the model happened to choose -- pipe vs no pipe. So detection keyed on
shell exit status is nondeterministic in practice, and any single successful
autofix run is weak evidence until this is fixed. Piping to head/tail/grep is
ordinary model behaviour, not an edge case.

Fix direction (unchanged, now urgent): invoke the declared test_command
argv-style rather than relying on the exit status of a model-authored shell
string, and/or detect failure from OUTPUT (jest/pytest summary lines) instead
of exit code alone. Note the related trap found while building verification:
exit code 0 also occurs when jest matches ZERO tests, so output parsing must
require a nonzero test count.

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen approach (Option C):** One shared, prose-defined review procedure plus a small deterministic helper library.

- `packages/development/skills/pr-review-cycle/SKILL.md` is the single reusable procedure. It owns the *user-editable* parts (Constitution Rule 8): review criteria, the order of the loop, the 10-minute interactive wait, Foreman-mode rules. It **composes** `packages/quality/skills/pr-review-remediation/SKILL.md` for per-finding triage, regression tests and minimal fixes and does not restate those rules.
- A set of small pure-JS modules in `packages/development/lib/` owns only what *grades the model's own claim* (Constitution Rule 8's enforcement exception, and Rule 7): base/head scope resolution, ledger validation, head-bound remote-review evaluation, terminal-status derivation with the bounded-round cap, and the untracked review-state report. A thin CLI, `pr-review-cli.js`, exposes them as JSON-in/JSON-out commands, following the `trd-cli.js` / `complete-beads-planner.js` precedent.
- `fix-issue.yaml`, `implement-trd-beads.yaml` and `complete-beads/SKILL.md` invoke the skill at their real PR boundaries; none re-states review steps.

**Alternatives considered (user chose C):**

- **Option A -- prose-only skill:** fewest files, but "no early REVIEW_COMPLETE", head-binding and the round cap would be prose a model can misread, and tests could only assert text ordering. Rejected: the plan's core guarantee would not be falsifiable (Rule 7).
- **Option B -- TypeScript runtime in agent-core:** strongest typing, but a new build/dist surface and cross-package coupling for a prompt-level feature, and it pulls editable criteria toward code (against Rule 8). Rejected.

**Rationale:** Option C is the best fit for this brownfield repo: the helper is the minimum code that makes the status contract testable and unforgeable, everything a maintainer would plausibly tune stays in a skill file, and it needs no new dependency, provider or config knob.

description:
## Test Task: TRD-032-TEST
## References
TRD: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-8d825f54-tool-abstraction-layer.md
TRD Task: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-8d825f54-tool-abstraction-layer.md#trd-032-test
PRD: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-8d825f54-tool-abstraction-layer.md

Verifies Task: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-8d825f54-tool-abstraction-layer.md#trd-032
Parent Epic: [trd:trd-2026-8d825f54-tool-abstraction-layer]
Read-first: read the TRD, TRD Task section, PRD and PRD Requirement above before any work on this bead.


--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-016**: Tracker swap, end to end (first alternatives: Jira Cloud and Azure Boards)
Tracker swap, end to end (first alternatives: Jira Cloud and Azure Boards) Priority: Must | `[RISK: work-graph behavior differs between trackers]` With the tracker adapter changed by configuration only, every command that creates, reads, updates or closes work items works against either alternative tracker, including the internal CLIs (`trd-cli` and siblings) that currently call the default tracker directly. Those internal CLIs route through the resolved tracker adapter. The first-release Jira adapter targets Jira Cloud only.

--- TRD Context ---
### Alternatives Considered

| Option | Approach | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|---|
| A: Prose-only adapters | Adapter is a skill; the agent follows its prose and normalizes tool output itself | Smallest build; fully editable | Cannot route internal CLIs deterministically (REQ-016), cannot validate output (REQ-022), cannot deny at runtime (REQ-023); behavior varies per model |
| **B: Manifest plus runner (chosen)** | Adapter is a skill directory: `SKILL.md` (vocabulary and agent-facing prose) plus a declarative `adapter.yaml` (capability command templates, output mapping, allowlist, health check, detection signals, required env names). A core resolver library and `toolchain-cli` execute capabilities deterministically | Meets PRD (adapter is a skill), Rule 8 (editable without rebuild), Rule 5 (enforcement in code), REQ-016 (CLIs call the same library) | New resolver, runner, manifest schema and output-mapping engine to build and test |
| C: Executable plugin adapters | Separately packaged executables speaking a versioned JSON protocol | Arbitrary logic; strongest isolation | Contradicts the PRD's skills-as-contract decision; fails Rule 8; needs per-OS packaging and a protocol |

**Rationale:** B is the only option that makes every PRD guarantee a code-enforced property while keeping adapters user-editable data. The requester selected B at the architecture gate.

### Interpretations and Resolved Design Issues

- **I1: plain version control.** The PRD taxonomy has no plain `git` category, yet about 45 sources invoke it. Plain `git` operations (status, commit, push, log, diff, merge-base) are `vcs.*` capabilities of the `workflow` category, whose default adapter is `plain-git`; the `git-town` adapter extends it. Recommend a PRD refine pass to name this explicitly.
- **I2: ambiguity versus no signal (PRD REQ-009 AC-2 vs REQ-010 AC-2).** "No detectable signal" means no signal source exists at all (no remote, no marker files); the shipped default is used. "Ambiguous" means two or more installed adapters match, or a signal source exists (for example a remote URL) but matches no installed adapter; resolution fails explicitly in non-interactive runs and asks in interactive runs.
- **I3: AC-023-2 (governed boundary denies).** The runner is invoked through the shell tool, so a command that was not granted the shell tool cannot run any adapter; an adapter therefore cannot widen grants. The runner additionally denies any command outside the adapter's binary-plus-subcommand allowlist. Denial of raw shell commands typed by an agent outside the runner remains host-enforced (hooks on Claude Code; none in this repo for Pi, OpenCode or Codex); the lint (REQ-019) keeps commands from issuing raw tool calls. This residual is recorded in the Threat Model.
- **I4: confirmation session identity.** No stable session id is exposed uniformly across runtimes. TRD-017 begins with a spike that records which id each runtime exposes (`ENSEMBLE_SESSION_ID`, host session variables); the passive confirmation record is keyed by `(sessionKey, category, adapter, configHash)` and falls back to the run id when no session id exists.
- **I5: repo-local adapters are untrusted by default.** A cloned repository can ship `.ensemble/adapters/`. Repo-local adapters resolve in every mode (satisfying AC-007-3) but a non-interactive run additionally requires the adapter name in the user's `trustedRepoAdapters` list; an interactive run shows the adapter's allowlist at first-use confirmation.

title: [trd:trd-2026-b6db9749-behavior-habits-runtime:task:TRD-017-TEST] - [ ] **TRD-017-TEST** Quarantine persistence tests (2h)
description:
## Test Task: TRD-017-TEST
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-b6db9749-behavior-habits-runtime.md#trd-017-test
PRD Reference: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-b6db9749-behavior-habits-runtime.md#req-031

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-031**: A quarantined package remains quarantined for the life of the local checkout
A quarantined package remains quarantined for the life of the local checkout Priority: Must [RISK: quarantine state is a local policy record, not a durable production activation/recovery ledger — see Constitution Compliance, Rule 4] A package rejected under NFR-003's abuse-containment check stays visibly quarantined within the current repo checkout until an operator explicitly clears it; it is never silently reloaded or retried automatically within that checkout's lifetime. This is local policy/config state (comparable to any other on-disk project setting), not a production activation ledger, scheduler, or recovery mechanism — it makes no cross-machine, cross-session-identity, or Foreman-visible claim. Feature Area 13: Cross-Role Observability

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-031-1: Given a package is quarantined | When the current process or session restarts against the same local checkout | Then the package remains quarantined without any automatic reload attempt
- AC-031-2: Given a quarantined package | When an operator inspects local state | Then the quarantine and its cause are visible in plain text, not merely absent from the active set with no explanation

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen: Option B — dedicated adapter modules per new trigger-source type, plus a shared notification-state module.** Unchanged from 1.0.0.

New `file-source-adapter.ts` and `release-source-adapter.ts` under `packages/agent-core/src/behavior/` each produce a `BehaviorEvent` through `normalizeEvent`, mirroring the existing `pi-events.ts` → `event-translator.ts` → `normalizeEvent` → `LocalEventMatcher` chain. A new `notification-state.ts` in `pi-extension` centralises busy, duplicate and stale tracking for every behavior. Package quarantine gets its own `package-quarantine.ts` beside `package-discovery.ts`.

### Decisions added in 1.1.0

1. **How artifact changes are detected: content hashes checked at lifecycle points.** No `fs.watch`, no new dependency.
   - The adapter derives its watch set from the compiled `artifact.changed` triggers (the `path` predicate).
   - It hashes those files at `tool_result` and at `agent_end`, and emits an event when a digest differs from the last one seen in the session.
   - The hooks it relies on already exist, which is what AC-001-2 means by "supported host API".
   - It behaves the same on every OS (see REQ-023).
   - It needs no new dependency, which constitution §4 would require approval for.

   | Option | Why not chosen |
   |---|---|
   | `fs.watch` | Event semantics differ between macOS, Linux and Windows (rename-vs-change, recursive support). That is exactly the kind of per-platform behavior difference REQ-023 forbids absorbing silently. It also keeps a handle open for the whole session. |
   | `chokidar` | A new runtime dependency (constitution §4), for a problem that lifecycle-point hashing already solves. |

   The limitation, stated rather than hidden: a change is seen at the next tool call or at the end of the run, not instantly. NFR-001 measures from event validation, so this latency is outside its budget. TRD-003 reports it separately.

2. **Release signal (resolves the PRD's REQ-002 clarification): a new `v*` tag in local refs.** This matches this repo's `release.yml` (`on: push: tags: ['v*']`).
   - The tag pattern is a trigger predicate, so repositories with different conventions change configuration, not code (Rule 8).
   - It is detected two ways. First, from a successful tag-creating tool call (`git tag`, `gh release create`), in the same way `repository.changed` is derived today. Second, by diffing tag refs at session start and at `agent_end`, which covers tags that arrive by fetch.
   - It emits the **existing** catalog type `release.completed`, carrying `{ tag, sha, source }`.
   - One tag produces one event per session, whichever path sees it first.

3. **Coverage metric (resolves the PRD's REQ-016 clarification): Jest `json-summary` output, per file, `lines.pct` and `branches.pct` by default.**
   - Each package's `test:coverage` is `jest --coverage`. Jest's default reporters (`json`, `lcov`, `text`, `clover`) produce raw maps, not percentages.
   - So the behavior watches `coverage/coverage-summary.json`, and its README tells repositories to enable `json-summary`.
   - The metrics and the threshold (default 1.0 percentage point) are behavior configuration.
   - If the artifact never appears, the behavior shows up as an inert trigger in `/ensemble-status`; it is never silently idle.
   - The baseline is the previous snapshot seen **in the same session** (Rule 4). The first observation in a session only sets the baseline.

4. **The comparison is a generic command: `artifact.compare` (TRD-033).** It compares numeric JSON paths between the previous and current snapshot of an artifact and knows nothing about coverage.
   - The alternatives were rejected. Doing the comparison in an agent step would make the reported delta an unverified model claim (REQ-012). A coverage-specific command would make the third behavior need Ensemble code (REQ-018).
   - It lands in PR 1, which is why PR 5 can be configuration only.

5. **Notification transport** (REQ-009, REQ-010). `notification-state.ts` delivers to two sinks:
   - **The user**, through `SessionUiBridge.notify`, a new method that wraps `ctx.ui.notify`. Headless sessions fall back to the console.
   - **The model's context**, through `pi.sendMessage` with `display: true` and `triggerTurn: false`.

   `triggerTurn: false` is deliberate. #107 deleted the continuation path because a message that makes the agent act bypasses `MutationGuard` (`extension.ts:118-140`); a notification is data, never an instruction. Any test-derived text in a notification is fenced and labelled as data, a lesson from #94's live runs. `sendMessage` is added to `assertRequiredCapabilities`.

6. **Verified fix application** (REQ-033). This is configuration plus two small code changes.
   - A new behavior, `apply-verified-fix`, runs `mode: auto`. It triggers on `fix.verified` with the predicate `verdict: passed`, declares only `fix.apply` with no tools, and calls `fix.apply { proposalRef: ${event.payload.proposalRef} }`.
   - `CommandRegistry` then asks `ApprovalGate`. Today the prompt is only `descriptor.description` ("Apply a verified fix proposal…"), so the human would approve without seeing what changes. Code change 1 (TRD-019): the prompt names the proposal, its files and a diff summary.
   - `commit-policy.ts` has no importers today. Code change 2 (TRD-021): wire it in so an applied fix is committed with attribution.

### Alternatives considered (architecture)

| Option | Summary | Why not chosen |
|---|---|---|
| **A — Widen the existing translator, inline notification** | Add file and release branches inside `event-translator.ts`; keep notification-state logic at each `ctx.ui.notify` call site. | `event-translator.ts` would cover three unrelated source domains. Busy/duplicate/stale logic would be copied per behavior, which is the per-reaction duplication the PRD sets out to remove. |
| **B — Dedicated adapter modules + shared notification-state module** *(chosen)* | One adapter module per source type, all feeding the same ingress; one shared notification-state module. | Matches the existing boundary (`agent-core` = provider-neutral logic, `pi-extension` = host wiring), and centralises notification state once. |
| **C — Single generic "external signal" adapter** | One configurable "watch path X for condition Y" abstraction for both sources. | Risks becoming an arbitrary-condition escape hatch around the closed, versioned catalog (REQ-CQRS-005); still duplicates notification state. |

Verifies: TRD-017
Satisfies: REQ-031
PRD ACs Proven: AC-031-1, AC-031-2
Proof of requirement: 
Target Files: packages/agent-core/tests/package-quarantine.test.ts` (new), packages/pi-extension/tests/package-authoring.e2e.test.ts` (extended)
Actions:

Test AC:
- [ ] Scenario: quarantine survives a restart -- Given package P quarantined, When a new `activate()` runs on the same checkout, Then P is not loaded and no load of P is attempted
- [ ] Scenario: the cause is readable -- Given P quarantined for requesting `bash` beyond its grant, When status is rendered, Then it shows P, the reason and the time in plain text
- [ ] Scenario: clearing works and corruption fails closed -- Given the record is removed, When activation runs, Then P loads; and Given the record is corrupt JSON, When activation runs, Then P stays quarantined with a diagnostic

## Test Task: TRD-025-TEST
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-b6db9749-behavior-habits-runtime.md#trd-025-test
PRD Reference: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-b6db9749-behavior-habits-runtime.md#req-021

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-021**: The complete local path is independently verified on Windows, Linux, and macOS
The complete local path is independently verified on Windows, Linux, and macOS Priority: Must [RISK: verification evidence does not yet exist for any of the three platforms as of this PRD]

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-021-1: Given the trigger/dispatch/notification path | When run on each of Windows | Then each platform has its own passing conformance suite run
- AC-021-2: Given a behavior works on one platform | When parity is claimed for another | Then that claim is backed by that platform's own conformance evidence, never inferred

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen: Option B — dedicated adapter modules per new trigger-source type, plus a shared notification-state module.** Unchanged from 1.0.0.

New `file-source-adapter.ts` and `release-source-adapter.ts` under `packages/agent-core/src/behavior/` each produce a `BehaviorEvent` through `normalizeEvent`, mirroring the existing `pi-events.ts` → `event-translator.ts` → `normalizeEvent` → `LocalEventMatcher` chain. A new `notification-state.ts` in `pi-extension` centralises busy, duplicate and stale tracking for every behavior. Package quarantine gets its own `package-quarantine.ts` beside `package-discovery.ts`.

### Decisions added in 1.1.0

1. **How artifact changes are detected: content hashes checked at lifecycle points.** No `fs.watch`, no new dependency.
   - The adapter derives its watch set from the compiled `artifact.changed` triggers (the `path` predicate).
   - It hashes those files at `tool_result` and at `agent_end`, and emits an event when a digest differs from the last one seen in the session.
   - The hooks it relies on already exist, which is what AC-001-2 means by "supported host API".
   - It behaves the same on every OS (see REQ-023).
   - It needs no new dependency, which constitution §4 would require approval for.

   | Option | Why not chosen |
   |---|---|
   | `fs.watch` | Event semantics differ between macOS, Linux and Windows (rename-vs-change, recursive support). That is exactly the kind of per-platform behavior difference REQ-023 forbids absorbing silently. It also keeps a handle open for the whole session. |
   | `chokidar` | A new runtime dependency (constitution §4), for a problem that lifecycle-point hashing already solves. |

   The limitation, stated rather than hidden: a change is seen at the next tool call or at the end of the run, not instantly. NFR-001 measures from event validation, so this latency is outside its budget. TRD-003 reports it separately.

2. **Release signal (resolves the PRD's REQ-002 clarification): a new `v*` tag in local refs.** This matches this repo's `release.yml` (`on: push: tags: ['v*']`).
   - The tag pattern is a trigger predicate, so repositories with different conventions change configuration, not code (Rule 8).
   - It is detected two ways. First, from a successful tag-creating tool call (`git tag`, `gh release create`), in the same way `repository.changed` is derived today. Second, by diffing tag refs at session start and at `agent_end`, which covers tags that arrive by fetch.
   - It emits the **existing** catalog type `release.completed`, carrying `{ tag, sha, source }`.
   - One tag produces one event per session, whichever path sees it first.

3. **Coverage metric (resolves the PRD's REQ-016 clarification): Jest `json-summary` output, per file, `lines.pct` and `branches.pct` by default.**
   - Each package's `test:coverage` is `jest --coverage`. Jest's default reporters (`json`, `lcov`, `text`, `clover`) produce raw maps, not percentages.
   - So the behavior watches `coverage/coverage-summary.json`, and its README tells repositories to enable `json-summary`.
   - The metrics and the threshold (default 1.0 percentage point) are behavior configuration.
   - If the artifact never appears, the behavior shows up as an inert trigger in `/ensemble-status`; it is never silently idle.
   - The baseline is the previous snapshot seen **in the same session** (Rule 4). The first observation in a session only sets the baseline.

4. **The comparison is a generic command: `artifact.compare` (TRD-033).** It compares numeric JSON paths between the previous and current snapshot of an artifact and knows nothing about coverage.
   - The alternatives were rejected. Doing the comparison in an agent step would make the reported delta an unverified model claim (REQ-012). A coverage-specific command would make the third behavior need Ensemble code (REQ-018).
   - It lands in PR 1, which is why PR 5 can be configuration only.

5. **Notification transport** (REQ-009, REQ-010). `notification-state.ts` delivers to two sinks:
   - **The user**, through `SessionUiBridge.notify`, a new method that wraps `ctx.ui.notify`. Headless sessions fall back to the console.
   - **The model's context**, through `pi.sendMessage` with `display: true` and `triggerTurn: false`.

   `triggerTurn: false` is deliberate. #107 deleted the continuation path because a message that makes the agent act bypasses `MutationGuard` (`extension.ts:118-140`); a notification is data, never an instruction. Any test-derived text in a notification is fenced and labelled as data, a lesson from #94's live runs. `sendMessage` is added to `assertRequiredCapabilities`.

6. **Verified fix application** (REQ-033). This is configuration plus two small code changes.
   - A new behavior, `apply-verified-fix`, runs `mode: auto`. It triggers on `fix.verified` with the predicate `verdict: passed`, declares only `fix.apply` with no tools, and calls `fix.apply { proposalRef: ${event.payload.proposalRef} }`.
   - `CommandRegistry` then asks `ApprovalGate`. Today the prompt is only `descriptor.description` ("Apply a verified fix proposal…"), so the human would approve without seeing what changes. Code change 1 (TRD-019): the prompt names the proposal, its files and a diff summary.
   - `commit-policy.ts` has no importers today. Code change 2 (TRD-021): wire it in so an applied fix is committed with attribution.

### Alternatives considered (architecture)

| Option | Summary | Why not chosen |
|---|---|---|
| **A — Widen the existing translator, inline notification** | Add file and release branches inside `event-translator.ts`; keep notification-state logic at each `ctx.ui.notify` call site. | `event-translator.ts` would cover three unrelated source domains. Busy/duplicate/stale logic would be copied per behavior, which is the per-reaction duplication the PRD sets out to remove. |
| **B — Dedicated adapter modules + shared notification-state module** *(chosen)* | One adapter module per source type, all feeding the same ingress; one shared notification-state module. | Matches the existing boundary (`agent-core` = provider-neutral logic, `pi-extension` = host wiring), and centralises notification state once. |
| **C — Single generic "external signal" adapter** | One configurable "watch path X for condition Y" abstraction for both sources. | Risks becoming an arbitrary-condition escape hatch around the closed, versioned catalog (REQ-CQRS-005); still duplicates notification state. |

Read-first: read the TRD, TRD Task section, PRD and PRD Requirement above before any work on this bead.


--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-015**: Commands and skills depend on capabilities, not tools
Commands and skills depend on capabilities, not tools Priority: Must | `[RISK: about 10 heavily coupled commands plus skills must be refactored without changing default behavior]` Shared commands, agents and skills reference capabilities and resolved adapters. They no longer name a specific tool outside an adapter. Acceptance is asserted through the commands' real entry points, not around them.

--- TRD Context ---
### Alternatives Considered

| Option | Approach | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|---|
| A: Prose-only adapters | Adapter is a skill; the agent follows its prose and normalizes tool output itself | Smallest build; fully editable | Cannot route internal CLIs deterministically (REQ-016), cannot validate output (REQ-022), cannot deny at runtime (REQ-023); behavior varies per model |
| **B: Manifest plus runner (chosen)** | Adapter is a skill directory: `SKILL.md` (vocabulary and agent-facing prose) plus a declarative `adapter.yaml` (capability command templates, output mapping, allowlist, health check, detection signals, required env names). A core resolver library and `toolchain-cli` execute capabilities deterministically | Meets PRD (adapter is a skill), Rule 8 (editable without rebuild), Rule 5 (enforcement in code), REQ-016 (CLIs call the same library) | New resolver, runner, manifest schema and output-mapping engine to build and test |
| C: Executable plugin adapters | Separately packaged executables speaking a versioned JSON protocol | Arbitrary logic; strongest isolation | Contradicts the PRD's skills-as-contract decision; fails Rule 8; needs per-OS packaging and a protocol |

**Rationale:** B is the only option that makes every PRD guarantee a code-enforced property while keeping adapters user-editable data. The requester selected B at the architecture gate.

### Interpretations and Resolved Design Issues

- **I1: plain version control.** The PRD taxonomy has no plain `git` category, yet about 45 sources invoke it. Plain `git` operations (status, commit, push, log, diff, merge-base) are `vcs.*` capabilities of the `workflow` category, whose default adapter is `plain-git`; the `git-town` adapter extends it. Recommend a PRD refine pass to name this explicitly.
- **I2: ambiguity versus no signal (PRD REQ-009 AC-2 vs REQ-010 AC-2).** "No detectable signal" means no signal source exists at all (no remote, no marker files); the shipped default is used. "Ambiguous" means two or more installed adapters match, or a signal source exists (for example a remote URL) but matches no installed adapter; resolution fails explicitly in non-interactive runs and asks in interactive runs.
- **I3: AC-023-2 (governed boundary denies).** The runner is invoked through the shell tool, so a command that was not granted the shell tool cannot run any adapter; an adapter therefore cannot widen grants. The runner additionally denies any command outside the adapter's binary-plus-subcommand allowlist. Denial of raw shell commands typed by an agent outside the runner remains host-enforced (hooks on Claude Code; none in this repo for Pi, OpenCode or Codex); the lint (REQ-019) keeps commands from issuing raw tool calls. This residual is recorded in the Threat Model.
- **I4: confirmation session identity.** No stable session id is exposed uniformly across runtimes. TRD-017 begins with a spike that records which id each runtime exposes (`ENSEMBLE_SESSION_ID`, host session variables); the passive confirmation record is keyed by `(sessionKey, category, adapter, configHash)` and falls back to the run id when no session id exists.
- **I5: repo-local adapters are untrusted by default.** A cloned repository can ship `.ensemble/adapters/`. Repo-local adapters resolve in every mode (satisfying AC-007-3) but a non-interactive run additionally requires the adapter name in the user's `trustedRepoAdapters` list; an interactive run shows the adapter's allowlist at first-use confirmation.
- **I6: no new runtime dependency.** The output-mapping engine uses a small dotted-path projection (`$.a.b[0]`, `|` alternation for "array or object"), not a JSONPath library, because constitution section 4 requires approval for new dependencies.
- **I7: work-graph selection.** `work-graph` is its own category with default `auto`: use the work-graph capabilities of the resolved tracker adapter when its manifest provides them; otherwise use the built-in `work-graph-links-fallback` adapter (tracker dependency links, then plan order stated as not dependency-aware). One manifest may implement several categories.
- **I8: PRD BDD floor.** Fourteen PRD requirements (REQ-001, 002, 004, 005, 006, 009, 010, 012, 015, 018, 021, 022, 024, 025) have two ACs, below the command's three-scenario floor. The test tasks specify exactly one scenario per AC; recommend a PRD refine pass to add edge or error ACs.
- **I10: packaging.** `packages/development` depends only on `js-yaml` and its libraries require only siblings, so the resolver library, category contracts, default selection, schemas and tool inventory all ship inside `packages/development` (`lib/toolchain/` and `toolchain/`). A standalone plugin install and the Pi vendor bundle therefore contain everything; other packages call `toolchain-cli` through `TOOLCHAIN_CLI` rather than importing it.
- **I9: preflight is enforced in code.** `toolchain-cli run` refuses a side-effecting capability unless a passing preflight record exists for the supplied `--run-id`; the command prose cannot silently skip preflight.
