title: [trd:trd-2026-15aa5acd-live-behavior-dispatch-autofix:task:TRD-029] - [ ] **TRD-029** Gate constitution-change proposals behind the inline confirmation; open a PR only on "yes" (6h)
description:
## Task: TRD-029
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-15aa5acd-live-behavior-dispatch-autofix.md#trd-029
PRD Reference: #req-007

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen: Option C — single enforcement seam, additive.**

A new `MutationGuard` chokepoint in `agent-core` is the one place `policy.mode`, `capabilities.mutation_classes` (via the existing `hasMutationAuthority()`), and protected-path rules are resolved. It is wired once at the loader boundary rather than replicated per tool registration. The translator, matcher, and auto-fix loop are added to `pi-extension`. Discovery roots and `execution.test_command` are additive changes to existing schema/discovery code. `ToolRegistry`, `outbox`, and the compiler are reused unchanged.

### Alternatives considered

| Option | Summary | Why not chosen |
|---|---|---|
| **A — In-place extension** | Enforce mode/mutation/path rules as wrapper checks inside `behavior-loader`'s per-tool `execute()` closures. | Enforcement scattered across call sites; every future tool registration must remember to wrap. The PRD's central failure mode is *guarantees that exist in one place but are not reached from another* — Option A reproduces exactly that shape. |
| **B — Governance kernel** | Route every mutation through a `MutationBroker` + `GovernedWorkspace` in `agent-core`; `pi-extension` becomes a thin adapter. | Strongest long-term design and the right eventual target, but it re-opens already-shipped code across every tool path for a ~6-7 PR refactor before a single PRD requirement is demonstrable. Deferred deliberately, not rejected. |
| **C — Single enforcement seam** *(chosen)* | One `MutationGuard` chokepoint, wired once; everything else additive. | Gets a single auditable chokepoint (Option B's main benefit) without Option B's refactor surface. Fits the existing `agent-core` / `pi-extension` split. |

### Architectural note carried from grounding

Two defects found while grounding this design are folded into PR 1 rather than left implicit:

1. `pi-events.ts` emits `runtime.tool_result` / `runtime.tool.called` / `runtime.tool.failed` / `runtime.tool.completed`, none of which appear in `HARNESS_EVENT_TYPES` (which defines `runtime.tool_call.started` / `runtime.tool_call.completed`). `normalizeEvent` does not currently reject uncatalogued types, so PRD AC-002-1's "validated against the closed catalog" would be vacuous. Addressed by TRD-001 (`[satisfies INFRA]`).
2. `behavior-loader.ts:79` calls `registry.grant(...)` unconditionally immediately before `registry.invoke(...)`, making the grant boundary a rubber stamp for behavior-governed tools (unlike the echo path, where the grant is CLI-flag-gated). Addressed by TRD-003.
Satisfies: REQ-007
PRD ACs: AC-007-1, AC-007-2, AC-007-3
Target File: packages/pi-extension/src/approval-gate.ts
Actions:

Implementation AC:
- [ ] Given a "no" answer, when the gate resolves, then no PR is opened and `constitution.md` is unchanged
- [ ] Given a "yes" answer, when the gate resolves, then a PR is opened and `constitution.md` remains unmodified until that PR merges.
Dependencies: TRD-022, TRD-018

description:
## Test Task: TRD-025-TEST
## References
TRD: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-8d825f54-tool-abstraction-layer.md
TRD Task: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-8d825f54-tool-abstraction-layer.md#trd-025-test

Verifies Task: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-8d825f54-tool-abstraction-layer.md#trd-025
Parent Epic: [trd:trd-2026-8d825f54-tool-abstraction-layer]
Read-first: read the TRD, TRD Task section, PRD and PRD Requirement above before any work on this bead.


--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-016**: Tracker swap, end to end (first alternatives: Jira Cloud and Azure Boards)
Tracker swap, end to end (first alternatives: Jira Cloud and Azure Boards) Priority: Must | `[RISK: work-graph behavior differs between trackers]` With the tracker adapter changed by configuration only, every command that creates, reads, updates or closes work items works against either alternative tracker, including the internal CLIs (`trd-cli` and siblings) that currently call the default tracker directly. Those internal CLIs route through the resolved tracker adapter. The first-release Jira adapter targets Jira Cloud only.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-016-2: Given an internal CLI that previously called the default tracker directly | When the tracker adapter is swapped | Then the CLI performs the same operation through the alternative adapter

--- TRD Context ---
### Alternatives Considered

| Option | Approach | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|---|
| A: Prose-only adapters | Adapter is a skill; the agent follows its prose and normalizes tool output itself | Smallest build; fully editable | Cannot route internal CLIs deterministically (REQ-016), cannot validate output (REQ-022), cannot deny at runtime (REQ-023); behavior varies per model |
| **B: Manifest plus runner (chosen)** | Adapter is a skill directory: `SKILL.md` (vocabulary and agent-facing prose) plus a declarative `adapter.yaml` (capability command templates, output mapping, allowlist, health check, detection signals, required env names). A core resolver library and `toolchain-cli` execute capabilities deterministically | Meets PRD (adapter is a skill), Rule 8 (editable without rebuild), Rule 5 (enforcement in code), REQ-016 (CLIs call the same library) | New resolver, runner, manifest schema and output-mapping engine to build and test |
| C: Executable plugin adapters | Separately packaged executables speaking a versioned JSON protocol | Arbitrary logic; strongest isolation | Contradicts the PRD's skills-as-contract decision; fails Rule 8; needs per-OS packaging and a protocol |

**Rationale:** B is the only option that makes every PRD guarantee a code-enforced property while keeping adapters user-editable data. The requester selected B at the architecture gate.

### Interpretations and Resolved Design Issues

- **I1: plain version control.** The PRD taxonomy has no plain `git` category, yet about 45 sources invoke it. Plain `git` operations (status, commit, push, log, diff, merge-base) are `vcs.*` capabilities of the `workflow` category, whose default adapter is `plain-git`; the `git-town` adapter extends it. Recommend a PRD refine pass to name this explicitly.
- **I2: ambiguity versus no signal (PRD REQ-009 AC-2 vs REQ-010 AC-2).** "No detectable signal" means no signal source exists at all (no remote, no marker files); the shipped default is used. "Ambiguous" means two or more installed adapters match, or a signal source exists (for example a remote URL) but matches no installed adapter; resolution fails explicitly in non-interactive runs and asks in interactive runs.
- **I3: AC-023-2 (governed boundary denies).** The runner is invoked through the shell tool, so a command that was not granted the shell tool cannot run any adapter; an adapter therefore cannot widen grants. The runner additionally denies any command outside the adapter's binary-plus-subcommand allowlist. Denial of raw shell commands typed by an agent outside the runner remains host-enforced (hooks on Claude Code; none in this repo for Pi, OpenCode or Codex); the lint (REQ-019) keeps commands from issuing raw tool calls. This residual is recorded in the Threat Model.
- **I4: confirmation session identity.** No stable session id is exposed uniformly across runtimes. TRD-017 begins with a spike that records which id each runtime exposes (`ENSEMBLE_SESSION_ID`, host session variables); the passive confirmation record is keyed by `(sessionKey, category, adapter, configHash)` and falls back to the run id when no session id exists.
- **I5: repo-local adapters are untrusted by default.** A cloned repository can ship `.ensemble/adapters/`. Repo-local adapters resolve in every mode (satisfying AC-007-3) but a non-interactive run additionally requires the adapter name in the user's `trustedRepoAdapters` list; an interactive run shows the adapter's allowlist at first-use confirmation.
- **I6: no new runtime dependency.** The output-mapping engine uses a small dotted-path projection (`$.a.b[0]`, `|` alternation for "array or object"), not a JSONPath library, because constitution section 4 requires approval for new dependencies.
- **I7: work-graph selection.** `work-graph` is its own category with default `auto`: use the work-graph capabilities of the resolved tracker adapter when its manifest provides them; otherwise use the built-in `work-graph-links-fallback` adapter (tracker dependency links, then plan order stated as not dependency-aware). One manifest may implement several categories.
- **I8: PRD BDD floor.** Fourteen PRD requirements (REQ-001, 002, 004, 005, 006, 009, 010, 012, 015, 018, 021, 022, 024, 025) have two ACs, below the command's three-scenario floor. The test tasks specify exactly one scenario per AC; recommend a PRD refine pass to add edge or error ACs.
- **I10: packaging.** `packages/development` depends only on `js-yaml` and its libraries require only siblings, so the resolver library, category contracts, default selection, schemas and tool inventory all ship inside `packages/development` (`lib/toolchain/` and `toolchain/`). A standalone plugin install and the Pi vendor bundle therefore contain everything; other packages call `toolchain-cli` through `TOOLCHAIN_CLI` rather than importing it.
- **I9: preflight is enforced in code.** `toolchain-cli run` refuses a side-effecting capability unless a passing preflight record exists for the supplied `--run-id`; the command prose cannot silently skip preflight.
Verifies: TRD-025
Satisfies: REQ-016
PRD ACs Proven: AC-016-2
Proof of requirement: 
Target Files: 
Actions:

Test AC:
- [ ] Scenario: Internal CLI works through swapped tracker -- Given an internal CLI that previously called the default tracker directly, When the tracker adapter is swapped to a fixture adapter, Then the CLI performs the same operation through the alternative adapter
Dependencies: TRD-025

title: [trd:trd-2026-70e784f2-code-review-process:task:TRD-025-TEST] - [ ] **TRD-025-TEST** Merge gate blockers (6h)
description:
## Test Task: TRD-025-TEST
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-70e784f2-code-review-process.md#trd-025-test
PRD Reference: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-70e784f2-code-review-process.md#req-008

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-008**: Every finding is answered before merge (Must)
Every finding is answered before merge (Must) An Important finding must be fixed or resolved with a stated reason before the PR can merge. Convergence

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-008-1: Given an Important finding is open | When merge is attempted | Then it is refused and names the open finding
- AC-008-4: Given a finding is Nit or Pre-existing | When merge is attempted | Then it does not block
- AC-017-1: Given a PR is reviewed | When the security review finds an issue | Then merge is blocked until it is fixed or closed with a stated reason
- AC-017-2: Given a later commit fixes the issue | When re-review runs | Then the security finding clears on its own
- AC-017-3: Given a security finding is a false positive | When the author closes it with a reason | Then the reason is recorded in the ledger
- AC-002-3: Given a PR description is missing any of the three sections | When its review status is computed | Then the PR is reported as not ready for approval and names the missing section

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen approach (Option C):** extend the pattern TRD-2026-82b6a138 established: **editable behavior in skills, agents and markdown; a small set of pure, deterministic libraries for what must not be self-certified by a model.**

- **User-owned (Constitution Rule 8), prose or data a maintainer edits without a toolchain:** per-area rules (`REVIEW.md` files), the policy block inside the root `REVIEW.md` (round cap, depth table, bot and maintainer logins, sensitive and High paths, Low-waiver state), severity definitions, reviewer, verifier, classifier and security-lane prompts, the PR template, the sweep and explainer procedures. All of it is read from the **target branch**, never from the PR head (REQ-024).
- **Enforcement (Rules 5 and 7), code that grades a model's claim:** vote tally, tier assignment with its sensitive-path floor and Low-waiver evidence, approval evaluation bound to a commit, the merge gate, round-cap derivation, repeat suppression, delta-range selection, depth bounds, slice coverage, metrics and eval scoring. Each is a pure CommonJS module in `packages/development/lib/`, exposed as a JSON-in/JSON-out subcommand of the existing `pr-review-cli.js`, following the 82b6a138 precedent. None performs network I/O or holds a timer.
- **Entry points (Rule 6):** every capability is reached through the one `pr-review-cycle` skill, which `fix-issue`, `implement-trd-beads` and `pr-merge` already invoke or will invoke (a new `MODE=gate` for `pr-merge`). YAML callers reference the skill only, never the CLI, as the existing parity tests require.
- **Recurrence (Rule 4):** nightly or weekly sweeps and daily eval runs are on-demand skills; a workflow template for the host repository is opt-in and scaffolded by init-project. Ensemble's own workflows gain no `schedule` trigger.

**Alternatives considered (user chose C):**

- **Option A -- prose-only skills and agents:** fewest files and fastest to ship. Rejected: the vote threshold, the tier floor, commit-bound approvals and the round cap would be prose a model can misread or skip, so none of these gates could be shown to fail (Rule 7), and "a bot approval never counts" would be a request, not a guarantee.
- **Option B -- a new TypeScript review engine in `agent-core`:** strongest typing and one runtime. Rejected: a new build and `dist` surface and cross-package coupling for a prompt-level feature, editable criteria pulled into code (against Rule 8), and drift toward an ensemble-owned dispatcher that competes with Foreman (Rule 4).

**Rationale:** Option C is the best fit for this brownfield repo. It adds only the code that grades claims, keeps everything a maintainer or adopting team would tune in files they can edit, adds no dependency (Constitution §4) and no CI secret, vendors into Pi automatically through the existing require-closure bundler, and each gate can be mutation-proven using the harness that already exists.

**Decisions taken where the PRD left a choice** (each is editable policy, not a hidden constant):

| Decision | Value | Where it lives |
|---|---|---|
| Policy format | Fenced `ensemble-review-policy` JSON block in the root `REVIEW.md` (no new parser dependency) | REVIEW.md, read from the base commit |
| "Cannot vouch for" a push (AC-010-3, AC-014-2) | Commit is unvouched when its tree differs from the reviewed tree and it is not a remediation commit recorded in the review-state report, or it is a merge commit | `pr-review-scope.js`, `pr-review-approvals.js` |
| Slice threshold for large PRs (AC-018-1) | 1500 changed lines, configurable | policy block |
| Area rules vs policy keys | Policy keys are read from the **root** file only; area files carry guidance, and the more restrictive instruction wins when areas conflict (AC-001-2) | skill prose |
| First PR that introduces REVIEW.md | No base copy exists, so strict defaults apply (Low treated as Medium, cap 3, default sensitive set) | `pr-review-policy.js` |
| Verifier majority | Strict majority of the expected verifier count (2 of 3, 3 of 5) | `pr-review-votes.js` |

PRD Reference: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-d6bbf322-new-feature-workflow.md#req-009

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-009**: Support manual and explicitly configured event-triggered starts
Support manual and explicitly configured event-triggered starts Priority: Must | Complexity: High | [RISK: event payloads can be incomplete, untrusted, or mistaken for user intent]

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-009-1: Given no event mapping is configured | When an event occurs | Then it does not start a `new-feature` run; manual invocation remains available

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen: Option C — hardened in-session stage composition with a dedicated atomic run-index store.**

`new-feature` is authored the same way every other product command in this repo is authored: a single orchestrating skill (`packages/development/commands/new-feature.yaml`, generated to runtime-specific prompts exactly like `fix-issue.yaml`) that executes each stage's existing skill body in-session — the same mechanism that loaded `ensemble-refine-prd`'s content into this session and had the agent execute its Phases directly. This is forced, not merely preferred: Pi's `ExtensionAPI` has no completion/invoke primitive that would let an extension programmatically run another skill and get its result back (confirmed — no `pi.invokeCommand` or equivalent exists); the only code-level "run a skill" mechanism, `createAgentPort()`, spawns a bounded, disposable `omp -p --no-session --no-extensions` subprocess in an isolated worktree, and does not fit a long-lived, project-resident workflow whose PRD/TRD stages use the interactive `--collab` review server.

What is new, and is the one piece of real infrastructure this TRD adds: a `RunIndexStore` (`packages/agent-core/src/new-feature/run-index.ts`) built on the one proven concurrency-safe pattern in this repo — `session.js`'s temp-file-then-`renameSync` atomic write plus `expectedRevision`/409-style optimistic concurrency — rather than `ProposalStore`'s plain `writeFileSync` (no atomicity, no lock, not adequate for PRD AC-005-3's fail-closed-on-malformed-index requirement). Runs are stored at `.ensemble/new-feature/<run-id>.json`, mirroring `ProposalStore`'s `.ensemble/proposals/<ref>.json` convention (also excluded from `tree-baseline.ts` drift detection, so this is consistent runtime-owned state, not a project-source mutation).

### Alternatives considered

| Option | Summary | Why not chosen |
|---|---|---|
| A — Plain JSON checkpoint | Same in-session composition, but checkpoints are a single `writeFileSync`, no atomicity/locking. | Fastest to build, but a crash mid-write can corrupt the run index, which directly violates AC-005-3's "fail closed with a recoverable diagnostic" requirement — the repo's own `ProposalStore` already demonstrates this gap is real, not hypothetical. |
| B — Subprocess-dispatched stages | New orchestrator module dispatches every stage as a bounded `createAgentPort()` subprocess; advances the run index only after subprocess exit 0 + artifact-on-disk confirmation. | Most rigorous completion signal (a real process boundary instead of self-reported bookkeeping), but substantially more build effort, and does not fit the interactive `--collab` review-server stages `create-prd`/`refine-prd` already use — those are long-lived, human-attended HTTP sessions, not bounded one-shot subprocess work, and would need bespoke carve-out handling under this option. |
| **C — Hardened in-session composition** *(chosen)* | In-session stage execution (like every existing product command), backed by a dedicated atomic `RunIndexStore`. | Reuses 100% of the existing skill-composition and `ask_user`-approval infrastructure (including the `--collab` review server, which needs no special-casing), while fixing Option A's one real correctness gap with the repo's one proven atomic-write pattern. Matches user-confirmed direction. |

### Honest trust-boundary note

Because stage execution stays in-session (per Option C), the approval gates implemented by TRD-014/TRD-017/TRD-019 are enforced by the orchestrating skill's own conditional logic checking `RunIndexStore`-persisted approval fields before it issues an implementation or `gh pr create` tool call — not by a separate runtime authorization chokepoint like `agent-core`'s `MutationGuard` (which exists elsewhere in this repo, gating CQRS-registered commands, but `new-feature`'s mutating actions are ordinary skill-level tool calls, same as `fix-issue`'s own gated PR-creation step, not CQRS commands). This is the same trust boundary every existing Ensemble product command already operates under. Building a `MutationGuard`-equivalent chokepoint for skill-level tool calls is a materially larger investment this PRD does not request and no other product command has; REQ-014's "runtime authority" is satisfied here by making the check a required precondition over persisted, validated store state rather than over prompt claims — which is what AC-014-2 actually asks for — not by inventing a new enforcement subsystem.

description:
## Task: TRD-017
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-82b6a138-pr-review-cycle-time.md#trd-017
PRD Reference: #req-022

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen approach (Option C):** One shared, prose-defined review procedure plus a small deterministic helper library.

- `packages/development/skills/pr-review-cycle/SKILL.md` is the single reusable procedure. It owns the *user-editable* parts (Constitution Rule 8): review criteria, the order of the loop, the 10-minute interactive wait, Foreman-mode rules. It **composes** `packages/quality/skills/pr-review-remediation/SKILL.md` for per-finding triage, regression tests and minimal fixes and does not restate those rules.
- A set of small pure-JS modules in `packages/development/lib/` owns only what *grades the model's own claim* (Constitution Rule 8's enforcement exception, and Rule 7): base/head scope resolution, ledger validation, head-bound remote-review evaluation, terminal-status derivation with the bounded-round cap, and the untracked review-state report. A thin CLI, `pr-review-cli.js`, exposes them as JSON-in/JSON-out commands, following the `trd-cli.js` / `complete-beads-planner.js` precedent.
- `fix-issue.yaml`, `implement-trd-beads.yaml` and `complete-beads/SKILL.md` invoke the skill at their real PR boundaries; none re-states review steps.

**Alternatives considered (user chose C):**

title: [trd:trd-2026-b6db9749-behavior-habits-runtime:task:TRD-005-TEST] - [ ] **TRD-005-TEST** Investigator state and non-mutation tests (2h)
description:
## Test Task: TRD-005-TEST
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-b6db9749-behavior-habits-runtime.md#trd-005-test
PRD Reference: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-b6db9749-behavior-habits-runtime.md#req-005

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-005**: Support a read-only investigator session mode
Support a read-only investigator session mode Priority: Must A behavior can invoke a read-only investigator session, distinct from the existing auto-fix ("Applier") mode, that diagnoses without mutating.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-005-1: Given a behavior configured with an investigator step | When it runs | Then it produces a typed, evidence-backed finding
- AC-005-2: Given the same behavior | When the investigator step completes | Then no workspace mutation has occurred as a side effect
- AC-005-3: Given the model/LLM provider is unreachable | When an investigator session is invoked | Then it fails with a distinct, visible error state within a bounded timeout — it never hangs indefinitely and never silently returns a stale or fabricated finding

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen: Option B — dedicated adapter modules per new trigger-source type, plus a shared notification-state module.** Unchanged from 1.0.0.

New `file-source-adapter.ts` and `release-source-adapter.ts` under `packages/agent-core/src/behavior/` each produce a `BehaviorEvent` through `normalizeEvent`, mirroring the existing `pi-events.ts` → `event-translator.ts` → `normalizeEvent` → `LocalEventMatcher` chain. A new `notification-state.ts` in `pi-extension` centralises busy, duplicate and stale tracking for every behavior. Package quarantine gets its own `package-quarantine.ts` beside `package-discovery.ts`.

### Decisions added in 1.1.0

1. **How artifact changes are detected: content hashes checked at lifecycle points.** No `fs.watch`, no new dependency.
   - The adapter derives its watch set from the compiled `artifact.changed` triggers (the `path` predicate).
   - It hashes those files at `tool_result` and at `agent_end`, and emits an event when a digest differs from the last one seen in the session.
   - The hooks it relies on already exist, which is what AC-001-2 means by "supported host API".
   - It behaves the same on every OS (see REQ-023).
   - It needs no new dependency, which constitution §4 would require approval for.

   | Option | Why not chosen |
   |---|---|
   | `fs.watch` | Event semantics differ between macOS, Linux and Windows (rename-vs-change, recursive support). That is exactly the kind of per-platform behavior difference REQ-023 forbids absorbing silently. It also keeps a handle open for the whole session. |
   | `chokidar` | A new runtime dependency (constitution §4), for a problem that lifecycle-point hashing already solves. |

   The limitation, stated rather than hidden: a change is seen at the next tool call or at the end of the run, not instantly. NFR-001 measures from event validation, so this latency is outside its budget. TRD-003 reports it separately.

2. **Release signal (resolves the PRD's REQ-002 clarification): a new `v*` tag in local refs.** This matches this repo's `release.yml` (`on: push: tags: ['v*']`).
   - The tag pattern is a trigger predicate, so repositories with different conventions change configuration, not code (Rule 8).
   - It is detected two ways. First, from a successful tag-creating tool call (`git tag`, `gh release create`), in the same way `repository.changed` is derived today. Second, by diffing tag refs at session start and at `agent_end`, which covers tags that arrive by fetch.
   - It emits the **existing** catalog type `release.completed`, carrying `{ tag, sha, source }`.
   - One tag produces one event per session, whichever path sees it first.

3. **Coverage metric (resolves the PRD's REQ-016 clarification): Jest `json-summary` output, per file, `lines.pct` and `branches.pct` by default.**
   - Each package's `test:coverage` is `jest --coverage`. Jest's default reporters (`json`, `lcov`, `text`, `clover`) produce raw maps, not percentages.
   - So the behavior watches `coverage/coverage-summary.json`, and its README tells repositories to enable `json-summary`.
   - The metrics and the threshold (default 1.0 percentage point) are behavior configuration.
   - If the artifact never appears, the behavior shows up as an inert trigger in `/ensemble-status`; it is never silently idle.
   - The baseline is the previous snapshot seen **in the same session** (Rule 4). The first observation in a session only sets the baseline.

4. **The comparison is a generic command: `artifact.compare` (TRD-033).** It compares numeric JSON paths between the previous and current snapshot of an artifact and knows nothing about coverage.
   - The alternatives were rejected. Doing the comparison in an agent step would make the reported delta an unverified model claim (REQ-012). A coverage-specific command would make the third behavior need Ensemble code (REQ-018).
   - It lands in PR 1, which is why PR 5 can be configuration only.

5. **Notification transport** (REQ-009, REQ-010). `notification-state.ts` delivers to two sinks:
   - **The user**, through `SessionUiBridge.notify`, a new method that wraps `ctx.ui.notify`. Headless sessions fall back to the console.
   - **The model's context**, through `pi.sendMessage` with `display: true` and `triggerTurn: false`.

   `triggerTurn: false` is deliberate. #107 deleted the continuation path because a message that makes the agent act bypasses `MutationGuard` (`extension.ts:118-140`); a notification is data, never an instruction. Any test-derived text in a notification is fenced and labelled as data, a lesson from #94's live runs. `sendMessage` is added to `assertRequiredCapabilities`.

6. **Verified fix application** (REQ-033). This is configuration plus two small code changes.
   - A new behavior, `apply-verified-fix`, runs `mode: auto`. It triggers on `fix.verified` with the predicate `verdict: passed`, declares only `fix.apply` with no tools, and calls `fix.apply { proposalRef: ${event.payload.proposalRef} }`.
   - `CommandRegistry` then asks `ApprovalGate`. Today the prompt is only `descriptor.description` ("Apply a verified fix proposal…"), so the human would approve without seeing what changes. Code change 1 (TRD-019): the prompt names the proposal, its files and a diff summary.
   - `commit-policy.ts` has no importers today. Code change 2 (TRD-021): wire it in so an applied fix is committed with attribution.

### Alternatives considered (architecture)

| Option | Summary | Why not chosen |
|---|---|---|
| **A — Widen the existing translator, inline notification** | Add file and release branches inside `event-translator.ts`; keep notification-state logic at each `ctx.ui.notify` call site. | `event-translator.ts` would cover three unrelated source domains. Busy/duplicate/stale logic would be copied per behavior, which is the per-reaction duplication the PRD sets out to remove. |
| **B — Dedicated adapter modules + shared notification-state module** *(chosen)* | One adapter module per source type, all feeding the same ingress; one shared notification-state module. | Matches the existing boundary (`agent-core` = provider-neutral logic, `pi-extension` = host wiring), and centralises notification state once. |
| **C — Single generic "external signal" adapter** | One configurable "watch path X for condition Y" abstraction for both sources. | Risks becoming an arbitrary-condition escape hatch around the closed, versioned catalog (REQ-CQRS-005); still duplicates notification state. |

Verifies: TRD-005
Satisfies: REQ-005
PRD ACs Proven: AC-005-1, AC-005-2, AC-005-3
Proof of requirement: 
Target Files: packages/pi-extension/tests/agent-port-unreachable.test.ts` (new, following the existing purpose-named `AgentPort` test files)
Actions:

Test AC:
- [ ] Scenario: a finding is typed and evidence-backed -- Given a stub agent returning a diagnosis, When the investigator step runs, Then `investigation.record` holds a typed finding with at least one evidence reference
- [ ] Scenario: investigation leaves the tree untouched -- Given a canonical workspace fingerprint taken before the run, When the investigator completes, Then the fingerprint after is identical
- [ ] Scenario: an unreachable provider fails fast and visibly -- Given the provider endpoint refuses connections, When the step runs, Then it ends in `provider-unreachable` within the configured timeout and no finding is recorded
- [ ] Scenario: a hung provider times out rather than hangs -- Given a provider that never responds, When the timeout elapses, Then the state is `timed-out`, not `cancelled`, and the step returns

title: [trd:trd-2026-70e784f2-code-review-process:task:TRD-028-TEST] - [ ] **TRD-028-TEST** Tier, approval and merge gates fail when broken (4h)
description:
## Test Task: TRD-028-TEST
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-70e784f2-code-review-process.md#trd-028-test
PRD Reference: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-70e784f2-code-review-process.md#req-025

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-025**: Every new gate can fail (Must)
Every new gate can fail (Must) Each gate this work adds is shown to block a bad case. Goals and Non-Goals Goals: Reduce PR landing time by spending human attention where risk is and by presenting authors only findings that are verified. Make review converge: fewer rounds, no repeated findings, one stop rule across commands. Make human versus automated approval unambiguous and bound to a commit. Make the reviewer measurable, so improvement is demonstrated with reverts and incidents as the guardrail. Make the workflow reusable in repositories other than ensemble. Non-Goals: Replacing CodeRabbit, adding a new review provider, or editing CodeRabbit's output. Zero-human merges, or automatic tightening of approval when revert rates change. An ensemble-owned scheduler for recurring work. Enforcing a model-spend budget. Dependency Map REQ-004 depends on REQ-001, REQ-024 REQ-005 depends on REQ-004, REQ-007 REQ-006 depends on REQ-005 REQ-008 depends on REQ-006, REQ-007 REQ-010 depends on REQ-009 REQ-011 depends on REQ-007, REQ-010 REQ-012 depends on REQ-002, REQ-003 REQ-013 depends on REQ-003, REQ-012 REQ-014 depends on REQ-012 REQ-015 depends on REQ-012, REQ-013 REQ-016 depends on REQ-004, REQ-012 REQ-017 depends on REQ-005, REQ-008 REQ-018 depends on REQ-004, REQ-016 REQ-019 depends on REQ-007, REQ-009, REQ-012 REQ-020 depends on REQ-005, REQ-019 REQ-021 depends on REQ-004, REQ-016, REQ-024 REQ-022 depends on REQ-023 REQ-025 depends on REQ-005, REQ-008, REQ-009, REQ-013, REQ-014 Clusters implemented together (each independently shippable): 1. Guidance, severity and convergence: REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-003, REQ-007, REQ-009, REQ-010, REQ-011 2. Verified findings, depth and scale: REQ-004, REQ-005, REQ-006, REQ-008, REQ-016, REQ-018 3. Risk tiers, approval semantics and the security lane: REQ-012, REQ-013, REQ-014, REQ-015, REQ-017 4. Metrics and eval set: REQ-019, REQ-020 5. Sweeps and explainers: REQ-021, REQ-022 REQ-023, REQ-024 and REQ-025 apply to every cluster. Circular dependencies: none identified. Implementation Readiness Gate | Dimension | Score (1-5) | Notes | |---|---|---| | Completeness | 4.5 | All elicited practices covered; adoption mechanism, thresholds, cohort and sweep cadence now specified | | Testability | 4 | Every Must has at least two Given/When/Then ACs and thresholds are now concrete; a few softer ACs remain (for example "delivered within minutes" in AC-022-1, "cannot vouch for" in AC-010-3 and AC-014-2) | | Clarity | 4.5 | All clarification markers resolved in 1.0.1 | | Feasibility | 4 | Within stated constraints; scope is large but split into five independently shippable clusters | | Overall | 4.25 | PASS (was 4.0) | Changelog | Date | Version | Changes | |---|---|---| | 2026-10-27 | 1.0.0 | Initial draft created via /ensemble:create-prd; Readiness Gate 4.0; Constitution Gate passed. | | 2026-10-27 | 1.0.1 | Refinement: resolved all 13 clarification markers (setup via project init flow; majority vote with 0/3/5 verifiers at Quick/Standard/Deep; cap range 1-5; kind-of-change tiers; Low waiver after 20 PRs over 30 days with zero reverts/incidents, maintainers only, no trusted list; bot list plus platform bots; default depth by tier; cohort 20 PRs and 30 days with 30/50/30% targets; code-owner-confirmed eval cases; weekly sweeps; explainers offered on High-tier PRs); Entry now requires finishing 82b6a138 first; fixed AC-013-3 ambiguity (sensitive areas are High); readiness 4.0 -> 4.25. |

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-025-1: Given each of the verification threshold | When it is deliberately broken (for example a threshold set to always pass) | Then its check fails
- AC-025-2: Given a gate's check passes only in a trivial case | When it is reviewed | Then a second case that must be refused is included and refused

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen approach (Option C):** extend the pattern TRD-2026-82b6a138 established: **editable behavior in skills, agents and markdown; a small set of pure, deterministic libraries for what must not be self-certified by a model.**

- **User-owned (Constitution Rule 8), prose or data a maintainer edits without a toolchain:** per-area rules (`REVIEW.md` files), the policy block inside the root `REVIEW.md` (round cap, depth table, bot and maintainer logins, sensitive and High paths, Low-waiver state), severity definitions, reviewer, verifier, classifier and security-lane prompts, the PR template, the sweep and explainer procedures. All of it is read from the **target branch**, never from the PR head (REQ-024).
- **Enforcement (Rules 5 and 7), code that grades a model's claim:** vote tally, tier assignment with its sensitive-path floor and Low-waiver evidence, approval evaluation bound to a commit, the merge gate, round-cap derivation, repeat suppression, delta-range selection, depth bounds, slice coverage, metrics and eval scoring. Each is a pure CommonJS module in `packages/development/lib/`, exposed as a JSON-in/JSON-out subcommand of the existing `pr-review-cli.js`, following the 82b6a138 precedent. None performs network I/O or holds a timer.
- **Entry points (Rule 6):** every capability is reached through the one `pr-review-cycle` skill, which `fix-issue`, `implement-trd-beads` and `pr-merge` already invoke or will invoke (a new `MODE=gate` for `pr-merge`). YAML callers reference the skill only, never the CLI, as the existing parity tests require.
- **Recurrence (Rule 4):** nightly or weekly sweeps and daily eval runs are on-demand skills; a workflow template for the host repository is opt-in and scaffolded by init-project. Ensemble's own workflows gain no `schedule` trigger.

**Alternatives considered (user chose C):**

- **Option A -- prose-only skills and agents:** fewest files and fastest to ship. Rejected: the vote threshold, the tier floor, commit-bound approvals and the round cap would be prose a model can misread or skip, so none of these gates could be shown to fail (Rule 7), and "a bot approval never counts" would be a request, not a guarantee.
- **Option B -- a new TypeScript review engine in `agent-core`:** strongest typing and one runtime. Rejected: a new build and `dist` surface and cross-package coupling for a prompt-level feature, editable criteria pulled into code (against Rule 8), and drift toward an ensemble-owned dispatcher that competes with Foreman (Rule 4).

**Rationale:** Option C is the best fit for this brownfield repo. It adds only the code that grades claims, keeps everything a maintainer or adopting team would tune in files they can edit, adds no dependency (Constitution §4) and no CI secret, vendors into Pi automatically through the existing require-closure bundler, and each gate can be mutation-proven using the harness that already exists.

**Decisions taken where the PRD left a choice** (each is editable policy, not a hidden constant):

| Decision | Value | Where it lives |
|---|---|---|
| Policy format | Fenced `ensemble-review-policy` JSON block in the root `REVIEW.md` (no new parser dependency) | REVIEW.md, read from the base commit |
| "Cannot vouch for" a push (AC-010-3, AC-014-2) | Commit is unvouched when its tree differs from the reviewed tree and it is not a remediation commit recorded in the review-state report, or it is a merge commit | `pr-review-scope.js`, `pr-review-approvals.js` |
| Slice threshold for large PRs (AC-018-1) | 1500 changed lines, configurable | policy block |
| Area rules vs policy keys | Policy keys are read from the **root** file only; area files carry guidance, and the more restrictive instruction wins when areas conflict (AC-001-2) | skill prose |
| First PR that introduces REVIEW.md | No base copy exists, so strict defaults apply (Low treated as Medium, cap 3, default sensitive set) | `pr-review-policy.js` |
| Verifier majority | Strict majority of the expected verifier count (2 of 3, 3 of 5) | `pr-review-votes.js` |

title: [trd:trd-2026-24fac9e9-skills-eval-harness:task:TRD-010] - [ ] **TRD-010** Repeats, concurrency and reliability (`evals/lib/exec.js`) (3h)
description:
## Task: TRD-010
## References
TRD: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-24fac9e9-skills-eval-harness.md
TRD Task: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-24fac9e9-skills-eval-harness.md#trd-010
PRD: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-24fac9e9-skills-eval-harness.md
PRD Requirement: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-24fac9e9-skills-eval-harness.md#req-007
PRD ACs: AC-007-1, AC-007-2, AC-007-3
Parent Epic: [trd:trd-2026-24fac9e9-skills-eval-harness]
Read-first: read the TRD, TRD Task section, PRD and PRD Requirement above before any work on this bead.


--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-007**: Each arm repeats, and reliability is defined (Must) [RISK: flaky or costly runs distort the result]
Each arm repeats, and reliability is defined (Must) [RISK: flaky or costly runs distort the result] Each arm runs a configured number of times, 5 by default, and an eval is reliable when at least 4 of 5 runs pass.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-007-1: Given an eval with default settings | When it runs | Then each arm executes 5 times
- AC-007-2: Given an arm where 4 of 5 runs pass | When results are computed | Then the eval counts as reliable; where 3 of 5 pass, it counts as not reliable
- AC-007-3: Given a maintainer sets a different count or bar on one eval | When it runs | Then that eval uses those values and the report states them

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen: Option C, extend `evals/` and put runtimes behind adapters.**

The repository already has a headless behavioral eval harness (`evals/run.js`, `evals/lib/sandbox.js`, `evals/lib/graders.js`, `.github/workflows/evals.yml`, five task-keyed scenarios, unit tests with a stub `claude`). It already provides a throwaway git sandbox, deterministic graders, a total spend cap (`--max-usd`), results files and an on-demand workflow. It lacks what the PRD is mostly about:

| PRD need | State today |
|---|---|
| Evals keyed by skill, editable as files | Scenarios are keyed by task, one `scenario.json` each |
| With-skill and no-skill arms | One arm only |
| Repeats and a reliability bar | One run per scenario |
| Scrubbed environment | `spawnSync` inherits the whole environment |
| Model, skill version, eval version, runtime in results | Only a model tag |
| Coverage per skill, result cache, replay, regression compare | None |
| Pi | None |

| Option | Summary | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| A. Extend in place | Add the above to `run.js`; Pi logic added inline | Simplest, but Claude Code and Pi logic would tangle in one file |
| B. Adopt an external eval tool | Replace the runner with a third-party tool and port graders | Needs a spike and a new-dependency approval (constitution, Approval Requirements); rework of five tested scenarios; unknown support for a no-skill arm and Pi |
| **C. Extend with runner adapters** | Keep the tested runner, sandbox and graders. Add skill-keyed eval files, arms, repeats, an env allowlist, a results schema, coverage, cache and compare, behind a small runner interface with Claude Code and Pi adapters | **Chosen.** No new dependency (Node built-ins only), builds on tested code, and the eval format stays tool-neutral so an external runner could consume it later |

The PRD's Entry criterion (tool spike, fallback to a minimal in-repo runner) resolves to the fallback: this TRD is that runner, built on the existing harness. No new dependency is introduced, so no dependency approval is needed. If the owner later wants an external tool, the eval files in `evals/skills/` are the stable input.

Decisions fixed by the PRD and carried here: deterministic checks decide verdicts; judged checks only supplement and use a different model; 5 runs per arm with 4 of 5 required; $50 per suite and 900 s per run by default; results committed as per-skill baseline summaries with full logs as CI artifacts; Claude Code and Pi; on-demand CI only; advisory regression check.
Satisfies: REQ-007
Target File: 
Actions:

Implementation AC:
- [ ] Given default settings, when an eval runs, then each arm executes 5 times, up to `--concurrency` (default 4) at once, with budget reserved per in-flight run
- [ ] Given an arm where 4 of 5 runs pass, when results are computed, then the eval is reliable; given 3 of 5, it is not reliable
- [ ] Given `repeats` or `bar` set in an eval, when it runs, then those values are used and the report states them

**Requirement REQ-003**: Evidence is bound to the exact head commit (Must) [RISK: a result for an old commit approving a new one would let unreviewed code land]
Evidence is bound to the exact head commit (Must) [RISK: a result for an old commit approving a new one would let unreviewed code land] A local-run result is valid only for the exact head commit it ran against, and the run itself executes against that exact commit and nothing else.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-003-3: Given the maintainer's working tree has uncommitted or unpushed changes | When a local run is requested | Then the run still executes against a clean checkout of the PR's head commit and the working-tree changes have no effect on the result
- AC-003-4: Given the PR head commit cannot be fetched | When a local run is requested | Then it stops without publishing any status and names the commit it could not obtain
- AC-009-1: Given the repository's test workflow with its Node version matrix | When the local run executes | Then every matrix entry that is a required gate today is run locally, which for this repository means `validate` and `test` on Node 22 and Node 24
- AC-009-2: Given a required workflow step that the local CI runner cannot run or does not mirror (an unsupported action, a missing runner feature, or a step absent from the configured list) | When the local run encounters it | Then the run fails, the failing step is named, and the PR is not approved on the strength of a partial run.
- AC-010-1: Given secrets are needed for a local run | When it executes | Then they come from gitignored local configuration or the environment and never from tracked files
- AC-015-1: Given a failing local run | When the merge flow stops | Then it reports the failing workflow, job and step and the exact head commit
- AC-015-2: Given the local CI runner's prerequisites (the repository's local CI entry point, git, or a required Node version) are unavailable | When the merge flow is invoked | Then it stops with a message naming the missing prerequisite rather than falling back to merging without evidence.

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-009**: The local run covers what hosted CI covers (Must)
The local run covers what hosted CI covers (Must) The local run executes the same workflows and jobs that hosted CI would, so a local pass is a meaningful predictor of a hosted pass.

title: Behavior tool-grant window spans the whole agent run, including the user's own work
description:
beginBehaviorScope() opens at turn_end when a continuation is injected; only agent_end or session_shutdown closes it (tool-grant-enforcement.ts:57-69). In an interactive session the injected turn and every following user and advisor message form one run, so the behavior's grants applied to unrelated user-directed work for several replies: 'tool todo is not granted to executing behavior(s) [investigate-test-failure, fix-failing-test]'; write, eval, task and learn were also blocked. It cleared only when that run finally ended. The code comment accepts 'an interjection landing inside a behavior turn'; observed scope is much wider. Also: the same agent_end then ran verification and a rollback of the whole working tree against a 6-minute-old snapshot.

Evidence: headless omp -p runs on dev (7b57d4a) in worktree /private/tmp/wt-e2e, planted bug scripts/lib/e2e-sum.js; logs in /tmp/e2e/ (e2e.jsonl, e2e2.jsonl, e2e3.jsonl, guard.jsonl, *-runtime-log.jsonl).

comments.text: Fixed in PR #94 (fix/behavior-scoped-write-boundary, not yet merged). Verified with headless omp runs loading the branch bundle; see PR description. Close on merge.

comments.author: ldangelo
comments.text: VERIFIED FIXED on dev (02db136). The window no longer waits for session_shutdown. closeBehaviorWindow() is called on THREE paths: agent_end (extension.ts:747, 'the window must not outlive the run'), session_shutdown as a fail-safe (754, 'a crashed or aborted run must never strand the user in a narrowed session'), and turn_end (763, checked before a new continuation is taken so a window opened by that handler is not judged against its own turn). The bead's specific defect -- grants spanning every following user and advisor message until the run ends -- is addressed by the agent_end and turn_end closes. RESIDUAL, tracked on br-o355 not here: I hit a tool denial live this session ('wait is not granted to executing behavior(s)') while a fix turn was legitimately in flight. That is the accepted 'interjection landing inside a behavior turn' case, and the open question it raises -- whether a window should ever REMOVE a capability the session already had -- is br-o355's.

comments.author: ldangelo
comments.text:
FOLLOW-UP: I closed this citing line numbers and a comment without reading
the conditional. Read it now. The close stands, but on different evidence.

turn_end's close is GATED, not unconditional:
    if (awaitingVerification && fixTurnFinished(event)) {
      closeBehaviorWindow();
      verifyPendingFix();
    }

So it depends on awaitingVerification always being set whenever a window is
opened. It is, and in the same handler:
    777  openBehaviorWindow(next.behaviors)
    808  awaitingVerification = { ... }
The window opens when a continuation is queued and the pairing is assigned a
few lines later, so the NEXT turn_end closes it. That is the actual fix for
this bead: the window ends with the fix turn, not with the whole agent run.

agent_end closes unconditionally as a backstop ("a run can end without a
finished fix turn -- aborted, errored, or cut short"), and session_shutdown
is a fail-safe.

NARROW RESIDUAL, not worth reopening but worth knowing: between 777 and 808
sits pi.sendUserMessage(). If that throws, the window is open and
awaitingVerification was never assigned, so turn_end's gate cannot fire and
only agent_end closes it -- i.e. the original symptom, in the error path
only. If anyone touches this code, assign awaitingVerification BEFORE
sending, or wrap the send so a failure closes the window.

ldangelo
comments.text:
LIVE REPRODUCTION, on the maintainer's own session, 2026-09-28.

An autofix continuation fired off a broken test file of mine. Some time later -- across several unrelated turns of my own work (editing source, running jest, rebuilding a bundle, launching a live trial run) -- a tool call was refused:

  tool 'wait' is not granted to executing behavior(s)
  [investigate-test-failure, fix-failing-test]
  (granted tools: [bash, edit, ensemble.bash, glob, grep, read])

This is the bead's original complaint, observed rather than argued: the behavior window was still open over work that had nothing to do with the fix turn, and it narrowed the operator's own toolset.

Mechanism, confirmed: the window closes at the first turn_end where fixTurnFinished(event) is true, and that predicate is 'the turn ended with NO tool calls'. Every turn I took used tools, so none of them qualified, and the window persisted across all of them.

I downgraded this to non-blocking earlier today on the grounds that it does not stop an approval from resolving. That was right about approvals and wrong about impact: it degrades every session it spans, and it took a refused tool call rather than a code reading to see it.

The close condition should be tied to the FIX TURN's identity -- the turn opened by sendUserMessage -- not to a heuristic about whether some turn happened to call tools.

comments.author: ldangelo
comments.text:
REASSESSED 2026-09-29 on feature/trd-2026-0fc1c1d0-behavior-runtime-pi-harness. Substantially narrowed, NOT closed.

PREMISE CHANGED. This bead describes a scope opened at turn_end when a CONTINUATION is injected, closed only at agent_end or session_shutdown. The continuation path was deleted by br-behavior-runtime-cqrs-xl24 (section 7 forbids two dispatch paths), so that mechanism no longer exists. beginBehaviorScope now opens immediately before matcher.onEvent and is released in a finally around it (extension.ts:162-177); agent_end and session_shutdown remain only as fail-safes against a crashed run stranding the user.

Window therefore went from 'the injected turn plus every following user and advisor message' to 'the duration of one dispatch'.

RESIDUAL RISK, still real. The dispatch is deliberately NOT awaited (extension.ts comment: the host stops waiting on a handler after 30s and blocks the tool as a fail-safe). So a behavior dispatch runs CONCURRENTLY with the user's own work, and the tool_call hook plus the scope are both process-global. A user tool call issued while a dispatch is in flight is still evaluated against the behavior's grants. The window is much smaller, but it is not zero, and the reported symptom -- 'tool todo is not granted to executing behavior(s)' hitting user-directed work -- remains reachable.

A real fix needs per-caller attribution at the tool_call hook so the scope applies only to calls originating from the behavior's own agent invocation. Whether Pi's tool_call event carries anything usable for that is unverified and should be checked before anyone designs around it.

CORRECTION to an earlier note of mine: I had recorded that tool-grant-enforcement.ts:104-107 'intersects rather than unions' scoped grants. That is wrong. Line 100-102 allows the call if ANY scoped behavior grants the tool, and 104-107 builds a union purely for the denial message. No intersection bug exists.

PR #94 (fix/behavior-scoped-write-boundary) is NOT on this branch -- git merge-base confirms c6b93dd 'merge: integrate #94, #95 and #96' is not an ancestor of HEAD. The narrowing described above came from the CQRS port, independently. At merge, check which implementation survives rather than assuming they compose.

title: [trd:trd-2026-b6db9749-behavior-habits-runtime:task:TRD-005] - [ ] **TRD-005** Give `AgentPort` distinct, bounded `provider-unreachable` and `timed-out` states, and prove a finding is typed and non-mutating (3h)
description:
## Task: TRD-005
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-b6db9749-behavior-habits-runtime.md#trd-005
PRD Reference: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-b6db9749-behavior-habits-runtime.md#req-005

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-005**: Support a read-only investigator session mode
Support a read-only investigator session mode Priority: Must A behavior can invoke a read-only investigator session, distinct from the existing auto-fix ("Applier") mode, that diagnoses without mutating.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-005-1: Given a behavior configured with an investigator step | When it runs | Then it produces a typed, evidence-backed finding
- AC-005-2: Given the same behavior | When the investigator step completes | Then no workspace mutation has occurred as a side effect
- AC-005-3: Given the model/LLM provider is unreachable | When an investigator session is invoked | Then it fails with a distinct, visible error state within a bounded timeout — it never hangs indefinitely and never silently returns a stale or fabricated finding

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen: Option B — dedicated adapter modules per new trigger-source type, plus a shared notification-state module.** Unchanged from 1.0.0.

New `file-source-adapter.ts` and `release-source-adapter.ts` under `packages/agent-core/src/behavior/` each produce a `BehaviorEvent` through `normalizeEvent`, mirroring the existing `pi-events.ts` → `event-translator.ts` → `normalizeEvent` → `LocalEventMatcher` chain. A new `notification-state.ts` in `pi-extension` centralises busy, duplicate and stale tracking for every behavior. Package quarantine gets its own `package-quarantine.ts` beside `package-discovery.ts`.

### Decisions added in 1.1.0

1. **How artifact changes are detected: content hashes checked at lifecycle points.** No `fs.watch`, no new dependency.
   - The adapter derives its watch set from the compiled `artifact.changed` triggers (the `path` predicate).
   - It hashes those files at `tool_result` and at `agent_end`, and emits an event when a digest differs from the last one seen in the session.
   - The hooks it relies on already exist, which is what AC-001-2 means by "supported host API".
   - It behaves the same on every OS (see REQ-023).
   - It needs no new dependency, which constitution §4 would require approval for.

   | Option | Why not chosen |
   |---|---|
   | `fs.watch` | Event semantics differ between macOS, Linux and Windows (rename-vs-change, recursive support). That is exactly the kind of per-platform behavior difference REQ-023 forbids absorbing silently. It also keeps a handle open for the whole session. |
   | `chokidar` | A new runtime dependency (constitution §4), for a problem that lifecycle-point hashing already solves. |

   The limitation, stated rather than hidden: a change is seen at the next tool call or at the end of the run, not instantly. NFR-001 measures from event validation, so this latency is outside its budget. TRD-003 reports it separately.

2. **Release signal (resolves the PRD's REQ-002 clarification): a new `v*` tag in local refs.** This matches this repo's `release.yml` (`on: push: tags: ['v*']`).
   - The tag pattern is a trigger predicate, so repositories with different conventions change configuration, not code (Rule 8).
   - It is detected two ways. First, from a successful tag-creating tool call (`git tag`, `gh release create`), in the same way `repository.changed` is derived today. Second, by diffing tag refs at session start and at `agent_end`, which covers tags that arrive by fetch.
   - It emits the **existing** catalog type `release.completed`, carrying `{ tag, sha, source }`.
   - One tag produces one event per session, whichever path sees it first.

3. **Coverage metric (resolves the PRD's REQ-016 clarification): Jest `json-summary` output, per file, `lines.pct` and `branches.pct` by default.**
   - Each package's `test:coverage` is `jest --coverage`. Jest's default reporters (`json`, `lcov`, `text`, `clover`) produce raw maps, not percentages.
   - So the behavior watches `coverage/coverage-summary.json`, and its README tells repositories to enable `json-summary`.
   - The metrics and the threshold (default 1.0 percentage point) are behavior configuration.
   - If the artifact never appears, the behavior shows up as an inert trigger in `/ensemble-status`; it is never silently idle.
   - The baseline is the previous snapshot seen **in the same session** (Rule 4). The first observation in a session only sets the baseline.

4. **The comparison is a generic command: `artifact.compare` (TRD-033).** It compares numeric JSON paths between the previous and current snapshot of an artifact and knows nothing about coverage.
   - The alternatives were rejected. Doing the comparison in an agent step would make the reported delta an unverified model claim (REQ-012). A coverage-specific command would make the third behavior need Ensemble code (REQ-018).
   - It lands in PR 1, which is why PR 5 can be configuration only.

5. **Notification transport** (REQ-009, REQ-010). `notification-state.ts` delivers to two sinks:
   - **The user**, through `SessionUiBridge.notify`, a new method that wraps `ctx.ui.notify`. Headless sessions fall back to the console.
   - **The model's context**, through `pi.sendMessage` with `display: true` and `triggerTurn: false`.

   `triggerTurn: false` is deliberate. #107 deleted the continuation path because a message that makes the agent act bypasses `MutationGuard` (`extension.ts:118-140`); a notification is data, never an instruction. Any test-derived text in a notification is fenced and labelled as data, a lesson from #94's live runs. `sendMessage` is added to `assertRequiredCapabilities`.

6. **Verified fix application** (REQ-033). This is configuration plus two small code changes.
   - A new behavior, `apply-verified-fix`, runs `mode: auto`. It triggers on `fix.verified` with the predicate `verdict: passed`, declares only `fix.apply` with no tools, and calls `fix.apply { proposalRef: ${event.payload.proposalRef} }`.
   - `CommandRegistry` then asks `ApprovalGate`. Today the prompt is only `descriptor.description` ("Apply a verified fix proposal…"), so the human would approve without seeing what changes. Code change 1 (TRD-019): the prompt names the proposal, its files and a diff summary.
   - `commit-policy.ts` has no importers today. Code change 2 (TRD-021): wire it in so an applied fix is committed with attribution.

### Alternatives considered (architecture)

| Option | Summary | Why not chosen |
|---|---|---|
| **A — Widen the existing translator, inline notification** | Add file and release branches inside `event-translator.ts`; keep notification-state logic at each `ctx.ui.notify` call site. | `event-translator.ts` would cover three unrelated source domains. Busy/duplicate/stale logic would be copied per behavior, which is the per-reaction duplication the PRD sets out to remove. |
| **B — Dedicated adapter modules + shared notification-state module** *(chosen)* | One adapter module per source type, all feeding the same ingress; one shared notification-state module. | Matches the existing boundary (`agent-core` = provider-neutral logic, `pi-extension` = host wiring), and centralises notification state once. |
| **C — Single generic "external signal" adapter** | One configurable "watch path X for condition Y" abstraction for both sources. | Risks becoming an arbitrary-condition escape hatch around the closed, versioned catalog (REQ-CQRS-005); still duplicates notification state. |
Satisfies: REQ-005

## Test Task: TRD-006-TEST
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-15aa5acd-live-behavior-dispatch-autofix.md#trd-006-test
PRD Reference: #req-009

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen: Option C — single enforcement seam, additive.**

A new `MutationGuard` chokepoint in `agent-core` is the one place `policy.mode`, `capabilities.mutation_classes` (via the existing `hasMutationAuthority()`), and protected-path rules are resolved. It is wired once at the loader boundary rather than replicated per tool registration. The translator, matcher, and auto-fix loop are added to `pi-extension`. Discovery roots and `execution.test_command` are additive changes to existing schema/discovery code. `ToolRegistry`, `outbox`, and the compiler are reused unchanged.

### Alternatives considered

| Option | Summary | Why not chosen |
|---|---|---|
| **A — In-place extension** | Enforce mode/mutation/path rules as wrapper checks inside `behavior-loader`'s per-tool `execute()` closures. | Enforcement scattered across call sites; every future tool registration must remember to wrap. The PRD's central failure mode is *guarantees that exist in one place but are not reached from another* — Option A reproduces exactly that shape. |
| **B — Governance kernel** | Route every mutation through a `MutationBroker` + `GovernedWorkspace` in `agent-core`; `pi-extension` becomes a thin adapter. | Strongest long-term design and the right eventual target, but it re-opens already-shipped code across every tool path for a ~6-7 PR refactor before a single PRD requirement is demonstrable. Deferred deliberately, not rejected. |
| **C — Single enforcement seam** *(chosen)* | One `MutationGuard` chokepoint, wired once; everything else additive. | Gets a single auditable chokepoint (Option B's main benefit) without Option B's refactor surface. Fits the existing `agent-core` / `pi-extension` split. |

### Architectural note carried from grounding

Two defects found while grounding this design are folded into PR 1 rather than left implicit:

1. `pi-events.ts` emits `runtime.tool_result` / `runtime.tool.called` / `runtime.tool.failed` / `runtime.tool.completed`, none of which appear in `HARNESS_EVENT_TYPES` (which defines `runtime.tool_call.started` / `runtime.tool_call.completed`). `normalizeEvent` does not currently reject uncatalogued types, so PRD AC-002-1's "validated against the closed catalog" would be vacuous. Addressed by TRD-001 (`[satisfies INFRA]`).
2. `behavior-loader.ts:79` calls `registry.grant(...)` unconditionally immediately before `registry.invoke(...)`, making the grant boundary a rubber stamp for behavior-governed tools (unlike the echo path, where the grant is CLI-flag-gated). Addressed by TRD-003.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-014-1: Given an event payload | When it is accepted | Then it is validated and an invalid or disallowed value is rejected before it changes run state or selects a tool

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen: Option C — hardened in-session stage composition with a dedicated atomic run-index store.**

`new-feature` is authored the same way every other product command in this repo is authored: a single orchestrating skill (`packages/development/commands/new-feature.yaml`, generated to runtime-specific prompts exactly like `fix-issue.yaml`) that executes each stage's existing skill body in-session — the same mechanism that loaded `ensemble-refine-prd`'s content into this session and had the agent execute its Phases directly. This is forced, not merely preferred: Pi's `ExtensionAPI` has no completion/invoke primitive that would let an extension programmatically run another skill and get its result back (confirmed — no `pi.invokeCommand` or equivalent exists); the only code-level "run a skill" mechanism, `createAgentPort()`, spawns a bounded, disposable `omp -p --no-session --no-extensions` subprocess in an isolated worktree, and does not fit a long-lived, project-resident workflow whose PRD/TRD stages use the interactive `--collab` review server.

What is new, and is the one piece of real infrastructure this TRD adds: a `RunIndexStore` (`packages/agent-core/src/new-feature/run-index.ts`) built on the one proven concurrency-safe pattern in this repo — `session.js`'s temp-file-then-`renameSync` atomic write plus `expectedRevision`/409-style optimistic concurrency — rather than `ProposalStore`'s plain `writeFileSync` (no atomicity, no lock, not adequate for PRD AC-005-3's fail-closed-on-malformed-index requirement). Runs are stored at `.ensemble/new-feature/<run-id>.json`, mirroring `ProposalStore`'s `.ensemble/proposals/<ref>.json` convention (also excluded from `tree-baseline.ts` drift detection, so this is consistent runtime-owned state, not a project-source mutation).

### Alternatives considered

| Option | Summary | Why not chosen |
|---|---|---|
| A — Plain JSON checkpoint | Same in-session composition, but checkpoints are a single `writeFileSync`, no atomicity/locking. | Fastest to build, but a crash mid-write can corrupt the run index, which directly violates AC-005-3's "fail closed with a recoverable diagnostic" requirement — the repo's own `ProposalStore` already demonstrates this gap is real, not hypothetical. |
| B — Subprocess-dispatched stages | New orchestrator module dispatches every stage as a bounded `createAgentPort()` subprocess; advances the run index only after subprocess exit 0 + artifact-on-disk confirmation. | Most rigorous completion signal (a real process boundary instead of self-reported bookkeeping), but substantially more build effort, and does not fit the interactive `--collab` review-server stages `create-prd`/`refine-prd` already use — those are long-lived, human-attended HTTP sessions, not bounded one-shot subprocess work, and would need bespoke carve-out handling under this option. |
| **C — Hardened in-session composition** *(chosen)* | In-session stage execution (like every existing product command), backed by a dedicated atomic `RunIndexStore`. | Reuses 100% of the existing skill-composition and `ask_user`-approval infrastructure (including the `--collab` review server, which needs no special-casing), while fixing Option A's one real correctness gap with the repo's one proven atomic-write pattern. Matches user-confirmed direction. |

### Honest trust-boundary note

Because stage execution stays in-session (per Option C), the approval gates implemented by TRD-014/TRD-017/TRD-019 are enforced by the orchestrating skill's own conditional logic checking `RunIndexStore`-persisted approval fields before it issues an implementation or `gh pr create` tool call — not by a separate runtime authorization chokepoint like `agent-core`'s `MutationGuard` (which exists elsewhere in this repo, gating CQRS-registered commands, but `new-feature`'s mutating actions are ordinary skill-level tool calls, same as `fix-issue`'s own gated PR-creation step, not CQRS commands). This is the same trust boundary every existing Ensemble product command already operates under. Building a `MutationGuard`-equivalent chokepoint for skill-level tool calls is a materially larger investment this PRD does not request and no other product command has; REQ-014's "runtime authority" is satisfied here by making the check a required precondition over persisted, validated store state rather than over prompt claims — which is what AC-014-2 actually asks for — not by inventing a new enforcement subsystem.

PRD ACs: AC-014-1
Target File: packages/agent-core/src/new-feature/event-mapping.ts

1. Every event payload, artifact reference, or user-supplied path crossing the workflow boundary (TRD-005's resume input, TRD-013's event payload) is validated against its schema/allow-list before it changes any `RunIndexStore` state or selects a tool to invoke.
2. An invalid or disallowed value is rejected at the boundary function itself, before the caller can act on it — not after a partial state change.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-025-1: Given each of the verification threshold | When it is deliberately broken (for example a threshold set to always pass) | Then its check fails
- AC-025-2: Given a gate's check passes only in a trivial case | When it is reviewed | Then a second case that must be refused is included and refused

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen approach (Option C):** extend the pattern TRD-2026-82b6a138 established: **editable behavior in skills, agents and markdown; a small set of pure, deterministic libraries for what must not be self-certified by a model.**

- **User-owned (Constitution Rule 8), prose or data a maintainer edits without a toolchain:** per-area rules (`REVIEW.md` files), the policy block inside the root `REVIEW.md` (round cap, depth table, bot and maintainer logins, sensitive and High paths, Low-waiver state), severity definitions, reviewer, verifier, classifier and security-lane prompts, the PR template, the sweep and explainer procedures. All of it is read from the **target branch**, never from the PR head (REQ-024).
- **Enforcement (Rules 5 and 7), code that grades a model's claim:** vote tally, tier assignment with its sensitive-path floor and Low-waiver evidence, approval evaluation bound to a commit, the merge gate, round-cap derivation, repeat suppression, delta-range selection, depth bounds, slice coverage, metrics and eval scoring. Each is a pure CommonJS module in `packages/development/lib/`, exposed as a JSON-in/JSON-out subcommand of the existing `pr-review-cli.js`, following the 82b6a138 precedent. None performs network I/O or holds a timer.
- **Entry points (Rule 6):** every capability is reached through the one `pr-review-cycle` skill, which `fix-issue`, `implement-trd-beads` and `pr-merge` already invoke or will invoke (a new `MODE=gate` for `pr-merge`). YAML callers reference the skill only, never the CLI, as the existing parity tests require.
- **Recurrence (Rule 4):** nightly or weekly sweeps and daily eval runs are on-demand skills; a workflow template for the host repository is opt-in and scaffolded by init-project. Ensemble's own workflows gain no `schedule` trigger.

**Alternatives considered (user chose C):**

- **Option A -- prose-only skills and agents:** fewest files and fastest to ship. Rejected: the vote threshold, the tier floor, commit-bound approvals and the round cap would be prose a model can misread or skip, so none of these gates could be shown to fail (Rule 7), and "a bot approval never counts" would be a request, not a guarantee.
- **Option B -- a new TypeScript review engine in `agent-core`:** strongest typing and one runtime. Rejected: a new build and `dist` surface and cross-package coupling for a prompt-level feature, editable criteria pulled into code (against Rule 8), and drift toward an ensemble-owned dispatcher that competes with Foreman (Rule 4).

**Rationale:** Option C is the best fit for this brownfield repo. It adds only the code that grades claims, keeps everything a maintainer or adopting team would tune in files they can edit, adds no dependency (Constitution §4) and no CI secret, vendors into Pi automatically through the existing require-closure bundler, and each gate can be mutation-proven using the harness that already exists.

**Decisions taken where the PRD left a choice** (each is editable policy, not a hidden constant):

| Decision | Value | Where it lives |
|---|---|---|
| Policy format | Fenced `ensemble-review-policy` JSON block in the root `REVIEW.md` (no new parser dependency) | REVIEW.md, read from the base commit |
| "Cannot vouch for" a push (AC-010-3, AC-014-2) | Commit is unvouched when its tree differs from the reviewed tree and it is not a remediation commit recorded in the review-state report, or it is a merge commit | `pr-review-scope.js`, `pr-review-approvals.js` |
| Slice threshold for large PRs (AC-018-1) | 1500 changed lines, configurable | policy block |
| Area rules vs policy keys | Policy keys are read from the **root** file only; area files carry guidance, and the more restrictive instruction wins when areas conflict (AC-001-2) | skill prose |
| First PR that introduces REVIEW.md | No base copy exists, so strict defaults apply (Low treated as Medium, cap 3, default sensitive set) | `pr-review-policy.js` |
| Verifier majority | Strict majority of the expected verifier count (2 of 3, 3 of 5) | `pr-review-votes.js` |

title: [trd:trd-2026-15aa5acd-live-behavior-dispatch-autofix:task:TRD-001] - [ ] **TRD-001** Reconcile `pi-events.ts` normalized event types with `HARNESS_EVENT_TYPES`, and make `normalizeEvent` reject uncatalogued types (4h)
description:
## Task: TRD-001
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-15aa5acd-live-behavior-dispatch-autofix.md#trd-001

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen: Option C — single enforcement seam, additive.**

A new `MutationGuard` chokepoint in `agent-core` is the one place `policy.mode`, `capabilities.mutation_classes` (via the existing `hasMutationAuthority()`), and protected-path rules are resolved. It is wired once at the loader boundary rather than replicated per tool registration. The translator, matcher, and auto-fix loop are added to `pi-extension`. Discovery roots and `execution.test_command` are additive changes to existing schema/discovery code. `ToolRegistry`, `outbox`, and the compiler are reused unchanged.

### Alternatives considered

| Option | Summary | Why not chosen |
|---|---|---|
| **A — In-place extension** | Enforce mode/mutation/path rules as wrapper checks inside `behavior-loader`'s per-tool `execute()` closures. | Enforcement scattered across call sites; every future tool registration must remember to wrap. The PRD's central failure mode is *guarantees that exist in one place but are not reached from another* — Option A reproduces exactly that shape. |
| **B — Governance kernel** | Route every mutation through a `MutationBroker` + `GovernedWorkspace` in `agent-core`; `pi-extension` becomes a thin adapter. | Strongest long-term design and the right eventual target, but it re-opens already-shipped code across every tool path for a ~6-7 PR refactor before a single PRD requirement is demonstrable. Deferred deliberately, not rejected. |
| **C — Single enforcement seam** *(chosen)* | One `MutationGuard` chokepoint, wired once; everything else additive. | Gets a single auditable chokepoint (Option B's main benefit) without Option B's refactor surface. Fits the existing `agent-core` / `pi-extension` split. |

### Architectural note carried from grounding

Two defects found while grounding this design are folded into PR 1 rather than left implicit:

1. `pi-events.ts` emits `runtime.tool_result` / `runtime.tool.called` / `runtime.tool.failed` / `runtime.tool.completed`, none of which appear in `HARNESS_EVENT_TYPES` (which defines `runtime.tool_call.started` / `runtime.tool_call.completed`). `normalizeEvent` does not currently reject uncatalogued types, so PRD AC-002-1's "validated against the closed catalog" would be vacuous. Addressed by TRD-001 (`[satisfies INFRA]`).
2. `behavior-loader.ts:79` calls `registry.grant(...)` unconditionally immediately before `registry.invoke(...)`, making the grant boundary a rubber stamp for behavior-governed tools (unlike the echo path, where the grant is CLI-flag-gated). Addressed by TRD-003.
Satisfies: INFRA
PRD ACs: AC-002-1
Target File: packages/pi-extension/src/pi-events.ts, packages/agent-core/src/behavior/event-catalog.ts, packages/agent-core/src/events.ts
Actions:

Implementation AC:
- [ ] Given a normalized event whose type is absent from the catalog, when `normalizeEvent` is called, then it throws rather than returning an event.
