Read-first: read the TRD, TRD Task section, PRD and PRD Requirement above before any work on this bead.


--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-006**: Default adapters for every category
Default adapters for every category Priority: Must Every category in the taxonomy ships with a default adapter reproducing ensemble's current behavior for the tool currently used.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-006-2: Given the worktree-manager category | When its default adapter is inspected | Then it covers worktree operations using plain source-control worktrees and no command invokes it yet

--- TRD Context ---
### Alternatives Considered

| Option | Approach | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|---|
| A: Prose-only adapters | Adapter is a skill; the agent follows its prose and normalizes tool output itself | Smallest build; fully editable | Cannot route internal CLIs deterministically (REQ-016), cannot validate output (REQ-022), cannot deny at runtime (REQ-023); behavior varies per model |
| **B: Manifest plus runner (chosen)** | Adapter is a skill directory: `SKILL.md` (vocabulary and agent-facing prose) plus a declarative `adapter.yaml` (capability command templates, output mapping, allowlist, health check, detection signals, required env names). A core resolver library and `toolchain-cli` execute capabilities deterministically | Meets PRD (adapter is a skill), Rule 8 (editable without rebuild), Rule 5 (enforcement in code), REQ-016 (CLIs call the same library) | New resolver, runner, manifest schema and output-mapping engine to build and test |
| C: Executable plugin adapters | Separately packaged executables speaking a versioned JSON protocol | Arbitrary logic; strongest isolation | Contradicts the PRD's skills-as-contract decision; fails Rule 8; needs per-OS packaging and a protocol |

**Rationale:** B is the only option that makes every PRD guarantee a code-enforced property while keeping adapters user-editable data. The requester selected B at the architecture gate.

### Interpretations and Resolved Design Issues

- **I1: plain version control.** The PRD taxonomy has no plain `git` category, yet about 45 sources invoke it. Plain `git` operations (status, commit, push, log, diff, merge-base) are `vcs.*` capabilities of the `workflow` category, whose default adapter is `plain-git`; the `git-town` adapter extends it. Recommend a PRD refine pass to name this explicitly.
- **I2: ambiguity versus no signal (PRD REQ-009 AC-2 vs REQ-010 AC-2).** "No detectable signal" means no signal source exists at all (no remote, no marker files); the shipped default is used. "Ambiguous" means two or more installed adapters match, or a signal source exists (for example a remote URL) but matches no installed adapter; resolution fails explicitly in non-interactive runs and asks in interactive runs.
- **I3: AC-023-2 (governed boundary denies).** The runner is invoked through the shell tool, so a command that was not granted the shell tool cannot run any adapter; an adapter therefore cannot widen grants. The runner additionally denies any command outside the adapter's binary-plus-subcommand allowlist. Denial of raw shell commands typed by an agent outside the runner remains host-enforced (hooks on Claude Code; none in this repo for Pi, OpenCode or Codex); the lint (REQ-019) keeps commands from issuing raw tool calls. This residual is recorded in the Threat Model.
- **I4: confirmation session identity.** No stable session id is exposed uniformly across runtimes. TRD-017 begins with a spike that records which id each runtime exposes (`ENSEMBLE_SESSION_ID`, host session variables); the passive confirmation record is keyed by `(sessionKey, category, adapter, configHash)` and falls back to the run id when no session id exists.
- **I5: repo-local adapters are untrusted by default.** A cloned repository can ship `.ensemble/adapters/`. Repo-local adapters resolve in every mode (satisfying AC-007-3) but a non-interactive run additionally requires the adapter name in the user's `trustedRepoAdapters` list; an interactive run shows the adapter's allowlist at first-use confirmation.
- **I6: no new runtime dependency.** The output-mapping engine uses a small dotted-path projection (`$.a.b[0]`, `|` alternation for "array or object"), not a JSONPath library, because constitution section 4 requires approval for new dependencies.
- **I7: work-graph selection.** `work-graph` is its own category with default `auto`: use the work-graph capabilities of the resolved tracker adapter when its manifest provides them; otherwise use the built-in `work-graph-links-fallback` adapter (tracker dependency links, then plan order stated as not dependency-aware). One manifest may implement several categories.
- **I8: PRD BDD floor.** Fourteen PRD requirements (REQ-001, 002, 004, 005, 006, 009, 010, 012, 015, 018, 021, 022, 024, 025) have two ACs, below the command's three-scenario floor. The test tasks specify exactly one scenario per AC; recommend a PRD refine pass to add edge or error ACs.
- **I10: packaging.** `packages/development` depends only on `js-yaml` and its libraries require only siblings, so the resolver library, category contracts, default selection, schemas and tool inventory all ship inside `packages/development` (`lib/toolchain/` and `toolchain/`). A standalone plugin install and the Pi vendor bundle therefore contain everything; other packages call `toolchain-cli` through `TOOLCHAIN_CLI` rather than importing it.
- **I9: preflight is enforced in code.** `toolchain-cli run` refuses a side-effecting capability unless a passing preflight record exists for the supplied `--run-id`; the command prose cannot silently skip preflight.
Verifies: TRD-042
Satisfies: REQ-006
PRD ACs Proven: AC-006-2

Target Files: 
Actions:

Test AC:
- [ ] Scenario: Worktree default adapter covers worktree operations -- Given the worktree-manager category, When the shipped default adapter `adapter-worktree-plain-git` is inspected through `toolchain-cli explain` and its `adapter.yaml`, Then its create, list, remove and prune capabilities all run `git worktree` subcommands and a scan of `packages/*/commands` finds no `worktree.*` capability reference

Read-first: read the TRD, TRD Task section, PRD and PRD Requirement above before any work on this bead.


--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-009**: Runs see only an allowed set of environment values (Must)
Runs see only an allowed set of environment values (Must)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-009-4: Given an eval change from a contributor | When it is proposed | Then it is reviewed like code before it runs with any credential, and a hosted CI run triggered from an untrusted source receives no secrets

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen: Option C, extend `evals/` and put runtimes behind adapters.**

The repository already has a headless behavioral eval harness (`evals/run.js`, `evals/lib/sandbox.js`, `evals/lib/graders.js`, `.github/workflows/evals.yml`, five task-keyed scenarios, unit tests with a stub `claude`). It already provides a throwaway git sandbox, deterministic graders, a total spend cap (`--max-usd`), results files and an on-demand workflow. It lacks what the PRD is mostly about:

| PRD need | State today |
|---|---|
| Evals keyed by skill, editable as files | Scenarios are keyed by task, one `scenario.json` each |
| With-skill and no-skill arms | One arm only |
| Repeats and a reliability bar | One run per scenario |
| Scrubbed environment | `spawnSync` inherits the whole environment |
| Model, skill version, eval version, runtime in results | Only a model tag |
| Coverage per skill, result cache, replay, regression compare | None |
| Pi | None |

| Option | Summary | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| A. Extend in place | Add the above to `run.js`; Pi logic added inline | Simplest, but Claude Code and Pi logic would tangle in one file |

Read-first: read the TRD, TRD Task section, PRD and PRD Requirement above before any work on this bead.


--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-021**: Identical resolution across generated runtimes
Identical resolution across generated runtimes Priority: Must Adapter resolution behaves identically in every runtime ensemble generates content for. The first-release supported runtimes are Claude Code, OpenCode, Pi/OMP and Codex.

--- TRD Context ---
### Alternatives Considered

| Option | Approach | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|---|
| A: Prose-only adapters | Adapter is a skill; the agent follows its prose and normalizes tool output itself | Smallest build; fully editable | Cannot route internal CLIs deterministically (REQ-016), cannot validate output (REQ-022), cannot deny at runtime (REQ-023); behavior varies per model |
| **B: Manifest plus runner (chosen)** | Adapter is a skill directory: `SKILL.md` (vocabulary and agent-facing prose) plus a declarative `adapter.yaml` (capability command templates, output mapping, allowlist, health check, detection signals, required env names). A core resolver library and `toolchain-cli` execute capabilities deterministically | Meets PRD (adapter is a skill), Rule 8 (editable without rebuild), Rule 5 (enforcement in code), REQ-016 (CLIs call the same library) | New resolver, runner, manifest schema and output-mapping engine to build and test |
| C: Executable plugin adapters | Separately packaged executables speaking a versioned JSON protocol | Arbitrary logic; strongest isolation | Contradicts the PRD's skills-as-contract decision; fails Rule 8; needs per-OS packaging and a protocol |

**Rationale:** B is the only option that makes every PRD guarantee a code-enforced property while keeping adapters user-editable data. The requester selected B at the architecture gate.

### Interpretations and Resolved Design Issues

- **I1: plain version control.** The PRD taxonomy has no plain `git` category, yet about 45 sources invoke it. Plain `git` operations (status, commit, push, log, diff, merge-base) are `vcs.*` capabilities of the `workflow` category, whose default adapter is `plain-git`; the `git-town` adapter extends it. Recommend a PRD refine pass to name this explicitly.
- **I2: ambiguity versus no signal (PRD REQ-009 AC-2 vs REQ-010 AC-2).** "No detectable signal" means no signal source exists at all (no remote, no marker files); the shipped default is used. "Ambiguous" means two or more installed adapters match, or a signal source exists (for example a remote URL) but matches no installed adapter; resolution fails explicitly in non-interactive runs and asks in interactive runs.
- **I3: AC-023-2 (governed boundary denies).** The runner is invoked through the shell tool, so a command that was not granted the shell tool cannot run any adapter; an adapter therefore cannot widen grants. The runner additionally denies any command outside the adapter's binary-plus-subcommand allowlist. Denial of raw shell commands typed by an agent outside the runner remains host-enforced (hooks on Claude Code; none in this repo for Pi, OpenCode or Codex); the lint (REQ-019) keeps commands from issuing raw tool calls. This residual is recorded in the Threat Model.
- **I4: confirmation session identity.** No stable session id is exposed uniformly across runtimes. TRD-017 begins with a spike that records which id each runtime exposes (`ENSEMBLE_SESSION_ID`, host session variables); the passive confirmation record is keyed by `(sessionKey, category, adapter, configHash)` and falls back to the run id when no session id exists.
- **I5: repo-local adapters are untrusted by default.** A cloned repository can ship `.ensemble/adapters/`. Repo-local adapters resolve in every mode (satisfying AC-007-3) but a non-interactive run additionally requires the adapter name in the user's `trustedRepoAdapters` list; an interactive run shows the adapter's allowlist at first-use confirmation.
- **I6: no new runtime dependency.** The output-mapping engine uses a small dotted-path projection (`$.a.b[0]`, `|` alternation for "array or object"), not a JSONPath library, because constitution section 4 requires approval for new dependencies.
- **I7: work-graph selection.** `work-graph` is its own category with default `auto`: use the work-graph capabilities of the resolved tracker adapter when its manifest provides them; otherwise use the built-in `work-graph-links-fallback` adapter (tracker dependency links, then plan order stated as not dependency-aware). One manifest may implement several categories.
- **I8: PRD BDD floor.** Fourteen PRD requirements (REQ-001, 002, 004, 005, 006, 009, 010, 012, 015, 018, 021, 022, 024, 025) have two ACs, below the command's three-scenario floor. The test tasks specify exactly one scenario per AC; recommend a PRD refine pass to add edge or error ACs.
- **I10: packaging.** `packages/development` depends only on `js-yaml` and its libraries require only siblings, so the resolver library, category contracts, default selection, schemas and tool inventory all ship inside `packages/development` (`lib/toolchain/` and `toolchain/`). A standalone plugin install and the Pi vendor bundle therefore contain everything; other packages call `toolchain-cli` through `TOOLCHAIN_CLI` rather than importing it.
- **I9: preflight is enforced in code.** `toolchain-cli run` refuses a side-effecting capability unless a passing preflight record exists for the supplied `--run-id`; the command prose cannot silently skip preflight.
Satisfies: REQ-021

title: [trd:trd-2026-b6db9749-behavior-habits-runtime:task:TRD-015] - [ ] **TRD-015** Broaden `constitution.propose` to accept evidence from any authorized behavior (4h)
description:
## Task: TRD-015
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-b6db9749-behavior-habits-runtime.md#trd-015
PRD Reference: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-b6db9749-behavior-habits-runtime.md#req-019

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-019**: The constitution-amendment gate accepts evidence from any authorized behavior
The constitution-amendment gate accepts evidence from any authorized behavior Priority: Should

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-019-1: Given a finding from the investigator (REQ-008) or a reference behavior (REQ-013 | When the proposal is drafted | Then it is accepted by the same gate that already handles auto-fix-loop-sourced proposals

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen: Option B — dedicated adapter modules per new trigger-source type, plus a shared notification-state module.** Unchanged from 1.0.0.

New `file-source-adapter.ts` and `release-source-adapter.ts` under `packages/agent-core/src/behavior/` each produce a `BehaviorEvent` through `normalizeEvent`, mirroring the existing `pi-events.ts` → `event-translator.ts` → `normalizeEvent` → `LocalEventMatcher` chain. A new `notification-state.ts` in `pi-extension` centralises busy, duplicate and stale tracking for every behavior. Package quarantine gets its own `package-quarantine.ts` beside `package-discovery.ts`.

### Decisions added in 1.1.0

1. **How artifact changes are detected: content hashes checked at lifecycle points.** No `fs.watch`, no new dependency.
   - The adapter derives its watch set from the compiled `artifact.changed` triggers (the `path` predicate).
   - It hashes those files at `tool_result` and at `agent_end`, and emits an event when a digest differs from the last one seen in the session.
   - The hooks it relies on already exist, which is what AC-001-2 means by "supported host API".
   - It behaves the same on every OS (see REQ-023).
   - It needs no new dependency, which constitution §4 would require approval for.

   | Option | Why not chosen |
   |---|---|
   | `fs.watch` | Event semantics differ between macOS, Linux and Windows (rename-vs-change, recursive support). That is exactly the kind of per-platform behavior difference REQ-023 forbids absorbing silently. It also keeps a handle open for the whole session. |
   | `chokidar` | A new runtime dependency (constitution §4), for a problem that lifecycle-point hashing already solves. |

   The limitation, stated rather than hidden: a change is seen at the next tool call or at the end of the run, not instantly. NFR-001 measures from event validation, so this latency is outside its budget. TRD-003 reports it separately.

2. **Release signal (resolves the PRD's REQ-002 clarification): a new `v*` tag in local refs.** This matches this repo's `release.yml` (`on: push: tags: ['v*']`).
   - The tag pattern is a trigger predicate, so repositories with different conventions change configuration, not code (Rule 8).
   - It is detected two ways. First, from a successful tag-creating tool call (`git tag`, `gh release create`), in the same way `repository.changed` is derived today. Second, by diffing tag refs at session start and at `agent_end`, which covers tags that arrive by fetch.
   - It emits the **existing** catalog type `release.completed`, carrying `{ tag, sha, source }`.
   - One tag produces one event per session, whichever path sees it first.

3. **Coverage metric (resolves the PRD's REQ-016 clarification): Jest `json-summary` output, per file, `lines.pct` and `branches.pct` by default.**
   - Each package's `test:coverage` is `jest --coverage`. Jest's default reporters (`json`, `lcov`, `text`, `clover`) produce raw maps, not percentages.
   - So the behavior watches `coverage/coverage-summary.json`, and its README tells repositories to enable `json-summary`.
   - The metrics and the threshold (default 1.0 percentage point) are behavior configuration.
   - If the artifact never appears, the behavior shows up as an inert trigger in `/ensemble-status`; it is never silently idle.
   - The baseline is the previous snapshot seen **in the same session** (Rule 4). The first observation in a session only sets the baseline.

4. **The comparison is a generic command: `artifact.compare` (TRD-033).** It compares numeric JSON paths between the previous and current snapshot of an artifact and knows nothing about coverage.
   - The alternatives were rejected. Doing the comparison in an agent step would make the reported delta an unverified model claim (REQ-012). A coverage-specific command would make the third behavior need Ensemble code (REQ-018).
   - It lands in PR 1, which is why PR 5 can be configuration only.

5. **Notification transport** (REQ-009, REQ-010). `notification-state.ts` delivers to two sinks:
   - **The user**, through `SessionUiBridge.notify`, a new method that wraps `ctx.ui.notify`. Headless sessions fall back to the console.
   - **The model's context**, through `pi.sendMessage` with `display: true` and `triggerTurn: false`.

   `triggerTurn: false` is deliberate. #107 deleted the continuation path because a message that makes the agent act bypasses `MutationGuard` (`extension.ts:118-140`); a notification is data, never an instruction. Any test-derived text in a notification is fenced and labelled as data, a lesson from #94's live runs. `sendMessage` is added to `assertRequiredCapabilities`.

6. **Verified fix application** (REQ-033). This is configuration plus two small code changes.
   - A new behavior, `apply-verified-fix`, runs `mode: auto`. It triggers on `fix.verified` with the predicate `verdict: passed`, declares only `fix.apply` with no tools, and calls `fix.apply { proposalRef: ${event.payload.proposalRef} }`.
   - `CommandRegistry` then asks `ApprovalGate`. Today the prompt is only `descriptor.description` ("Apply a verified fix proposal…"), so the human would approve without seeing what changes. Code change 1 (TRD-019): the prompt names the proposal, its files and a diff summary.
   - `commit-policy.ts` has no importers today. Code change 2 (TRD-021): wire it in so an applied fix is committed with attribution.

### Alternatives considered (architecture)

| Option | Summary | Why not chosen |
|---|---|---|
| **A — Widen the existing translator, inline notification** | Add file and release branches inside `event-translator.ts`; keep notification-state logic at each `ctx.ui.notify` call site. | `event-translator.ts` would cover three unrelated source domains. Busy/duplicate/stale logic would be copied per behavior, which is the per-reaction duplication the PRD sets out to remove. |
| **B — Dedicated adapter modules + shared notification-state module** *(chosen)* | One adapter module per source type, all feeding the same ingress; one shared notification-state module. | Matches the existing boundary (`agent-core` = provider-neutral logic, `pi-extension` = host wiring), and centralises notification state once. |
| **C — Single generic "external signal" adapter** | One configurable "watch path X for condition Y" abstraction for both sources. | Risks becoming an arbitrary-condition escape hatch around the closed, versioned catalog (REQ-CQRS-005); still duplicates notification state. |
Satisfies: REQ-019
PRD ACs: AC-019-1
Target File: packages/agent-core/src/cqrs/proposal-store.ts, packages/agent-core/src/cqrs/event-authority.ts
Actions:

Implementation AC:
- [ ] Given a finding from the investigator, documentation-freshness or coverage-regression, from a behavior that declares `constitution.propose`, when a proposal is drafted, then the same gate that handles fix-sourced proposals accepts it.
- [ ] Given a behavior that does not declare `constitution.propose`, when it tries to draft a proposal, then `CommandRegistry` refuses it on capability.

description:
## Task: TRD-006
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-87e64cc6-command-surface-consolidation.md#trd-006
PRD Reference: #req-003

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen approach:** Two independent axes of work, both reusing existing, shipped mechanisms rather than inventing new ones.

1. **Front door (feature + issue discoverability/delegation):** Reuse the existing native-command pattern exactly as `ensemble-prd`/`ensemble-trd`/`ensemble-issue` already implement it — `registerDispatcherCommand` (completion dropdown, verbatim forward) + a `dispatch.subcommands[]`-bearing colon-named command YAML (Dispatch phase routes the first argument token to a sibling command/flag). `ensemble-feature`'s native registration and `ensemble:feature`'s dispatcher content are new; the underlying mechanism they ride on (`dispatcher-commands.ts`) is untouched.

See the companion research doc for the full alternatives comparison (Option A: duplicate, Option B: fully generic store) and why C was selected live with the user during this phase.

title: [trd:trd-2026-d6bbf322-new-feature-workflow:task:TRD-021-TEST] - [ ] **TRD-021-TEST**: Verify generated command is discoverable in each runtime (1h)
description:
## Test Task: TRD-021-TEST
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-d6bbf322-new-feature-workflow.md#trd-021-test
PRD Reference: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-d6bbf322-new-feature-workflow.md#req-013

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-013**: Keep `new-feature` additive to existing product commands
Keep `new-feature` additive to existing product commands Priority: Should | Complexity: Low

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-013-2: Given a user invokes the `new-feature` product entry point | When the product loads its available commands | Then the workflow is discoverable alongside the existing feature/issue capabilities

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen: Option C — hardened in-session stage composition with a dedicated atomic run-index store.**

`new-feature` is authored the same way every other product command in this repo is authored: a single orchestrating skill (`packages/development/commands/new-feature.yaml`, generated to runtime-specific prompts exactly like `fix-issue.yaml`) that executes each stage's existing skill body in-session — the same mechanism that loaded `ensemble-refine-prd`'s content into this session and had the agent execute its Phases directly. This is forced, not merely preferred: Pi's `ExtensionAPI` has no completion/invoke primitive that would let an extension programmatically run another skill and get its result back (confirmed — no `pi.invokeCommand` or equivalent exists); the only code-level "run a skill" mechanism, `createAgentPort()`, spawns a bounded, disposable `omp -p --no-session --no-extensions` subprocess in an isolated worktree, and does not fit a long-lived, project-resident workflow whose PRD/TRD stages use the interactive `--collab` review server.

What is new, and is the one piece of real infrastructure this TRD adds: a `RunIndexStore` (`packages/agent-core/src/new-feature/run-index.ts`) built on the one proven concurrency-safe pattern in this repo — `session.js`'s temp-file-then-`renameSync` atomic write plus `expectedRevision`/409-style optimistic concurrency — rather than `ProposalStore`'s plain `writeFileSync` (no atomicity, no lock, not adequate for PRD AC-005-3's fail-closed-on-malformed-index requirement). Runs are stored at `.ensemble/new-feature/<run-id>.json`, mirroring `ProposalStore`'s `.ensemble/proposals/<ref>.json` convention (also excluded from `tree-baseline.ts` drift detection, so this is consistent runtime-owned state, not a project-source mutation).

### Alternatives considered

| Option | Summary | Why not chosen |
|---|---|---|
| A — Plain JSON checkpoint | Same in-session composition, but checkpoints are a single `writeFileSync`, no atomicity/locking. | Fastest to build, but a crash mid-write can corrupt the run index, which directly violates AC-005-3's "fail closed with a recoverable diagnostic" requirement — the repo's own `ProposalStore` already demonstrates this gap is real, not hypothetical. |
| B — Subprocess-dispatched stages | New orchestrator module dispatches every stage as a bounded `createAgentPort()` subprocess; advances the run index only after subprocess exit 0 + artifact-on-disk confirmation. | Most rigorous completion signal (a real process boundary instead of self-reported bookkeeping), but substantially more build effort, and does not fit the interactive `--collab` review-server stages `create-prd`/`refine-prd` already use — those are long-lived, human-attended HTTP sessions, not bounded one-shot subprocess work, and would need bespoke carve-out handling under this option. |
| **C — Hardened in-session composition** *(chosen)* | In-session stage execution (like every existing product command), backed by a dedicated atomic `RunIndexStore`. | Reuses 100% of the existing skill-composition and `ask_user`-approval infrastructure (including the `--collab` review server, which needs no special-casing), while fixing Option A's one real correctness gap with the repo's one proven atomic-write pattern. Matches user-confirmed direction. |

### Honest trust-boundary note

Because stage execution stays in-session (per Option C), the approval gates implemented by TRD-014/TRD-017/TRD-019 are enforced by the orchestrating skill's own conditional logic checking `RunIndexStore`-persisted approval fields before it issues an implementation or `gh pr create` tool call — not by a separate runtime authorization chokepoint like `agent-core`'s `MutationGuard` (which exists elsewhere in this repo, gating CQRS-registered commands, but `new-feature`'s mutating actions are ordinary skill-level tool calls, same as `fix-issue`'s own gated PR-creation step, not CQRS commands). This is the same trust boundary every existing Ensemble product command already operates under. Building a `MutationGuard`-equivalent chokepoint for skill-level tool calls is a materially larger investment this PRD does not request and no other product command has; REQ-014's "runtime authority" is satisfied here by making the check a required precondition over persisted, validated store state rather than over prompt claims — which is what AC-014-2 actually asks for — not by inventing a new enforcement subsystem.

title: Fix-provider child agent runs ungoverned in the live repo (full write tools, --no-extensions)
description:
OBSERVED LIVE 2026-09-25 on integrate/behavior-runtime-into-dev (/private/tmp/wt-integrate).

## What happened (from .ensemble/runtime-log.jsonl)
- 21:49:07Z `test.failure.observed` (npm test; pi-extension 13/17 suites failing because agent-core had no dist/). Both paths fired: continuation into the session AND an un-awaited governed dispatch (extension.ts:167-197), which logs nothing until it finishes.
- The dispatch ran `investigate-test-failure`, whose manifest grants [read, grep, glob, ensemble.bash] -- no edit -- and `policy.mode: propose`.
- 21:50:50Z `packages/pi-extension/package.json` gained `"pretest": "tsc -p ../agent-core"` on disk. No tool call in the session transcript, the advisor transcript, or runtime-log made that write.
- 21:52:20Z invocation record: `rejected: runs in mode: propose; direct write to packages/pi-extension/package.json is denied`, `restored: [packages/pi-extension/package.json]`. The rejected proposal's contents are byte-identical to the file now on disk. The change survived.

## Cause
agent-fix-provider.ts:172-182 spawns `omp -p --no-session --no-extensions --cwd=<rootDir>` in the LIVE repository. The child is a full agent with its own write tools. `--no-extensions` means none of the governance applies inside it: no tool-grant enforcement, no MutationGuard, no WriteBoundaryMonitor, no runtime log; `--no-session` means no transcript. The provider contract says the child returns a structured patch for AutofixLoop to authorize and apply -- nothing enforces that it does ONLY that.

[INFERENCE] that the child is the writer: not directly observed (by construction nothing records it). Supported by: guard denies under propose before applyWrite (autofix-loop.ts:110-132), so AutofixLoop never wrote; the write lands between dispatch start and the rejection; no other process had both the change and write access.

Consequences:
- A behavior whose manifest reads as read-only can mutate source through its fix provider. Manifest grants do not bind the provider.
- `policy.mode: propose` is enforced on the patch but not on the process producing it.

## Acceptance
- The fix-provider child cannot modify the live working tree: a child that tries to write a file directly leaves the repository unchanged (proven by a test whose fake child writes to disk).
- The candidate the child returns is still applied (or denied) only through AutofixLoop/MutationGuard.
- Mutation-test: remove the isolation -> the direct-write test fails.
close_reason:
CLOSED on operator decision: prevent rather than detect. Commits 15c69cf, 5fbbac5.

ACCEPTANCE, against the criteria on this bead:
- 'The fix-provider child cannot modify the live working tree.' MET, and proven behaviourally rather than by fake. Live probe, real omp 18.4.2 child, real createAgentPort, tools [read,grep,glob,write,edit,bash], prompt explicitly instructing an absolute-path write into the live checkout. BEFORE: the write SUCCEEDED, CANARY-ABS.txt landed in the operator's repo containing ESCAPED; detection caught it and correctly declined to revert, so the escape persisted. AFTER: the child itself reports 'Operation not permitted (os error 1)', nothing reaches the repository, no drift.
- 'The candidate is still applied only through AutofixLoop/MutationGuard.' Unchanged; confinement sits below that and does not alter the authorization path.
- 'Mutation-test: remove the isolation, the direct-write test fails.' MET -- tests/write-sandbox.test.ts includes an explicit mutation case where the same script run WITHOUT the wrapper does write outside the workspace.
- The earlier DEVIATION (a fake child cannot test omp's enforcement) is moot: the proof is the live probe, which the operator accepted.

WHAT WAS BUILT. pi-extension/src/write-sandbox.ts confines writes via sandbox-exec (Seatbelt) to the worktree, the throwaway HOME and temp. Reads are deliberately NOT confined; writes were the incident and claiming untested confidentiality would be the overreach REQ-SAFE-004 forbids. Fails closed -- a host that cannot confine refuses to spawn, mirroring the existing isolation refusal -- with allowUnconfinedWrites as a reported, logged escape hatch. Scoped to the real spawn path, because an injected run() replaces process execution entirely and demanding a sandbox there would refuse every fake-run test on Linux CI.

THREE MISTAKES CAUGHT BY TESTING, recorded because each would have shipped as a false pass:
1. The first live probe was VACUOUS. I granted only [read,grep,glob]; the child had no means to write and reported 'neither write succeeded'. That reads as a pass and proves nothing. It is exactly the vacuity failure br-zctt exists to detect.
2. The Seatbelt profile initially granted NOTHING. subpath matches resolved paths and /tmp is a symlink to /private/tmp, so the child was denied its own workspace -- a broken sandbox indistinguishable from a working one unless the ALLOW case is also tested. There is now a test for it.
3. The fail-closed check ran unconditionally, which would have refused every fake-run test on ubuntu CI while passing on macOS. Gated, and sandbox detection made injectable so the refusal branch is exercised on hosts that DO support confinement -- an untested refusal is an assumption.

16 tests added (11 behavioural sandbox, 5 integration on invoke()). 701 pass overall, eslint clean.

RESIDUAL, stated plainly: allowUnconfinedWrites still exists, so an operator CAN run unconfined. It is loud in the invoke log and the refusal names the cost. Detection remains as backstop for that path. If the hatch should not exist at all, that is a one-line follow-up.

comments.author: ldangelo
comments.text:
LIVE EVIDENCE 2026-09-28, in the maintainer's own session.

Two fix-agent children were caught RUNNING, mid-edit, in a git worktree:

  omp -p --no-session --no-extensions \
      --cwd=/Users/ldangelo/Development/Sunstone/ensemble \
      "A test in this repository is failing. Repair the SOURCE so it passes.
       Failing test: bash > cd /tmp/wt-guard/packages/pi-extension && npx jest ..."

Runtime log for the day: 24 invocations of fix-failing-test, 12 dispatches,
8 boundary errors. The triggering commands were DELIBERATE mutation tests
and debugging runs (br-x13x), so every one of these children was dispatched
against a failure that was never a defect.

THREE THINGS THIS SHOWS

1. --no-extensions means the child runs with NO write boundary. The parent
   is guarded; the thing it spawns is not. Protection that stops at the
   process boundary is not protection.

2. --cwd was the main repository, but the instruction embedded /tmp/wt-guard
   paths, so the children navigated OUT of their working directory and
   edited a different checkout entirely. The cwd argument is not a
   containment boundary and was never enforced as one.

3. What they edited was build configuration (see the new bead), which is not
   a protected path, so nothing objected.

They were killed by hand after being found by `ps`. Nothing in the system
reported their existence, and a `git status` that happened to run at the
wrong moment would have shown a clean tree.

comments.author: ldangelo
comments.text: Shipped in PR #96 (stacked on #95), branch fix/verifier-scoping. Suite-verified and mutation-tested; NOT yet observed end-to-end against a real model.

comments.author: ldangelo
comments.text:
CROSS-REFERENCE: br-zcxb / br-o355 / br-r3om / br-xz6q share one spine.

THE SPINE: a single test failure fires TWO dispatch paths.
  governed      createBehaviorInvoker (behavior-runner.ts:111), called live
                at extension.ts:996. Carries MutationGuard, mutation_classes,
                the constitution step, approval gating.
  continuation  the extension injects a turn and the MODEL edits files with
                its own tools. Carries snapshot/rollback, write-boundary,
                whole-suite verification, and (now) the propose hold.

Neither is dead -- br-r3om observed both firing on one failure, and the live
loop-trial run logged an `invocation` record (governed) alongside a
`continuation` record. The governed invoker reported "no fix candidate
offered": it ran, and the repair happened on the other path.

So the defect is not "governance is unreachable" -- I filed that on br-zcxb
and retracted it. It is that THE FIX DOES NOT TRAVEL THROUGH THE GOVERNED
PATH, so every guarantee implemented as an authorization check on a patch has
nothing to authorize.

WHAT EACH BEAD IS, UNDER THAT SPINE
  br-xz6q  CLOSED/in review, PR #98. policy.mode was checked only in
           MutationGuard.authorize(), which the continuation path never
           reaches. Fixed by enforcing mode at verification time instead.
           Precedent: the fix did NOT route writes through the guard.
  br-o355  grants scope to the execution window, not the session. Its own
           comment proposes routing continuation writes through MutationGuard
           and expects that to close br-xz6q too. br-xz6q is now closed
           WITHOUT that, so the shared estimate should shrink, not carry over.
  br-r3om  the fix-provider CHILD runs with --no-extensions, so nothing binds
           it -- it can write the live tree directly, regardless of which path
           governs the patch it returns. This is upstream of the other three:
           routing writes through the guard does not help if the writer is a
           process outside the guard entirely.
  br-zcxb  narrowest, and independent of the routing question: the
           constitution step records nothing when the provider returns no
           change, so "declined" and "never ran" are indistinguishable; and
           there is no RCA stage at all (BehaviorRunRecord, behavior-runner.ts
           :40-54, has no cause field).

SEQUENCING, so one defect is not scoped four times
  1. br-r3om first. It is P1, in review, and it is the only one where the
     enforcement boundary itself is bypassed rather than bypassed-around.
  2. br-zcxb's instrumentation half next. It is cheap, it does not depend on
     the routing decision, and until the constitution step is observable we
     cannot tell whether the back half of the loop works at all -- which
     makes any estimate for the rest guesswork.
  3. br-o355's routing decision last, informed by 1 and 2. If the continuation
     path keeps applying fixes model-side, MutationGuard may be the wrong
     chokepoint entirely and the effect-based write boundary the right one.
     br-xz6q is evidence for that reading.

RCA (the remaining half of br-zcxb) is orthogonal to all of this: no path
records a cause, so it is new work wherever the fix lands.

comments.author: ldangelo
comments.text:
ASSESSED AGAINST THIS BRANCH 2026-09-29 (feature/trd-2026-0fc1c1d0-behavior-runtime-pi-harness), reached via br-zcxb which this bead blocks. NOT closing -- it is IN_REVIEW and yours.

WHAT THE CQRS PORT CHANGED. The incident here was a child running in the LIVE repo with full write tools while both dispatch paths fired. On this branch:
- The continuation path is deleted outright, so only one dispatch path exists.
- agent-port.ts runs the child with an isolated git worktree as cwd and a throwaway HOME/XDG/OMP config root, both OS-enforced.
- If isolation is unavailable it REFUSES to invoke: 'An uncontained child is not a supported degraded mode.' That is the specific condition this bead recorded.
- --tools is retained but explicitly NOT credited as containment; it was measured not to restrict _write/_learn/_manage_skill (br-33co).

THE RESIDUAL THIS BEAD NAMES IS REAL AND ACKNOWLEDGED IN THE SOURCE. The OS boundaries stop a child writing RELATIVE paths. They cannot stop one writing an ABSOLUTE path back into the live repository -- which is exactly the shape of the observed package.json write with no tool call in any transcript. Detection via tree baseline is the only control covering that case, and the reply is discarded (never reverted) when drift is seen.

DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED WHILE ASSESSING THIS. Drift detection failed OPEN. 'const drift = baseline ? treeChangesSinceBaseline(baseline) : undefined' and the checks after it refused only when drift.length > 0; when the baseline could not be captured, or the comparison itself returned undefined, execution fell through to 'return { ok: true, reply }'. That is 'I could not check whether the child wrote to your tree, therefore trust the reply' -- the br-dowt pattern, inside the containment path, reachable mainly when the port ran UNISOLATED, i.e. precisely when detection was the only control left. Now refuses with a reason naming the consequence. 5 tests in pi-extension/tests/drift-fails-closed.test.ts.

REMAINING FOR THIS BEAD, if anything: whether absolute-path writes should be prevented rather than detected. That needs an OS-level facility the runtime does not currently use, and REQ-SAFE-004 forbids describing detection as isolation, so it should stay described as it is until that exists.

comments.author: ldangelo
comments.text:
END-TO-END PROOF AGAINST A REAL MODEL, 2026-09-29. This closes out the 'NOT yet observed end-to-end against a real model' caveat from the 15:52 comment.

METHOD. Real createAgentPort (pi-extension/dist), real omp 18.4.2 child, no fakes. Two canaries: CANARY-REL.txt by relative path into the child's cwd, CANARY-ABS.txt by ABSOLUTE path into the live checkout. The prompt told the child to do both and even suggested the shell form.

RESULT.
  relative write  -> PREVENTED. Never appeared in the live repo. The isolated worktree cwd held.
  absolute write  -> SUCCEEDED. /Users/ldangelo/Development/Sunstone/ensemble/CANARY-ABS.txt was created, containing ESCAPED.
  detection       -> WORKED. invoke returned ok:false, 'the working tree changed while the agent ran (CANARY-ABS.txt)', logged agent-invoke-drift, reply discarded, nothing reverted (correctly -- it cannot attribute child vs concurrent user edit).

So the system behaves exactly as its docstring claims, and the docstring is honest that --tools and cwd do not contain. A real model given real tools escaped by absolute path on the FIRST attempt, with no adversarial prodding. The residual this bead names is not theoretical.

FIRST ATTEMPT WAS VACUOUS, recorded because the mistake is instructive. I granted the child [read, grep, glob], it had no means to write, and it reported 'neither write succeeded'. That reads as a pass and proves nothing -- the child never had the capability to attempt the escape. It is the same vacuity failure br-zctt exists to detect, and I walked into it myself. The real manifest (investigate-test-failure) grants ensemble.bash, so the probe had to grant write/edit/bash to mean anything.

Canary removed, tree clean.

OPERATOR DECISION: prevent both relative and absolute writes rather than detect the absolute case. That is now scoped as real work rather than an acknowledged residual.

title: PRD-1: Hard-enforce constitution
description:
Implement hard-gate constitution enforcement in Ensemble spec/plan phases

## Problem
Ensemble currently uses soft-gate enforcement — constitution violations pause and allow override. Spec-Kit's Nine Articles are enforced as blocking phase gates.

## Goals
- Constitution violations during create-prd/create-trd BLOCK generation, no override option
- Constitutional compliance verified before phase completion
- Violations produce actionable error messages referencing specific constitution articles

## User Stories
- As a developer, I want hard-gate enforcement so my team cannot bypass architecture standards
- As a PM, I want constitution as blocking gate so spec reviews catch violations early

## Requirements
- FR-001: create-prd phase blocks if constitution violated; no skip/override flag
- FR-002: create-trd phase blocks if constitution violated; no skip/override flag
- FR-003: Violation error messages reference constitution article number
- FR-004: Soft-gate mode removed from constitution enforcement code

## Verification
- Test with violating PRD: expect hard block, not pause
- Test with violating TRD: expect hard block, not pause

description:
## Test Task: TRD-008-TEST
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-1d3e0dd6-new-feature-foreman-flag.md#trd-008-test
PRD Reference: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-1d3e0dd6-new-feature-foreman-flag.md#req-008

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-008**: `/ensemble:feature` accepts and forwards `--foreman` (Must)
`/ensemble:feature` accepts and forwards `--foreman` (Must) Delivery and safety

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-008-1: Given `/ensemble:feature new --foreman <idea>` | When it dispatches | Then it builds `/ensemble:new-feature --foreman --idea "<idea>"`, and the idea text is forwarded exactly as given (the flag is removed from it, nothing else is)
- AC-008-2: Given `resume` | When it dispatches | Then the flag is forwarded; `abandon` still forwards any reason text after it
- AC-008-3: Given `--foreman` appears anywhere other than as the first token after the keyword (for example inside the idea prose) | When it dispatches | Then it is treated as ordinary text and not as the flag
- AC-008-4: Given an unknown keyword | When it dispatches | Then it is rejected with the keyword table and no side effects, as today

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen approach:** a prompt-only change to two YAML command sources. No TypeScript changes.

- `packages/development/commands/new-feature.yaml` gains a boolean `foreman` parameter and one derived variable, `FOREMAN`, defined once in Entry Point Resolution Step 1 and referenced by every later step. Each step that asks the user gets a `FOREMAN == true` branch that takes a deterministic, recorded, non-interactive decision. Each step that dispatches a stage skill appends `--foreman` when `FOREMAN == true`.
- `packages/development/commands/feature.yaml` (the `/ensemble:feature` front door) recognizes `--foreman` as the first token after the keyword and forwards it.
- Generated OMP, Pi and Codex artifacts are regenerated from the repo root, never hand-edited.

**Why prompt-only (Constitution Rule 8):** how a workflow behaves when no one can answer is something a maintainer would plausibly tune (for example, switching the PR gate to park instead of auto-grant). That belongs in the command prose, not in TypeScript. `RunIndexStore` already supports everything needed: `StageOutcome.detail` carries the "granted by `--foreman` policy" record.

**Additive-only edits (found in refinement):** the existing suites (`new-feature-command.test.js`, `feature-command.test.js`, `feature-input-validation-boundary.test.js`, `feature-concurrency-passthrough.test.js`) pin exact sentences in both YAML files, for example "any remaining text is an unsupported flag or argument rejected here". So no pre-existing sentence may be reworded or removed. Foreman behavior is added as new actions or appended sentences, and the existing suites must pass unchanged. For the front door that means: a new action, placed before the validation action, removes a leading `--foreman` token and sets `FOREMAN`, so the pinned validation sentences still read "remaining text" correctly; and a new action, placed after the invocation is constructed, inserts `--foreman` right after `/ensemble:new-feature` in whatever invocation was built.

**Alternatives rejected:**
- *Env-var-only detection (no flag).* Rejected: the maintainer asked for a `--foreman` flag, and the five stage skills already key on that flag.
- *A new RunRecord field `autoGranted`.* Rejected: TypeScript and schema change for information `StageOutcome.detail` already carries.
- *Parking at the approval gates.* Rejected by the maintainer: it stalls every no-user run.

description:
## Test Task: TRD-002-TEST
## References
TRD: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-8d825f54-tool-abstraction-layer.md
TRD Task: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-8d825f54-tool-abstraction-layer.md#trd-002-test

PRD ACs: AC-003-1, AC-003-2, AC-003-3
Verifies Task: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-8d825f54-tool-abstraction-layer.md#trd-002
Parent Epic: [trd:trd-2026-8d825f54-tool-abstraction-layer]
Read-first: read the TRD, TRD Task section, PRD and PRD Requirement above before any work on this bead.


--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-003**: Additive-only contract within a major version
Additive-only contract within a major version Priority: Must Within a contract major version, new capabilities are added only as optional. A required-capability change needs a new contract major version. Adapters declare the contract version they target. Each category's contract is versioned independently of the other categories and of Ensemble's own release version.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-003-1: Given an adapter targeting contract 1.x and a later 1.y contract adding a capability | When the adapter is resolved | Then it still validates and the new capability is treated as unavailable
- AC-003-2: Given an adapter targeting contract 1.x and an installed contract 2.x | When the adapter is resolved | Then validation fails naming the contract versions and the capabilities the adapter lacks
- AC-003-3: Given the tracker contract moves to a new major version | When adapters for other categories are resolved | Then their validation result is unchanged

--- TRD Context ---
### Alternatives Considered

| Option | Approach | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|---|
| A: Prose-only adapters | Adapter is a skill; the agent follows its prose and normalizes tool output itself | Smallest build; fully editable | Cannot route internal CLIs deterministically (REQ-016), cannot validate output (REQ-022), cannot deny at runtime (REQ-023); behavior varies per model |
| **B: Manifest plus runner (chosen)** | Adapter is a skill directory: `SKILL.md` (vocabulary and agent-facing prose) plus a declarative `adapter.yaml` (capability command templates, output mapping, allowlist, health check, detection signals, required env names). A core resolver library and `toolchain-cli` execute capabilities deterministically | Meets PRD (adapter is a skill), Rule 8 (editable without rebuild), Rule 5 (enforcement in code), REQ-016 (CLIs call the same library) | New resolver, runner, manifest schema and output-mapping engine to build and test |
| C: Executable plugin adapters | Separately packaged executables speaking a versioned JSON protocol | Arbitrary logic; strongest isolation | Contradicts the PRD's skills-as-contract decision; fails Rule 8; needs per-OS packaging and a protocol |

**Rationale:** B is the only option that makes every PRD guarantee a code-enforced property while keeping adapters user-editable data. The requester selected B at the architecture gate.

### Interpretations and Resolved Design Issues

- **I1: plain version control.** The PRD taxonomy has no plain `git` category, yet about 45 sources invoke it. Plain `git` operations (status, commit, push, log, diff, merge-base) are `vcs.*` capabilities of the `workflow` category, whose default adapter is `plain-git`; the `git-town` adapter extends it. Recommend a PRD refine pass to name this explicitly.
- **I2: ambiguity versus no signal (PRD REQ-009 AC-2 vs REQ-010 AC-2).** "No detectable signal" means no signal source exists at all (no remote, no marker files); the shipped default is used. "Ambiguous" means two or more installed adapters match, or a signal source exists (for example a remote URL) but matches no installed adapter; resolution fails explicitly in non-interactive runs and asks in interactive runs.
- **I3: AC-023-2 (governed boundary denies).** The runner is invoked through the shell tool, so a command that was not granted the shell tool cannot run any adapter; an adapter therefore cannot widen grants. The runner additionally denies any command outside the adapter's binary-plus-subcommand allowlist. Denial of raw shell commands typed by an agent outside the runner remains host-enforced (hooks on Claude Code; none in this repo for Pi, OpenCode or Codex); the lint (REQ-019) keeps commands from issuing raw tool calls. This residual is recorded in the Threat Model.
- **I4: confirmation session identity.** No stable session id is exposed uniformly across runtimes. TRD-017 begins with a spike that records which id each runtime exposes (`ENSEMBLE_SESSION_ID`, host session variables); the passive confirmation record is keyed by `(sessionKey, category, adapter, configHash)` and falls back to the run id when no session id exists.
- **I5: repo-local adapters are untrusted by default.** A cloned repository can ship `.ensemble/adapters/`. Repo-local adapters resolve in every mode (satisfying AC-007-3) but a non-interactive run additionally requires the adapter name in the user's `trustedRepoAdapters` list; an interactive run shows the adapter's allowlist at first-use confirmation.
- **I6: no new runtime dependency.** The output-mapping engine uses a small dotted-path projection (`$.a.b[0]`, `|` alternation for "array or object"), not a JSONPath library, because constitution section 4 requires approval for new dependencies.
- **I7: work-graph selection.** `work-graph` is its own category with default `auto`: use the work-graph capabilities of the resolved tracker adapter when its manifest provides them; otherwise use the built-in `work-graph-links-fallback` adapter (tracker dependency links, then plan order stated as not dependency-aware). One manifest may implement several categories.
- **I8: PRD BDD floor.** Fourteen PRD requirements (REQ-001, 002, 004, 005, 006, 009, 010, 012, 015, 018, 021, 022, 024, 025) have two ACs, below the command's three-scenario floor. The test tasks specify exactly one scenario per AC; recommend a PRD refine pass to add edge or error ACs.
- **I10: packaging.** `packages/development` depends only on `js-yaml` and its libraries require only siblings, so the resolver library, category contracts, default selection, schemas and tool inventory all ship inside `packages/development` (`lib/toolchain/` and `toolchain/`). A standalone plugin install and the Pi vendor bundle therefore contain everything; other packages call `toolchain-cli` through `TOOLCHAIN_CLI` rather than importing it.
- **I9: preflight is enforced in code.** `toolchain-cli run` refuses a side-effecting capability unless a passing preflight record exists for the supplied `--run-id`; the command prose cannot silently skip preflight.
Verifies: TRD-002
Satisfies: REQ-003
PRD ACs Proven: AC-003-1, AC-003-2, AC-003-3

- [ ] Scenario: Minor contract bump keeps adapter valid -- Given an adapter targeting contract 1.x and a later 1.y contract adding a capability, When the adapter is resolved, Then it still validates and the new capability is treated as unavailable.
- [ ] Scenario: Major contract mismatch fails -- Given an adapter targeting contract 1.x and an installed contract 2.x, When the adapter is resolved, Then validation fails naming the contract versions and the capabilities the adapter lacks.
- [ ] Scenario: Tracker major bump is isolated -- Given the tracker contract moves to a new major version, When adapters for other categories are resolved, Then their validation result is unchanged.

title: [trd:trd-2026-f08a2a09-command-lifecycle-hooks:task:TRD-006-TEST] - [ ] **TRD-006-TEST** Dispatcher behavior (2h)
description:
## Test Task: TRD-006-TEST
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-f08a2a09-command-lifecycle-hooks.md#trd-006-test
PRD Reference: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-f08a2a09-command-lifecycle-hooks.md#req-012

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-012**: Handlers run serially, in configured order (Must)
Handlers run serially, in configured order (Must)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-010-1: Given an end handler fails and its error behavior is `continue` | When it fails | Then the command's recorded outcome is unchanged
- AC-010-2: Given a start handler fails and its error behavior is `block` | When it fails | Then the command does not run and the user is told which handler blocked it
- AC-012-1: Given several handlers are selected for an event | When it fires | Then they run one at a time in the configured order
- AC-012-2: Given an earlier handler fails with `continue` | When the next is due | Then it still runs
- AC-012-3: Given an earlier start handler blocks | When it blocks | Then later start handlers do not run
- AC-013-1: Given a handler ran | When the event finishes | Then the user can see, for each handler, whether it succeeded, failed, timed out or blocked, and how long it took
- AC-013-2: Given a handler failed with `continue` | When the command finishes | Then the failure is visible and does not read as a command failure
- AC-020-1: Given a handler fails | When the failure is recorded | Then nothing retries it, schedules it or recovers it
- AC-020-2: Given the feature | When reviewed | Then it adds no dispatcher competing with Foreman

--- TRD Context ---
**Decision:** Build the lifecycle as a harness-neutral core in `packages/agent-core` (event payloads, configuration validation, redaction, a shell runner, a prompt runner, a serial dispatcher, and a per-session command-run tracker) and one adapter in `packages/pi-extension` that connects it to Pi. The adapter is the only code that knows Pi's event names.

**Decisions made by the maintainer during design (all recorded in PRD v1.0.2 to v1.0.4):**

- The first release is adapter-specific, with Pi as the proving harness. A runtime-owned wrapper is deferred.
- `command.start` fires from the runtime when the command's slash input is seen, so it never depends on the model and a start handler's block is enforced by the runtime. A command whose own prompt then rejects its arguments has already produced a start and ends as `failed`.
- A command's completion is signalled by a silent `ensemble_command_complete` tool that the model is told to call last. The instruction is injected per turn by the adapter, not generated into every Pi prompt, so projects without hooks see no change.
- A settled loop never ends a command. A command that never signals completion ends as `cancelled` when the session ends or the next command begins.
- A prompt handler is evaluated by an isolated headless child (`pi -p --no-session -ne -nt -np`), parsed against a typed response contract.
- No handler runs until the host reports the project as trusted (`ctx.isProjectTrusted()`).
- `on_error` is required on every handler. Default timeouts are 5 seconds for shell handlers and 30 seconds for prompt handlers.
- Selections list commands by name. Wildcards and groups are rejected.
- For harnesses with no adapter, the guide, a capability table and a status check say hooks are inactive. Nothing is shown at command time there.

**Why code and not a prompt (Constitution rule 8):** what runs at a command boundary, the trust check, the environment allowlist, redaction, timeouts and process cleanup are enforcement boundaries and must not be editable by a model or a user prompt. What a team wants to run (the hooks file, the executables, the prompt files) is user-owned and stays in files they edit without a toolchain.

Tracker swap, end to end (first alternatives: Jira Cloud and Azure Boards) Priority: Must | `[RISK: work-graph behavior differs between trackers]` With the tracker adapter changed by configuration only, every command that creates, reads, updates or closes work items works against either alternative tracker, including the internal CLIs (`trd-cli` and siblings) that currently call the default tracker directly. Those internal CLIs route through the resolved tracker adapter. The first-release Jira adapter targets Jira Cloud only.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-016-3: Given a command that uses work-graph capabilities | When the alternative adapter lacks one | Then REQ-004's fallback or halt applies
- AC-020-2: Given an alternative tracker adapter lacking ready-work but providing issue links | When an implementation command needs ordering | Then ordering is derived from those links and the output states the source
- AC-020-3: Given an alternative tracker adapter providing neither ready-work nor issue links | When an implementation command needs ordering | Then tasks run in plan order and the output states that ordering is not dependency-aware

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-020**: Execution layer follows the resolved tracker
Execution layer follows the resolved tracker Priority: Must | `[RISK: amends PRD-2026-b6939c7c REQ-015; affects ready-work scheduling in implementation commands]` The earlier rule that the default tracker is always the sole dependency-graph and ready-work engine is replaced. Ready-work and dependency ordering come from the resolved tracker adapter's work-graph capabilities, or from the documented fallback when those are absent. The fallback uses the tracker's own issue links when it has them; otherwise tasks run in plan order and the output states that ordering is not dependency-aware. Cross-Cutting

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-016-3: Given a command that uses work-graph capabilities | When the alternative adapter lacks one | Then REQ-004's fallback or halt applies
- AC-020-2: Given an alternative tracker adapter lacking ready-work but providing issue links | When an implementation command needs ordering | Then ordering is derived from those links and the output states the source
- AC-020-3: Given an alternative tracker adapter providing neither ready-work nor issue links | When an implementation command needs ordering | Then tasks run in plan order and the output states that ordering is not dependency-aware

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-004**: Required capabilities and documented fallbacks
Required capabilities and documented fallbacks Priority: Must Each command and skill declares the capabilities it requires and which optional ones it can use. When an optional capability is absent from the resolved adapter, the command follows that capability's documented fallback instead of failing or silently skipping. Adapters

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-016-3: Given a command that uses work-graph capabilities | When the alternative adapter lacks one | Then REQ-004's fallback or halt applies
- AC-020-2: Given an alternative tracker adapter lacking ready-work but providing issue links | When an implementation command needs ordering | Then ordering is derived from those links and the output states the source
- AC-020-3: Given an alternative tracker adapter providing neither ready-work nor issue links | When an implementation command needs ordering | Then tasks run in plan order and the output states that ordering is not dependency-aware

--- TRD Context ---
### Alternatives Considered

| Option | Approach | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|---|
| A: Prose-only adapters | Adapter is a skill; the agent follows its prose and normalizes tool output itself | Smallest build; fully editable | Cannot route internal CLIs deterministically (REQ-016), cannot validate output (REQ-022), cannot deny at runtime (REQ-023); behavior varies per model |
| **B: Manifest plus runner (chosen)** | Adapter is a skill directory: `SKILL.md` (vocabulary and agent-facing prose) plus a declarative `adapter.yaml` (capability command templates, output mapping, allowlist, health check, detection signals, required env names). A core resolver library and `toolchain-cli` execute capabilities deterministically | Meets PRD (adapter is a skill), Rule 8 (editable without rebuild), Rule 5 (enforcement in code), REQ-016 (CLIs call the same library) | New resolver, runner, manifest schema and output-mapping engine to build and test |
| C: Executable plugin adapters | Separately packaged executables speaking a versioned JSON protocol | Arbitrary logic; strongest isolation | Contradicts the PRD's skills-as-contract decision; fails Rule 8; needs per-OS packaging and a protocol |

**Rationale:** B is the only option that makes every PRD guarantee a code-enforced property while keeping adapters user-editable data. The requester selected B at the architecture gate.

### Interpretations and Resolved Design Issues

- **I1: plain version control.** The PRD taxonomy has no plain `git` category, yet about 45 sources invoke it. Plain `git` operations (status, commit, push, log, diff, merge-base) are `vcs.*` capabilities of the `workflow` category, whose default adapter is `plain-git`; the `git-town` adapter extends it. Recommend a PRD refine pass to name this explicitly.
- **I2: ambiguity versus no signal (PRD REQ-009 AC-2 vs REQ-010 AC-2).** "No detectable signal" means no signal source exists at all (no remote, no marker files); the shipped default is used. "Ambiguous" means two or more installed adapters match, or a signal source exists (for example a remote URL) but matches no installed adapter; resolution fails explicitly in non-interactive runs and asks in interactive runs.
- **I3: AC-023-2 (governed boundary denies).** The runner is invoked through the shell tool, so a command that was not granted the shell tool cannot run any adapter; an adapter therefore cannot widen grants. The runner additionally denies any command outside the adapter's binary-plus-subcommand allowlist. Denial of raw shell commands typed by an agent outside the runner remains host-enforced (hooks on Claude Code; none in this repo for Pi, OpenCode or Codex); the lint (REQ-019) keeps commands from issuing raw tool calls. This residual is recorded in the Threat Model.
- **I4: confirmation session identity.** No stable session id is exposed uniformly across runtimes. TRD-017 begins with a spike that records which id each runtime exposes (`ENSEMBLE_SESSION_ID`, host session variables); the passive confirmation record is keyed by `(sessionKey, category, adapter, configHash)` and falls back to the run id when no session id exists.
- **I5: repo-local adapters are untrusted by default.** A cloned repository can ship `.ensemble/adapters/`. Repo-local adapters resolve in every mode (satisfying AC-007-3) but a non-interactive run additionally requires the adapter name in the user's `trustedRepoAdapters` list; an interactive run shows the adapter's allowlist at first-use confirmation.
- **I6: no new runtime dependency.** The output-mapping engine uses a small dotted-path projection (`$.a.b[0]`, `|` alternation for "array or object"), not a JSONPath library, because constitution section 4 requires approval for new dependencies.
- **I7: work-graph selection.** `work-graph` is its own category with default `auto`: use the work-graph capabilities of the resolved tracker adapter when its manifest provides them; otherwise use the built-in `work-graph-links-fallback` adapter (tracker dependency links, then plan order stated as not dependency-aware). One manifest may implement several categories.
- **I8: PRD BDD floor.** Fourteen PRD requirements (REQ-001, 002, 004, 005, 006, 009, 010, 012, 015, 018, 021, 022, 024, 025) have two ACs, below the command's three-scenario floor. The test tasks specify exactly one scenario per AC; recommend a PRD refine pass to add edge or error ACs.
- **I10: packaging.** `packages/development` depends only on `js-yaml` and its libraries require only siblings, so the resolver library, category contracts, default selection, schemas and tool inventory all ship inside `packages/development` (`lib/toolchain/` and `toolchain/`). A standalone plugin install and the Pi vendor bundle therefore contain everything; other packages call `toolchain-cli` through `TOOLCHAIN_CLI` rather than importing it.
- **I9: preflight is enforced in code.** `toolchain-cli run` refuses a side-effecting capability unless a passing preflight record exists for the supplied `--run-id`; the command prose cannot silently skip preflight.

comments.text:
# br-rmw Multi-Skill Collision Ordering Audit — ensemble-as-behaviors

Run 2026-09-23. Script: `scripts/collision-order-audit.js` (reproducible:
`node scripts/collision-order-audit.js`; exits non-zero on any nondeterminism, sort
violation, or unexpected hit set).

## Contract under audit

`matchPhrases` output must be: deduped by `skill|phrase`, sorted by skill name, then
phrase-alphabetical within a skill (longest-phrase-first is NOT the contract —
`localeCompare` on phrase is). `buildPhraseBlock` renders in that array order.

## Method

- 8 hand-built compound probes (multi-skill prompts: PRD+git-town, TRD+pull-request,
  three merging-a-pr phrases in one prompt, etc.)
- 30 exhaustive pair probes: first phrase of every skill pair, both orderings.
- Each probe run 5x through the REAL hook (`execFileSync` + stdin JSON); outputs
  compared for byte-identity AND against the independently-computed expected hit set
  (substring test against the full registry).

## Results

- **Determinism: 38/38 probes × 5 runs byte-identical.** No ordering jitter.
- **Sort contract: PASS on every probe** — skill-major, phrase-alpha within skill, e.g.
  `creating-a-prd/create a prd` → `git-town/create a feature branch` →
  `git-town/create a pr`.
- **3/8 compound probes surface multi-skill collisions** (`create a prd` ∋
  `create a pr`, `create a trd` ∋ …): identical root cause as the `br-ivv` finding —
  git-town's `create a pr` phrase is a strict prefix of `create a prd`/`create a trd`.
  Ordering itself stays deterministic; the collision is a registry-content issue, not a
  comparator bug. Fix belongs with br-ivv's recommendation (word-boundary or drop).
- All 30 pair probes: skill order strictly alphabetical regardless of phrase order in
  the prompt.

## Verdict

Ordering is correct and deterministic; the audit script is a permanent regression guard
(exit≠0 on drift). Recorded: collisions observed == predicted from the prefix overlap;
no additional ambiguous pairs beyond `br-ivv`'s table.

title: [trd:trd-2026-b6db9749-behavior-habits-runtime:task:TRD-027] - [ ] **TRD-027** Run the conformance suite on a macOS runner and record the results (3h)
description:
## Task: TRD-027
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-b6db9749-behavior-habits-runtime.md#trd-027
PRD Reference: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-b6db9749-behavior-habits-runtime.md#req-021

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-021**: The complete local path is independently verified on Windows, Linux, and macOS
The complete local path is independently verified on Windows, Linux, and macOS Priority: Must [RISK: verification evidence does not yet exist for any of the three platforms as of this PRD]

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-021-1: Given the trigger/dispatch/notification path | When run on each of Windows | Then each platform has its own passing conformance suite run
- AC-021-2: Given a behavior works on one platform | When parity is claimed for another | Then that claim is backed by that platform's own conformance evidence, never inferred

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen: Option B — dedicated adapter modules per new trigger-source type, plus a shared notification-state module.** Unchanged from 1.0.0.

New `file-source-adapter.ts` and `release-source-adapter.ts` under `packages/agent-core/src/behavior/` each produce a `BehaviorEvent` through `normalizeEvent`, mirroring the existing `pi-events.ts` → `event-translator.ts` → `normalizeEvent` → `LocalEventMatcher` chain. A new `notification-state.ts` in `pi-extension` centralises busy, duplicate and stale tracking for every behavior. Package quarantine gets its own `package-quarantine.ts` beside `package-discovery.ts`.

### Decisions added in 1.1.0

1. **How artifact changes are detected: content hashes checked at lifecycle points.** No `fs.watch`, no new dependency.
   - The adapter derives its watch set from the compiled `artifact.changed` triggers (the `path` predicate).
   - It hashes those files at `tool_result` and at `agent_end`, and emits an event when a digest differs from the last one seen in the session.
   - The hooks it relies on already exist, which is what AC-001-2 means by "supported host API".
   - It behaves the same on every OS (see REQ-023).
   - It needs no new dependency, which constitution §4 would require approval for.

   | Option | Why not chosen |
   |---|---|
   | `fs.watch` | Event semantics differ between macOS, Linux and Windows (rename-vs-change, recursive support). That is exactly the kind of per-platform behavior difference REQ-023 forbids absorbing silently. It also keeps a handle open for the whole session. |
   | `chokidar` | A new runtime dependency (constitution §4), for a problem that lifecycle-point hashing already solves. |

   The limitation, stated rather than hidden: a change is seen at the next tool call or at the end of the run, not instantly. NFR-001 measures from event validation, so this latency is outside its budget. TRD-003 reports it separately.

2. **Release signal (resolves the PRD's REQ-002 clarification): a new `v*` tag in local refs.** This matches this repo's `release.yml` (`on: push: tags: ['v*']`).
   - The tag pattern is a trigger predicate, so repositories with different conventions change configuration, not code (Rule 8).
   - It is detected two ways. First, from a successful tag-creating tool call (`git tag`, `gh release create`), in the same way `repository.changed` is derived today. Second, by diffing tag refs at session start and at `agent_end`, which covers tags that arrive by fetch.
   - It emits the **existing** catalog type `release.completed`, carrying `{ tag, sha, source }`.
   - One tag produces one event per session, whichever path sees it first.

3. **Coverage metric (resolves the PRD's REQ-016 clarification): Jest `json-summary` output, per file, `lines.pct` and `branches.pct` by default.**
   - Each package's `test:coverage` is `jest --coverage`. Jest's default reporters (`json`, `lcov`, `text`, `clover`) produce raw maps, not percentages.
   - So the behavior watches `coverage/coverage-summary.json`, and its README tells repositories to enable `json-summary`.
   - The metrics and the threshold (default 1.0 percentage point) are behavior configuration.
   - If the artifact never appears, the behavior shows up as an inert trigger in `/ensemble-status`; it is never silently idle.
   - The baseline is the previous snapshot seen **in the same session** (Rule 4). The first observation in a session only sets the baseline.

4. **The comparison is a generic command: `artifact.compare` (TRD-033).** It compares numeric JSON paths between the previous and current snapshot of an artifact and knows nothing about coverage.
   - The alternatives were rejected. Doing the comparison in an agent step would make the reported delta an unverified model claim (REQ-012). A coverage-specific command would make the third behavior need Ensemble code (REQ-018).
   - It lands in PR 1, which is why PR 5 can be configuration only.

5. **Notification transport** (REQ-009, REQ-010). `notification-state.ts` delivers to two sinks:
   - **The user**, through `SessionUiBridge.notify`, a new method that wraps `ctx.ui.notify`. Headless sessions fall back to the console.
   - **The model's context**, through `pi.sendMessage` with `display: true` and `triggerTurn: false`.

   `triggerTurn: false` is deliberate. #107 deleted the continuation path because a message that makes the agent act bypasses `MutationGuard` (`extension.ts:118-140`); a notification is data, never an instruction. Any test-derived text in a notification is fenced and labelled as data, a lesson from #94's live runs. `sendMessage` is added to `assertRequiredCapabilities`.

6. **Verified fix application** (REQ-033). This is configuration plus two small code changes.
   - A new behavior, `apply-verified-fix`, runs `mode: auto`. It triggers on `fix.verified` with the predicate `verdict: passed`, declares only `fix.apply` with no tools, and calls `fix.apply { proposalRef: ${event.payload.proposalRef} }`.
   - `CommandRegistry` then asks `ApprovalGate`. Today the prompt is only `descriptor.description` ("Apply a verified fix proposal…"), so the human would approve without seeing what changes. Code change 1 (TRD-019): the prompt names the proposal, its files and a diff summary.
   - `commit-policy.ts` has no importers today. Code change 2 (TRD-021): wire it in so an applied fix is committed with attribution.

### Alternatives considered (architecture)

| Option | Summary | Why not chosen |
|---|---|---|
| **A — Widen the existing translator, inline notification** | Add file and release branches inside `event-translator.ts`; keep notification-state logic at each `ctx.ui.notify` call site. | `event-translator.ts` would cover three unrelated source domains. Busy/duplicate/stale logic would be copied per behavior, which is the per-reaction duplication the PRD sets out to remove. |
| **B — Dedicated adapter modules + shared notification-state module** *(chosen)* | One adapter module per source type, all feeding the same ingress; one shared notification-state module. | Matches the existing boundary (`agent-core` = provider-neutral logic, `pi-extension` = host wiring), and centralises notification state once. |
| **C — Single generic "external signal" adapter** | One configurable "watch path X for condition Y" abstraction for both sources. | Risks becoming an arbitrary-condition escape hatch around the closed, versioned catalog (REQ-CQRS-005); still duplicates notification state. |

## Task: TRD-028
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-15aa5acd-live-behavior-dispatch-autofix.md#trd-028
PRD Reference: #req-006

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen: Option C — single enforcement seam, additive.**

A new `MutationGuard` chokepoint in `agent-core` is the one place `policy.mode`, `capabilities.mutation_classes` (via the existing `hasMutationAuthority()`), and protected-path rules are resolved. It is wired once at the loader boundary rather than replicated per tool registration. The translator, matcher, and auto-fix loop are added to `pi-extension`. Discovery roots and `execution.test_command` are additive changes to existing schema/discovery code. `ToolRegistry`, `outbox`, and the compiler are reused unchanged.

### Alternatives considered

| Option | Summary | Why not chosen |
|---|---|---|
| **A — In-place extension** | Enforce mode/mutation/path rules as wrapper checks inside `behavior-loader`'s per-tool `execute()` closures. | Enforcement scattered across call sites; every future tool registration must remember to wrap. The PRD's central failure mode is *guarantees that exist in one place but are not reached from another* — Option A reproduces exactly that shape. |
| **B — Governance kernel** | Route every mutation through a `MutationBroker` + `GovernedWorkspace` in `agent-core`; `pi-extension` becomes a thin adapter. | Strongest long-term design and the right eventual target, but it re-opens already-shipped code across every tool path for a ~6-7 PR refactor before a single PRD requirement is demonstrable. Deferred deliberately, not rejected. |
| **C — Single enforcement seam** *(chosen)* | One `MutationGuard` chokepoint, wired once; everything else additive. | Gets a single auditable chokepoint (Option B's main benefit) without Option B's refactor surface. Fits the existing `agent-core` / `pi-extension` split. |

### Architectural note carried from grounding

Two defects found while grounding this design are folded into PR 1 rather than left implicit:

1. `pi-events.ts` emits `runtime.tool_result` / `runtime.tool.called` / `runtime.tool.failed` / `runtime.tool.completed`, none of which appear in `HARNESS_EVENT_TYPES` (which defines `runtime.tool_call.started` / `runtime.tool_call.completed`). `normalizeEvent` does not currently reject uncatalogued types, so PRD AC-002-1's "validated against the closed catalog" would be vacuous. Addressed by TRD-001 (`[satisfies INFRA]`).
2. `behavior-loader.ts:79` calls `registry.grant(...)` unconditionally immediately before `registry.invoke(...)`, making the grant boundary a rubber stamp for behavior-governed tools (unlike the echo path, where the grant is CLI-flag-gated). Addressed by TRD-003.
