NOTE vs acceptance #1: a compound command whose LAST stage is the runner still fires on a non-zero exit even when its summary shows zero failures (e.g. a coverage threshold) -- that exit genuinely is the runner's.

title: WriteBoundaryMonitor reverts legitimate git pull/checkout, leaving HEAD and working tree out of sync
description:
OBSERVED LIVE 2026-09-26: WriteBoundaryMonitor reverted a legitimate `git pull --ff-only` in the main checkout, leaving the repo half-updated.

Sequence: PR #86 merged into the feature branch; `git pull --ff-only` in the main checkout (clean tree, 6557f47 -> 5f9a99b) ran inside a bash tool call while the behavior runtime was armed. After the call the monitor reported "Write boundary violation ... was reverted" for 4 paths the pull legitimately changed:
- packages/agent-core/src/behavior/workspace-snapshot.ts (guardrail-source)
- packages/agent-core/tests/pipe-masked-failure.test.ts (test-file)
- packages/agent-core/tests/write-boundary.test.ts (test-file)
- packages/pi-extension/tests/agent-fix-provider.test.ts (test-file)

Result: HEAD = 5f9a99b but those 4 files hold their 6557f47 contents (git status: 4 x M, 167 lines of the merged fixes undone in the working tree). A later `git commit -a` would silently revert the merged fixes. The monitor cannot be worked around from the session (any restore is reverted too); it has to be repaired from a shell outside the session.

The monitor treats every tool call that changes a protected path as tampering. It cannot tell an agent editing a guardrail from git moving HEAD to a commit that already contains the change (pull, checkout, merge, rebase, reset, stash pop). Reverting in the second case does not protect anything -- the content is already committed upstream -- it only desynchronises the working tree from HEAD.

Acceptance:
- A tool call that moves HEAD and leaves protected paths matching the new HEAD's blobs is not reverted (compare post-call content against `git show HEAD:<path>`, not only against the pre-call snapshot).
- When the monitor does revert, it never leaves a protected path differing from HEAD without saying so explicitly (the message must name the HEAD mismatch and the repair command).
- Test: simulate pull (commit on a second branch, then ff-merge inside a monitored call) -> no revert.
close_reason: done

comments.text: 2026-09-27 dev e2e: confirmed the write boundary is not scoped to behaviors at all. extension.ts:438-440 runs monitor.check() on every tool_result; activation snapshots every tracked and untracked test file and guardrail source. With NO behavior running (no dispatch or continuation in the log), a plain user request to append a line to scripts/tests/yaml-scalar.test.js was reverted and the model told to 'Fix the source under test instead'. So no one can edit tests from an omp session in an armed repo, and any git pull/checkout touching protected paths is undone. The fix needs to scope the monitor to behavior execution (or to fix-agent writes), not only to exempt git. description:
## Test Task: TRD-010-TEST
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-f08a2a09-command-lifecycle-hooks.md#trd-010-test
PRD Reference: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-f08a2a09-command-lifecycle-hooks.md#req-002

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-002**: `command.start` fires after resolution, before the workflow (Must)
`command.start` fires after resolution, before the workflow (Must)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-001-1: Given a command is invoked | When it begins | Then exactly one `command
- AC-002-1: Given a command invocation | When the command has been resolved from its input | Then `command
- AC-002-2: Given an invocation whose arguments the command's own workflow then rejects | When it rejects them | Then rejects, when it rejects them, then the invocation has already produced a `command
- AC-002-3: Given a `command.start` handler is configured to block | When it blocks | Then the command's workflow does not begin
- AC-004-5: Given a `command.start` handler blocked the command | When the block occurs | Then `command

--- TRD Context ---
**Decision:** Build the lifecycle as a harness-neutral core in `packages/agent-core` (event payloads, configuration validation, redaction, a shell runner, a prompt runner, a serial dispatcher, and a per-session command-run tracker) and one adapter in `packages/pi-extension` that connects it to Pi. The adapter is the only code that knows Pi's event names.

**Decisions made by the maintainer during design (all recorded in PRD v1.0.2 to v1.0.4):**

- The first release is adapter-specific, with Pi as the proving harness. A runtime-owned wrapper is deferred.
- `command.start` fires from the runtime when the command's slash input is seen, so it never depends on the model and a start handler's block is enforced by the runtime. A command whose own prompt then rejects its arguments has already produced a start and ends as `failed`.
- A command's completion is signalled by a silent `ensemble_command_complete` tool that the model is told to call last. The instruction is injected per turn by the adapter, not generated into every Pi prompt, so projects without hooks see no change.
- A settled loop never ends a command. A command that never signals completion ends as `cancelled` when the session ends or the next command begins.
- A prompt handler is evaluated by an isolated headless child (`pi -p --no-session -ne -nt -np`), parsed against a typed response contract.
- No handler runs until the host reports the project as trusted (`ctx.isProjectTrusted()`).
- `on_error` is required on every handler. Default timeouts are 5 seconds for shell handlers and 30 seconds for prompt handlers.
- Selections list commands by name. Wildcards and groups are rejected.
- For harnesses with no adapter, the guide, a capability table and a status check say hooks are inactive. Nothing is shown at command time there.

**Why code and not a prompt (Constitution rule 8):** what runs at a command boundary, the trust check, the environment allowlist, redaction, timeouts and process cleanup are enforcement boundaries and must not be editable by a model or a user prompt. What a team wants to run (the hooks file, the executables, the prompt files) is user-owned and stays in files they edit without a toolchain.

title: pi model tiers: decide handling of no-modelRoles hosts (@default drop), tier no-op without custom roles, and unmapped low tier
description:
## Context
PR #230 (https://github.com/Sunstone-Partners/ensemble/pull/230, merged as df7c8d2) changed the pi generator (packages/pi/src/transformers/agent-transformer.ts, resolveModelValue / MODEL_TIER_ROLES) to emit `model: "@high,@default"` (8 agents) and `model: "@medium,@default"` (16 agents) in packages/pi/agents/*.md instead of the bare words `high` / `medium` (which omp matched as a model-name substring, e.g. `openrouter/openai/o3-mini-high`). Post-merge review found three design-level gaps that cannot be fixed by documentation alone. Docs/lockfile drift is fixed separately in the follow-up PR that lands this bead.

## Host behaviour (verified in @oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent src/config/model-resolver.ts)
- `high` / `medium` are CUSTOM roles. getModelRoleAlias (~960-968) only treats `@x` as a role alias when x is a built-in role or `settings.getModelRole(x)` is set. An unconfigured `@high` therefore stays a LITERAL pattern (resolveConfiguredRolePattern ~1075-1104 `if (!role) return [normalized]`) that matches no model.
- `@default` resolves through `modelRoles.default`. With it unset, `default` has no priority.json chain (priority.json keys: smol, slow, designer), so resolveConfiguredRolePattern returns undefined and resolveConfiguredModelPatterns (~1124-1133) drops it from the list.
- resolveEffectiveAgentModelSelection (~1149-1180) returns the configured agent patterns whenever any exist, and inherits the parent session model only for a LONE session-inherited pattern (isSessionInheritedAgentPattern ~999-1008: `default`, `@default`, `*`, `@task`), never for a list.
- Matrix: (a) tier role configured -> agent runs on it. (b) tier role not configured, `modelRoles.default` configured -> `@high` fails, agent runs on the `default` model; tiering is a no-op. (c) neither configured -> patterns collapse to the unmatched literal `@high` / `@medium`; sdk.ts ~2402 reports `Model "@high" not found` and the session has no model ("No model selected", session/agent-session.ts ~5563).

## Gaps
1. (A-1) Case (c) is a regression for hosts with no `modelRoles` at all: before #230 the bare word matched a model by substring, now the agent cannot start. Not fixable inside ensemble without dropping tiers, because omp inherits the parent session model only for a lone `@default` entry, not for a list.
2. (A-2) Case (b): consumers without custom `high`/`medium` roles get no tiering at all.
3. (A-6) The tier vocabulary is `high|medium|low` (schemas/agent-yaml-schema.json, scripts/lint-model-ids.js) but MODEL_TIER_ROLES maps only `high` and `medium`, so a future `model: low` agent would silently keep the bare-word substring bug.

## Decision needed
Pick one (or combine):
- Accept and document: the README "Model tiers and omp roles" section (added by the follow-up PR) already states cases (a)-(c); add `low` handling or a lint that rejects unmapped tiers.
- Ask omp upstream for a list-tail parent-inheritance fallback (session model when every list entry is unresolved).
- Emit built-in roles per tier (e.g. `@slow` for high, `@smol` for low) which resolve without user config, trading away the custom-role names.
- Map `low` in MODEL_TIER_ROLES (and test it), at minimum so every schema tier is handled.

References: PR #230, commit df7c8d2, packages/pi/README.md "Model tiers and omp roles".

title: [trd:trd-2026-b6db9749-behavior-habits-runtime:task:TRD-009-TEST] - [ ] **TRD-009-TEST** Evidence-backed notification tests (2h)
description:
## Test Task: TRD-009-TEST
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-b6db9749-behavior-habits-runtime.md#trd-009-test
PRD Reference: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-b6db9749-behavior-habits-runtime.md#req-009

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-009**: Notify/steer the main session with evidence-backed results
Notify/steer the main session with evidence-backed results Priority: Must

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-009-1: Given a behavior produces a user-relevant result | When it completes | Then the main session receives a concise message referencing the specific evidence
- AC-009-2: Given the message is delivered | When inspected | Then it never claims an action was applied unless independently verified as such
- AC-012-1: Given a message states a behavior's outcome | When reviewed | Then every asserted fact traces to recorded evidence, never to an unverified model claim alone

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen: Option B — dedicated adapter modules per new trigger-source type, plus a shared notification-state module.** Unchanged from 1.0.0.

New `file-source-adapter.ts` and `release-source-adapter.ts` under `packages/agent-core/src/behavior/` each produce a `BehaviorEvent` through `normalizeEvent`, mirroring the existing `pi-events.ts` → `event-translator.ts` → `normalizeEvent` → `LocalEventMatcher` chain. A new `notification-state.ts` in `pi-extension` centralises busy, duplicate and stale tracking for every behavior. Package quarantine gets its own `package-quarantine.ts` beside `package-discovery.ts`.

### Decisions added in 1.1.0

1. **How artifact changes are detected: content hashes checked at lifecycle points.** No `fs.watch`, no new dependency.
   - The adapter derives its watch set from the compiled `artifact.changed` triggers (the `path` predicate).
   - It hashes those files at `tool_result` and at `agent_end`, and emits an event when a digest differs from the last one seen in the session.
   - The hooks it relies on already exist, which is what AC-001-2 means by "supported host API".
   - It behaves the same on every OS (see REQ-023).
   - It needs no new dependency, which constitution §4 would require approval for.

   | Option | Why not chosen |
   |---|---|
   | `fs.watch` | Event semantics differ between macOS, Linux and Windows (rename-vs-change, recursive support). That is exactly the kind of per-platform behavior difference REQ-023 forbids absorbing silently. It also keeps a handle open for the whole session. |
   | `chokidar` | A new runtime dependency (constitution §4), for a problem that lifecycle-point hashing already solves. |

   The limitation, stated rather than hidden: a change is seen at the next tool call or at the end of the run, not instantly. NFR-001 measures from event validation, so this latency is outside its budget. TRD-003 reports it separately.

2. **Release signal (resolves the PRD's REQ-002 clarification): a new `v*` tag in local refs.** This matches this repo's `release.yml` (`on: push: tags: ['v*']`).
   - The tag pattern is a trigger predicate, so repositories with different conventions change configuration, not code (Rule 8).
   - It is detected two ways. First, from a successful tag-creating tool call (`git tag`, `gh release create`), in the same way `repository.changed` is derived today. Second, by diffing tag refs at session start and at `agent_end`, which covers tags that arrive by fetch.
   - It emits the **existing** catalog type `release.completed`, carrying `{ tag, sha, source }`.
   - One tag produces one event per session, whichever path sees it first.

3. **Coverage metric (resolves the PRD's REQ-016 clarification): Jest `json-summary` output, per file, `lines.pct` and `branches.pct` by default.**
   - Each package's `test:coverage` is `jest --coverage`. Jest's default reporters (`json`, `lcov`, `text`, `clover`) produce raw maps, not percentages.
   - So the behavior watches `coverage/coverage-summary.json`, and its README tells repositories to enable `json-summary`.
   - The metrics and the threshold (default 1.0 percentage point) are behavior configuration.
   - If the artifact never appears, the behavior shows up as an inert trigger in `/ensemble-status`; it is never silently idle.
   - The baseline is the previous snapshot seen **in the same session** (Rule 4). The first observation in a session only sets the baseline.

4. **The comparison is a generic command: `artifact.compare` (TRD-033).** It compares numeric JSON paths between the previous and current snapshot of an artifact and knows nothing about coverage.
   - The alternatives were rejected. Doing the comparison in an agent step would make the reported delta an unverified model claim (REQ-012). A coverage-specific command would make the third behavior need Ensemble code (REQ-018).
   - It lands in PR 1, which is why PR 5 can be configuration only.

5. **Notification transport** (REQ-009, REQ-010). `notification-state.ts` delivers to two sinks:
   - **The user**, through `SessionUiBridge.notify`, a new method that wraps `ctx.ui.notify`. Headless sessions fall back to the console.
   - **The model's context**, through `pi.sendMessage` with `display: true` and `triggerTurn: false`.

   `triggerTurn: false` is deliberate. #107 deleted the continuation path because a message that makes the agent act bypasses `MutationGuard` (`extension.ts:118-140`); a notification is data, never an instruction. Any test-derived text in a notification is fenced and labelled as data, a lesson from #94's live runs. `sendMessage` is added to `assertRequiredCapabilities`.

6. **Verified fix application** (REQ-033). This is configuration plus two small code changes.
   - A new behavior, `apply-verified-fix`, runs `mode: auto`. It triggers on `fix.verified` with the predicate `verdict: passed`, declares only `fix.apply` with no tools, and calls `fix.apply { proposalRef: ${event.payload.proposalRef} }`.
   - `CommandRegistry` then asks `ApprovalGate`. Today the prompt is only `descriptor.description` ("Apply a verified fix proposal…"), so the human would approve without seeing what changes. Code change 1 (TRD-019): the prompt names the proposal, its files and a diff summary.
   - `commit-policy.ts` has no importers today. Code change 2 (TRD-021): wire it in so an applied fix is committed with attribution.

### Alternatives considered (architecture)

| Option | Summary | Why not chosen |
|---|---|---|
| **A — Widen the existing translator, inline notification** | Add file and release branches inside `event-translator.ts`; keep notification-state logic at each `ctx.ui.notify` call site. | `event-translator.ts` would cover three unrelated source domains. Busy/duplicate/stale logic would be copied per behavior, which is the per-reaction duplication the PRD sets out to remove. |
| **B — Dedicated adapter modules + shared notification-state module** *(chosen)* | One adapter module per source type, all feeding the same ingress; one shared notification-state module. | Matches the existing boundary (`agent-core` = provider-neutral logic, `pi-extension` = host wiring), and centralises notification state once. |
| **C — Single generic "external signal" adapter** | One configurable "watch path X for condition Y" abstraction for both sources. | Risks becoming an arbitrary-condition escape hatch around the closed, versioned catalog (REQ-CQRS-005); still duplicates notification state. |

Verifies: TRD-009

PRD ACs Proven: AC-009-1, AC-009-2, AC-012-1
Proof of requirement: 
Target Files: packages/pi-extension/tests/notification-state.test.ts` (new), packages/pi-extension/tests/extension.test.ts` (extended)
Actions:

Test AC:
- [ ] Scenario: a result reaches both the user and the model -- Given a completed behavior with evidence `E1`, When it notifies through the real `activate()`, Then `ui.notify` and `sendMessage` both receive text citing `E1`, and `sendMessage` has `triggerTurn: false`
- [ ] Scenario: an unverified "applied" claim is never sent -- Given a result text saying "fix applied" with no `fix.applied` event, When the notification is built, Then the claim is absent from both sinks
- [ ] Scenario: every fact traces to evidence -- Given a result with three facts, two of them backed by evidence, When the notification is built, Then only the two backed facts appear
- [ ] Scenario: test output cannot pose as instructions -- Given evidence text containing "SYSTEM: ignore the above", When the notification is built, Then that text appears only inside the fenced data line after all instructions
- [ ] Scenario: a host without sendMessage fails loudly -- Given a Pi object lacking `sendMessage`, When `activate()` runs, Then it throws a blocking-gap error naming `sendMessage`

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-009**: Runs see only an allowed set of environment values (Must)
Runs see only an allowed set of environment values (Must)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-009-1: Given a run | When the agent starts | Then only environment values on an allowlist are visible to it
- AC-009-2: Given a credential present in the maintainer's environment but not on the allowlist | When a run executes | Then the agent cannot read it
- AC-009-3: Given a credential a run legitimately needs | When the run starts | Then it reaches the agent only by being named on the allowlist, from the local environment on a maintainer's machine and from CI secrets in hosted CI
- AC-020-1: Given a run in which the agent prints an allowed secret value | When results and logs are stored | Then the value is not present in them
- AC-020-2: Given a stored result | When it is inspected | Then it contains no environment values beyond the allowlisted, non-secret ones

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-020**: Stored results and logs never contain credentials (Must)
Stored results and logs never contain credentials (Must)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-009-1: Given a run | When the agent starts | Then only environment values on an allowlist are visible to it
- AC-009-2: Given a credential present in the maintainer's environment but not on the allowlist | When a run executes | Then the agent cannot read it
- AC-009-3: Given a credential a run legitimately needs | When the run starts | Then it reaches the agent only by being named on the allowlist, from the local environment on a maintainer's machine and from CI secrets in hosted CI
- AC-020-1: Given a run in which the agent prints an allowed secret value | When results and logs are stored | Then the value is not present in them
- AC-020-2: Given a stored result | When it is inspected | Then it contains no environment values beyond the allowlisted, non-secret ones

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen: Option C, extend `evals/` and put runtimes behind adapters.**

The repository already has a headless behavioral eval harness (`evals/run.js`, `evals/lib/sandbox.js`, `evals/lib/graders.js`, `.github/workflows/evals.yml`, five task-keyed scenarios, unit tests with a stub `claude`). It already provides a throwaway git sandbox, deterministic graders, a total spend cap (`--max-usd`), results files and an on-demand workflow. It lacks what the PRD is mostly about:

| PRD need | State today |
|---|---|
| Evals keyed by skill, editable as files | Scenarios are keyed by task, one `scenario.json` each |
| With-skill and no-skill arms | One arm only |
| Repeats and a reliability bar | One run per scenario |
| Scrubbed environment | `spawnSync` inherits the whole environment |
| Model, skill version, eval version, runtime in results | Only a model tag |
| Coverage per skill, result cache, replay, regression compare | None |
| Pi | None |

| Option | Summary | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| A. Extend in place | Add the above to `run.js`; Pi logic added inline | Simplest, but Claude Code and Pi logic would tangle in one file |
| B. Adopt an external eval tool | Replace the runner with a third-party tool and port graders | Needs a spike and a new-dependency approval (constitution, Approval Requirements); rework of five tested scenarios; unknown support for a no-skill arm and Pi |
| **C. Extend with runner adapters** | Keep the tested runner, sandbox and graders. Add skill-keyed eval files, arms, repeats, an env allowlist, a results schema, coverage, cache and compare, behind a small runner interface with Claude Code and Pi adapters | **Chosen.** No new dependency (Node built-ins only), builds on tested code, and the eval format stays tool-neutral so an external runner could consume it later |

The PRD's Entry criterion (tool spike, fallback to a minimal in-repo runner) resolves to the fallback: this TRD is that runner, built on the existing harness. No new dependency is introduced, so no dependency approval is needed. If the owner later wants an external tool, the eval files in `evals/skills/` are the stable input.

Decisions fixed by the PRD and carried here: deterministic checks decide verdicts; judged checks only supplement and use a different model; 5 runs per arm with 4 of 5 required; $50 per suite and 900 s per run by default; results committed as per-skill baseline summaries with full logs as CI artifacts; Claude Code and Pi; on-demand CI only; advisory regression check.

title: Governed fix-agent child outlives its session (orphaned, PPID 1); shutdown handler times out
description:
In headless runs the fix-failing-test governed dispatch spawns 'omp -p --no-session --no-extensions --tools=read,grep,glob' late in the session. The host exited and the child kept running reparented to PID 1, its result never consumed; stderr showed 'Extension error (ensemble-behavior-runtime.ts): handler timed out after 2000ms'. Read-only tools, so no writes, but it is wasted model spend and an unowned process. Abort in-flight dispatches on session_shutdown.

Evidence: headless omp -p runs on dev (7b57d4a) in worktree /private/tmp/wt-e2e, planted bug scripts/lib/e2e-sum.js; logs in /tmp/e2e/ (e2e.jsonl, e2e2.jsonl, e2e3.jsonl, guard.jsonl, *-runtime-log.jsonl).
close_reason: Fixed: extension.ts now owns an AbortController whose signal is passed to createWorkflowDispatcher, and session_shutdown ABORTS BEFORE draining. Order is the fix -- draining first waits on a child that has no reason to stop, the host handler times out (2s observed), and the child is orphaned to PID 1 exactly as reported. execFile already honoured an AbortSignal; the signal simply never reached it, because the dispatcher accepted one and nothing ever passed it. 3 tests: the agent receives a defined signal (the gap), an aborted signal is visible to it, and the abort-before-drain ordering is asserted against source since a runtime test would have to race the host timeout.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-006-1: Given an eval | When it runs | Then both a with-skill arm and a baseline arm run against identical workspaces and the same task
- AC-006-2: Given the baseline arm | When it runs | Then the skill under test is not available to the agent
- AC-006-3: Given a baseline arm where the skill under test is still reachable by any means | When the run starts | Then the harness aborts that eval with a message naming the leak
- AC-006-4: Given a skill whose subject the agent may already know well | When its baseline arm runs | Then the baseline is the same agent with the skill unavailable, and a near-zero uplift is reported as a valid result, not an error

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen: Option C, extend `evals/` and put runtimes behind adapters.**

The repository already has a headless behavioral eval harness (`evals/run.js`, `evals/lib/sandbox.js`, `evals/lib/graders.js`, `.github/workflows/evals.yml`, five task-keyed scenarios, unit tests with a stub `claude`). It already provides a throwaway git sandbox, deterministic graders, a total spend cap (`--max-usd`), results files and an on-demand workflow. It lacks what the PRD is mostly about:

| PRD need | State today |
|---|---|
| Evals keyed by skill, editable as files | Scenarios are keyed by task, one `scenario.json` each |
| With-skill and no-skill arms | One arm only |
| Repeats and a reliability bar | One run per scenario |
| Scrubbed environment | `spawnSync` inherits the whole environment |
| Model, skill version, eval version, runtime in results | Only a model tag |
| Coverage per skill, result cache, replay, regression compare | None |
| Pi | None |

| Option | Summary | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| A. Extend in place | Add the above to `run.js`; Pi logic added inline | Simplest, but Claude Code and Pi logic would tangle in one file |
| B. Adopt an external eval tool | Replace the runner with a third-party tool and port graders | Needs a spike and a new-dependency approval (constitution, Approval Requirements); rework of five tested scenarios; unknown support for a no-skill arm and Pi |
| **C. Extend with runner adapters** | Keep the tested runner, sandbox and graders. Add skill-keyed eval files, arms, repeats, an env allowlist, a results schema, coverage, cache and compare, behind a small runner interface with Claude Code and Pi adapters | **Chosen.** No new dependency (Node built-ins only), builds on tested code, and the eval format stays tool-neutral so an external runner could consume it later |

The PRD's Entry criterion (tool spike, fallback to a minimal in-repo runner) resolves to the fallback: this TRD is that runner, built on the existing harness. No new dependency is introduced, so no dependency approval is needed. If the owner later wants an external tool, the eval files in `evals/skills/` are the stable input.

Decisions fixed by the PRD and carried here: deterministic checks decide verdicts; judged checks only supplement and use a different model; 5 runs per arm with 4 of 5 required; $50 per suite and 900 s per run by default; results committed as per-skill baseline summaries with full logs as CI artifacts; Claude Code and Pi; on-demand CI only; advisory regression check.

title: [trd:trd-2026-d6bbf322-new-feature-workflow:task:TRD-010] - [ ] **TRD-010**: Enforce single-active-run-per-project with create-time exclusivity (3h)
description:
## Task: TRD-010
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-d6bbf322-new-feature-workflow.md#trd-010
PRD Reference: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-d6bbf322-new-feature-workflow.md#req-008

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-008**: Allow only one active feature run per project
Allow only one active feature run per project Priority: Must | Complexity: Medium Triggering and Human Decisions

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-008-1: Given a project already has an active or paused `new-feature` run | When a user tries to start another run in that project | Then the workflow blocks the second start and identifies how to resume or explicitly abandon the active run
- AC-008-2: Given a run is explicitly abandoned or completed | When the project index records that terminal outcome | Then a new run can be started without deleting the abandoned run's artifacts or history
- AC-008-3: Given a run is merely interrupted or has not been updated recently | When another run is requested | Then it remains active and is not automatically expired or abandoned

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen: Option C — hardened in-session stage composition with a dedicated atomic run-index store.**

`new-feature` is authored the same way every other product command in this repo is authored: a single orchestrating skill (`packages/development/commands/new-feature.yaml`, generated to runtime-specific prompts exactly like `fix-issue.yaml`) that executes each stage's existing skill body in-session — the same mechanism that loaded `ensemble-refine-prd`'s content into this session and had the agent execute its Phases directly. This is forced, not merely preferred: Pi's `ExtensionAPI` has no completion/invoke primitive that would let an extension programmatically run another skill and get its result back (confirmed — no `pi.invokeCommand` or equivalent exists); the only code-level "run a skill" mechanism, `createAgentPort()`, spawns a bounded, disposable `omp -p --no-session --no-extensions` subprocess in an isolated worktree, and does not fit a long-lived, project-resident workflow whose PRD/TRD stages use the interactive `--collab` review server.

What is new, and is the one piece of real infrastructure this TRD adds: a `RunIndexStore` (`packages/agent-core/src/new-feature/run-index.ts`) built on the one proven concurrency-safe pattern in this repo — `session.js`'s temp-file-then-`renameSync` atomic write plus `expectedRevision`/409-style optimistic concurrency — rather than `ProposalStore`'s plain `writeFileSync` (no atomicity, no lock, not adequate for PRD AC-005-3's fail-closed-on-malformed-index requirement). Runs are stored at `.ensemble/new-feature/<run-id>.json`, mirroring `ProposalStore`'s `.ensemble/proposals/<ref>.json` convention (also excluded from `tree-baseline.ts` drift detection, so this is consistent runtime-owned state, not a project-source mutation).

### Alternatives considered

| Option | Summary | Why not chosen |
|---|---|---|
| A — Plain JSON checkpoint | Same in-session composition, but checkpoints are a single `writeFileSync`, no atomicity/locking. | Fastest to build, but a crash mid-write can corrupt the run index, which directly violates AC-005-3's "fail closed with a recoverable diagnostic" requirement — the repo's own `ProposalStore` already demonstrates this gap is real, not hypothetical. |
| B — Subprocess-dispatched stages | New orchestrator module dispatches every stage as a bounded `createAgentPort()` subprocess; advances the run index only after subprocess exit 0 + artifact-on-disk confirmation. | Most rigorous completion signal (a real process boundary instead of self-reported bookkeeping), but substantially more build effort, and does not fit the interactive `--collab` review-server stages `create-prd`/`refine-prd` already use — those are long-lived, human-attended HTTP sessions, not bounded one-shot subprocess work, and would need bespoke carve-out handling under this option. |
| **C — Hardened in-session composition** *(chosen)* | In-session stage execution (like every existing product command), backed by a dedicated atomic `RunIndexStore`. | Reuses 100% of the existing skill-composition and `ask_user`-approval infrastructure (including the `--collab` review server, which needs no special-casing), while fixing Option A's one real correctness gap with the repo's one proven atomic-write pattern. Matches user-confirmed direction. |

### Honest trust-boundary note

Because stage execution stays in-session (per Option C), the approval gates implemented by TRD-014/TRD-017/TRD-019 are enforced by the orchestrating skill's own conditional logic checking `RunIndexStore`-persisted approval fields before it issues an implementation or `gh pr create` tool call — not by a separate runtime authorization chokepoint like `agent-core`'s `MutationGuard` (which exists elsewhere in this repo, gating CQRS-registered commands, but `new-feature`'s mutating actions are ordinary skill-level tool calls, same as `fix-issue`'s own gated PR-creation step, not CQRS commands). This is the same trust boundary every existing Ensemble product command already operates under. Building a `MutationGuard`-equivalent chokepoint for skill-level tool calls is a materially larger investment this PRD does not request and no other product command has; REQ-014's "runtime authority" is satisfied here by making the check a required precondition over persisted, validated store state rather than over prompt claims — which is what AC-014-2 actually asks for — not by inventing a new enforcement subsystem.
Satisfies: REQ-008
PRD ACs: AC-008-1, AC-008-2, AC-008-3
Target File: packages/agent-core/src/new-feature/run-index.ts
Actions:
1. `createRun()` first writes a marker file `.ensemble/new-feature/active.lock` using `fs.writeFileSync(path, runId, { flag: "wx" })` — write-exclusive, which fails atomically (`EEXIST`) if another active/paused run's marker already exists; this is the create-time exclusivity primitive `mutate()`'s `expectedRevision` check cannot provide (there is no prior revision for a brand-new file).
2. On `EEXIST`, reject the second start, identifying the existing active/paused run's id and how to resume or abandon it.
3. On `abandon()`/`complete()`, remove `active.lock` (but never delete the run's own `.json` history file), permitting a new `createRun()` to succeed.
4. Never remove `active.lock` or mark a run abandoned based on elapsed time alone — only an explicit user/abandon action does so.
Implementation AC:
- [ ] Given `active.lock` already exists, when `createRun()` is called, then it throws a typed "run already active" error naming the existing `runId` and does not write a second run file.
- [ ] Given a run is completed or abandoned, when `active.lock` is removed, then a subsequent `createRun()` succeeds and the terminal run's `.json` file still exists on disk.
- [ ] Given a run has not been updated in a long time but is still `active`/`paused`, when `createRun()` is called again, then it is still rejected (no auto-expiry).
Dependencies: TRD-002

title: [trd:trd-2026-15aa5acd-live-behavior-dispatch-autofix:task:TRD-028-TEST] - [ ] **TRD-028-TEST** Retry-budget and counter-reset tests (4h)
description:
## Test Task: TRD-028-TEST
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-15aa5acd-live-behavior-dispatch-autofix.md#trd-028-test
PRD Reference: #req-006

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen: Option C — single enforcement seam, additive.**

A new `MutationGuard` chokepoint in `agent-core` is the one place `policy.mode`, `capabilities.mutation_classes` (via the existing `hasMutationAuthority()`), and protected-path rules are resolved. It is wired once at the loader boundary rather than replicated per tool registration. The translator, matcher, and auto-fix loop are added to `pi-extension`. Discovery roots and `execution.test_command` are additive changes to existing schema/discovery code. `ToolRegistry`, `outbox`, and the compiler are reused unchanged.

### Alternatives considered

| Option | Summary | Why not chosen |
|---|---|---|
| **A — In-place extension** | Enforce mode/mutation/path rules as wrapper checks inside `behavior-loader`'s per-tool `execute()` closures. | Enforcement scattered across call sites; every future tool registration must remember to wrap. The PRD's central failure mode is *guarantees that exist in one place but are not reached from another* — Option A reproduces exactly that shape. |
| **B — Governance kernel** | Route every mutation through a `MutationBroker` + `GovernedWorkspace` in `agent-core`; `pi-extension` becomes a thin adapter. | Strongest long-term design and the right eventual target, but it re-opens already-shipped code across every tool path for a ~6-7 PR refactor before a single PRD requirement is demonstrable. Deferred deliberately, not rejected. |
| **C — Single enforcement seam** *(chosen)* | One `MutationGuard` chokepoint, wired once; everything else additive. | Gets a single auditable chokepoint (Option B's main benefit) without Option B's refactor surface. Fits the existing `agent-core` / `pi-extension` split. |

### Architectural note carried from grounding

Two defects found while grounding this design are folded into PR 1 rather than left implicit:

1. `pi-events.ts` emits `runtime.tool_result` / `runtime.tool.called` / `runtime.tool.failed` / `runtime.tool.completed`, none of which appear in `HARNESS_EVENT_TYPES` (which defines `runtime.tool_call.started` / `runtime.tool_call.completed`). `normalizeEvent` does not currently reject uncatalogued types, so PRD AC-002-1's "validated against the closed catalog" would be vacuous. Addressed by TRD-001 (`[satisfies INFRA]`).
2. `behavior-loader.ts:79` calls `registry.grant(...)` unconditionally immediately before `registry.invoke(...)`, making the grant boundary a rubber stamp for behavior-governed tools (unlike the echo path, where the grant is CLI-flag-gated). Addressed by TRD-003.

title: [trd:trd-2026-1d3e0dd6-new-feature-foreman-flag:task:TRD-008] - [ ] **TRD-008** Front door accepts and forwards `--foreman` (`packages/development/commands/feature.yaml`) (2h)
description:
## Task: TRD-008
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-1d3e0dd6-new-feature-foreman-flag.md#trd-008
PRD Reference: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-1d3e0dd6-new-feature-foreman-flag.md#req-008

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-008**: `/ensemble:feature` accepts and forwards `--foreman` (Must)
`/ensemble:feature` accepts and forwards `--foreman` (Must) Delivery and safety

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-008-1: Given `/ensemble:feature new --foreman <idea>` | When it dispatches | Then it builds `/ensemble:new-feature --foreman --idea "<idea>"`, and the idea text is forwarded exactly as given (the flag is removed from it, nothing else is)
- AC-008-2: Given `resume` | When it dispatches | Then the flag is forwarded; `abandon` still forwards any reason text after it
- AC-008-3: Given `--foreman` appears anywhere other than as the first token after the keyword (for example inside the idea prose) | When it dispatches | Then it is treated as ordinary text and not as the flag
- AC-008-4: Given an unknown keyword | When it dispatches | Then it is rejected with the keyword table and no side effects, as today

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen approach:** a prompt-only change to two YAML command sources. No TypeScript changes.

- `packages/development/commands/new-feature.yaml` gains a boolean `foreman` parameter and one derived variable, `FOREMAN`, defined once in Entry Point Resolution Step 1 and referenced by every later step. Each step that asks the user gets a `FOREMAN == true` branch that takes a deterministic, recorded, non-interactive decision. Each step that dispatches a stage skill appends `--foreman` when `FOREMAN == true`.
- `packages/development/commands/feature.yaml` (the `/ensemble:feature` front door) recognizes `--foreman` as the first token after the keyword and forwards it.
- Generated OMP, Pi and Codex artifacts are regenerated from the repo root, never hand-edited.

**Why prompt-only (Constitution Rule 8):** how a workflow behaves when no one can answer is something a maintainer would plausibly tune (for example, switching the PR gate to park instead of auto-grant). That belongs in the command prose, not in TypeScript. `RunIndexStore` already supports everything needed: `StageOutcome.detail` carries the "granted by `--foreman` policy" record.

**Additive-only edits (found in refinement):** the existing suites (`new-feature-command.test.js`, `feature-command.test.js`, `feature-input-validation-boundary.test.js`, `feature-concurrency-passthrough.test.js`) pin exact sentences in both YAML files, for example "any remaining text is an unsupported flag or argument rejected here". So no pre-existing sentence may be reworded or removed. Foreman behavior is added as new actions or appended sentences, and the existing suites must pass unchanged. For the front door that means: a new action, placed before the validation action, removes a leading `--foreman` token and sets `FOREMAN`, so the pinned validation sentences still read "remaining text" correctly; and a new action, placed after the invocation is constructed, inserts `--foreman` right after `/ensemble:new-feature` in whatever invocation was built.

**Alternatives rejected:**
- *Env-var-only detection (no flag).* Rejected: the maintainer asked for a `--foreman` flag, and the five stage skills already key on that flag.
- *A new RunRecord field `autoGranted`.* Rejected: TypeScript and schema change for information `StageOutcome.detail` already carries.
- *Parking at the approval gates.* Rejected by the maintainer: it stalls every no-user run.
Satisfies: REQ-008
PRD ACs: AC-008-1, AC-008-2, AC-008-3, AC-008-4
Target File: 
Actions:

Implementation AC:
- [ ] Given `new --foreman <idea>`, when the front door dispatches, then a new action placed before the validation action removes the leading `--foreman` token and sets `FOREMAN`, and a new action placed after the invocation is constructed inserts `--foreman` immediately after `/ensemble:new-feature`, giving `/ensemble:new-feature --foreman --idea "<idea>"` with the idea text otherwise unchanged
- [ ] Given `resume`, `status` or `abandon` with `--foreman`, when it dispatches, then the flag is inserted into the constructed invocation by the same post-construction action and `abandon` still forwards any reason after it
- [ ] Given `--foreman` anywhere other than the first token after the keyword, when it dispatches, then it is ordinary text
- [ ] Given an unknown keyword, empty arguments, or extra text after `resume`/`status` once a leading `--foreman` has been removed, when it dispatches, then it is rejected with the keyword table and no side effects, by the existing validation sentences, which are not reworded

description:
## Test Task: TRD-036-TEST
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-70e784f2-code-review-process.md#trd-036-test
PRD Reference: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-70e784f2-code-review-process.md#req-022

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-022**: Explainers for context sharing (Should)
Explainers for context sharing (Should) Anyone can get an up-to-date explainer for a slice of the codebase, replacing line-by-line reading of trivial diffs for learning. Cross-cutting requirements

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-022-1: Given a maintainer requests an explainer for a named module | When it is produced | Then it reflects the code as it is now and is delivered within minutes
- AC-022-2: Given an explainer is produced | When it is read | Then it names the files it was derived from

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen approach (Option C):** extend the pattern TRD-2026-82b6a138 established: **editable behavior in skills, agents and markdown; a small set of pure, deterministic libraries for what must not be self-certified by a model.**

- **User-owned (Constitution Rule 8), prose or data a maintainer edits without a toolchain:** per-area rules (`REVIEW.md` files), the policy block inside the root `REVIEW.md` (round cap, depth table, bot and maintainer logins, sensitive and High paths, Low-waiver state), severity definitions, reviewer, verifier, classifier and security-lane prompts, the PR template, the sweep and explainer procedures. All of it is read from the **target branch**, never from the PR head (REQ-024).
- **Enforcement (Rules 5 and 7), code that grades a model's claim:** vote tally, tier assignment with its sensitive-path floor and Low-waiver evidence, approval evaluation bound to a commit, the merge gate, round-cap derivation, repeat suppression, delta-range selection, depth bounds, slice coverage, metrics and eval scoring. Each is a pure CommonJS module in `packages/development/lib/`, exposed as a JSON-in/JSON-out subcommand of the existing `pr-review-cli.js`, following the 82b6a138 precedent. None performs network I/O or holds a timer.
- **Entry points (Rule 6):** every capability is reached through the one `pr-review-cycle` skill, which `fix-issue`, `implement-trd-beads` and `pr-merge` already invoke or will invoke (a new `MODE=gate` for `pr-merge`). YAML callers reference the skill only, never the CLI, as the existing parity tests require.
- **Recurrence (Rule 4):** nightly or weekly sweeps and daily eval runs are on-demand skills; a workflow template for the host repository is opt-in and scaffolded by init-project. Ensemble's own workflows gain no `schedule` trigger.

**Alternatives considered (user chose C):**

- **Option A -- prose-only skills and agents:** fewest files and fastest to ship. Rejected: the vote threshold, the tier floor, commit-bound approvals and the round cap would be prose a model can misread or skip, so none of these gates could be shown to fail (Rule 7), and "a bot approval never counts" would be a request, not a guarantee.
- **Option B -- a new TypeScript review engine in `agent-core`:** strongest typing and one runtime. Rejected: a new build and `dist` surface and cross-package coupling for a prompt-level feature, editable criteria pulled into code (against Rule 8), and drift toward an ensemble-owned dispatcher that competes with Foreman (Rule 4).

**Rationale:** Option C is the best fit for this brownfield repo. It adds only the code that grades claims, keeps everything a maintainer or adopting team would tune in files they can edit, adds no dependency (Constitution §4) and no CI secret, vendors into Pi automatically through the existing require-closure bundler, and each gate can be mutation-proven using the harness that already exists.

**Decisions taken where the PRD left a choice** (each is editable policy, not a hidden constant):

| Decision | Value | Where it lives |
|---|---|---|
| Policy format | Fenced `ensemble-review-policy` JSON block in the root `REVIEW.md` (no new parser dependency) | REVIEW.md, read from the base commit |
| "Cannot vouch for" a push (AC-010-3, AC-014-2) | Commit is unvouched when its tree differs from the reviewed tree and it is not a remediation commit recorded in the review-state report, or it is a merge commit | `pr-review-scope.js`, `pr-review-approvals.js` |
| Slice threshold for large PRs (AC-018-1) | 1500 changed lines, configurable | policy block |
| Area rules vs policy keys | Policy keys are read from the **root** file only; area files carry guidance, and the more restrictive instruction wins when areas conflict (AC-001-2) | skill prose |
| First PR that introduces REVIEW.md | No base copy exists, so strict defaults apply (Low treated as Medium, cap 3, default sensitive set) | `pr-review-policy.js` |
| Verifier majority | Strict majority of the expected verifier count (2 of 3, 3 of 5) | `pr-review-votes.js` |

Each is a pure CommonJS module in `packages/development/lib/`, exposed as a JSON-in/JSON-out subcommand of the existing `pr-review-cli.js`, following the 82b6a138 precedent. - **Entry points (Rule 6):** every capability is reached through the one `pr-review-cycle` skill, which `fix-issue`, `implement-trd-beads` and `pr-merge` already invoke or will invoke (a new `MODE=gate` for `pr-merge`). YAML callers reference the skill only, never the CLI, as the existing parity tests require.
- **Recurrence (Rule 4):** nightly or weekly sweeps and daily eval runs are on-demand skills; a workflow template for the host repository is opt-in and scaffolded by init-project. Ensemble's own workflows gain no `schedule` trigger.

**Alternatives considered (user chose C):**

- **Option A -- prose-only skills and agents:** fewest files and fastest to ship. Rejected: the vote threshold, the tier floor, commit-bound approvals and the round cap would be prose a model can misread or skip, so none of these gates could be shown to fail (Rule 7), and "a bot approval never counts" would be a request, not a guarantee.
- **Option B -- a new TypeScript review engine in `agent-core`:** strongest typing and one runtime. Rejected: a new build and `dist` surface and cross-package coupling for a prompt-level feature, editable criteria pulled into code (against Rule 8), and drift toward an ensemble-owned dispatcher that competes with Foreman (Rule 4).

**Rationale:** Option C is the best fit for this brownfield repo. It adds only the code that grades claims, keeps everything a maintainer or adopting team would tune in files they can edit, adds no dependency (Constitution §4) and no CI secret, vendors into Pi automatically through the existing require-closure bundler, and each gate can be mutation-proven using the harness that already exists.

**Decisions taken where the PRD left a choice** (each is editable policy, not a hidden constant):

| Decision | Value | Where it lives |
|---|---|---|
| Policy format | Fenced `ensemble-review-policy` JSON block in the root `REVIEW.md` (no new parser dependency) | REVIEW.md, read from the base commit |
| "Cannot vouch for" a push (AC-010-3, AC-014-2) | Commit is unvouched when its tree differs from the reviewed tree and it is not a remediation commit recorded in the review-state report, or it is a merge commit | `pr-review-scope.js`, `pr-review-approvals.js` |
| Slice threshold for large PRs (AC-018-1) | 1500 changed lines, configurable | policy block |
| Area rules vs policy keys | Policy keys are read from the **root** file only; area files carry guidance, and the more restrictive instruction wins when areas conflict (AC-001-2) | skill prose |
| First PR that introduces REVIEW.md | No base copy exists, so strict defaults apply (Low treated as Medium, cap 3, default sensitive set) | `pr-review-policy.js` |
| Verifier majority | Strict majority of the expected verifier count (2 of 3, 3 of 5) | `pr-review-votes.js` |

Read-first: read the TRD, TRD Task section, PRD and PRD Requirement above before any work on this bead.


--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-024**: Default equivalence with no configuration
Default equivalence with no configuration Priority: Must | `[RISK: large refactor must be behavior-preserving]` A project that configures nothing behaves exactly as before: the same default adapters are selected and the same instruction sequences are produced.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-024-1: Given an unconfigured project | When refactored commands are generated | Then the default-toolchain equivalence snapshots match pre-refactor output
- AC-024-2: Given an unconfigured project | When a refactored command opens a change request | Then it produces the same default-host instruction sequence as before

--- TRD Context ---
### Alternatives Considered

| Option | Approach | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|---|
| A: Prose-only adapters | Adapter is a skill; the agent follows its prose and normalizes tool output itself | Smallest build; fully editable | Cannot route internal CLIs deterministically (REQ-016), cannot validate output (REQ-022), cannot deny at runtime (REQ-023); behavior varies per model |
| **B: Manifest plus runner (chosen)** | Adapter is a skill directory: `SKILL.md` (vocabulary and agent-facing prose) plus a declarative `adapter.yaml` (capability command templates, output mapping, allowlist, health check, detection signals, required env names). A core resolver library and `toolchain-cli` execute capabilities deterministically | Meets PRD (adapter is a skill), Rule 8 (editable without rebuild), Rule 5 (enforcement in code), REQ-016 (CLIs call the same library) | New resolver, runner, manifest schema and output-mapping engine to build and test |
| C: Executable plugin adapters | Separately packaged executables speaking a versioned JSON protocol | Arbitrary logic; strongest isolation | Contradicts the PRD's skills-as-contract decision; fails Rule 8; needs per-OS packaging and a protocol |

**Rationale:** B is the only option that makes every PRD guarantee a code-enforced property while keeping adapters user-editable data. The requester selected B at the architecture gate.

### Interpretations and Resolved Design Issues

- **I1: plain version control.** The PRD taxonomy has no plain `git` category, yet about 45 sources invoke it. Plain `git` operations (status, commit, push, log, diff, merge-base) are `vcs.*` capabilities of the `workflow` category, whose default adapter is `plain-git`; the `git-town` adapter extends it. Recommend a PRD refine pass to name this explicitly.
- **I2: ambiguity versus no signal (PRD REQ-009 AC-2 vs REQ-010 AC-2).** "No detectable signal" means no signal source exists at all (no remote, no marker files); the shipped default is used. "Ambiguous" means two or more installed adapters match, or a signal source exists (for example a remote URL) but matches no installed adapter; resolution fails explicitly in non-interactive runs and asks in interactive runs.
- **I3: AC-023-2 (governed boundary denies).** The runner is invoked through the shell tool, so a command that was not granted the shell tool cannot run any adapter; an adapter therefore cannot widen grants. The runner additionally denies any command outside the adapter's binary-plus-subcommand allowlist. Denial of raw shell commands typed by an agent outside the runner remains host-enforced (hooks on Claude Code; none in this repo for Pi, OpenCode or Codex); the lint (REQ-019) keeps commands from issuing raw tool calls. This residual is recorded in the Threat Model.
- **I4: confirmation session identity.** No stable session id is exposed uniformly across runtimes. TRD-017 begins with a spike that records which id each runtime exposes (`ENSEMBLE_SESSION_ID`, host session variables); the passive confirmation record is keyed by `(sessionKey, category, adapter, configHash)` and falls back to the run id when no session id exists.
- **I5: repo-local adapters are untrusted by default.** A cloned repository can ship `.ensemble/adapters/`. Repo-local adapters resolve in every mode (satisfying AC-007-3) but a non-interactive run additionally requires the adapter name in the user's `trustedRepoAdapters` list; an interactive run shows the adapter's allowlist at first-use confirmation.
- **I6: no new runtime dependency.** The output-mapping engine uses a small dotted-path projection (`$.a.b[0]`, `|` alternation for "array or object"), not a JSONPath library, because constitution section 4 requires approval for new dependencies.
- **I7: work-graph selection.** `work-graph` is its own category with default `auto`: use the work-graph capabilities of the resolved tracker adapter when its manifest provides them; otherwise use the built-in `work-graph-links-fallback` adapter (tracker dependency links, then plan order stated as not dependency-aware). One manifest may implement several categories.
- **I8: PRD BDD floor.** Fourteen PRD requirements (REQ-001, 002, 004, 005, 006, 009, 010, 012, 015, 018, 021, 022, 024, 025) have two ACs, below the command's three-scenario floor. The test tasks specify exactly one scenario per AC; recommend a PRD refine pass to add edge or error ACs.
- **I10: packaging.** `packages/development` depends only on `js-yaml` and its libraries require only siblings, so the resolver library, category contracts, default selection, schemas and tool inventory all ship inside `packages/development` (`lib/toolchain/` and `toolchain/`). A standalone plugin install and the Pi vendor bundle therefore contain everything; other packages call `toolchain-cli` through `TOOLCHAIN_CLI` rather than importing it.
- **I9: preflight is enforced in code.** `toolchain-cli run` refuses a side-effecting capability unless a passing preflight record exists for the supplied `--run-id`; the command prose cannot silently skip preflight.
Satisfies: REQ-024

Read-first: read the TRD, TRD Task section, PRD and PRD Requirement above before any work on this bead.


--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-003**: Evidence is bound to the exact head commit (Must) [RISK: a result for an old commit approving a new one would let unreviewed code land]
Evidence is bound to the exact head commit (Must) [RISK: a result for an old commit approving a new one would let unreviewed code land] A local-run result is valid only for the exact head commit it ran against, and the run itself executes against that exact commit and nothing else.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-003-1: Given a passing local run for commit A | When a new commit B is pushed to the PR | Then the PR no longer counts as approved until a local run passes for B
- AC-003-2: Given a passing local run for commit A | When the PR head is force-pushed to a different commit | Then the earlier result does not approve the new head
- AC-004-5: Given a published status | When its description is read | Then it carries the run record: the runner identity, a hash of the workflow set run, and a digest of the run log, and the head SHA is established by the commit the status is posted on.
- AC-004-6: Given a status whose run record does not match the PR's current head SHA or the repository's configured workflow set | When the merge flow evaluates it | Then the merge is refused and the mismatch is reported

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-004**: Evidence is published where branch protection can enforce it (Must) [RISK: verified -- the required checks on `dev` are pinned to the GitHub Actions app (app id 15368); a status posted with a personal token or the `gh` CLI is not from that app and will not satisfy them, leaving the PR unmergeable]
Evidence is published where branch protection can enforce it (Must) [RISK: verified -- the required checks on `dev` are pinned to the GitHub Actions app (app id 15368); a status posted with a personal token or the `gh` CLI is not from that app and will not satisfy them, leaving the PR unmergeable] The local run's result is published to GitHub as a status on the head commit, posted by a maintainer-owned GitHub App under a name that branch protection can pin to that app.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-003-1: Given a passing local run for commit A | When a new commit B is pushed to the PR | Then the PR no longer counts as approved until a local run passes for B
- AC-003-2: Given a passing local run for commit A | When the PR head is force-pushed to a different commit | Then the earlier result does not approve the new head
- AC-004-5: Given a published status | When its description is read | Then it carries the run record: the runner identity, a hash of the workflow set run, and a digest of the run log, and the head SHA is established by the commit the status is posted on.
- AC-004-6: Given a status whose run record does not match the PR's current head SHA or the repository's configured workflow set | When the merge flow evaluates it | Then the merge is refused and the mismatch is reported

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen approach (Option C):** A `local-ci-gate` skill owns the editable procedure; a small set of pure-JS helpers in `packages/development/lib/` owns only what must be unforgeable; `pr-merge.yaml` invokes the skill.

- `packages/development/skills/local-ci-gate/SKILL.md` is the single reusable procedure and owns everything a maintainer would plausibly tune (Constitution Rule 8): the order of the run, the messages, the bead wording, and how failures are explained.
- Pure-JS modules in `packages/development/lib/` own only what grades a claim or protects a boundary (Rules 7 and 8's enforcement exception): run-record verification, bot-vs-human classification, bead dedupe keys, approval-set config validation, and GitHub App credential handling. They make no network calls except the one module whose purpose is to post a status.
- `packages/git/commands/pr-merge.yaml` calls the skill at its existing Merge phase. It does not restate gate logic.
- The gate runs in-session in the maintainer's own process. There is no daemon, scheduler or background sweep (Rule 4; REQ-012).

**Alternatives considered (user chose C):**

- **Option A -- prose-only:** fewest files, but head-binding, run-record verification and human/bot classification would be prose a model can misread, and tests could only assert wording. Rejected: the PRD's core property is that evidence cannot be reused across commits.
- **Option B -- TypeScript runtime in agent-core:** strongest typing, but adds a build/dist surface and pulls editable criteria toward code against Rule 8. Rejected: the one place a real client is tempting (App JWT signing) needs only Node's built-in `crypto`.

**Dependency decision (user approved):** no new dependency. The App's RS256 JWT is signed with Node `crypto`; the REST calls use `fetch`. This avoids the constitution's new-dependency approval gate and keeps the signing path small and auditable.

**Rationale:** Option C matches repository precedent (TRD-2026-82b6a138), keeps editable behavior out of TypeScript, and is the minimum code that makes the trust properties testable.
Satisfies: REQ-003, REQ-004
Target File: packages/development/lib/local-ci-record.js
Actions:

Implementation AC:
- [ ] Given a runner identity, a workflow set and a log, when `buildRecord` runs, then it returns a description of at most 100 characters of the fixed form `ci-local <8-hex> | set:<8-hex> | log:<12-hex>` where the first field is the short git blob hash of the repository's `scripts/ci-local.js` at the PR head, with the log as a digest and never the log text and with the head SHA left implicit because the status is posted on that commit
- [ ] Given a published description, when `parseRecord` runs, then it round-trips the same fields and rejects a malformed, over-length or truncated string
- [ ] Given a record, the PR's current head SHA, the commit the status was posted on, and the configured workflow set, when `verifyRecord` runs, then it passes only when the status's commit equals the head SHA and the set hash recomputed from configuration equals `set:`
- [ ] Given a status posted on commit A and a PR now at commit B, when it runs, then it returns `ok:false` with `headMismatch` naming both SHAs
- [ ] Given a configured workflow set that has changed since the status was posted, when it runs, then it returns `ok:false` with `setMismatch` naming the difference

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-014-3: Given a user-owned strategy | When the workflow is packaged | Then it is represented in an editable prompt, skill, or behavior artifact rather than requiring a code rebuild to specialize it

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen: Option C — hardened in-session stage composition with a dedicated atomic run-index store.**

`new-feature` is authored the same way every other product command in this repo is authored: a single orchestrating skill (`packages/development/commands/new-feature.yaml`, generated to runtime-specific prompts exactly like `fix-issue.yaml`) that executes each stage's existing skill body in-session — the same mechanism that loaded `ensemble-refine-prd`'s content into this session and had the agent execute its Phases directly. This is forced, not merely preferred: Pi's `ExtensionAPI` has no completion/invoke primitive that would let an extension programmatically run another skill and get its result back (confirmed — no `pi.invokeCommand` or equivalent exists); the only code-level "run a skill" mechanism, `createAgentPort()`, spawns a bounded, disposable `omp -p --no-session --no-extensions` subprocess in an isolated worktree, and does not fit a long-lived, project-resident workflow whose PRD/TRD stages use the interactive `--collab` review server.

What is new, and is the one piece of real infrastructure this TRD adds: a `RunIndexStore` (`packages/agent-core/src/new-feature/run-index.ts`) built on the one proven concurrency-safe pattern in this repo — `session.js`'s temp-file-then-`renameSync` atomic write plus `expectedRevision`/409-style optimistic concurrency — rather than `ProposalStore`'s plain `writeFileSync` (no atomicity, no lock, not adequate for PRD AC-005-3's fail-closed-on-malformed-index requirement). Runs are stored at `.ensemble/new-feature/<run-id>.json`, mirroring `ProposalStore`'s `.ensemble/proposals/<ref>.json` convention (also excluded from `tree-baseline.ts` drift detection, so this is consistent runtime-owned state, not a project-source mutation).

### Alternatives considered

| Option | Summary | Why not chosen |
|---|---|---|
| A — Plain JSON checkpoint | Same in-session composition, but checkpoints are a single `writeFileSync`, no atomicity/locking. | Fastest to build, but a crash mid-write can corrupt the run index, which directly violates AC-005-3's "fail closed with a recoverable diagnostic" requirement — the repo's own `ProposalStore` already demonstrates this gap is real, not hypothetical. |
| B — Subprocess-dispatched stages | New orchestrator module dispatches every stage as a bounded `createAgentPort()` subprocess; advances the run index only after subprocess exit 0 + artifact-on-disk confirmation. | Most rigorous completion signal (a real process boundary instead of self-reported bookkeeping), but substantially more build effort, and does not fit the interactive `--collab` review-server stages `create-prd`/`refine-prd` already use — those are long-lived, human-attended HTTP sessions, not bounded one-shot subprocess work, and would need bespoke carve-out handling under this option. |
| **C — Hardened in-session composition** *(chosen)* | In-session stage execution (like every existing product command), backed by a dedicated atomic `RunIndexStore`. | Reuses 100% of the existing skill-composition and `ask_user`-approval infrastructure (including the `--collab` review server, which needs no special-casing), while fixing Option A's one real correctness gap with the repo's one proven atomic-write pattern. Matches user-confirmed direction. |

### Honest trust-boundary note

Because stage execution stays in-session (per Option C), the approval gates implemented by TRD-014/TRD-017/TRD-019 are enforced by the orchestrating skill's own conditional logic checking `RunIndexStore`-persisted approval fields before it issues an implementation or `gh pr create` tool call — not by a separate runtime authorization chokepoint like `agent-core`'s `MutationGuard` (which exists elsewhere in this repo, gating CQRS-registered commands, but `new-feature`'s mutating actions are ordinary skill-level tool calls, same as `fix-issue`'s own gated PR-creation step, not CQRS commands). This is the same trust boundary every existing Ensemble product command already operates under. Building a `MutationGuard`-equivalent chokepoint for skill-level tool calls is a materially larger investment this PRD does not request and no other product command has; REQ-014's "runtime authority" is satisfied here by making the check a required precondition over persisted, validated store state rather than over prompt claims — which is what AC-014-2 actually asks for — not by inventing a new enforcement subsystem.

title: [trd:trd-2026-4dec59b8-local-ci-pr-approval:task:TRD-014] - [ ] **TRD-014** gh-based status publisher (`local-ci-status.js`) (4h)
description:
## Task: TRD-014
## References
TRD: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-4dec59b8-local-ci-pr-approval.md
TRD Task: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-4dec59b8-local-ci-pr-approval.md#trd-014
PRD: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-4dec59b8-local-ci-pr-approval.md
PRD Requirement: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-4dec59b8-local-ci-pr-approval.md#req-004
PRD Requirement: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-4dec59b8-local-ci-pr-approval.md#req-010
PRD ACs: AC-004-1, AC-004-2, AC-004-7, AC-010-2
Parent Epic: [trd:trd-2026-4dec59b8-local-ci-pr-approval]
Read-first: read the TRD, TRD Task section, PRD and PRD Requirement above before any work on this bead.


--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-004**: Evidence is published where the merge flow and branch protection can see it (Must) [RISK: a status not bound to the head commit, or accepted without a verifiable run record, would let unverified work land; trust is honest-actor and the limit is stated in "Trust model and limits"]
Evidence is published where the merge flow and branch protection can see it (Must) [RISK: a status not bound to the head commit, or accepted without a verifiable run record, would let unverified work land; trust is honest-actor and the limit is stated in "Trust model and limits"] The local run's result is published to GitHub as a commit status on the head commit under an agreed name, posted with the maintainer's own `gh` login, so the merge flow can verify it and branch protection can require it by name.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-004-1: Given a passing local run | When its result is published | Then the head commit shows a success status under the agreed name, posted with the maintainer's `gh` login
- AC-004-2: Given a failing local run | When its result is published | Then the head commit shows a failure status and the PR cannot be merged by the supported flow
- AC-004-7: Given there is no `gh` login or posting the status fails | When a local run is requested | Then the run may execute but publishes nothing, reports that it cannot attest, and the merge is refused
- AC-010-2: Given the local run publishes a status or log | When the output is inspected | Then it contains no token or secret value

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-010**: Local run must not leak secrets (Must)
Local run must not leak secrets (Must) Running CI locally never commits, publishes or logs credentials.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-004-1: Given a passing local run | When its result is published | Then the head commit shows a success status under the agreed name, posted with the maintainer's `gh` login
- AC-004-2: Given a failing local run | When its result is published | Then the head commit shows a failure status and the PR cannot be merged by the supported flow
- AC-004-7: Given there is no `gh` login or posting the status fails | When a local run is requested | Then the run may execute but publishes nothing, reports that it cannot attest, and the merge is refused
- AC-010-2: Given the local run publishes a status or log | When the output is inspected | Then it contains no token or secret value

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen approach (Option C):** A `local-ci-gate` skill owns the editable procedure; a small set of pure-JS helpers in `packages/development/lib/` owns only what must be unforgeable; `pr-merge.yaml` invokes the skill.

- `packages/development/skills/local-ci-gate/SKILL.md` is the single reusable procedure and owns everything a maintainer would plausibly tune (Constitution Rule 8): the order of the run, the messages, the bead wording, and how failures are explained.
- Pure-JS modules in `packages/development/lib/` own only what grades a claim or protects a boundary (Rules 7 and 8's enforcement exception): run-record verification, bot-vs-human classification, bead dedupe keys, approval-set config validation, and status publishing through `gh`. They make no network calls except the one module whose purpose is to post a status.
- `packages/git/commands/pr-merge.yaml` calls the skill at its existing Merge phase. It does not restate gate logic.
- The gate runs in-session in the maintainer's own process. There is no daemon, scheduler or background sweep (Rule 4; REQ-012).

**Alternatives considered (user chose C):**

- **Option A -- prose-only:** fewest files, but head-binding, run-record verification and human/bot classification would be prose a model can misread, and tests could only assert wording. Rejected: the PRD's core property is that evidence cannot be reused across commits.
- **Option B -- TypeScript runtime in agent-core:** strongest typing, but adds a build/dist surface and pulls editable criteria toward code against Rule 8. Rejected: the one place a real client is tempting (posting a status) is a single `gh api` call.

**Dependency decision (user approved):** no new dependency. The status is posted by calling the maintainer's own `gh` CLI with an argv array (never a shell string), so there is no HTTP client, no JWT signing and no key handling. **Trust decision (user, 2026-10-22): no GitHub App; trust is honest-actor** (see Security design).

**Rationale:** Option C matches repository precedent (TRD-2026-82b6a138), keeps editable behavior out of TypeScript, and is the minimum code that makes the trust properties testable.
Satisfies: REQ-004, REQ-010
Target File: packages/development/lib/local-ci-status.js
Actions:

Implementation AC:
- [ ] Given a repository `owner/repo`, a 40-hex head SHA, a state, a context and a run-record description, when `postStatus` runs, then it calls `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/statuses/<sha>` with an argv array (`execFile`-style, no shell, no string concatenation into a command line) carrying `state`, `context` and `description` as separate fields, after validating the SHA is exactly 40 hex characters and `owner/repo` matches `^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$`
- [ ] Given a passing or failing gate result, when `postStatus` runs, then it posts `success` or `failure` respectively and rejects any other state before making a call
- [ ] Given `gh` is not logged in (`gh auth status` exits non-zero) or `gh` is not installed, when `postStatus` runs, then it posts nothing and returns `{published:false, reason:'cannot attest'}` and the caller refuses the merge (AC-004-7)
- [ ] Given `gh api` exits non-zero, times out, or returns a response that is not parseable JSON or whose `state` or commit does not match what was posted, when `postStatus` runs, then it returns `{published:false, reason:'post failed'}` with a redacted message and never reports success
- [ ] Given a description longer than 100 characters (the bound TRD-003 enforces), when `postStatus` runs, then it is rejected before any call is made
- [ ] Given any thrown error, stderr text or response containing a token-shaped string (`ghp_`, `gho_`, `ghs_`, `ghu_`, `ghr_`, `github_pat_`) or the value of `GH_TOKEN` or `GITHUB_TOKEN`, when output is produced, then `redact` has removed it from every returned or logged string
- [ ] Given the module is inspected, when it runs, then it never invokes `gh auth token` or `gh auth status --show-token`, never reads or writes a token file, and never places a token in a status, log, bead or argument list
Dependencies: TRD-003

title: Support multiple change requests per Overview approval in refinement-review
description:
## Goal

The Overview tab's approval flow (`packages/core/lib/refinement-review`) currently supports exactly one live decision per session. `session.approval` is a single object (`{decision, author, note, decidedAt}`), and `POST /api/approval` in `server.js` overwrites it outright — the handler comment says so directly: "A later decision overwrites the earlier one."

That means a second "Request changes" submission silently discards the first one's note and author. On a long-lived, multi-reviewer session (`--long-lived`, `--reviewers N`) this is a real loss: two different stakeholders — or the same one, twice, as understanding evolves — can each want to log a distinct change request against the Overview, and only the most recent survives.

Change the model so a session can accumulate multiple change requests instead of clobbering them.

## Current Behavior (for reference)

- `packages/core/lib/refinement-review/session.js`: `session.approval` — singular, nullable object; `validateSession` shape-checks it but never treats it as a list.
- `packages/core/lib/refinement-review/server.js` (`POST /api/approval`): `s.approval = { decision, author, note, decidedAt }` — unconditional overwrite, routed through `mutate()` so it serializes with question/comment writes and broadcasts over SSE.
- `packages/core/lib/refinement-review/ui/app.js` + `ui/index.html`: single note textarea, single Approve / Request Changes button pair, renders only `state.session.approval` (the one current decision) in `#rr-approval-state`.
- The completion artifact (`/api/complete` handler) copies `finalSession.approval || null` verbatim into the written artifact.

## Proposed Change

- Replace (or augment) `session.approval` with `session.approvals: []` — an append-only list of `{id, decision, author, note, decidedAt}` entries. Keep `decision` semantics per-entry (`approved` | `changes-requested`); do not collapse multiple change requests into one.
- `POST /api/approval` appends a new entry instead of overwriting. Define what "current status" means for the summary badge once multiple entries exist (e.g. most recent entry's `decision`, or "approved" only when the latest entry is `approved` and no unresolved change request postdates it) — needs an explicit decision, not an implicit one.
- Backward compatibility: existing session files and completion artifacts on disk have the old singular `session.approval` shape. Decide migration path (read-time upcast to a one-element `approvals` array vs. dual-write during a transition window) and update `validateSession` accordingly.
- UI: render the full list of change requests (author, note, timestamp) on the Overview tab, not just the latest — this is the visible product behavior the bead title describes. Multiple pending change requests should be individually distinguishable, not merged.
- Completion artifact shape changes accordingly (`approvals: [...]` instead of `approval: {...}|null`) — audit any downstream consumer of the artifact (Phase 3 Enhancement / Feedback Integration in `refine-prd`/`refine-trd`) that currently reads `finalSession.approval`.

## Acceptance

1. Two sequential `POST /api/approval` calls with `decision: 'changes-requested'` from different authors both persist — neither note is lost — and both are visible on the Overview tab.
2. The same author submitting a second change request (e.g., refining their first note) also persists as a distinct entry rather than overwriting the first.
3. `validateSession` accepts sessions written before this change (singular `approval`) without erroring, and upcasts them consistently.
4. The completion artifact written by `/api/complete` includes the full approval/change-request history, not just the latest entry.
5. Existing server.test.js coverage for `/api/approval` is updated for the new shape; add a test asserting the second submission does not clobber the first.

## Out of Scope

- Any UI for resolving/dismissing an individual change request (mirrors comment resolution, but not requested here — flag as a natural follow-up, don't build it).
- Changing the single-reviewer (non `--long-lived`, non `--reviewers`) approval UX beyond supporting multiple entries.
