title: [trd:trd-2026-d6bbf322-new-feature-workflow:task:TRD-002] - [ ] **TRD-002**: Implement `RunIndexStore` core (`createRun`, `findActive`, `resolveByArtifact`, `mutate`) on atomic-write + optimistic concurrency (6h)
description:
## Task: TRD-002
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-d6bbf322-new-feature-workflow.md#trd-002
PRD Reference: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-d6bbf322-new-feature-workflow.md#req-005

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-005**: Persist checkpoints and identify the active run from a project-local index
Persist checkpoints and identify the active run from a project-local index Priority: Must | Complexity: Medium

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-005-1: Given any stage reaches a success | When the workflow records the checkpoint | Then a project-local run index identifies the active run, exact current stage, stage outcome, and available PRD, TRD, and bead references
- AC-005-2: Given the user starts or resumes the workflow in a later session | When the project index is valid | Then the workflow discovers the active run and stage from that index without requiring prior chat history
- AC-005-3: Given the project index is absent | When the workflow tries to resume | Then it fails closed with a recoverable diagnostic instead of guessing from files or advancing the run

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen: Option C — hardened in-session stage composition with a dedicated atomic run-index store.**

`new-feature` is authored the same way every other product command in this repo is authored: a single orchestrating skill (`packages/development/commands/new-feature.yaml`, generated to runtime-specific prompts exactly like `fix-issue.yaml`) that executes each stage's existing skill body in-session — the same mechanism that loaded `ensemble-refine-prd`'s content into this session and had the agent execute its Phases directly. This is forced, not merely preferred: Pi's `ExtensionAPI` has no completion/invoke primitive that would let an extension programmatically run another skill and get its result back (confirmed — no `pi.invokeCommand` or equivalent exists); the only code-level "run a skill" mechanism, `createAgentPort()`, spawns a bounded, disposable `omp -p --no-session --no-extensions` subprocess in an isolated worktree, and does not fit a long-lived, project-resident workflow whose PRD/TRD stages use the interactive `--collab` review server.

What is new, and is the one piece of real infrastructure this TRD adds: a `RunIndexStore` (`packages/agent-core/src/new-feature/run-index.ts`) built on the one proven concurrency-safe pattern in this repo — `session.js`'s temp-file-then-`renameSync` atomic write plus `expectedRevision`/409-style optimistic concurrency — rather than `ProposalStore`'s plain `writeFileSync` (no atomicity, no lock, not adequate for PRD AC-005-3's fail-closed-on-malformed-index requirement). Runs are stored at `.ensemble/new-feature/<run-id>.json`, mirroring `ProposalStore`'s `.ensemble/proposals/<ref>.json` convention (also excluded from `tree-baseline.ts` drift detection, so this is consistent runtime-owned state, not a project-source mutation).

### Alternatives considered

| Option | Summary | Why not chosen |
|---|---|---|
| A — Plain JSON checkpoint | Same in-session composition, but checkpoints are a single `writeFileSync`, no atomicity/locking. | Fastest to build, but a crash mid-write can corrupt the run index, which directly violates AC-005-3's "fail closed with a recoverable diagnostic" requirement — the repo's own `ProposalStore` already demonstrates this gap is real, not hypothetical. |
| B — Subprocess-dispatched stages | New orchestrator module dispatches every stage as a bounded `createAgentPort()` subprocess; advances the run index only after subprocess exit 0 + artifact-on-disk confirmation. | Most rigorous completion signal (a real process boundary instead of self-reported bookkeeping), but substantially more build effort, and does not fit the interactive `--collab` review-server stages `create-prd`/`refine-prd` already use — those are long-lived, human-attended HTTP sessions, not bounded one-shot subprocess work, and would need bespoke carve-out handling under this option. |
| **C — Hardened in-session composition** *(chosen)* | In-session stage execution (like every existing product command), backed by a dedicated atomic `RunIndexStore`. | Reuses 100% of the existing skill-composition and `ask_user`-approval infrastructure (including the `--collab` review server, which needs no special-casing), while fixing Option A's one real correctness gap with the repo's one proven atomic-write pattern. Matches user-confirmed direction. |

### Honest trust-boundary note

Because stage execution stays in-session (per Option C), the approval gates implemented by TRD-014/TRD-017/TRD-019 are enforced by the orchestrating skill's own conditional logic checking `RunIndexStore`-persisted approval fields before it issues an implementation or `gh pr create` tool call — not by a separate runtime authorization chokepoint like `agent-core`'s `MutationGuard` (which exists elsewhere in this repo, gating CQRS-registered commands, but `new-feature`'s mutating actions are ordinary skill-level tool calls, same as `fix-issue`'s own gated PR-creation step, not CQRS commands). This is the same trust boundary every existing Ensemble product command already operates under. Building a `MutationGuard`-equivalent chokepoint for skill-level tool calls is a materially larger investment this PRD does not request and no other product command has; REQ-014's "runtime authority" is satisfied here by making the check a required precondition over persisted, validated store state rather than over prompt claims — which is what AC-014-2 actually asks for — not by inventing a new enforcement subsystem.
Satisfies: REQ-005
PRD ACs: AC-005-1, AC-005-2, AC-005-3
Target File: packages/agent-core/src/new-feature/run-index.ts
Actions:
1. Implement `writeRunAtomic(filePath, value)` by porting `session.js`'s temp-file-then-`renameSync` pattern (`mkdirSync` recursive, `.${basename}.${pid}.${Date.now()}.tmp`, `fsyncSync` before rename).
2. Implement `mutate(runId, expectedRevision, updater)`: load current record, reject a mismatched `expectedRevision` with a typed `REVISION_CONFLICT` (`{ code: "REVISION_CONFLICT", status: 409, currentRevision }`), else apply `updater`, bump `revision` by 1, `updatedAt = now()`, write atomically.
3. Implement `findActive(projectRoot)`: read every `.ensemble/new-feature/*.json` under `projectRoot`, return the one record (if any) whose `status` is `"active"` or `"paused"`.
4. Implement `resolveByArtifact(projectRoot, path)`: scan indexed runs' `artifacts[]` for an exact path match; return the owning `RunRecord` or `undefined`.
5. On a malformed or internally inconsistent run file (JSON parse failure, missing required field, `stage` not in the fixed enum), throw a typed `RUN_INDEX_CORRUPT` error carrying the file path and reason — never silently skip or fall back to directory-scan guessing.
Implementation AC:
- [ ] Given two `mutate()` calls against the same `runId` race with the same stale `expectedRevision`, when the second call applies, then it is rejected with `REVISION_CONFLICT` and the first writer's change is preserved.
- [ ] Given a run file is truncated or has a non-enum `stage` value, when `findActive`/`resolveByArtifact` reads it, then a typed `RUN_INDEX_CORRUPT` error is thrown rather than the file being skipped or guessed at.
- [ ] Given a process crash simulated by killing the writer between `openSync` and `renameSync`, when the store is reopened, then the prior valid run file is intact (the `.tmp` file, if any, is orphaned but never renamed over the real file).
Dependencies: TRD-001
close_reason: Implemented: packages/agent-core/src/new-feature/run-index.ts (writeRunAtomic, mutate, findActive, resolveByArtifact, createRun). Ported session.js's atomic-write pattern. Typechecks clean.

description:
## Test Task: TRD-024-TEST
## References
TRD: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-8d825f54-tool-abstraction-layer.md
TRD Task: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-8d825f54-tool-abstraction-layer.md#trd-024-test

PRD ACs: AC-020-1
Verifies Task: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-8d825f54-tool-abstraction-layer.md#trd-024
Parent Epic: [trd:trd-2026-8d825f54-tool-abstraction-layer]
Read-first: read the TRD, TRD Task section, PRD and PRD Requirement above before any work on this bead.


--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-020**: Execution layer follows the resolved tracker
Execution layer follows the resolved tracker Priority: Must | `[RISK: amends PRD-2026-b6939c7c REQ-015; affects ready-work scheduling in implementation commands]` The earlier rule that the default tracker is always the sole dependency-graph and ready-work engine is replaced. Ready-work and dependency ordering come from the resolved tracker adapter's work-graph capabilities, or from the documented fallback when those are absent. The fallback uses the tracker's own issue links when it has them; otherwise tasks run in plan order and the output states that ordering is not dependency-aware. Cross-Cutting

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-020-1: Given the default tracker adapter | When implementation commands run | Then ready-work comes from its work-graph capabilities as today

--- TRD Context ---
### Alternatives Considered

| Option | Approach | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|---|
| A: Prose-only adapters | Adapter is a skill; the agent follows its prose and normalizes tool output itself | Smallest build; fully editable | Cannot route internal CLIs deterministically (REQ-016), cannot validate output (REQ-022), cannot deny at runtime (REQ-023); behavior varies per model |
| **B: Manifest plus runner (chosen)** | Adapter is a skill directory: `SKILL.md` (vocabulary and agent-facing prose) plus a declarative `adapter.yaml` (capability command templates, output mapping, allowlist, health check, detection signals, required env names). A core resolver library and `toolchain-cli` execute capabilities deterministically | Meets PRD (adapter is a skill), Rule 8 (editable without rebuild), Rule 5 (enforcement in code), REQ-016 (CLIs call the same library) | New resolver, runner, manifest schema and output-mapping engine to build and test |
| C: Executable plugin adapters | Separately packaged executables speaking a versioned JSON protocol | Arbitrary logic; strongest isolation | Contradicts the PRD's skills-as-contract decision; fails Rule 8; needs per-OS packaging and a protocol |

**Rationale:** B is the only option that makes every PRD guarantee a code-enforced property while keeping adapters user-editable data. The requester selected B at the architecture gate.

### Interpretations and Resolved Design Issues

- **I1: plain version control.** The PRD taxonomy has no plain `git` category, yet about 45 sources invoke it. Plain `git` operations (status, commit, push, log, diff, merge-base) are `vcs.*` capabilities of the `workflow` category, whose default adapter is `plain-git`; the `git-town` adapter extends it. Recommend a PRD refine pass to name this explicitly.
- **I2: ambiguity versus no signal (PRD REQ-009 AC-2 vs REQ-010 AC-2).** "No detectable signal" means no signal source exists at all (no remote, no marker files); the shipped default is used. "Ambiguous" means two or more installed adapters match, or a signal source exists (for example a remote URL) but matches no installed adapter; resolution fails explicitly in non-interactive runs and asks in interactive runs.
- **I3: AC-023-2 (governed boundary denies).** The runner is invoked through the shell tool, so a command that was not granted the shell tool cannot run any adapter; an adapter therefore cannot widen grants. The runner additionally denies any command outside the adapter's binary-plus-subcommand allowlist. Denial of raw shell commands typed by an agent outside the runner remains host-enforced (hooks on Claude Code; none in this repo for Pi, OpenCode or Codex); the lint (REQ-019) keeps commands from issuing raw tool calls. This residual is recorded in the Threat Model.
- **I4: confirmation session identity.** No stable session id is exposed uniformly across runtimes. TRD-017 begins with a spike that records which id each runtime exposes (`ENSEMBLE_SESSION_ID`, host session variables); the passive confirmation record is keyed by `(sessionKey, category, adapter, configHash)` and falls back to the run id when no session id exists.
- **I5: repo-local adapters are untrusted by default.** A cloned repository can ship `.ensemble/adapters/`. Repo-local adapters resolve in every mode (satisfying AC-007-3) but a non-interactive run additionally requires the adapter name in the user's `trustedRepoAdapters` list; an interactive run shows the adapter's allowlist at first-use confirmation.
- **I6: no new runtime dependency.** The output-mapping engine uses a small dotted-path projection (`$.a.b[0]`, `|` alternation for "array or object"), not a JSONPath library, because constitution section 4 requires approval for new dependencies.
- **I7: work-graph selection.** `work-graph` is its own category with default `auto`: use the work-graph capabilities of the resolved tracker adapter when its manifest provides them; otherwise use the built-in `work-graph-links-fallback` adapter (tracker dependency links, then plan order stated as not dependency-aware). One manifest may implement several categories.
- **I8: PRD BDD floor.** Fourteen PRD requirements (REQ-001, 002, 004, 005, 006, 009, 010, 012, 015, 018, 021, 022, 024, 025) have two ACs, below the command's three-scenario floor. The test tasks specify exactly one scenario per AC; recommend a PRD refine pass to add edge or error ACs.
- **I10: packaging.** `packages/development` depends only on `js-yaml` and its libraries require only siblings, so the resolver library, category contracts, default selection, schemas and tool inventory all ship inside `packages/development` (`lib/toolchain/` and `toolchain/`). A standalone plugin install and the Pi vendor bundle therefore contain everything; other packages call `toolchain-cli` through `TOOLCHAIN_CLI` rather than importing it.
- **I9: preflight is enforced in code.** `toolchain-cli run` refuses a side-effecting capability unless a passing preflight record exists for the supplied `--run-id`; the command prose cannot silently skip preflight.
Verifies: TRD-024
Satisfies: REQ-020
PRD ACs Proven: AC-020-1
Proof of requirement: 
Target Files: 
Actions:

Test AC:
- [ ] Scenario: Default adapter ready-work from work-graph -- Given the default tracker adapter, When implementation commands run, Then ready-work comes from its work-graph capabilities as today

title: [trd:trd-2026-70e784f2-code-review-process:task:TRD-024] - [ ] **TRD-024** Approval evaluator (`pr-review-approvals.js`) (6h)
description:
## Task: TRD-024
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-70e784f2-code-review-process.md#trd-024
PRD Reference: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-70e784f2-code-review-process.md#req-014

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-014**: Human approval means a person, on a specific commit (Must) [RISK: weak approval semantics let unreviewed code merge]
Human approval means a person, on a specific commit (Must) [RISK: weak approval semantics let unreviewed code merge] An approval is a person's decision about one commit, and an automated approval never fills a human slot.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-014-1: Given an approval is recorded by an agent or automated account | When approval requirements are evaluated | Then it does not count toward any required human approval; an account is automated if the repository's configured bot/agent list names it or the platform marks it as a bot
- AC-014-2: Given an approval was given | When new commits are pushed that the system cannot vouch for | Then the approval no longer counts and approval is requested again
- AC-014-3: Given an agent authored a PR on a person's instruction | When approvals are counted | Then that person counts as one of the required reviewers, as if they had written the code themselves
- AC-014-4: Given a High-tier PR | When approvals are counted | Then two distinct people are required
- AC-014-5: Given the Low-tier waiver has been enabled (REQ-013) | When a PR is evaluated | Then the waiver applies only to PRs authored by repository maintainers; every other author's Low PR still requires one human approval

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen approach (Option C):** extend the pattern TRD-2026-82b6a138 established: **editable behavior in skills, agents and markdown; a small set of pure, deterministic libraries for what must not be self-certified by a model.**

- **User-owned (Constitution Rule 8), prose or data a maintainer edits without a toolchain:** per-area rules (`REVIEW.md` files), the policy block inside the root `REVIEW.md` (round cap, depth table, bot and maintainer logins, sensitive and High paths, Low-waiver state), severity definitions, reviewer, verifier, classifier and security-lane prompts, the PR template, the sweep and explainer procedures. All of it is read from the **target branch**, never from the PR head (REQ-024).
- **Enforcement (Rules 5 and 7), code that grades a model's claim:** vote tally, tier assignment with its sensitive-path floor and Low-waiver evidence, approval evaluation bound to a commit, the merge gate, round-cap derivation, repeat suppression, delta-range selection, depth bounds, slice coverage, metrics and eval scoring. Each is a pure CommonJS module in `packages/development/lib/`, exposed as a JSON-in/JSON-out subcommand of the existing `pr-review-cli.js`, following the 82b6a138 precedent. None performs network I/O or holds a timer.
- **Entry points (Rule 6):** every capability is reached through the one `pr-review-cycle` skill, which `fix-issue`, `implement-trd-beads` and `pr-merge` already invoke or will invoke (a new `MODE=gate` for `pr-merge`). YAML callers reference the skill only, never the CLI, as the existing parity tests require.
- **Recurrence (Rule 4):** nightly or weekly sweeps and daily eval runs are on-demand skills; a workflow template for the host repository is opt-in and scaffolded by init-project. Ensemble's own workflows gain no `schedule` trigger.

**Alternatives considered (user chose C):**

- **Option A -- prose-only skills and agents:** fewest files and fastest to ship. Rejected: the vote threshold, the tier floor, commit-bound approvals and the round cap would be prose a model can misread or skip, so none of these gates could be shown to fail (Rule 7), and "a bot approval never counts" would be a request, not a guarantee.
- **Option B -- a new TypeScript review engine in `agent-core`:** strongest typing and one runtime. Rejected: a new build and `dist` surface and cross-package coupling for a prompt-level feature, editable criteria pulled into code (against Rule 8), and drift toward an ensemble-owned dispatcher that competes with Foreman (Rule 4).

**Rationale:** Option C is the best fit for this brownfield repo. It adds only the code that grades claims, keeps everything a maintainer or adopting team would tune in files they can edit, adds no dependency (Constitution §4) and no CI secret, vendors into Pi automatically through the existing require-closure bundler, and each gate can be mutation-proven using the harness that already exists.

**Decisions taken where the PRD left a choice** (each is editable policy, not a hidden constant):

| Decision | Value | Where it lives |
|---|---|---|
| Policy format | Fenced `ensemble-review-policy` JSON block in the root `REVIEW.md` (no new parser dependency) | REVIEW.md, read from the base commit |
| "Cannot vouch for" a push (AC-010-3, AC-014-2) | Commit is unvouched when its tree differs from the reviewed tree and it is not a remediation commit recorded in the review-state report, or it is a merge commit | `pr-review-scope.js`, `pr-review-approvals.js` |
| Slice threshold for large PRs (AC-018-1) | 1500 changed lines, configurable | policy block |
| Area rules vs policy keys | Policy keys are read from the **root** file only; area files carry guidance, and the more restrictive instruction wins when areas conflict (AC-001-2) | skill prose |
| First PR that introduces REVIEW.md | No base copy exists, so strict defaults apply (Low treated as Medium, cap 3, default sensitive set) | `pr-review-policy.js` |
| Verifier majority | Strict majority of the expected verifier count (2 of 3, 3 of 5) | `pr-review-votes.js` |
Satisfies: REQ-014
PRD ACs: AC-014-1, AC-014-2, AC-014-3, AC-014-4, AC-014-5
Target File: 
Actions:

Implementation AC:
- [ ] Given reviews, a head SHA and tree, a tier and the policy bot list, when `evaluateApprovals` runs, then approvals by a configured bot login or a platform-marked bot are returned in `ignored[]` with reason `automated` and never count
- [ ] Given an approval bound to a commit other than the head whose tree differs from the head tree, when it runs, then it no longer counts (reason `stale-commit`); an approval whose commit tree equals the head tree still counts
- [ ] Given an agent-authored PR with a `directedBy` person, when it runs, then that person fills one required human slot; Medium needs one human, High two distinct people, and an effective-Low PR needs none
- [ ] Given the Low waiver is enabled, when the author is not a repository maintainer, then one human is still required

title: policy.mode: propose does not gate mutations on the continuation path (live repro)
description:
REPRODUCED LIVE, 2026-09-28, first real end-to-end run of the loop.

Repo: ~/Development/Sunstone/loop-trial, using the PRODUCTION
.ensemble/behaviors/fix-failing-test/behavior.yaml (policy.mode: propose),
with only test_command and mutation_classes changed.

WHAT HAPPENED
A deliberately broken `add(a,b) { return a - b; }` was detected, repaired to
`a + b` ON DISK, and verified -- with no human approval step anywhere.
`mode: propose` is supposed to make MutationGuard.authorize() deny every
direct mutation and require a human to apply the proposal instead.

  git diff src/math.js  ->  -  return a - b;
                            +  return a + b;

  runtime-log: {"kind":"verification","status":"passed","detail":"2 passed, 2 total"}
  no approval was requested; nothing was left for a human to apply.

WHY
The continuation path (pi.sendUserMessage injects a turn, the MODEL applies
the change with its own edit calls) never passes a write through
MutationGuard, so `mode` is not consulted at all. behavior.yaml's own comment
documents this and says the continuation path is "what fires in practice" --
the live run confirms it: the governed dispatch produced no candidate
("working tree changed while the provider ran (src/math.js) -- cannot
attribute, nothing reverted") while the continuation had already applied the
fix.

WHY THIS IS P1
`propose` was adopted (2026-09-25) BECAUSE a live run applied an uncommitted,
unreviewed change to packages/agent-core/src/behavior/outbox.ts. The setting
chosen to prevent that does not prevent it. A mode that claims to gate and
does not is worse than no mode: it buys false confidence in exactly the
situation it was introduced to make safe.

NOT the same as br-o355 (grant scoping to the execution window), though they
share the continuation-path root cause. Cross-referenced.

OPTIONS
(a) Route continuation-applied writes through MutationGuard before they land.
(b) Under `propose`, hold the fix turn's writes and present them for approval
    instead of letting them land (the write boundary already reverts and
    quarantines protected paths -- this is the same mechanism, widened).
(c) Refuse to dispatch a `propose` behavior down the continuation path at all,
    so the mode's guarantee is honest even if narrower.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #98 (squashed to dev as fba80cb). Under policy.mode: propose a verified-passing fix is now reverted and held for /ensemble-approve rather than landing unreviewed. Mutation-tested three ways (gate disabled -> gating test fails; gate applied to every mode -> 5 fail including the auto control; hold loses contents -> re-apply assertion fails). Verified live twice on the merged bundle: {"status":"passed","heldForApproval":["1"]} with src/math.js reverted and git status clean.

comments.author: ldangelo
comments.text: Fixed in e93716e, PR open against dev. Verified live: {"status":"passed","heldForApproval":["1"]} with src/math.js reverted and git status clean. Follow-on limitation filed as br-ze8h (held fixes die with a headless session).

title: guards: push-adjacent fail-closed hardening (control-flow, -c flag forms, xargs|sh, OOM in commandsOf)
description: pr-review-cycle round-3 review of PR #181 (after the 2-round cap) proved bypasses of the protected-branch rule on a real bare origin: toplevel for/if/while/{ }/function definitions and bash -c wrapping them; bash -c -- "<payload>"; echo "<push>" | xargs -I@ sh -c @. title: [trd:trd-2026-24fac9e9-skills-eval-harness:task:TRD-018] - [ ] **TRD-018** Result cache (`evals/lib/cache.js`) (4h)
description:
## Task: TRD-018
## References
TRD: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-24fac9e9-skills-eval-harness.md
TRD Task: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-24fac9e9-skills-eval-harness.md#trd-018
PRD: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-24fac9e9-skills-eval-harness.md
PRD Requirement: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-24fac9e9-skills-eval-harness.md#req-011
PRD ACs: AC-011-1, AC-011-2, AC-011-3
Parent Epic: [trd:trd-2026-24fac9e9-skills-eval-harness]
Read-first: read the TRD, TRD Task section, PRD and PRD Requirement above before any work on this bead.


--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-011**: Unchanged results are reused (Should)
Unchanged results are reused (Should)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-011-1: Given a skill | When the suite runs | Then the stored result is reused and no new model spend occurs
- AC-011-2: Given any of the three has changed | When the suite runs | Then the affected eval runs again
- AC-011-3: Given a stored result whose skill | When the suite runs at any later date | Then the result is reused with no age limit, and a maintainer can force a fresh run

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen: Option C, extend `evals/` and put runtimes behind adapters.**

The repository already has a headless behavioral eval harness (`evals/run.js`, `evals/lib/sandbox.js`, `evals/lib/graders.js`, `.github/workflows/evals.yml`, five task-keyed scenarios, unit tests with a stub `claude`). It already provides a throwaway git sandbox, deterministic graders, a total spend cap (`--max-usd`), results files and an on-demand workflow. It lacks what the PRD is mostly about:

| PRD need | State today |
|---|---|
| Evals keyed by skill, editable as files | Scenarios are keyed by task, one `scenario.json` each |
| With-skill and no-skill arms | One arm only |
| Repeats and a reliability bar | One run per scenario |
| Scrubbed environment | `spawnSync` inherits the whole environment |
| Model, skill version, eval version, runtime in results | Only a model tag |
| Coverage per skill, result cache, replay, regression compare | None |
| Pi | None |

| Option | Summary | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| A. Extend in place | Add the above to `run.js`; Pi logic added inline | Simplest, but Claude Code and Pi logic would tangle in one file |
| B. Adopt an external eval tool | Replace the runner with a third-party tool and port graders | Needs a spike and a new-dependency approval (constitution, Approval Requirements); rework of five tested scenarios; unknown support for a no-skill arm and Pi |
| **C. Extend with runner adapters** | Keep the tested runner, sandbox and graders. Add skill-keyed eval files, arms, repeats, an env allowlist, a results schema, coverage, cache and compare, behind a small runner interface with Claude Code and Pi adapters | **Chosen.** No new dependency (Node built-ins only), builds on tested code, and the eval format stays tool-neutral so an external runner could consume it later |

The PRD's Entry criterion (tool spike, fallback to a minimal in-repo runner) resolves to the fallback: this TRD is that runner, built on the existing harness. No new dependency is introduced, so no dependency approval is needed. If the owner later wants an external tool, the eval files in `evals/skills/` are the stable input.

Decisions fixed by the PRD and carried here: deterministic checks decide verdicts; judged checks only supplement and use a different model; 5 runs per arm with 4 of 5 required; $50 per suite and 900 s per run by default; results committed as per-skill baseline summaries with full logs as CI artifacts; Claude Code and Pi; on-demand CI only; advisory regression check.
Satisfies: REQ-011
Target File: 
Actions:

Implementation AC:
- [ ] Given a skill hash, eval version, model, runtime and arm that match a stored result, when the suite runs, then the stored result is reused and no model call is made
- [ ] Given any of those changed, when the suite runs, then the affected eval runs again
- [ ] Given a stored result of any age with matching inputs, when the suite runs, then it is reused, and `--refresh` forces a fresh run
Dependencies: TRD-014

title: [trd:trd-2026-70e784f2-code-review-process:task:TRD-023] - [ ] **TRD-023** Tier assignment: change kinds, sensitive floor and raise-only (`pr-review-tier.js`) (4h)
description:
## Task: TRD-023
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-70e784f2-code-review-process.md#trd-023
PRD Reference: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-70e784f2-code-review-process.md#req-012

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-012**: Change-driven risk tier (Must) [RISK: a mislabelled tier merges risky code with too little human review]
Change-driven risk tier (Must) [RISK: a mislabelled tier merges risky code with too little human review] Each PR is assigned a Low, Medium or High risk tier from the change itself, not from who wrote it.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-012-1: Given a PR | When review begins | Then a tier is assigned from the kind of change: Low for documentation, copy and additive changes behind a flag; Medium for ordinary product changes; High for sensitive areas (REQ-003) and any path an owner has listed as High
- AC-012-2: Given two PRs with identical changes from different authors | When tiers are assigned | Then they receive the same tier
- AC-012-3: Given a second assessment indicates a Low or Medium PR nonetheless needs another person | When it is evaluated | Then the tier is raised
- AC-013-2: Given an agent or the author proposes a tier | When it is lower than the assigned tier | Then it is ignored; only a code owner can lower a tier
- AC-013-3: Given a PR touches a sensitive area (REQ-003) | When its tier is set | Then the tier is High and two humans are required, regardless of what the classifier concluded

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen approach (Option C):** extend the pattern TRD-2026-82b6a138 established: **editable behavior in skills, agents and markdown; a small set of pure, deterministic libraries for what must not be self-certified by a model.**

- **User-owned (Constitution Rule 8), prose or data a maintainer edits without a toolchain:** per-area rules (`REVIEW.md` files), the policy block inside the root `REVIEW.md` (round cap, depth table, bot and maintainer logins, sensitive and High paths, Low-waiver state), severity definitions, reviewer, verifier, classifier and security-lane prompts, the PR template, the sweep and explainer procedures. All of it is read from the **target branch**, never from the PR head (REQ-024).
- **Enforcement (Rules 5 and 7), code that grades a model's claim:** vote tally, tier assignment with its sensitive-path floor and Low-waiver evidence, approval evaluation bound to a commit, the merge gate, round-cap derivation, repeat suppression, delta-range selection, depth bounds, slice coverage, metrics and eval scoring. Each is a pure CommonJS module in `packages/development/lib/`, exposed as a JSON-in/JSON-out subcommand of the existing `pr-review-cli.js`, following the 82b6a138 precedent. None performs network I/O or holds a timer.
- **Entry points (Rule 6):** every capability is reached through the one `pr-review-cycle` skill, which `fix-issue`, `implement-trd-beads` and `pr-merge` already invoke or will invoke (a new `MODE=gate` for `pr-merge`). YAML callers reference the skill only, never the CLI, as the existing parity tests require.
- **Recurrence (Rule 4):** nightly or weekly sweeps and daily eval runs are on-demand skills; a workflow template for the host repository is opt-in and scaffolded by init-project. Ensemble's own workflows gain no `schedule` trigger.

**Alternatives considered (user chose C):**

- **Option A -- prose-only skills and agents:** fewest files and fastest to ship. Rejected: the vote threshold, the tier floor, commit-bound approvals and the round cap would be prose a model can misread or skip, so none of these gates could be shown to fail (Rule 7), and "a bot approval never counts" would be a request, not a guarantee.
- **Option B -- a new TypeScript review engine in `agent-core`:** strongest typing and one runtime. Rejected: a new build and `dist` surface and cross-package coupling for a prompt-level feature, editable criteria pulled into code (against Rule 8), and drift toward an ensemble-owned dispatcher that competes with Foreman (Rule 4).

**Rationale:** Option C is the best fit for this brownfield repo. It adds only the code that grades claims, keeps everything a maintainer or adopting team would tune in files they can edit, adds no dependency (Constitution §4) and no CI secret, vendors into Pi automatically through the existing require-closure bundler, and each gate can be mutation-proven using the harness that already exists.

**Decisions taken where the PRD left a choice** (each is editable policy, not a hidden constant):

| Decision | Value | Where it lives |
|---|---|---|
| Policy format | Fenced `ensemble-review-policy` JSON block in the root `REVIEW.md` (no new parser dependency) | REVIEW.md, read from the base commit |
| "Cannot vouch for" a push (AC-010-3, AC-014-2) | Commit is unvouched when its tree differs from the reviewed tree and it is not a remediation commit recorded in the review-state report, or it is a merge commit | `pr-review-scope.js`, `pr-review-approvals.js` |
| Slice threshold for large PRs (AC-018-1) | 1500 changed lines, configurable | policy block |
| Area rules vs policy keys | Policy keys are read from the **root** file only; area files carry guidance, and the more restrictive instruction wins when areas conflict (AC-001-2) | skill prose |
| First PR that introduces REVIEW.md | No base copy exists, so strict defaults apply (Low treated as Medium, cap 3, default sensitive set) | `pr-review-policy.js` |
| Verifier majority | Strict majority of the expected verifier count (2 of 3, 3 of 5) | `pr-review-votes.js` |
Satisfies: REQ-012
PRD ACs: AC-012-1, AC-012-2, AC-012-3, AC-013-2, AC-013-3
Target File: 
Actions:

Implementation AC:
- [ ] Given classifier output `kinds[{ kind, paths[] }]` with kind in {docs, copy, additive-behind-flag, product, other} and path classification, when `assignTier` runs, then all-low kinds give Low, ordinary product changes Medium, and any sensitive or owner-listed High path gives High; a missing, unknown or uncited kind is treated as `other` (Medium); identical facts give an identical tier regardless of author
- [ ] Given a second assessment `{ needsAnotherPerson, reason, evidencePaths[] }`, when `assignTier` runs, then exactly `true` raises the tier one level, `false` leaves it, and any other value is treated as `true` (fail toward more review)
- [ ] Given a proposed tier lower than the computed one, when it runs, then the proposal is ignored; only a code-owner decision (supplied as CODEOWNERS-checked input) can lower it
Dependencies: TRD-001, TRD-002

title: [trd:trd-2026-d6bbf322-new-feature-workflow:task:TRD-004] - [ ] **TRD-004**: Implement inline stage execution and artifact-reference recording (5h)
description:
## Task: TRD-004
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-d6bbf322-new-feature-workflow.md#trd-004
PRD Reference: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-d6bbf322-new-feature-workflow.md#req-004

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-004**: Bind every stage to explicit, traceable artifacts
Bind every stage to explicit, traceable artifacts Priority: Must | Complexity: High | [RISK: an incorrect artifact association can cause implementation of an unreviewed or unrelated plan]

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-004-1: Given a stage produces or refines an artifact | When its outcome is recorded | Then the run record identifies the exact artifact reference, artifact type, producing stage, and the run to which it belongs
- AC-004-2: Given a later stage requires a PRD | When that stage begins | Then it consumes the exact reference recorded by its prerequisite stage and not a path selected by recency, filename similarity, or conversation context
- AC-004-3: Given a PRD or TRD is revised during its refinement stage | When the revised artifact is accepted | Then the run's current reference is updated while the prior artifact/version remains available for review and recovery

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen: Option C — hardened in-session stage composition with a dedicated atomic run-index store.**

`new-feature` is authored the same way every other product command in this repo is authored: a single orchestrating skill (`packages/development/commands/new-feature.yaml`, generated to runtime-specific prompts exactly like `fix-issue.yaml`) that executes each stage's existing skill body in-session — the same mechanism that loaded `ensemble-refine-prd`'s content into this session and had the agent execute its Phases directly. This is forced, not merely preferred: Pi's `ExtensionAPI` has no completion/invoke primitive that would let an extension programmatically run another skill and get its result back (confirmed — no `pi.invokeCommand` or equivalent exists); the only code-level "run a skill" mechanism, `createAgentPort()`, spawns a bounded, disposable `omp -p --no-session --no-extensions` subprocess in an isolated worktree, and does not fit a long-lived, project-resident workflow whose PRD/TRD stages use the interactive `--collab` review server.

What is new, and is the one piece of real infrastructure this TRD adds: a `RunIndexStore` (`packages/agent-core/src/new-feature/run-index.ts`) built on the one proven concurrency-safe pattern in this repo — `session.js`'s temp-file-then-`renameSync` atomic write plus `expectedRevision`/409-style optimistic concurrency — rather than `ProposalStore`'s plain `writeFileSync` (no atomicity, no lock, not adequate for PRD AC-005-3's fail-closed-on-malformed-index requirement). Runs are stored at `.ensemble/new-feature/<run-id>.json`, mirroring `ProposalStore`'s `.ensemble/proposals/<ref>.json` convention (also excluded from `tree-baseline.ts` drift detection, so this is consistent runtime-owned state, not a project-source mutation).

### Alternatives considered

| Option | Summary | Why not chosen |
|---|---|---|
| A — Plain JSON checkpoint | Same in-session composition, but checkpoints are a single `writeFileSync`, no atomicity/locking. | Fastest to build, but a crash mid-write can corrupt the run index, which directly violates AC-005-3's "fail closed with a recoverable diagnostic" requirement — the repo's own `ProposalStore` already demonstrates this gap is real, not hypothetical. |
| B — Subprocess-dispatched stages | New orchestrator module dispatches every stage as a bounded `createAgentPort()` subprocess; advances the run index only after subprocess exit 0 + artifact-on-disk confirmation. | Most rigorous completion signal (a real process boundary instead of self-reported bookkeeping), but substantially more build effort, and does not fit the interactive `--collab` review-server stages `create-prd`/`refine-prd` already use — those are long-lived, human-attended HTTP sessions, not bounded one-shot subprocess work, and would need bespoke carve-out handling under this option. |
| **C — Hardened in-session composition** *(chosen)* | In-session stage execution (like every existing product command), backed by a dedicated atomic `RunIndexStore`. | Reuses 100% of the existing skill-composition and `ask_user`-approval infrastructure (including the `--collab` review server, which needs no special-casing), while fixing Option A's one real correctness gap with the repo's one proven atomic-write pattern. Matches user-confirmed direction. |

### Honest trust-boundary note

Because stage execution stays in-session (per Option C), the approval gates implemented by TRD-014/TRD-017/TRD-019 are enforced by the orchestrating skill's own conditional logic checking `RunIndexStore`-persisted approval fields before it issues an implementation or `gh pr create` tool call — not by a separate runtime authorization chokepoint like `agent-core`'s `MutationGuard` (which exists elsewhere in this repo, gating CQRS-registered commands, but `new-feature`'s mutating actions are ordinary skill-level tool calls, same as `fix-issue`'s own gated PR-creation step, not CQRS commands). This is the same trust boundary every existing Ensemble product command already operates under. Building a `MutationGuard`-equivalent chokepoint for skill-level tool calls is a materially larger investment this PRD does not request and no other product command has; REQ-014's "runtime authority" is satisfied here by making the check a required precondition over persisted, validated store state rather than over prompt claims — which is what AC-014-2 actually asks for — not by inventing a new enforcement subsystem.
Satisfies: REQ-004
PRD ACs: AC-004-1, AC-004-2, AC-004-3
Target File: packages/development/commands/new-feature.yaml
Actions:
1. For each of `prd_create`/`prd_refine`/`trd_create`/`trd_refine`/`beads_plan`, read that stage's existing skill body (`ensemble-create-prd`, `ensemble-refine-prd`, `ensemble-create-trd`, `ensemble-refine-trd`, the beads-planning skill) and execute its instructions in-session — the same mechanism that loaded `ensemble-refine-prd`'s content into this session.
2. Immediately after a stage's outcome is `success`, call `RunIndexStore.mutate()` to append the produced artifact's exact `{ type, path, documentId, version, producingStage, recordedAt }` to `artifacts[]` before advancing `stage`.
3. When a later stage consumes a PRD/TRD, pass it the exact recorded `artifacts[]` entry's `path` — never a path selected by globbing, recency, or conversational context.
4. On a PRD/TRD revision during refinement, append the new artifact entry rather than overwriting the prior one; the prior entry remains in `artifacts[]` for history and recovery (AC-004-3).
Implementation AC:
- [ ] Given `prd_create` completes, when the checkpoint is recorded, then `artifacts[]` gains an entry with `type: "prd"`, the exact file path, `documentId`, and `producingStage: "prd_create"`.
- [ ] Given `trd_create` begins, when it needs the PRD, then it is invoked with the exact `path` from the `artifacts[]` entry recorded by `prd_refine`, not a freshly globbed path.
- [ ] Given `prd_refine` revises the PRD, when the revision is accepted, then both the prior and the new artifact entries are present in `artifacts[]`.
Dependencies: TRD-003
close_reason: Implemented: Execute Stage phase in new-feature.yaml -- in-session dispatch to existing skills (create-prd/refine-prd/create-trd/refine-trd/implement-trd-beads --plan), success/decline recording via RunIndexStore.mutate() with atomic artifact-append + stage-advance. Passes generate --validate.

title: [trd:trd-2026-82b6a138-pr-review-cycle-time:task:TRD-018] - [ ] **TRD-018** Final audit, documentation and verification (4h)
description:
## Task: TRD-018
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-82b6a138-pr-review-cycle-time.md#trd-018
PRD Reference: #req-021

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen approach (Option C):** One shared, prose-defined review procedure plus a small deterministic helper library.

- `packages/development/skills/pr-review-cycle/SKILL.md` is the single reusable procedure. It owns the *user-editable* parts (Constitution Rule 8): review criteria, the order of the loop, the 10-minute interactive wait, Foreman-mode rules. It **composes** `packages/quality/skills/pr-review-remediation/SKILL.md` for per-finding triage, regression tests and minimal fixes and does not restate those rules.
- A set of small pure-JS modules in `packages/development/lib/` owns only what *grades the model's own claim* (Constitution Rule 8's enforcement exception, and Rule 7): base/head scope resolution, ledger validation, head-bound remote-review evaluation, terminal-status derivation with the bounded-round cap, and the untracked review-state report. A thin CLI, `pr-review-cli.js`, exposes them as JSON-in/JSON-out commands, following the `trd-cli.js` / `complete-beads-planner.js` precedent.
- `fix-issue.yaml`, `implement-trd-beads.yaml` and `complete-beads/SKILL.md` invoke the skill at their real PR boundaries; none re-states review steps.

**Alternatives considered (user chose C):**

- **Option A -- prose-only skill:** fewest files, but "no early REVIEW_COMPLETE", head-binding and the round cap would be prose a model can misread, and tests could only assert text ordering. Rejected: the plan's core guarantee would not be falsifiable (Rule 7).
- **Option B -- TypeScript runtime in agent-core:** strongest typing, but a new build/dist surface and cross-package coupling for a prompt-level feature, and it pulls editable criteria toward code (against Rule 8). Rejected.

**Rationale:** Option C is the best fit for this brownfield repo: the helper is the minimum code that makes the status contract testable and unforgeable, everything a maintainer would plausibly tune stays in a skill file, and it needs no new dependency, provider or config knob.
Satisfies: REQ-021
PRD ACs: AC-021-1, AC-021-2

- [ ] Given the complete change, when it is inspected, then no HerdR change, merge automation, new review provider, dashboard, new dependency or new configuration knob has been added
- [ ] Given the documentation, when updated, then the `packages/development` CHANGELOG and README describe the skill and both integrations, and `npm run validate`, `npm run generate:validate` and `npm test` all pass

TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-87e64cc6-command-surface-consolidation.md#trd-004-test

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen approach:** Two independent axes of work, both reusing existing, shipped mechanisms rather than inventing new ones.

1. **Front door (feature + issue discoverability/delegation):** Reuse the existing native-command pattern exactly as `ensemble-prd`/`ensemble-trd`/`ensemble-issue` already implement it — `registerDispatcherCommand` (completion dropdown, verbatim forward) + a `dispatch.subcommands[]`-bearing colon-named command YAML (Dispatch phase routes the first argument token to a sibling command/flag). `ensemble-feature`'s native registration and `ensemble:feature`'s dispatcher content are new; the underlying mechanism they ride on (`dispatcher-commands.ts`) is untouched.
2. **Issue resumability (REQ-019):** Option C — shared stage-agnostic I/O primitives extracted into a new `run-index-core.ts`; the existing feature `RunIndexStore` is refactored to call into it internally with its public API, `Stage`, and `RunRecord` unchanged; a new, independent `issue-run-index.ts` thin wrapper is built on the same core with its own `IssueStage`/`IssueRunRecord`. See the companion research doc for the full alternatives comparison (Option A: duplicate, Option B: fully generic store) and why C was selected live with the user during this phase.

**Alternatives considered:** Design Option A (duplicate everything, fastest, no shared plumbing) and Design Option B (fully generic parameterized store) were both presented and rejected in favor of Option C — see [Research: Run-Index Architecture](./TRD-2026-87e64cc6-command-surface-consolidation-research.md) for the full tradeoff analysis.

title: [trd:trd-2026-4dec59b8-local-ci-pr-approval:task:TRD-004] - [ ] **TRD-004** GitHub App client (`local-ci-app.js`) (5h)
description:
## Task: TRD-004
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-4dec59b8-local-ci-pr-approval.md#trd-004
PRD Reference: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-4dec59b8-local-ci-pr-approval.md#req-004

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-004**: Evidence is published where branch protection can enforce it (Must) [RISK: verified -- the required checks on `dev` are pinned to the GitHub Actions app (app id 15368); a status posted with a personal token or the `gh` CLI is not from that app and will not satisfy them, leaving the PR unmergeable]
Evidence is published where branch protection can enforce it (Must) [RISK: verified -- the required checks on `dev` are pinned to the GitHub Actions app (app id 15368); a status posted with a personal token or the `gh` CLI is not from that app and will not satisfy them, leaving the PR unmergeable] The local run's result is published to GitHub as a status on the head commit, posted by a maintainer-owned GitHub App under a name that branch protection can pin to that app.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-004-1: Given a passing local run | When its result is published | Then the head commit shows a success status under the agreed name, posted by the maintainer-owned app
- AC-004-2: Given a failing local run | When its result is published | Then the head commit shows a failure status and the PR cannot be merged by the supported flow
- AC-010-1: Given secrets are needed for a local run | When it executes | Then they come from gitignored local configuration or the environment and never from tracked files
- AC-010-2: Given the local run publishes a status or log | When the output is inspected | Then it contains no token or secret value
- AC-018-1: Given the app credential | When the repository | Then the credential does not appear in any of them
- AC-018-2: Given the credential is absent | When a local run is requested | Then the run may execute but publishes nothing and reports that it cannot attest
- AC-018-3: Given the credential is suspected to be exposed | When the maintainer follows the documented rotation procedure | Then the old credential stops working and the app can post again with a new one

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen approach (Option C):** A `local-ci-gate` skill owns the editable procedure; a small set of pure-JS helpers in `packages/development/lib/` owns only what must be unforgeable; `pr-merge.yaml` invokes the skill.

- `packages/development/skills/local-ci-gate/SKILL.md` is the single reusable procedure and owns everything a maintainer would plausibly tune (Constitution Rule 8): the order of the run, the messages, the bead wording, and how failures are explained.
- Pure-JS modules in `packages/development/lib/` own only what grades a claim or protects a boundary (Rules 7 and 8's enforcement exception): run-record verification, bot-vs-human classification, bead dedupe keys, approval-set config validation, and GitHub App credential handling. They make no network calls except the one module whose purpose is to post a status.
- `packages/git/commands/pr-merge.yaml` calls the skill at its existing Merge phase. It does not restate gate logic.
- The gate runs in-session in the maintainer's own process. There is no daemon, scheduler or background sweep (Rule 4; REQ-012).

**Alternatives considered (user chose C):**

- **Option A -- prose-only:** fewest files, but head-binding, run-record verification and human/bot classification would be prose a model can misread, and tests could only assert wording. Rejected: the PRD's core property is that evidence cannot be reused across commits.
- **Option B -- TypeScript runtime in agent-core:** strongest typing, but adds a build/dist surface and pulls editable criteria toward code against Rule 8. Rejected: the one place a real client is tempting (App JWT signing) needs only Node's built-in `crypto`.

**Dependency decision (user approved):** no new dependency. The App's RS256 JWT is signed with Node `crypto`; the REST calls use `fetch`. This avoids the constitution's new-dependency approval gate and keeps the signing path small and auditable.

**Rationale:** Option C matches repository precedent (TRD-2026-82b6a138), keeps editable behavior out of TypeScript, and is the minimum code that makes the trust properties testable.
Satisfies: REQ-004
PRD ACs: AC-004-1, AC-004-2, AC-010-1, AC-010-2, AC-018-1, AC-018-2, AC-018-3
Target File: packages/development/lib/local-ci-app.js, .gitignore
Actions:

Implementation AC:
- [ ] Given an App id and private key, when `signAppJwt` runs, then it returns an RS256 JWT built only with Node `crypto` and no added dependency
- [ ] Given a valid JWT, when `postStatus` runs, then it exchanges for an installation token and posts the state, context and run-record description on the head SHA
- [ ] Given no credential, when `postStatus` runs, then it posts nothing and returns `{published:false, reason:'cannot attest'}`
- [ ] Given any thrown error or response, when output is produced, then `redact` has removed the key, JWT and token from every string
- [ ] Given a key that is no longer valid, when `postStatus` runs, then it returns a clear authentication failure and publishes nothing
- [ ] Given the credential is read from the environment or from `.ensemble/local-ci-app.pem`, when the repository is inspected, then `.gitignore` contains a rule that ignores `.ensemble/local-ci-app.pem` and any `*.pem`, and `git check-ignore` confirms it before the first run is allowed to read the file
- [ ] Given a run starts, when the preflight executes, then it refuses to read any credential file that `git ls-files` reports as tracked and names the file without printing its contents
Dependencies: TRD-001

title: [trd:trd-2026-d6bbf322-new-feature-workflow:task:TRD-014] - [ ] **TRD-014**: Implement the implementation-approval checkpoint (5h)
description:
## Task: TRD-014
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-d6bbf322-new-feature-workflow.md#trd-014
PRD Reference: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-d6bbf322-new-feature-workflow.md#req-010

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-010**: Require explicit user approval before implementation
Require explicit user approval before implementation Priority: Must | Complexity: Medium

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-010-1: Given PRD refinement | When the workflow reaches the implementation checkpoint | Then it presents the accepted PRD/TRD references and bead plan and waits for an explicit approval to begin implementation
- AC-010-2: Given implementation approval is absent or declined | When the workflow is invoked | Then it does not execute implementation work and preserves the run at the approval checkpoint for later resume

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen: Option C — hardened in-session stage composition with a dedicated atomic run-index store.**

`new-feature` is authored the same way every other product command in this repo is authored: a single orchestrating skill (`packages/development/commands/new-feature.yaml`, generated to runtime-specific prompts exactly like `fix-issue.yaml`) that executes each stage's existing skill body in-session — the same mechanism that loaded `ensemble-refine-prd`'s content into this session and had the agent execute its Phases directly. This is forced, not merely preferred: Pi's `ExtensionAPI` has no completion/invoke primitive that would let an extension programmatically run another skill and get its result back (confirmed — no `pi.invokeCommand` or equivalent exists); the only code-level "run a skill" mechanism, `createAgentPort()`, spawns a bounded, disposable `omp -p --no-session --no-extensions` subprocess in an isolated worktree, and does not fit a long-lived, project-resident workflow whose PRD/TRD stages use the interactive `--collab` review server.

What is new, and is the one piece of real infrastructure this TRD adds: a `RunIndexStore` (`packages/agent-core/src/new-feature/run-index.ts`) built on the one proven concurrency-safe pattern in this repo — `session.js`'s temp-file-then-`renameSync` atomic write plus `expectedRevision`/409-style optimistic concurrency — rather than `ProposalStore`'s plain `writeFileSync` (no atomicity, no lock, not adequate for PRD AC-005-3's fail-closed-on-malformed-index requirement). Runs are stored at `.ensemble/new-feature/<run-id>.json`, mirroring `ProposalStore`'s `.ensemble/proposals/<ref>.json` convention (also excluded from `tree-baseline.ts` drift detection, so this is consistent runtime-owned state, not a project-source mutation).

### Alternatives considered

| Option | Summary | Why not chosen |
|---|---|---|
| A — Plain JSON checkpoint | Same in-session composition, but checkpoints are a single `writeFileSync`, no atomicity/locking. | Fastest to build, but a crash mid-write can corrupt the run index, which directly violates AC-005-3's "fail closed with a recoverable diagnostic" requirement — the repo's own `ProposalStore` already demonstrates this gap is real, not hypothetical. |
| B — Subprocess-dispatched stages | New orchestrator module dispatches every stage as a bounded `createAgentPort()` subprocess; advances the run index only after subprocess exit 0 + artifact-on-disk confirmation. | Most rigorous completion signal (a real process boundary instead of self-reported bookkeeping), but substantially more build effort, and does not fit the interactive `--collab` review-server stages `create-prd`/`refine-prd` already use — those are long-lived, human-attended HTTP sessions, not bounded one-shot subprocess work, and would need bespoke carve-out handling under this option. |
| **C — Hardened in-session composition** *(chosen)* | In-session stage execution (like every existing product command), backed by a dedicated atomic `RunIndexStore`. | Reuses 100% of the existing skill-composition and `ask_user`-approval infrastructure (including the `--collab` review server, which needs no special-casing), while fixing Option A's one real correctness gap with the repo's one proven atomic-write pattern. Matches user-confirmed direction. |

### Honest trust-boundary note

Because stage execution stays in-session (per Option C), the approval gates implemented by TRD-014/TRD-017/TRD-019 are enforced by the orchestrating skill's own conditional logic checking `RunIndexStore`-persisted approval fields before it issues an implementation or `gh pr create` tool call — not by a separate runtime authorization chokepoint like `agent-core`'s `MutationGuard` (which exists elsewhere in this repo, gating CQRS-registered commands, but `new-feature`'s mutating actions are ordinary skill-level tool calls, same as `fix-issue`'s own gated PR-creation step, not CQRS commands). This is the same trust boundary every existing Ensemble product command already operates under. Building a `MutationGuard`-equivalent chokepoint for skill-level tool calls is a materially larger investment this PRD does not request and no other product command has; REQ-014's "runtime authority" is satisfied here by making the check a required precondition over persisted, validated store state rather than over prompt claims — which is what AC-014-2 actually asks for — not by inventing a new enforcement subsystem.
Satisfies: REQ-010
PRD ACs: AC-010-1, AC-010-2
Target File: packages/development/commands/new-feature.yaml
Actions:
1. At `stage: "implementation_approval"`, present the accepted PRD/TRD references and the bead plan via `ask_user`, then wait for an explicit approval response.
2. On explicit approval, call `RunIndexStore.mutate()` setting `implementationApprovedAt = now()` and advance `stage` to `"implementation"`.
3. On absent or declined approval, perform no implementation work and leave the run parked at `implementation_approval` for later resume.
Implementation AC:
- [ ] Given the checkpoint is reached, when presented, then the exact PRD/TRD refs and bead plan shown match the run record's `artifacts[]`/`beadRefs`.
- [ ] Given approval is declined or not given, when the command exits this turn, then `implementationApprovedAt` remains `null` and `stage` remains `"implementation_approval"`.
Dependencies: TRD-002, TRD-004
close_reason: Implemented + tests green

title: [trd:trd-2026-70e784f2-code-review-process:task:TRD-032-TEST] - [ ] **TRD-032-TEST** Metrics and eval CLI end to end (3h)
description:
## Test Task: TRD-032-TEST
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-70e784f2-code-review-process.md#trd-032-test
PRD Reference: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-70e784f2-code-review-process.md#req-019

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-019**: Review metrics with a revert and incident guardrail (Must)
Review metrics with a revert and incident guardrail (Must) The process reports the measures behind the success criteria, so improvement is shown rather than assumed.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-019-3: Given a post-change cohort and the baseline cohort | When compared | Then targets are expressed relative to baseline: median human approvals and p95 human wait down, rounds-to-pass down by at least 30%, PRs needing five or more rounds down by at least 50%, and noise rate down by at least 30%
- AC-019-4: Given the metrics are reported | When revert or incident counts for the cohort exceed baseline | Then the report marks the cohort as failing the guardrail regardless of other results
- AC-020-2: Given the reviewer's rules | When the eval set is run | Then each case is scored for whether the reviewer found the bug, and the result is reported

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen approach (Option C):** extend the pattern TRD-2026-82b6a138 established: **editable behavior in skills, agents and markdown; a small set of pure, deterministic libraries for what must not be self-certified by a model.**

- **User-owned (Constitution Rule 8), prose or data a maintainer edits without a toolchain:** per-area rules (`REVIEW.md` files), the policy block inside the root `REVIEW.md` (round cap, depth table, bot and maintainer logins, sensitive and High paths, Low-waiver state), severity definitions, reviewer, verifier, classifier and security-lane prompts, the PR template, the sweep and explainer procedures. All of it is read from the **target branch**, never from the PR head (REQ-024).
- **Enforcement (Rules 5 and 7), code that grades a model's claim:** vote tally, tier assignment with its sensitive-path floor and Low-waiver evidence, approval evaluation bound to a commit, the merge gate, round-cap derivation, repeat suppression, delta-range selection, depth bounds, slice coverage, metrics and eval scoring. Each is a pure CommonJS module in `packages/development/lib/`, exposed as a JSON-in/JSON-out subcommand of the existing `pr-review-cli.js`, following the 82b6a138 precedent. None performs network I/O or holds a timer.
- **Entry points (Rule 6):** every capability is reached through the one `pr-review-cycle` skill, which `fix-issue`, `implement-trd-beads` and `pr-merge` already invoke or will invoke (a new `MODE=gate` for `pr-merge`). YAML callers reference the skill only, never the CLI, as the existing parity tests require.
- **Recurrence (Rule 4):** nightly or weekly sweeps and daily eval runs are on-demand skills; a workflow template for the host repository is opt-in and scaffolded by init-project. Ensemble's own workflows gain no `schedule` trigger.

**Alternatives considered (user chose C):**

- **Option A -- prose-only skills and agents:** fewest files and fastest to ship. Rejected: the vote threshold, the tier floor, commit-bound approvals and the round cap would be prose a model can misread or skip, so none of these gates could be shown to fail (Rule 7), and "a bot approval never counts" would be a request, not a guarantee.
- **Option B -- a new TypeScript review engine in `agent-core`:** strongest typing and one runtime. Rejected: a new build and `dist` surface and cross-package coupling for a prompt-level feature, editable criteria pulled into code (against Rule 8), and drift toward an ensemble-owned dispatcher that competes with Foreman (Rule 4).

**Rationale:** Option C is the best fit for this brownfield repo. It adds only the code that grades claims, keeps everything a maintainer or adopting team would tune in files they can edit, adds no dependency (Constitution §4) and no CI secret, vendors into Pi automatically through the existing require-closure bundler, and each gate can be mutation-proven using the harness that already exists.

**Decisions taken where the PRD left a choice** (each is editable policy, not a hidden constant):

| Decision | Value | Where it lives |
|---|---|---|
| Policy format | Fenced `ensemble-review-policy` JSON block in the root `REVIEW.md` (no new parser dependency) | REVIEW.md, read from the base commit |
| "Cannot vouch for" a push (AC-010-3, AC-014-2) | Commit is unvouched when its tree differs from the reviewed tree and it is not a remediation commit recorded in the review-state report, or it is a merge commit | `pr-review-scope.js`, `pr-review-approvals.js` |
| Slice threshold for large PRs (AC-018-1) | 1500 changed lines, configurable | policy block |
| Area rules vs policy keys | Policy keys are read from the **root** file only; area files carry guidance, and the more restrictive instruction wins when areas conflict (AC-001-2) | skill prose |
| First PR that introduces REVIEW.md | No base copy exists, so strict defaults apply (Low treated as Medium, cap 3, default sensitive set) | `pr-review-policy.js` |
| Verifier majority | Strict majority of the expected verifier count (2 of 3, 3 of 5) | `pr-review-votes.js` |
Verifies Task: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-70e784f2-code-review-process.md#trd-032
Verifies: TRD-032

PRD ACs Proven: AC-019-3, AC-019-4, AC-020-2

title: Same piped-stdout truncation in sibling CLIs that still end in process.exit(code) (PR #241 C03, pre-existing)
description:
Follow-on from PR #241 review (finding C03, Pre-existing, not blocking).

Location: packages/development/lib/toolchain-cli.js:1036, prd-cli.js:387, trd-graph-cli.js:152, pr-review-cli.js:641, local-ci-cli.js:593, beads-refine-cli.js:99, packages/product/lib/prd-cli.js:214, reqnroll-cli.js:249, plus vendored pi/codex copies

Failure mode: Sibling CLIs still call process.exit(code) after process.stdout.write, so piped output over 64 KiB is cut. Reproduced with `prd-cli list` on 600-800 synthetic PRDs: piped 65536 bytes and JSON.parse fails. toolchain-cli with a >64 KiB envelope was NOT executed [INFERENCE]; its `run tracker.list` output is MB-scale and parsed as JSON by beads-build.yaml:123, the highest exposure. No sibling output on repo data measured over 64 KiB. Not touched by PR #241; its CHANGELOG scopes the fix to trd-cli.js.

Proposed fix: Apply the same process.exitCode wrapper (plus the EPIPE handler from C02) to toolchain-cli.js first, then the rest, regenerating vendored copies, each with a real-OS-pipe test like trd-cli-flush.test.js.

Source: PR #241 review (Merge241Fast), verified by 5 independent verifiers (5 real / 0 not-real).

## Task: TRD-042
## References
TRD: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-8d825f54-tool-abstraction-layer.md
TRD Task: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-8d825f54-tool-abstraction-layer.md#trd-042
PRD: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-8d825f54-tool-abstraction-layer.md
PRD Requirement: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-8d825f54-tool-abstraction-layer.md#req-001
PRD Requirement: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-8d825f54-tool-abstraction-layer.md#req-006
PRD ACs: AC-006-2
Parent Epic: [trd:trd-2026-8d825f54-tool-abstraction-layer]
Read-first: read the TRD, TRD Task section, PRD and PRD Requirement above before any work on this bead.


--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-001**: Capability taxonomy covering all tool categories
Capability taxonomy covering all tool categories Priority: Must Ensemble defines a taxonomy of tool categories covering every external tool its sources invoke: source-control host and change requests, branching workflow, worktree manager, work tracking, work graph and ready-work queue, local CI, review automation, lint automation, test runner, end-to-end and quality checks, container and deployment, infrastructure as code, platform and cloud, and package/build runner. The CI category covers only tools an agent invokes to run CI locally; hosted CI definitions are repository infrastructure and out of scope.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-006-2: Given the worktree-manager category | When its default adapter is inspected | Then it covers worktree operations using plain source-control worktrees and no command invokes it yet

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-006**: Default adapters for every category
Default adapters for every category Priority: Must Every category in the taxonomy ships with a default adapter reproducing ensemble's current behavior for the tool currently used.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-006-2: Given the worktree-manager category | When its default adapter is inspected | Then it covers worktree operations using plain source-control worktrees and no command invokes it yet

--- TRD Context ---
### Alternatives Considered

| Option | Approach | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|---|
| A: Prose-only adapters | Adapter is a skill; the agent follows its prose and normalizes tool output itself | Smallest build; fully editable | Cannot route internal CLIs deterministically (REQ-016), cannot validate output (REQ-022), cannot deny at runtime (REQ-023); behavior varies per model |
| **B: Manifest plus runner (chosen)** | Adapter is a skill directory: `SKILL.md` (vocabulary and agent-facing prose) plus a declarative `adapter.yaml` (capability command templates, output mapping, allowlist, health check, detection signals, required env names). A core resolver library and `toolchain-cli` execute capabilities deterministically | Meets PRD (adapter is a skill), Rule 8 (editable without rebuild), Rule 5 (enforcement in code), REQ-016 (CLIs call the same library) | New resolver, runner, manifest schema and output-mapping engine to build and test |
| C: Executable plugin adapters | Separately packaged executables speaking a versioned JSON protocol | Arbitrary logic; strongest isolation | Contradicts the PRD's skills-as-contract decision; fails Rule 8; needs per-OS packaging and a protocol |

**Rationale:** B is the only option that makes every PRD guarantee a code-enforced property while keeping adapters user-editable data. The requester selected B at the architecture gate.

### Interpretations and Resolved Design Issues

- **I1: plain version control.** The PRD taxonomy has no plain `git` category, yet about 45 sources invoke it. Plain `git` operations (status, commit, push, log, diff, merge-base) are `vcs.*` capabilities of the `workflow` category, whose default adapter is `plain-git`; the `git-town` adapter extends it. Recommend a PRD refine pass to name this explicitly.
- **I2: ambiguity versus no signal (PRD REQ-009 AC-2 vs REQ-010 AC-2).** "No detectable signal" means no signal source exists at all (no remote, no marker files); the shipped default is used. "Ambiguous" means two or more installed adapters match, or a signal source exists (for example a remote URL) but matches no installed adapter; resolution fails explicitly in non-interactive runs and asks in interactive runs.
- **I3: AC-023-2 (governed boundary denies).** The runner is invoked through the shell tool, so a command that was not granted the shell tool cannot run any adapter; an adapter therefore cannot widen grants. The runner additionally denies any command outside the adapter's binary-plus-subcommand allowlist. Denial of raw shell commands typed by an agent outside the runner remains host-enforced (hooks on Claude Code; none in this repo for Pi, OpenCode or Codex); the lint (REQ-019) keeps commands from issuing raw tool calls. This residual is recorded in the Threat Model.
- **I4: confirmation session identity.** No stable session id is exposed uniformly across runtimes. TRD-017 begins with a spike that records which id each runtime exposes (`ENSEMBLE_SESSION_ID`, host session variables); the passive confirmation record is keyed by `(sessionKey, category, adapter, configHash)` and falls back to the run id when no session id exists.
- **I5: repo-local adapters are untrusted by default.** A cloned repository can ship `.ensemble/adapters/`. Repo-local adapters resolve in every mode (satisfying AC-007-3) but a non-interactive run additionally requires the adapter name in the user's `trustedRepoAdapters` list; an interactive run shows the adapter's allowlist at first-use confirmation.

## Test Task: TRD-003-TEST
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-1d3e0dd6-new-feature-foreman-flag.md#trd-003-test
PRD Reference: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-1d3e0dd6-new-feature-foreman-flag.md#req-003

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-003**: Retry of a failed stage needs no confirmation (Must)
Retry of a failed stage needs no confirmation (Must)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-003-1: Given a run parked with `stageOutcome.kind == "failure"` and an invocation with `--foreman` | When entry resolution runs | Then the "Retry <stage>?" question is not asked and the parked stage is retried once, as the explicit retry
- AC-003-2: Given that retry fails | When the invocation ends | Then the failure is recorded at the same stage and nothing retries again within that invocation (Foreman owns any further retry)
- AC-003-3: Given a failed run and an invocation without `--foreman` | When it runs | Then the confirmation question is asked as today

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen approach:** a prompt-only change to two YAML command sources. No TypeScript changes.

- `packages/development/commands/new-feature.yaml` gains a boolean `foreman` parameter and one derived variable, `FOREMAN`, defined once in Entry Point Resolution Step 1 and referenced by every later step. Each step that asks the user gets a `FOREMAN == true` branch that takes a deterministic, recorded, non-interactive decision. Each step that dispatches a stage skill appends `--foreman` when `FOREMAN == true`.
- `packages/development/commands/feature.yaml` (the `/ensemble:feature` front door) recognizes `--foreman` as the first token after the keyword and forwards it.
- Generated OMP, Pi and Codex artifacts are regenerated from the repo root, never hand-edited.

**Why prompt-only (Constitution Rule 8):** how a workflow behaves when no one can answer is something a maintainer would plausibly tune (for example, switching the PR gate to park instead of auto-grant). That belongs in the command prose, not in TypeScript. `RunIndexStore` already supports everything needed: `StageOutcome.detail` carries the "granted by `--foreman` policy" record.

**Additive-only edits (found in refinement):** the existing suites (`new-feature-command.test.js`, `feature-command.test.js`, `feature-input-validation-boundary.test.js`, `feature-concurrency-passthrough.test.js`) pin exact sentences in both YAML files, for example "any remaining text is an unsupported flag or argument rejected here". So no pre-existing sentence may be reworded or removed. Foreman behavior is added as new actions or appended sentences, and the existing suites must pass unchanged. For the front door that means: a new action, placed before the validation action, removes a leading `--foreman` token and sets `FOREMAN`, so the pinned validation sentences still read "remaining text" correctly; and a new action, placed after the invocation is constructed, inserts `--foreman` right after `/ensemble:new-feature` in whatever invocation was built.

**Alternatives rejected:**
- *Env-var-only detection (no flag).* Rejected: the maintainer asked for a `--foreman` flag, and the five stage skills already key on that flag.
- *A new RunRecord field `autoGranted`.* Rejected: TypeScript and schema change for information `StageOutcome.detail` already carries.
- *Parking at the approval gates.* Rejected by the maintainer: it stalls every no-user run.

## Task: TRD-010
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-82b6a138-pr-review-cycle-time.md#trd-010
PRD Reference: #req-012

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen approach (Option C):** One shared, prose-defined review procedure plus a small deterministic helper library.

- `packages/development/skills/pr-review-cycle/SKILL.md` is the single reusable procedure. It owns the *user-editable* parts (Constitution Rule 8): review criteria, the order of the loop, the 10-minute interactive wait, Foreman-mode rules. It **composes** `packages/quality/skills/pr-review-remediation/SKILL.md` for per-finding triage, regression tests and minimal fixes and does not restate those rules.
- A set of small pure-JS modules in `packages/development/lib/` owns only what *grades the model's own claim* (Constitution Rule 8's enforcement exception, and Rule 7): base/head scope resolution, ledger validation, head-bound remote-review evaluation, terminal-status derivation with the bounded-round cap, and the untracked review-state report. A thin CLI, `pr-review-cli.js`, exposes them as JSON-in/JSON-out commands, following the `trd-cli.js` / `complete-beads-planner.js` precedent.
- `fix-issue.yaml`, `implement-trd-beads.yaml` and `complete-beads/SKILL.md` invoke the skill at their real PR boundaries; none re-states review steps.

**Alternatives considered (user chose C):**

- **Option A -- prose-only skill:** fewest files, but "no early REVIEW_COMPLETE", head-binding and the round cap would be prose a model can misread, and tests could only assert text ordering. Rejected: the plan's core guarantee would not be falsifiable (Rule 7).
- **Option B -- TypeScript runtime in agent-core:** strongest typing, but a new build/dist surface and cross-package coupling for a prompt-level feature, and it pulls editable criteria toward code (against Rule 8). Rejected.

**Rationale:** Option C is the best fit for this brownfield repo: the helper is the minimum code that makes the status contract testable and unforgeable, everything a maintainer would plausibly tune stays in a skill file, and it needs no new dependency, provider or config knob.

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-015**: Commands and skills depend on capabilities, not tools
Commands and skills depend on capabilities, not tools Priority: Must | `[RISK: about 10 heavily coupled commands plus skills must be refactored without changing default behavior]` Shared commands, agents and skills reference capabilities and resolved adapters. They no longer name a specific tool outside an adapter. Acceptance is asserted through the commands' real entry points, not around them.

--- TRD Context ---
### Alternatives Considered

| Option | Approach | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|---|
| A: Prose-only adapters | Adapter is a skill; the agent follows its prose and normalizes tool output itself | Smallest build; fully editable | Cannot route internal CLIs deterministically (REQ-016), cannot validate output (REQ-022), cannot deny at runtime (REQ-023); behavior varies per model |

| C: Executable plugin adapters | Separately packaged executables speaking a versioned JSON protocol | Arbitrary logic; strongest isolation | Contradicts the PRD's skills-as-contract decision; fails Rule 8; needs per-OS packaging and a protocol |

**Rationale:** B is the only option that makes every PRD guarantee a code-enforced property while keeping adapters user-editable data. The requester selected B at the architecture gate.

### Interpretations and Resolved Design Issues

- **I1: plain version control.** The PRD taxonomy has no plain `git` category, yet about 45 sources invoke it. Plain `git` operations (status, commit, push, log, diff, merge-base) are `vcs.*` capabilities of the `workflow` category, whose default adapter is `plain-git`; the `git-town` adapter extends it. Recommend a PRD refine pass to name this explicitly.
- **I2: ambiguity versus no signal (PRD REQ-009 AC-2 vs REQ-010 AC-2).** "No detectable signal" means no signal source exists at all (no remote, no marker files); the shipped default is used.
