- **I3: AC-023-2 (governed boundary denies).** The runner is invoked through the shell tool, so a command that was not granted the shell tool cannot run any adapter; an adapter therefore cannot widen grants. The runner additionally denies any command outside the adapter's binary-plus-subcommand allowlist. Denial of raw shell commands typed by an agent outside the runner remains host-enforced (hooks on Claude Code; none in this repo for Pi, OpenCode or Codex); the lint (REQ-019) keeps commands from issuing raw tool calls. This residual is recorded in the Threat Model.
- **I4: confirmation session identity.** No stable session id is exposed uniformly across runtimes. TRD-017 begins with a spike that records which id each runtime exposes (`ENSEMBLE_SESSION_ID`, host session variables); the passive confirmation record is keyed by `(sessionKey, category, adapter, configHash)` and falls back to the run id when no session id exists.
- **I5: repo-local adapters are untrusted by default.** A cloned repository can ship `.ensemble/adapters/`. Repo-local adapters resolve in every mode (satisfying AC-007-3) but a non-interactive run additionally requires the adapter name in the user's `trustedRepoAdapters` list; an interactive run shows the adapter's allowlist at first-use confirmation.
- **I6: no new runtime dependency.** The output-mapping engine uses a small dotted-path projection (`$.a.b[0]`, `|` alternation for "array or object"), not a JSONPath library, because constitution section 4 requires approval for new dependencies.
- **I7: work-graph selection.** `work-graph` is its own category with default `auto`: use the work-graph capabilities of the resolved tracker adapter when its manifest provides them; otherwise use the built-in `work-graph-links-fallback` adapter (tracker dependency links, then plan order stated as not dependency-aware). One manifest may implement several categories.
- **I8: PRD BDD floor.** Fourteen PRD requirements (REQ-001, 002, 004, 005, 006, 009, 010, 012, 015, 018, 021, 022, 024, 025) have two ACs, below the command's three-scenario floor. The test tasks specify exactly one scenario per AC; recommend a PRD refine pass to add edge or error ACs.
- **I10: packaging.** `packages/development` depends only on `js-yaml` and its libraries require only siblings, so the resolver library, category contracts, default selection, schemas and tool inventory all ship inside `packages/development` (`lib/toolchain/` and `toolchain/`). A standalone plugin install and the Pi vendor bundle therefore contain everything; other packages call `toolchain-cli` through `TOOLCHAIN_CLI` rather than importing it.
- **I9: preflight is enforced in code.** `toolchain-cli run` refuses a side-effecting capability unless a passing preflight record exists for the supplied `--run-id`; the command prose cannot silently skip preflight.

title: [trd:trd-2026-d6bbf322-new-feature-workflow:task:TRD-017] - [ ] **TRD-017**: Implement the PR-creation checkpoint (4h)
description:
## Task: TRD-017
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-d6bbf322-new-feature-workflow.md#trd-017
PRD Reference: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-d6bbf322-new-feature-workflow.md#req-011

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-011**: Make PR creation optional and separately approved
Make PR creation optional and separately approved Priority: Must | Complexity: High | [RISK: opening a PR is an externally visible write and may notify collaborators] Product Entry, Safety, and Compatibility

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-011-1: Given all required implementation work is reported complete | When the user chooses not to create a PR | Then the workflow records completion without making a PR-hosting service write
- AC-011-2: Given the user requests PR creation and a supported PR-creation capability is configured | When the workflow is ready to create the PR | Then it presents the target repository/branch and proposed title/body and obtains a separate, immediate explicit approval before the external create operation
- AC-011-3: Given PR approval is absent | When the workflow reaches this optional stage | Then it creates no PR, reports the outcome, and preserves the completed implementation record

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen: Option C — hardened in-session stage composition with a dedicated atomic run-index store.**

`new-feature` is authored the same way every other product command in this repo is authored: a single orchestrating skill (`packages/development/commands/new-feature.yaml`, generated to runtime-specific prompts exactly like `fix-issue.yaml`) that executes each stage's existing skill body in-session — the same mechanism that loaded `ensemble-refine-prd`'s content into this session and had the agent execute its Phases directly. This is forced, not merely preferred: Pi's `ExtensionAPI` has no completion/invoke primitive that would let an extension programmatically run another skill and get its result back (confirmed — no `pi.invokeCommand` or equivalent exists); the only code-level "run a skill" mechanism, `createAgentPort()`, spawns a bounded, disposable `omp -p --no-session --no-extensions` subprocess in an isolated worktree, and does not fit a long-lived, project-resident workflow whose PRD/TRD stages use the interactive `--collab` review server.

What is new, and is the one piece of real infrastructure this TRD adds: a `RunIndexStore` (`packages/agent-core/src/new-feature/run-index.ts`) built on the one proven concurrency-safe pattern in this repo — `session.js`'s temp-file-then-`renameSync` atomic write plus `expectedRevision`/409-style optimistic concurrency — rather than `ProposalStore`'s plain `writeFileSync` (no atomicity, no lock, not adequate for PRD AC-005-3's fail-closed-on-malformed-index requirement). Runs are stored at `.ensemble/new-feature/<run-id>.json`, mirroring `ProposalStore`'s `.ensemble/proposals/<ref>.json` convention (also excluded from `tree-baseline.ts` drift detection, so this is consistent runtime-owned state, not a project-source mutation).

### Alternatives considered

| Option | Summary | Why not chosen |
|---|---|---|
| A — Plain JSON checkpoint | Same in-session composition, but checkpoints are a single `writeFileSync`, no atomicity/locking. | Fastest to build, but a crash mid-write can corrupt the run index, which directly violates AC-005-3's "fail closed with a recoverable diagnostic" requirement — the repo's own `ProposalStore` already demonstrates this gap is real, not hypothetical. |
| B — Subprocess-dispatched stages | New orchestrator module dispatches every stage as a bounded `createAgentPort()` subprocess; advances the run index only after subprocess exit 0 + artifact-on-disk confirmation. | Most rigorous completion signal (a real process boundary instead of self-reported bookkeeping), but substantially more build effort, and does not fit the interactive `--collab` review-server stages `create-prd`/`refine-prd` already use — those are long-lived, human-attended HTTP sessions, not bounded one-shot subprocess work, and would need bespoke carve-out handling under this option. |
| **C — Hardened in-session composition** *(chosen)* | In-session stage execution (like every existing product command), backed by a dedicated atomic `RunIndexStore`. | Reuses 100% of the existing skill-composition and `ask_user`-approval infrastructure (including the `--collab` review server, which needs no special-casing), while fixing Option A's one real correctness gap with the repo's one proven atomic-write pattern. Matches user-confirmed direction. |

### Honest trust-boundary note

Because stage execution stays in-session (per Option C), the approval gates implemented by TRD-014/TRD-017/TRD-019 are enforced by the orchestrating skill's own conditional logic checking `RunIndexStore`-persisted approval fields before it issues an implementation or `gh pr create` tool call — not by a separate runtime authorization chokepoint like `agent-core`'s `MutationGuard` (which exists elsewhere in this repo, gating CQRS-registered commands, but `new-feature`'s mutating actions are ordinary skill-level tool calls, same as `fix-issue`'s own gated PR-creation step, not CQRS commands). This is the same trust boundary every existing Ensemble product command already operates under. Building a `MutationGuard`-equivalent chokepoint for skill-level tool calls is a materially larger investment this PRD does not request and no other product command has; REQ-014's "runtime authority" is satisfied here by making the check a required precondition over persisted, validated store state rather than over prompt claims — which is what AC-014-2 actually asks for — not by inventing a new enforcement subsystem.
Satisfies: REQ-011
PRD ACs: AC-011-1, AC-011-2, AC-011-3
Target File: packages/development/commands/new-feature.yaml
Actions:
1. PR creation is entered only if the user opts in after implementation completes; declining records completion with no `PrProvider` call made at all.
2. On opt-in with `PrProvider.isAvailable() === true`, present the target repository/branch and proposed title/body via `ask_user`, then require a separate, immediate explicit approval before calling `createPullRequest()`.
3. On `mutate()`, set `prApprovedAt = now()` only after that separate approval, immediately before the create call — never in the same approval step as implementation.
4. On absent/declined approval, or `isAvailable() === false`, create no PR, report the outcome, and leave the completed implementation record untouched.
Implementation AC:
- [ ] Given the user declines PR creation, when completion is recorded, then no `gh pr create` invocation occurs.
- [ ] Given approval is granted, when the create call is made, then it is preceded by a presentation of the exact target repo/branch/title/body and a separate approval distinct from the implementation approval.
- [ ] Given `isAvailable()` is `false`, when the PR stage is reached, then no PR is created and the implementation completion record is preserved unchanged.
Dependencies: TRD-016, TRD-014
close_reason: Implemented + tests green

Execution layer follows the resolved tracker Priority: Must | `[RISK: amends PRD-2026-b6939c7c REQ-015; affects ready-work scheduling in implementation commands]` The earlier rule that the default tracker is always the sole dependency-graph and ready-work engine is replaced. **Acceptance Criteria:**

--- TRD Context ---
### Alternatives Considered

| Option | Approach | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|---|
| A: Prose-only adapters | Adapter is a skill; the agent follows its prose and normalizes tool output itself | Smallest build; fully editable | Cannot route internal CLIs deterministically (REQ-016), cannot validate output (REQ-022), cannot deny at runtime (REQ-023); behavior varies per model |
| **B: Manifest plus runner (chosen)** | Adapter is a skill directory: `SKILL.md` (vocabulary and agent-facing prose) plus a declarative `adapter.yaml` (capability command templates, output mapping, allowlist, health check, detection signals, required env names). A core resolver library and `toolchain-cli` execute capabilities deterministically | Meets PRD (adapter is a skill), Rule 8 (editable without rebuild), Rule 5 (enforcement in code), REQ-016 (CLIs call the same library) | New resolver, runner, manifest schema and output-mapping engine to build and test |
| C: Executable plugin adapters | Separately packaged executables speaking a versioned JSON protocol | Arbitrary logic; strongest isolation | Contradicts the PRD's skills-as-contract decision; fails Rule 8; needs per-OS packaging and a protocol |

**Rationale:** B is the only option that makes every PRD guarantee a code-enforced property while keeping adapters user-editable data. The requester selected B at the architecture gate.

### Interpretations and Resolved Design Issues

- **I1: plain version control.** The PRD taxonomy has no plain `git` category, yet about 45 sources invoke it. Plain `git` operations (status, commit, push, log, diff, merge-base) are `vcs.*` capabilities of the `workflow` category, whose default adapter is `plain-git`; the `git-town` adapter extends it. Recommend a PRD refine pass to name this explicitly.
- **I2: ambiguity versus no signal (PRD REQ-009 AC-2 vs REQ-010 AC-2).** "No detectable signal" means no signal source exists at all (no remote, no marker files); the shipped default is used. "Ambiguous" means two or more installed adapters match, or a signal source exists (for example a remote URL) but matches no installed adapter; resolution fails explicitly in non-interactive runs and asks in interactive runs.
- **I3: AC-023-2 (governed boundary denies).** The runner is invoked through the shell tool, so a command that was not granted the shell tool cannot run any adapter; an adapter therefore cannot widen grants. The runner additionally denies any command outside the adapter's binary-plus-subcommand allowlist. Denial of raw shell commands typed by an agent outside the runner remains host-enforced (hooks on Claude Code; none in this repo for Pi, OpenCode or Codex); the lint (REQ-019) keeps commands from issuing raw tool calls. This residual is recorded in the Threat Model.
- **I4: confirmation session identity.** No stable session id is exposed uniformly across runtimes. TRD-017 begins with a spike that records which id each runtime exposes (`ENSEMBLE_SESSION_ID`, host session variables); the passive confirmation record is keyed by `(sessionKey, category, adapter, configHash)` and falls back to the run id when no session id exists.
- **I5: repo-local adapters are untrusted by default.** A cloned repository can ship `.ensemble/adapters/`. Repo-local adapters resolve in every mode (satisfying AC-007-3) but a non-interactive run additionally requires the adapter name in the user's `trustedRepoAdapters` list; an interactive run shows the adapter's allowlist at first-use confirmation.
- **I6: no new runtime dependency.** The output-mapping engine uses a small dotted-path projection (`$.a.b[0]`, `|` alternation for "array or object"), not a JSONPath library, because constitution section 4 requires approval for new dependencies.
- **I7: work-graph selection.** `work-graph` is its own category with default `auto`: use the work-graph capabilities of the resolved tracker adapter when its manifest provides them; otherwise use the built-in `work-graph-links-fallback` adapter (tracker dependency links, then plan order stated as not dependency-aware). One manifest may implement several categories.
- **I8: PRD BDD floor.** Fourteen PRD requirements (REQ-001, 002, 004, 005, 006, 009, 010, 012, 015, 018, 021, 022, 024, 025) have two ACs, below the command's three-scenario floor. The test tasks specify exactly one scenario per AC; recommend a PRD refine pass to add edge or error ACs.
- **I10: packaging.** `packages/development` depends only on `js-yaml` and its libraries require only siblings, so the resolver library, category contracts, default selection, schemas and tool inventory all ship inside `packages/development` (`lib/toolchain/` and `toolchain/`). A standalone plugin install and the Pi vendor bundle therefore contain everything; other packages call `toolchain-cli` through `TOOLCHAIN_CLI` rather than importing it.
- **I9: preflight is enforced in code.** `toolchain-cli run` refuses a side-effecting capability unless a passing preflight record exists for the supplied `--run-id`; the command prose cannot silently skip preflight.

title: [trd:trd-2026-b6db9749-behavior-habits-runtime:task:TRD-032] - [ ] **TRD-032** Define the local-acceptance / queued / delivered / committed-by-Foreman states (3h)
description:
## Task: TRD-032
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-b6db9749-behavior-habits-runtime.md#trd-032
PRD Reference: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-b6db9749-behavior-habits-runtime.md#req-025

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-025**: A versioned contract distinguishes local-acceptance states from Foreman commitment
A versioned contract distinguishes local-acceptance states from Foreman commitment Priority: Could [RISK: listed as an unresolved decision in the governing architecture doc §14; not required for this PRD's own exit criteria]

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-025-1: Given a governed tool call succeeds locally | When its result status is reported | Then it is exactly one of "accepted locally," "queued locally," "delivered," or "committed by Foreman" — never conflated

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen: Option B — dedicated adapter modules per new trigger-source type, plus a shared notification-state module.** Unchanged from 1.0.0.

New `file-source-adapter.ts` and `release-source-adapter.ts` under `packages/agent-core/src/behavior/` each produce a `BehaviorEvent` through `normalizeEvent`, mirroring the existing `pi-events.ts` → `event-translator.ts` → `normalizeEvent` → `LocalEventMatcher` chain. A new `notification-state.ts` in `pi-extension` centralises busy, duplicate and stale tracking for every behavior. Package quarantine gets its own `package-quarantine.ts` beside `package-discovery.ts`.

### Decisions added in 1.1.0

1. **How artifact changes are detected: content hashes checked at lifecycle points.** No `fs.watch`, no new dependency.
   - The adapter derives its watch set from the compiled `artifact.changed` triggers (the `path` predicate).
   - It hashes those files at `tool_result` and at `agent_end`, and emits an event when a digest differs from the last one seen in the session.
   - The hooks it relies on already exist, which is what AC-001-2 means by "supported host API".
   - It behaves the same on every OS (see REQ-023).
   - It needs no new dependency, which constitution §4 would require approval for.

   | Option | Why not chosen |
   |---|---|
   | `fs.watch` | Event semantics differ between macOS, Linux and Windows (rename-vs-change, recursive support). That is exactly the kind of per-platform behavior difference REQ-023 forbids absorbing silently. It also keeps a handle open for the whole session. |
   | `chokidar` | A new runtime dependency (constitution §4), for a problem that lifecycle-point hashing already solves. |

   The limitation, stated rather than hidden: a change is seen at the next tool call or at the end of the run, not instantly. NFR-001 measures from event validation, so this latency is outside its budget. TRD-003 reports it separately.

2. **Release signal (resolves the PRD's REQ-002 clarification): a new `v*` tag in local refs.** This matches this repo's `release.yml` (`on: push: tags: ['v*']`).
   - The tag pattern is a trigger predicate, so repositories with different conventions change configuration, not code (Rule 8).
   - It is detected two ways. First, from a successful tag-creating tool call (`git tag`, `gh release create`), in the same way `repository.changed` is derived today. Second, by diffing tag refs at session start and at `agent_end`, which covers tags that arrive by fetch.
   - It emits the **existing** catalog type `release.completed`, carrying `{ tag, sha, source }`.
   - One tag produces one event per session, whichever path sees it first.

3. **Coverage metric (resolves the PRD's REQ-016 clarification): Jest `json-summary` output, per file, `lines.pct` and `branches.pct` by default.**
   - Each package's `test:coverage` is `jest --coverage`. Jest's default reporters (`json`, `lcov`, `text`, `clover`) produce raw maps, not percentages.
   - So the behavior watches `coverage/coverage-summary.json`, and its README tells repositories to enable `json-summary`.
   - The metrics and the threshold (default 1.0 percentage point) are behavior configuration.
   - If the artifact never appears, the behavior shows up as an inert trigger in `/ensemble-status`; it is never silently idle.
   - The baseline is the previous snapshot seen **in the same session** (Rule 4). The first observation in a session only sets the baseline.

4. **The comparison is a generic command: `artifact.compare` (TRD-033).** It compares numeric JSON paths between the previous and current snapshot of an artifact and knows nothing about coverage.
   - The alternatives were rejected. Doing the comparison in an agent step would make the reported delta an unverified model claim (REQ-012). A coverage-specific command would make the third behavior need Ensemble code (REQ-018).
   - It lands in PR 1, which is why PR 5 can be configuration only.

5. **Notification transport** (REQ-009, REQ-010). `notification-state.ts` delivers to two sinks:
   - **The user**, through `SessionUiBridge.notify`, a new method that wraps `ctx.ui.notify`. Headless sessions fall back to the console.
   - **The model's context**, through `pi.sendMessage` with `display: true` and `triggerTurn: false`.

   `triggerTurn: false` is deliberate. #107 deleted the continuation path because a message that makes the agent act bypasses `MutationGuard` (`extension.ts:118-140`); a notification is data, never an instruction. Any test-derived text in a notification is fenced and labelled as data, a lesson from #94's live runs. `sendMessage` is added to `assertRequiredCapabilities`.

6. **Verified fix application** (REQ-033). This is configuration plus two small code changes.
   - A new behavior, `apply-verified-fix`, runs `mode: auto`. It triggers on `fix.verified` with the predicate `verdict: passed`, declares only `fix.apply` with no tools, and calls `fix.apply { proposalRef: ${event.payload.proposalRef} }`.
   - `CommandRegistry` then asks `ApprovalGate`. Today the prompt is only `descriptor.description` ("Apply a verified fix proposal…"), so the human would approve without seeing what changes. Code change 1 (TRD-019): the prompt names the proposal, its files and a diff summary.
   - `commit-policy.ts` has no importers today. Code change 2 (TRD-021): wire it in so an applied fix is committed with attribution.

### Alternatives considered (architecture)

| Option | Summary | Why not chosen |
|---|---|---|
| **A — Widen the existing translator, inline notification** | Add file and release branches inside `event-translator.ts`; keep notification-state logic at each `ctx.ui.notify` call site. | `event-translator.ts` would cover three unrelated source domains. Busy/duplicate/stale logic would be copied per behavior, which is the per-reaction duplication the PRD sets out to remove. |
| **B — Dedicated adapter modules + shared notification-state module** *(chosen)* | One adapter module per source type, all feeding the same ingress; one shared notification-state module. | Matches the existing boundary (`agent-core` = provider-neutral logic, `pi-extension` = host wiring), and centralises notification state once. |
| **C — Single generic "external signal" adapter** | One configurable "watch path X for condition Y" abstraction for both sources. | Risks becoming an arbitrary-condition escape hatch around the closed, versioned catalog (REQ-CQRS-005); still duplicates notification state. |
Satisfies: REQ-025

## Task: TRD-027
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-15aa5acd-live-behavior-dispatch-autofix.md#trd-027
PRD Reference: #req-005

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen: Option C — single enforcement seam, additive.**

A new `MutationGuard` chokepoint in `agent-core` is the one place `policy.mode`, `capabilities.mutation_classes` (via the existing `hasMutationAuthority()`), and protected-path rules are resolved. It is wired once at the loader boundary rather than replicated per tool registration. The translator, matcher, and auto-fix loop are added to `pi-extension`. Discovery roots and `execution.test_command` are additive changes to existing schema/discovery code. `ToolRegistry`, `outbox`, and the compiler are reused unchanged.

### Alternatives considered

| Option | Summary | Why not chosen |
|---|---|---|
| **A — In-place extension** | Enforce mode/mutation/path rules as wrapper checks inside `behavior-loader`'s per-tool `execute()` closures. | Enforcement scattered across call sites; every future tool registration must remember to wrap. The PRD's central failure mode is *guarantees that exist in one place but are not reached from another* — Option A reproduces exactly that shape. |
| **B — Governance kernel** | Route every mutation through a `MutationBroker` + `GovernedWorkspace` in `agent-core`; `pi-extension` becomes a thin adapter. | Strongest long-term design and the right eventual target, but it re-opens already-shipped code across every tool path for a ~6-7 PR refactor before a single PRD requirement is demonstrable. Deferred deliberately, not rejected. |
| **C — Single enforcement seam** *(chosen)* | One `MutationGuard` chokepoint, wired once; everything else additive. | Gets a single auditable chokepoint (Option B's main benefit) without Option B's refactor surface. Fits the existing `agent-core` / `pi-extension` split. |

### Architectural note carried from grounding

Two defects found while grounding this design are folded into PR 1 rather than left implicit:

1. `pi-events.ts` emits `runtime.tool_result` / `runtime.tool.called` / `runtime.tool.failed` / `runtime.tool.completed`, none of which appear in `HARNESS_EVENT_TYPES` (which defines `runtime.tool_call.started` / `runtime.tool_call.completed`). `normalizeEvent` does not currently reject uncatalogued types, so PRD AC-002-1's "validated against the closed catalog" would be vacuous. Addressed by TRD-001 (`[satisfies INFRA]`).
2. `behavior-loader.ts:79` calls `registry.grant(...)` unconditionally immediately before `registry.invoke(...)`, making the grant boundary a rubber stamp for behavior-governed tools (unlike the echo path, where the grant is CLI-flag-gated). Addressed by TRD-003.

**Chosen approach (Option C):** One shared, prose-defined review procedure plus a small deterministic helper library.

- `packages/development/skills/pr-review-cycle/SKILL.md` is the single reusable procedure. It owns the *user-editable* parts (Constitution Rule 8): review criteria, the order of the loop, the 10-minute interactive wait, Foreman-mode rules. It **composes** `packages/quality/skills/pr-review-remediation/SKILL.md` for per-finding triage, regression tests and minimal fixes and does not restate those rules.
- A set of small pure-JS modules in `packages/development/lib/` owns only what *grades the model's own claim* (Constitution Rule 8's enforcement exception, and Rule 7): base/head scope resolution, ledger validation, head-bound remote-review evaluation, terminal-status derivation with the bounded-round cap, and the untracked review-state report. A thin CLI, `pr-review-cli.js`, exposes them as JSON-in/JSON-out commands, following the `trd-cli.js` / `complete-beads-planner.js` precedent.
- `fix-issue.yaml`, `implement-trd-beads.yaml` and `complete-beads/SKILL.md` invoke the skill at their real PR boundaries; none re-states review steps.

**Alternatives considered (user chose C):**

- **Option A -- prose-only skill:** fewest files, but "no early REVIEW_COMPLETE", head-binding and the round cap would be prose a model can misread, and tests could only assert text ordering. Rejected: the plan's core guarantee would not be falsifiable (Rule 7).
- **Option B -- TypeScript runtime in agent-core:** strongest typing, but a new build/dist surface and cross-package coupling for a prompt-level feature, and it pulls editable criteria toward code (against Rule 8). Rejected.

**Rationale:** Option C is the best fit for this brownfield repo: the helper is the minimum code that makes the status contract testable and unforgeable, everything a maintainer would plausibly tune stays in a skill file, and it needs no new dependency, provider or config knob.

Full title: - [ ] **TRD-048** Taxonomy coverage check: complete `packages/development/toolchain/tool-inventory.yaml` (tool binary to exactly one of the 14 categories, plus `ignoredCommands` for generic shell words) and add `scripts/lib/taxonomy-coverage.js` plus `scripts/check-taxonomy-coverage.js` (guarded by `require.main`, exported `checkCoverage(root)`): a tool mapped to two categories fails, a command-position token in a shared source's fenced shell block that is neither in the inventory nor in `ignoredCommands` fails with class `UNMAPPED_TOOL`, naming file and tool, and every category in `packages/development/toolchain/categories/` must have exactly one default in `packages/development/toolchain/toolchain.default.yaml` whose adapter directory exists; wire into `npm run validate` (5h)

## Task: TRD-048
## References
TRD: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-8d825f54-tool-abstraction-layer.md
TRD Task: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-8d825f54-tool-abstraction-layer.md#trd-048

PRD ACs: AC-001-1, AC-001-2, AC-006-1
Parent Epic: [trd:trd-2026-8d825f54-tool-abstraction-layer]
Read-first: read the TRD, TRD Task section, PRD and PRD Requirement above before any work on this bead.


--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-001**: Capability taxonomy covering all tool categories
Capability taxonomy covering all tool categories Priority: Must Ensemble defines a taxonomy of tool categories covering every external tool its sources invoke: source-control host and change requests, branching workflow, worktree manager, work tracking, work graph and ready-work queue, local CI, review automation, lint automation, test runner, end-to-end and quality checks, container and deployment, infrastructure as code, platform and cloud, and package/build runner. The CI category covers only tools an agent invokes to run CI locally; hosted CI definitions are repository infrastructure and out of scope.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-001-1: Given the tool inventory of shared command | When each tool is checked against the taxonomy | Then every tool maps to exactly one category
- AC-001-2: Given a shared source that invokes a tool belonging to no category | When validation runs | Then it fails and names the file and the unmapped tool
- AC-006-1: Given each category in the taxonomy | When shipped adapters are listed | Then each category has a default adapter

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-006**: Default adapters for every category
Default adapters for every category Priority: Must Every category in the taxonomy ships with a default adapter reproducing ensemble's current behavior for the tool currently used.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-001-1: Given the tool inventory of shared command | When each tool is checked against the taxonomy | Then every tool maps to exactly one category
- AC-001-2: Given a shared source that invokes a tool belonging to no category | When validation runs | Then it fails and names the file and the unmapped tool
- AC-006-1: Given each category in the taxonomy | When shipped adapters are listed | Then each category has a default adapter

--- TRD Context ---
### Alternatives Considered

| Option | Approach | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|---|
| A: Prose-only adapters | Adapter is a skill; the agent follows its prose and normalizes tool output itself | Smallest build; fully editable | Cannot route internal CLIs deterministically (REQ-016), cannot validate output (REQ-022), cannot deny at runtime (REQ-023); behavior varies per model |
| **B: Manifest plus runner (chosen)** | Adapter is a skill directory: `SKILL.md` (vocabulary and agent-facing prose) plus a declarative `adapter.yaml` (capability command templates, output mapping, allowlist, health check, detection signals, required env names). A core resolver library and `toolchain-cli` execute capabilities deterministically | Meets PRD (adapter is a skill), Rule 8 (editable without rebuild), Rule 5 (enforcement in code), REQ-016 (CLIs call the same library) | New resolver, runner, manifest schema and output-mapping engine to build and test |
| C: Executable plugin adapters | Separately packaged executables speaking a versioned JSON protocol | Arbitrary logic; strongest isolation | Contradicts the PRD's skills-as-contract decision; fails Rule 8; needs per-OS packaging and a protocol |

**Rationale:** B is the only option that makes every PRD guarantee a code-enforced property while keeping adapters user-editable data. The requester selected B at the architecture gate.

### Interpretations and Resolved Design Issues

- **I1: plain version control.** The PRD taxonomy has no plain `git` category, yet about 45 sources invoke it. Plain `git` operations (status, commit, push, log, diff, merge-base) are `vcs.*` capabilities of the `workflow` category, whose default adapter is `plain-git`; the `git-town` adapter extends it. Recommend a PRD refine pass to name this explicitly.
- **I2: ambiguity versus no signal (PRD REQ-009 AC-2 vs REQ-010 AC-2).** "No detectable signal" means no signal source exists at all (no remote, no marker files); the shipped default is used. "Ambiguous" means two or more installed adapters match, or a signal source exists (for example a remote URL) but matches no installed adapter; resolution fails explicitly in non-interactive runs and asks in interactive runs.
- **I3: AC-023-2 (governed boundary denies).** The runner is invoked through the shell tool, so a command that was not granted the shell tool cannot run any adapter; an adapter therefore cannot widen grants. The runner additionally denies any command outside the adapter's binary-plus-subcommand allowlist. Denial of raw shell commands typed by an agent outside the runner remains host-enforced (hooks on Claude Code; none in this repo for Pi, OpenCode or Codex); the lint (REQ-019) keeps commands from issuing raw tool calls. This residual is recorded in the Threat Model.
- **I4: confirmation session identity.** No stable session id is exposed uniformly across runtimes. TRD-017 begins with a spike that records which id each runtime exposes (`ENSEMBLE_SESSION_ID`, host session variables); the passive confirmation record is keyed by `(sessionKey, category, adapter, configHash)` and falls back to the run id when no session id exists.
- **I5: repo-local adapters are untrusted by default.** A cloned repository can ship `.ensemble/adapters/`. Repo-local adapters resolve in every mode (satisfying AC-007-3) but a non-interactive run additionally requires the adapter name in the user's `trustedRepoAdapters` list; an interactive run shows the adapter's allowlist at first-use confirmation.
- **I6: no new runtime dependency.** The output-mapping engine uses a small dotted-path projection (`$.a.b[0]`, `|` alternation for "array or object"), not a JSONPath library, because constitution section 4 requires approval for new dependencies.
- **I7: work-graph selection.** `work-graph` is its own category with default `auto`: use the work-graph capabilities of the resolved tracker adapter when its manifest provides them; otherwise use the built-in `work-graph-links-fallback` adapter (tracker dependency links, then plan order stated as not dependency-aware). One manifest may implement several categories.
- **I8: PRD BDD floor.** Fourteen PRD requirements (REQ-001, 002, 004, 005, 006, 009, 010, 012, 015, 018, 021, 022, 024, 025) have two ACs, below the command's three-scenario floor. The test tasks specify exactly one scenario per AC; recommend a PRD refine pass to add edge or error ACs.
- **I10: packaging.** `packages/development` depends only on `js-yaml` and its libraries require only siblings, so the resolver library, category contracts, default selection, schemas and tool inventory all ship inside `packages/development` (`lib/toolchain/` and `toolchain/`). A standalone plugin install and the Pi vendor bundle therefore contain everything; other packages call `toolchain-cli` through `TOOLCHAIN_CLI` rather than importing it.
- **I9: preflight is enforced in code.** `toolchain-cli run` refuses a side-effecting capability unless a passing preflight record exists for the supplied `--run-id`; the command prose cannot silently skip preflight.
Satisfies: REQ-001, REQ-006

Evidence is published where branch protection can enforce it (Must) [RISK: verified -- the required checks on `dev` are pinned to the GitHub Actions app (app id 15368); a status posted with a personal token or the `gh` CLI is not from that app and will not satisfy them, leaving the PR unmergeable] The local run's result is published to GitHub as a status on the head commit, posted by a maintainer-owned GitHub App under a name that branch protection can pin to that app.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-004-3: Given branch protection on the target branch requires the local-run status pinned to the maintainer-owned app | When a PR has only a hosted-CI success and no local status | Then it cannot merge; and when it has a passing status from the app, then it can
- AC-014-1: Given the local gate has been enabled | When the maintainer follows the documented rollback | Then branch protection requires the hosted checks again and the merge flow honors CodeRabbit as before
- AC-016-1: Given one of those commands is about to open a PR | When it runs the local gate and it passes | Then the PR is opened with the approval status already published for its head commit

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen approach (Option C):** A `local-ci-gate` skill owns the editable procedure; a small set of pure-JS helpers in `packages/development/lib/` owns only what must be unforgeable; `pr-merge.yaml` invokes the skill.

- `packages/development/skills/local-ci-gate/SKILL.md` is the single reusable procedure and owns everything a maintainer would plausibly tune (Constitution Rule 8): the order of the run, the messages, the bead wording, and how failures are explained.
- Pure-JS modules in `packages/development/lib/` own only what grades a claim or protects a boundary (Rules 7 and 8's enforcement exception): run-record verification, bot-vs-human classification, bead dedupe keys, approval-set config validation, and GitHub App credential handling. They make no network calls except the one module whose purpose is to post a status.
- `packages/git/commands/pr-merge.yaml` calls the skill at its existing Merge phase. It does not restate gate logic.
- The gate runs in-session in the maintainer's own process. There is no daemon, scheduler or background sweep (Rule 4; REQ-012).

**Alternatives considered (user chose C):**

- **Option A -- prose-only:** fewest files, but head-binding, run-record verification and human/bot classification would be prose a model can misread, and tests could only assert wording. Rejected: the PRD's core property is that evidence cannot be reused across commits.
- **Option B -- TypeScript runtime in agent-core:** strongest typing, but adds a build/dist surface and pulls editable criteria toward code against Rule 8. Rejected: the one place a real client is tempting (App JWT signing) needs only Node's built-in `crypto`.

**Dependency decision (user approved):** no new dependency. The App's RS256 JWT is signed with Node `crypto`; the REST calls use `fetch`. This avoids the constitution's new-dependency approval gate and keeps the signing path small and auditable.

**Rationale:** Option C matches repository precedent (TRD-2026-82b6a138), keeps editable behavior out of TypeScript, and is the minimum code that makes the trust properties testable.

title: [trd:trd-2026-70e784f2-code-review-process:task:TRD-012] - [ ] **TRD-012** Round-cap cutover: one shared cap in status, pr-merge and quality loop (6h)
description:
## Task: TRD-012
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-70e784f2-code-review-process.md#trd-012
PRD Reference: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-70e784f2-code-review-process.md#req-009

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-009**: One round policy for every review procedure (Must)
One round policy for every review procedure (Must) A single round cap governs `pr-review-cycle` and `pr-merge`, replacing the current 2 and 5.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-009-1: Given any ensemble review procedure runs on a PR | When the round count reaches the cap | Then the reviewer stops iterating and asks the author to step back and reconsider the approach
- AC-009-2: Given no repository setting | When the cap applies | Then it is 3 rounds; a repository may configure any value from 1 to 5, and a value outside that range is ignored with a warning and the default is used
- AC-009-3: Given a repository sets a different cap in its review rules | When review runs | Then that value is used by every procedure and no procedure keeps a private number
- AC-009-4: Given PRD-2026-82b6a138 stated a 2-round cap | When this requirement ships | Then that PRD is updated so it no longer contradicts the shared cap

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen approach (Option C):** extend the pattern TRD-2026-82b6a138 established: **editable behavior in skills, agents and markdown; a small set of pure, deterministic libraries for what must not be self-certified by a model.**

- **User-owned (Constitution Rule 8), prose or data a maintainer edits without a toolchain:** per-area rules (`REVIEW.md` files), the policy block inside the root `REVIEW.md` (round cap, depth table, bot and maintainer logins, sensitive and High paths, Low-waiver state), severity definitions, reviewer, verifier, classifier and security-lane prompts, the PR template, the sweep and explainer procedures. All of it is read from the **target branch**, never from the PR head (REQ-024).
- **Enforcement (Rules 5 and 7), code that grades a model's claim:** vote tally, tier assignment with its sensitive-path floor and Low-waiver evidence, approval evaluation bound to a commit, the merge gate, round-cap derivation, repeat suppression, delta-range selection, depth bounds, slice coverage, metrics and eval scoring. Each is a pure CommonJS module in `packages/development/lib/`, exposed as a JSON-in/JSON-out subcommand of the existing `pr-review-cli.js`, following the 82b6a138 precedent. None performs network I/O or holds a timer.
- **Entry points (Rule 6):** every capability is reached through the one `pr-review-cycle` skill, which `fix-issue`, `implement-trd-beads` and `pr-merge` already invoke or will invoke (a new `MODE=gate` for `pr-merge`). YAML callers reference the skill only, never the CLI, as the existing parity tests require.
- **Recurrence (Rule 4):** nightly or weekly sweeps and daily eval runs are on-demand skills; a workflow template for the host repository is opt-in and scaffolded by init-project. Ensemble's own workflows gain no `schedule` trigger.

**Alternatives considered (user chose C):**

- **Option A -- prose-only skills and agents:** fewest files and fastest to ship. Rejected: the vote threshold, the tier floor, commit-bound approvals and the round cap would be prose a model can misread or skip, so none of these gates could be shown to fail (Rule 7), and "a bot approval never counts" would be a request, not a guarantee.
- **Option B -- a new TypeScript review engine in `agent-core`:** strongest typing and one runtime. Rejected: a new build and `dist` surface and cross-package coupling for a prompt-level feature, editable criteria pulled into code (against Rule 8), and drift toward an ensemble-owned dispatcher that competes with Foreman (Rule 4).

**Rationale:** Option C is the best fit for this brownfield repo. It adds only the code that grades claims, keeps everything a maintainer or adopting team would tune in files they can edit, adds no dependency (Constitution §4) and no CI secret, vendors into Pi automatically through the existing require-closure bundler, and each gate can be mutation-proven using the harness that already exists.

**Decisions taken where the PRD left a choice** (each is editable policy, not a hidden constant):

| Decision | Value | Where it lives |
|---|---|---|

PRD Reference: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-70e784f2-code-review-process.md#req-022

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-022**: Explainers for context sharing (Should)
Explainers for context sharing (Should) Anyone can get an up-to-date explainer for a slice of the codebase, replacing line-by-line reading of trivial diffs for learning. Cross-cutting requirements

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-022-3: Given a PR is High tier | When its review report is produced | Then it offers an explainer for each touched sensitive module, and an explainer is generated only if requested

--- TRD Context ---
**Chosen approach (Option C):** extend the pattern TRD-2026-82b6a138 established: **editable behavior in skills, agents and markdown; a small set of pure, deterministic libraries for what must not be self-certified by a model.**

- **User-owned (Constitution Rule 8), prose or data a maintainer edits without a toolchain:** per-area rules (`REVIEW.md` files), the policy block inside the root `REVIEW.md` (round cap, depth table, bot and maintainer logins, sensitive and High paths, Low-waiver state), severity definitions, reviewer, verifier, classifier and security-lane prompts, the PR template, the sweep and explainer procedures. All of it is read from the **target branch**, never from the PR head (REQ-024).
- **Enforcement (Rules 5 and 7), code that grades a model's claim:** vote tally, tier assignment with its sensitive-path floor and Low-waiver evidence, approval evaluation bound to a commit, the merge gate, round-cap derivation, repeat suppression, delta-range selection, depth bounds, slice coverage, metrics and eval scoring. Each is a pure CommonJS module in `packages/development/lib/`, exposed as a JSON-in/JSON-out subcommand of the existing `pr-review-cli.js`, following the 82b6a138 precedent. None performs network I/O or holds a timer.
- **Entry points (Rule 6):** every capability is reached through the one `pr-review-cycle` skill, which `fix-issue`, `implement-trd-beads` and `pr-merge` already invoke or will invoke (a new `MODE=gate` for `pr-merge`). YAML callers reference the skill only, never the CLI, as the existing parity tests require.
- **Recurrence (Rule 4):** nightly or weekly sweeps and daily eval runs are on-demand skills; a workflow template for the host repository is opt-in and scaffolded by init-project. Ensemble's own workflows gain no `schedule` trigger.

**Alternatives considered (user chose C):**

- **Option A -- prose-only skills and agents:** fewest files and fastest to ship. Rejected: the vote threshold, the tier floor, commit-bound approvals and the round cap would be prose a model can misread or skip, so none of these gates could be shown to fail (Rule 7), and "a bot approval never counts" would be a request, not a guarantee.
- **Option B -- a new TypeScript review engine in `agent-core`:** strongest typing and one runtime. Rejected: a new build and `dist` surface and cross-package coupling for a prompt-level feature, editable criteria pulled into code (against Rule 8), and drift toward an ensemble-owned dispatcher that competes with Foreman (Rule 4).

**Rationale:** Option C is the best fit for this brownfield repo. It adds only the code that grades claims, keeps everything a maintainer or adopting team would tune in files they can edit, adds no dependency (Constitution §4) and no CI secret, vendors into Pi automatically through the existing require-closure bundler, and each gate can be mutation-proven using the harness that already exists.

title: Behavior: pre-PR verification gate (tests, typecheck, lint, and non-vacuity)
description:
RECOMMENDATION 2 of 5. The user's own suggestion, scoped tighter than 'ensure tests pass'.

TRIGGER: pull_request.proposed.
ACTION: in an isolated workspace run tests, typecheck and lint; block on failure AND on vacuous success.

WHY THE NON-VACUITY CLAUSE MATTERS: a gate that accepts 'Tests: 0 total, exit 0' is worse than no gate, because it manufactures confidence. See br-cwrh for the evidence that this is the dominant local failure shape, and br-91nr for the same defect in the router/pytest path.

WORK: one new command verification.run -- like fix.verify but not bound to a proposal -- reusing createIsolatedWorkspace and verifyOutput. Depends on br-cwrh landing the non-vacuity signal first.

Start in propose mode. Promote to blocking only after it has been right for a sustained period: a gate that is wrong twice in a week teaches people to bypass it.
close_reason: verification.run command + pre-pr-verification behavior delivered in propose mode. Non-vacuity checked BEFORE verdict so a zero-test run is never reported as a pass. 19 tests. The blocking half is NOT delivered and cannot be: see comment.

comments.author: ldangelo
comments.text:
DELIVERED AS A REPORTER, NOT A GATE -- and the difference is not cosmetic.

PREMISE CHECKED FIRST, because br-jg0l failed on exactly this. A behavior CANNOT block a PR:
- It is an asynchronous observer. Nothing waits on its verdict.
- Worse, its run may not even resolve before the session ends -- workflow-dispatch.ts writes the dispatch record BEFORE entering the interpreter precisely because 'the session's lifetime is not ours to control' (br-mr22).
- Branch protection's required checks are ['release-gate','source-branch']. Blocking means being one of those, i.e. CI.
So 'promote to blocking after it has been right for a sustained period' is not available through this mechanism. That is not a maturity gate; the path does not exist. If blocking is wanted, it belongs in .github/workflows as a required check, which is the shape br-jg0l settled on for the same reason.

WHAT LANDED:
- verification.run (agent-core/src/cqrs/commands.ts) -- runs a command in an isolated workspace against the tree AS IT STANDS. Separate command rather than an optional proposalRef on fix.verify, because an optional binding on a security-relevant command is how the binding ends up skipped. Refuses to fall back to the live tree when isolation is unavailable: verifying in the live tree would make verification a mutation.
- vacuous is its OWN result field, not folded into the verdict. 'Your code is broken' and 'nothing was checked' send a reader to completely different places; a consumer seeing only 'not passed' loses that and sends them to debug code that never ran.
- .ensemble/behaviors/pre-pr-verification/ -- tests, typecheck, lint as three separate runs (a && b && c reports only the first failure; this reports everything wrong in one pass). Vacuity is branched on BEFORE the verdict: a vacuous run is inconclusive, so a naive 'is it passed?' branch would route it to the failure arm and describe 'nothing ran' as 'tests failed'.
- 19 tests (7 command, 12 package).

TRIGGER IS LEGITIMATE, per br-d7lm: pull_request.proposed is LAUNCH-INPUT. Nothing here emits or awaits it; Foreman starts a session with it as the triggering fact. So the behavior is reachable, and explainInertTrigger correctly stays silent about it.

DEFECT FOUND WHILE AUTHORING, filed as br-n3gj: I wrote 'next:' on command steps and it compiled clean. There is no such field -- flow is declaration order. Both shipped manifests now say so, and the tests assert the order so a reorder fails the build.

title: No RCA stage: the rule provider is asked to judge a constitution change with no diagnosis in hand
description:
The stated product is: failing test -> RCA -> constitution updated to prevent
recurrence -> fix -> verify. What actually ships is detect -> fix -> verify
(-> hold, after br-xz6q). Steps 2 and 3 do not run, and cannot.

EVIDENCE (first live end-to-end run, loop-trial, 2026-09-28)
Record kinds in .ensemble/runtime-log.jsonl:
  activation, dispatch, continuation, invocation, verification, event x40
No rca record. No constitution record. The trial behavior DOES grant
constitution.propose, so this is not a capability denial -- the step never
executed.

ROOT CAUSE: same shape as br-xz6q -- the feature lives on the path that does
not run.

  proposeConstitutionChange is CALLED in exactly one place:
    packages/pi-extension/src/behavior-runner.ts:241 (inside runBehavior)
  extension.ts only WIRES the provider (lines 986/1008/1174); it never calls
  it, and never calls runBehavior.

  $ grep -rn runBehavior packages/pi-extension/src packages/pi-extension/tests \
      packages/agent-core/src | grep -v behavior-runner.ts
  (no output)

  runBehavior has ZERO callers, including from tests. The governed
  AutofixLoop path -- MutationGuard, capability enforcement, constitution
  proposal, approval/apply -- is dead code. The live loop is the continuation
  path in extension.ts, which implements none of it.

RCA is worse: there is no root-cause stage anywhere in the codebase, on
either path. It was never built, only described. The fix agent is handed the
failure and asked to repair it; whatever diagnosis happens is internal to
that model call and is neither recorded nor used to drive a rule change.

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS
The constitution step is the entire point of the product: without it the
system fixes the same class of bug forever and learns nothing. A loop that
detects and repairs is a test-fixer; the constitution update is what makes it
a system that prevents recurrence.

It also means the governed path's safety properties are theoretical. Every
capability/mutation_class guarantee reviewed to date is enforced in code that
never executes. br-xz6q was one instance of that gap; this is the general
case, and it should be checked whether anything else believed to be enforced
is only enforced there.

RELATED CONFIG GAP (do not fix silently -- needs a human decision)
  ensemble/.ensemble/behaviors/fix-failing-test/behavior.yaml
    mutation_classes: [artifact.write]
The user's own production behavior omits constitution.propose, so even once
the step is reachable it would be denied there. The trial repo has
[artifact.write, constitution.propose]. Deciding whether the real repo should
grant a behavior the right to amend the constitution is the user's call.

SCOPE
1. Decide whether the continuation path grows RCA + constitution stages, or
   the governed path becomes reachable and the continuation path feeds it.
   (The second is more code but keeps one enforcement point.)
2. Build an actual RCA stage that records a cause and passes it to the
   constitution proposal, rather than leaving diagnosis implicit.
3. Delete or revive runBehavior. Leaving unreachable governance code in the
   tree is how br-xz6q survived review.
close_reason:
CLOSED as resolved, but the FRAMING is obsolete rather than the concern, so the reasoning matters more than usual.

THE ROOT CAUSE ON THIS BEAD NO LONGER EXISTS. It reads: proposeConstitutionChange is called only from behavior-runner.ts:241, extension.ts never calls runBehavior, so the step cannot run. On this branch behavior-runner.ts is DELETED and proposeConstitutionChange does not exist. The CQRS port removed the dual-path problem outright; one-dispatch-path.test.ts pins that a single dispatch path remains. So the bead cannot be closed by 'the fix landed' -- the thing it described was removed underneath it.

BOTH COMPLAINTS ARE NOW SATISFIED BY THE REPLACEMENT.
1. RCA stage. fix-failing-test has a record-diagnosis step that records the diagnosis as a fact SEPARATELY from any fix, so a confident diagnosis with no candidate is still recorded. The chain is: investigate.diagnosis -> fix.propose(rationale) -> proposal.rationale -> fix.verified.payload.rationale -> constitution-learning.assess(diagnosis).
2. 'Declined' vs 'never ran'. constitution.no_change_warranted is its own declared outcome, so a run that judged no rule warranted is now distinguishable from one that never executed.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY MISSING, AND IS NOW FIXED. The consuming half was untested. commands.test.ts proves fix.verified CARRIES rationale and evidence; nothing proved the manifest RESOLVES them. A ${...} input naming a payload field that does not exist resolves to nothing and the step runs anyway, with a prompt missing the one input this bead is about -- silent, no error. Added agent-core/tests/shipped-constitution-manifest.test.ts, 7 tests against the SHIPPED manifest and the SHIPPED prompt, covering the whole last mile:
- the diagnosis, evidence and proposalRef reach the assessment
- the manifest declares both inputs (not only a comment claiming so)
- the real assess.md actually renders {{diagnosis}} and {{evidence}} -- a template that dropped them would receive the values and discard them, leaving the assessment as blind as before while every manifest-level test stayed green
- no placeholder lacks a matching input, which would render as a literal {{foo}} and read to the model as a formatting glitch rather than missing data
Mutation-checked: deleting the diagnosis input fails 2 tests.

FOUND WHILE VERIFYING, FILED AS br-6yt6. reference-flow.e2e.test.ts -- the repository's end-to-end proof -- embeds INLINE COPIES of the manifests rather than running the shipped ones, and the constitution-learning copy has already drifted: it still passes only proposalRef and detail, predating this fix. It would have stayed green if the shipped manifest lost the diagnosis inputs entirely. Mitigated for this input pair by the new test; not fixed in general, and the e2e is protected so changing it needs operator approval.

546 agent-core tests pass, eslint clean. Commits 5eb36b0, 2fb52ad.

comments.author: ldangelo
comments.text:
CORRECTION -- the central claim of this bead was WRONG. Retracting it.

I claimed "runBehavior has zero callers, the entire governed path is dead
code". `runBehavior` is not a symbol in this repo at all, which is why the
grep came back empty. The real export is createBehaviorInvoker
(behavior-runner.ts:111), and it IS called live at extension.ts:996.

My own evidence disputed the claim before I filed it: the live run logged an
`invocation` record, and that record is written by the onRecord callback
passed into createBehaviorInvoker at extension.ts:1024. I read that log and
still filed "unreachable". An empty grep for a name I never confirmed existed
is not evidence of absence.

WHAT THE LIVE RECORD ACTUALLY SAYS
  keys: [behavior, issue, note]
  outcome: null
  note: "no fix candidate offered"
  constitution: null

So the governed invoker ran, and:

1. It offered NO FIX CANDIDATE. The repair happened on the continuation path
   (the model edited files itself). So MutationGuard / mutation_classes did
   not gate the actual fix -- not because the code is dead, but because the
   fix does not travel through it. That is br-o355's territory, and it is the
   accurate version of what I was reaching for.

2. The constitution step IS reachable. mayPropose was true (the trial
   behavior grants constitution.propose), so the code at behavior-runner.ts:
   241 called the provider. record.constitution stayed null.

REAL DEFECT, narrower than claimed: the constitution step is UNOBSERVABLE.
When the provider returns no change, behavior-runner.ts:241-273 records
nothing at all -- no declined record, no "no change implied" note. So the log
cannot distinguish:
    (a) provider never called
    (b) provider called, model said no rule change is warranted
Those need different fixes and look identical in the log. Note that (b) may
well be CORRECT here: `a - b` -> `a + b` is a typo, and a typo does not imply
a constitutional rule. I cannot tell which happened, and that is the bug.

STILL TRUE, re-verified with correct symbols: there is no RCA stage.
BehaviorRunRecord (behavior-runner.ts:40-54) has fields for outcome,
proposal, constitution, treeDrift, note -- and nothing for a cause. Diagnosis
is internal to the fix model's call, unrecorded, and does not feed the
constitution proposal. The read-only investigate-test-failure behavior exists
but is not wired as a stage of this loop.

REVISED SCOPE
  1. Record the constitution step's outcome in ALL cases, including "no
     change implied", so declining is distinguishable from not running.
  2. Confirm by observation (not by reading) whether the rule provider is
     invoked on a live run -- the current log cannot answer it.
  3. Build an RCA stage that records a cause and passes it to the
     constitution proposal.
  4. Route the continuation path's fix through capability enforcement, or
     accept that mutation_classes does not gate model-applied fixes and say
     so explicitly. (Overlaps br-o355.)

Dropping priority from P1: the loop is not missing its back half the way I
said. It is under-instrumented, and RCA is genuinely absent.

comments.author: ldangelo
comments.text:
CROSS-REFERENCE: br-zcxb / br-o355 / br-r3om / br-xz6q share one spine.

THE SPINE: a single test failure fires TWO dispatch paths.
  governed      createBehaviorInvoker (behavior-runner.ts:111), called live
                at extension.ts:996. Carries MutationGuard, mutation_classes,
                the constitution step, approval gating.
  continuation  the extension injects a turn and the MODEL edits files with
                its own tools. Carries snapshot/rollback, write-boundary,
                whole-suite verification, and (now) the propose hold.

Neither is dead -- br-r3om observed both firing on one failure, and the live
loop-trial run logged an `invocation` record (governed) alongside a
`continuation` record. The governed invoker reported "no fix candidate
offered": it ran, and the repair happened on the other path.

So the defect is not "governance is unreachable" -- I filed that on br-zcxb
and retracted it. It is that THE FIX DOES NOT TRAVEL THROUGH THE GOVERNED
PATH, so every guarantee implemented as an authorization check on a patch has
nothing to authorize.

WHAT EACH BEAD IS, UNDER THAT SPINE
  br-xz6q  CLOSED/in review, PR #98. policy.mode was checked only in
           MutationGuard.authorize(), which the continuation path never
           reaches. Fixed by enforcing mode at verification time instead.
           Precedent: the fix did NOT route writes through the guard.
  br-o355  grants scope to the execution window, not the session. Its own
           comment proposes routing continuation writes through MutationGuard
           and expects that to close br-xz6q too. br-xz6q is now closed
           WITHOUT that, so the shared estimate should shrink, not carry over.
  br-r3om  the fix-provider CHILD runs with --no-extensions, so nothing binds
           it -- it can write the live tree directly, regardless of which path
           governs the patch it returns. This is upstream of the other three:
           routing writes through the guard does not help if the writer is a
           process outside the guard entirely.
  br-zcxb  narrowest, and independent of the routing question: the
           constitution step records nothing when the provider returns no
           change, so "declined" and "never ran" are indistinguishable; and
           there is no RCA stage at all (BehaviorRunRecord, behavior-runner.ts
           :40-54, has no cause field).

SEQUENCING, so one defect is not scoped four times
  1. br-r3om first. It is P1, in review, and it is the only one where the
     enforcement boundary itself is bypassed rather than bypassed-around.
  2. br-zcxb's instrumentation half next. It is cheap, it does not depend on
     the routing decision, and until the constitution step is observable we
     cannot tell whether the back half of the loop works at all -- which
     makes any estimate for the rest guesswork.
  3. br-o355's routing decision last, informed by 1 and 2. If the continuation
     path keeps applying fixes model-side, MutationGuard may be the wrong
     chokepoint entirely and the effect-based write boundary the right one.
     br-xz6q is evidence for that reading.

RCA (the remaining half of br-zcxb) is orthogonal to all of this: no path
records a cause, so it is new work wherever the fix lands.

comments.author: ldangelo
comments.text:
ANSWERED BY OBSERVATION. PR #101.

The open question was whether the rule provider is ever invoked on a live
run. The log could not say, because the step recorded nothing unless a change
came back. Instrumented it, rebuilt the bundle, re-ran the same scenario:

  constitution: {"status": "none",
                 "detail": "rule provider ran and implied no constitution change"}

The provider RAN. It has been running all along. It declined, silently, and
the silence is what I misread as "the step never fires".

Its judgement also looks CORRECT. The failure under repair was `a - b` where
`a + b` was meant. A typo does not imply a constitutional rule, and a system
that amended its constitution over one would be worse, not better. So the
back half of the loop is not missing -- on this input it had nothing to say,
and now says so.

That retires the instrumentation half of this bead and the second item of the
revised scope. Statuses now recorded: skipped (capability gate refused,
provider not called), unavailable (granted but no provider configured), none
(ran, no change implied).

REMAINING, and now the whole of this bead: there is still no RCA stage.
BehaviorRunRecord has no field for a cause, no path computes one, and the
rule provider is therefore asked to judge a constitution change from the raw
failure rather than from a diagnosis. That is plausibly WHY it declines: with
no cause in hand, "no rule implied" is the only safe answer it can give.

That reframes the remaining work. It is not "wire up the constitution step",
it is "give it something to reason from". Worth testing before building:
re-run with a failure that genuinely implies a rule (say, a fix that would
have to touch a guardrail) and see whether the provider proposes anything at
all. If it declines there too, the gap is the missing RCA input, not the
provider.

comments.author: ldangelo
comments.text:
HYPOTHESIS DISPROVED by direct experiment. The rule provider does not need an
RCA stage to produce a rule.

Called createAgentConstitutionProvider directly -- real model subprocess,
real prompt, real parser -- bypassing dispatch and the session lifecycle
entirely, so the br-mr22 race could not interfere. Two inputs, differing only
in the failure output:

CONTROL, an ordinary typo (-1 !== 3):
  NO AMENDMENT                                              [16.7s]

TREATMENT, same typo plus one extra line of real output --
"guard.test.js: suite did not load" with the summary counting it as passed:
  PROPOSED                                                  [28.8s]
  rationale: "The run reported 'guard.test.js: suite did not load' but only
             counted assertion results, so once the ordinary math bug is
             fixed the run would pass while a whole suite never executed."
  rule: "- Any test suite that fails to load, compile, or be discovered must
         make the test command exit non-zero, and a passing run must execute
         every test file in the repo; a green result where any suite did not
         load or was left out counts as a failure."

So the provider discriminates correctly on failure output ALONE. It declines
ordinary bugs and proposes on a systemic gap, from the same 8000-char
failure excerpt, with no diagnosis in hand. My "it declines because it has no
cause to reason from" was wrong.

Worth noting what it proposed: that rule is precisely the defect this repo
actually shipped and had to fix -- a suite that fails to LOAD being counted
as a pass, which is why unloadable suites now report `inconclusive` rather
than `failed`. The learning half of the loop can produce a rule that would
have prevented a real bug of ours. It has never been allowed to.

WHAT THIS BEAD IS NOW. Nothing. Both halves are resolved:
  - observability: PR #101, merged-pending
  - "no RCA input": disproved above
The remaining blocker is entirely br-mr22 -- the governed run that carries
this step is killed at session end, so the provider is never reached in a
real run. Nothing about RCA needs building to unblock step 3.

An RCA stage may still be worth having for OTHER reasons (a recorded cause is
useful to a human reading the log, and to the fix provider). But it is not a
prerequisite for the constitution step, and this bead should not be used to
justify it. Closing in favour of br-mr22.

Method note: this question survived three full live runs without being
answered, because each run lost the dispatch race. Testing the component
directly took one call and 46 seconds. When a lifecycle keeps eating the
evidence, call the function.

comments.author: ldangelo
comments.text:
Re-reviewed after br-behavior-runtime-cqrs-xl24. STILL VALID, partially mitigated.

The constitution-learning behavior's assess step (.ensemble/behaviors/constitution-learning/behavior.yaml:42-54) receives proposalRef, detail and command from the fix.verified event -- but NOT the diagnosis produced by investigation.record. The two behaviors are joined by an event, and fix.verified's payload does not carry the diagnosis forward, so the rule provider still judges an amendment without the RCA in hand.

Mitigated in that assess now has tools [read, grep, glob] and can investigate for itself, and it must emit warrantsRule plus evidence to proceed. Not fixed: self-directed investigation is not the same as being handed the diagnosis that was already produced.

Likely fix: carry investigation output on the fix.proposed/fix.verified payload, or have constitution-learning read the proposal's evidence refs from the ProposalStore.
